instruments.name: Law Overlap Detection System
instruments.summary: This AI-driven initiative automates the identification of legal overlaps and contradictions within the National Registry of Legislation. It helps government officials and legal experts ensure that new regulations do not conflict with existing laws. By streamlining legislative drafting, the tool benefits legal workers by providing a simplified legal environment.

instruments.name: Incorporation of Artificial Intelligence into the Electronic Administrative Records System
instruments.summary: This initiative uses artificial intelligence to automatically summarise appeals submitted by citizens to the Social Security administration. It helps caseworkers quickly understand the main issues raised and classify each appeal for the appropriate handling. The system was developed to speed up processing times and manage growing workloads while ensuring citizens’ appeals are handled more efficiently.

instruments.name: Responsible Use of Artificial Intelligence Policy (Subnational: Newfoundland and Labrador)
instruments.summary: The Government of Newfoundland and Labrador’s Responsible Use of Artificial Intelligence Policy sets clear rules for how AI can be used safely and responsibly across government. It ensures AI is approved, transparent, and subject to human oversight, while protecting privacy, fairness, and public trust. The policy supports responsible innovation and consistent decision-making across departments.

instruments.name: Technical and Ethical Guidelines on Artificial Intelligence for the Capital District of Bogotá (Subnational: Bogotá D.C.)
instruments.summary: Bogotá, through its District Commission for Digital Transformation, created official guidelines to guide public entities in the responsible and transparent use of artificial intelligence. The initiative sets out clear rules and a common process with human oversight and risk management. It responds to the rapid growth in the use of AI and aims to build trust and harness innovation to strengthen Bogotá’s position as a digital capital.

instruments.name: Satellite-based system for waterlogging detection using artificial intelligence
instruments.summary: A satellite-based AI system was developed for the public water management authority JP “Vode Vojvodine” to detect waterlogging and map risk areas across Vojvodina, helping them make faster and more informed decisions. The platform combines satellite images, weather data and soil information to identify where excess water may cause damage. It was created to reduce agricultural losses and support better planning, prevention and response to extreme weather conditions.

instruments.name: AI eGovernment Chatbots
instruments.summary: This initiative aims at the development and deployment of sovereign, state-operated AI assistants across public administration websites and portals to support citizens with information and public services. It addresses service accessibility and contact centre capacity by providing faster and more reliable digital assistance.

instruments.name: DigiTeks - Application of AI for understanding the Serbian language and digitalization in the field of legislation
instruments.summary: The initiative is a flexible module for automatic text correction, designed to improve efficiency, quality, and reliability in writing and communication. While targeted at “JP Službeni Glasnik”, it potentially benefits institutions, professionals, and anyone working with Serbian-language content. Developed to address the need for accurate OCR and text analysis, it opens opportunities for integration with existing tools and broader language applications.

instruments.name: VODOSTAI - Software platform for flood prediction and prevention based on artificial intelligence methods and IoT devices
instruments.summary: VodostAI is a software platform that uses AI and data from IoT sensors to help predict floods and support early warnings. It helps water authorities, municipalities, and emergency services prepare and respond sooner, reducing damage and risk to people. It was developed to improve forecasting and decision-making where data are limited or arrive too late for effective action.

instruments.name: Science and Technology Parks as AI Innovation Infrastructure
instruments.summary: This initiative develops and strengthens Science and Technology Parks in Serbia as innovation infrastructure for AI development, providing specialised infrastructure, mentoring, and support services for AI start-ups and innovative companies. By fostering collaboration with research and higher education institutions, it accelerates AI-based entrepreneurship, supports commercialisation of AI solutions, and drives economic growth, employment, and the adoption of advanced technologies nationwide.

instruments.name: Detecting tax evasion using artificial intelligence
instruments.summary: The initiative leverages artificial intelligence and big data analytics to strengthen risk based approaches to personal income tax compliance. By identifying atypical taxpayer behaviour, it supports more targeted audits and efficient allocation of enforcement resources. The project contributes to the broader modernisation of the Serbian Tax Administration and promotes evidence based policymaking in tax administration.

instruments.name: Prediction of daily inflows in the reservoirs at the Drina River basin based on Artificial Intelligence – DrinaAI
instruments.summary: The initiative uses artificial intelligence to predict daily water inflows into reservoirs in the Drina River basin. It helps water managers and energy operators plan more effectively. It was developed to improve forecasting accuracy and support better decision making in water and energy management.

instruments.name: AI Strategy for the Federal Public Service 2025-27
instruments.summary: The AI Strategy lays out a plan for how the government will move forward with AI from 2025–2027. It highlights the importance of coordinating across federal departments, learning from collective experiences, and supporting departments of all sizes and maturity as they explore this technology. It also sets out the role of leaders in adapting AI to their organisations’ mandates. This role includes ensuring strong data foundations and the use of agile practices.

instruments.name: Generative AI Literacy Programme
instruments.summary: This initiative is a Generative AI Literacy Programme for public servants at Brazil’s National Telecommunications Agency. It offers workshops, guidance and examples to help staff use AI safely and effectively in real work tasks. It was created to build essential digital skills, promote responsible AI use and support the safe adoption of AI in daily administrative activities.

instruments.name: Use of Artificial Intelligence Models in the Qualitative Evaluation of Responses - Avalia
instruments.summary: Anatel has developed AvalIA, a tool that uses artificial intelligence models to automatically assess the quality of telecommunications companies' responses to consumer complaints. This initiative seeks to make customer service more efficient and transparent, benefiting both consumers and the regulatory agency itself. AvalIA was created to expand and improve the analysis of companies' responses, ensuring that consumers receive more appropriate information and more effective solutions.

instruments.name: Government of Canada AI Registry - Minimum Viable Product
instruments.summary: This version of the Government of Canada (GC) AI Register is a minimum viable product (MVP), or an early version with only basic features and content that is used to gather feedback. It was assembled from existing sources of information, including Algorithmic Impact Assessments, Access to Information requests, responses to Parliamentary Questions, Personal Information Banks, and the GC Service Inventory.

instruments.name: Public Service Commission (PSC) AI Agent for Travel
instruments.summary: The AI Agent for Travel is an artificial intelligence assistant that gives public service employees quick, clear answers about travel rules and expense claims. It was created by government staff to reduce the large number of emails, delays, and confusion caused by complex travel policies. The assistant provides answers in seconds, saves staff time, and lowers administrative costs.

instruments.name: Use of artificial intelligence for the characterisation of the environmental regulatory burden of projects
instruments.summary: The initiative quantifies the environmental regulatory burden in Chile by analysing environmental permits to identify the specific obligations generated. By providing objective evidence, it supports authorities and investors in creating a more transparent and efficient regulatory framework. The tool was developed to overcome the challenges of manual data processing, transforming thousands of pages of complex requirements into clear, comparable data for a more effective regulatory evaluation.

instruments.name: AI Pilot: CV screening in consultants’ recruitment
instruments.summary: Formez PA's AI Pilot for CV Screening is an internal tool that helps Formez’ selection committees review CVs from candidates applying to become consultants for Formez PA's project activities. It uses natural language processing to identify skills and create a preliminary ranking based on job requirements, reducing manual workload for staff. Launched in May 2025, it addresses the sharp rise in internal applications via the inPA portal while keeping human judgement central to decisions.

instruments.name: Camilla - Digital Assistant for Public Sector Competitions
instruments.summary: Camilla is a generative AI virtual assistant that helps citizens access clear, up-to-date information on public recruitment competitions through the inPA Portal, Italy’s single gateway for public administration hiring. Developed by Formez PA with CSI Piemonte, it enhances access to notices, simplifies participation, and reduces the workload of staff managing assistance requests.

instruments.name: OpenCouncil (Subnational: Municipality of Chania)
instruments.summary: Municipal council meetings are the core of local democracy, yet citizens rarely engage with them. In Greece, meetings are legally public but practically inaccessible: hours of unstructured video, no searchable records, and no way to know when your neighbourhood is discussed. The 2024 OECD Survey on Drivers of Trust found that only 21% of Greeks believe they can influence government, among the lowest in Europe.

instruments.name: AI Brownfield Site
instruments.summary: Austria has great potential in terms of industrial and commercial brownfield sites. The initiative is a nationwide public AI-based map that identifies these brownfields primarily based on geodata and aerial photographs. It was created to provide reliable information on unused industrial and commercial sites for planners, municipalities, developers and researchers. The goal is to support land recycling and reduce land consumption by making these opportunities visible.

instruments.name: Innovation, Automation, and AI Acceleration (i3A)
instruments.summary: AAFC’s Innovation, Automation and AI Acceleration (i3A) advances responsible AI adoption by combining a Centre of Expertise, cross-functional pods, enterprise training, tool deployment, and innovation showcases. The programme builds skills and capacity while enabling employees closest to delivery to test and scale solutions that reduce repetitive work, improve efficiency, and strengthen service delivery and data management across the organisation.

instruments.name: Use of Artificial Intelligence by Courts
instruments.summary: Two publications were developed 1) to support courts in determining whether and how to best use AI tools to enhance court operations and 2) in responding to the use of AI by court users, including litigants, counsel, and others engaging directly with the court respectively.

instruments.name: DaFNE chatbot
instruments.summary: DaFNE (Database for Research on Sustainable Development) is an online platform, used to manage and publish nationally funded research projects. Research results are stored there in the form of report files (PDF). To facilitate broad and easy access to these results for multiple stakeholder groups, a chatbot was developed to support an efficient information retrieval. This chatbot is a text-based dialogue system, based on a vector database and LLM, which only accesses publicly available projects.

instruments.name: PolluSense
instruments.summary: PolluSense is an AI-driven pilot that uses satellite data to detect industrial pollution in Canadian freshwater ecosystems in near-real time. It supports compliance with the Canadian Environmental Protection Act and the Fisheries Act by automatically flagging water-quality changes for analyst review and routing confirmed events to regional officers. It enables cost-effective, continuous monitoring, improving response times, enforcement, and freshwater protection.

instruments.name: AI Copilot for the National Post Provider
instruments.summary: Posta Kopilot is an AI-powered mobile application that assists postal workers with manual mail sorting at the National Post of Serbia (Pošta Srbije), which processes over 2.1 million pieces daily. By interpreting address information and guiding sorting decisions in real time, it has increased sorting efficiency by over 20% and cut new-employee onboarding from several months to a few weeks. Developed through Serbia's Innovation Fund GovTech programme with LambdaWorks.

instruments.name: Tax return nudging
instruments.summary:
Tax control reviews a large number of tax forms for undisclosed rental incomes each year, taking up time and manpower. A prediction model has been developed which has the ability to predict the likelihood of an undisclosed rental income on a tax form before the tax form is submitted.
This has resulted in substantial gains in tax collection, and both freed up time and manpower otherwise used in more difficult tax control cases.

instruments.name: Data Sharing AI (DSAI) - Proof of Value
instruments.summary: Data governance in Ireland is overseen by the Data Governance Board under the Data Sharing and Governance Act 2019, enabling transparent data sharing across Public Sector Bodies. The OGCIO Data Governance Unit provides a Playbook to ensure secure, transparent sharing under the Act. This PoV shows how governed AI agents can support drafting DSAs at Stage 3 of the Playbook, with no autonomous decisions, full Human in the Loop oversight, and strong adherence to governance principles.

instruments.name: Prototyping AI Apps for Addressing Labor Shortages through Cross-Ministerial Collaboration
instruments.summary: Japan is developing a prototype AI agent that automates routine administrative work common across ministries/agencies, allowing policymakers to focus on strategic tasks. By combining the knowledge of government staff with Digital Agency’s engineering skills the aim is to create user‑centered tools that fit real operations and gather issues from frontline teams, prioritize feasible improvements, and accelerate practical solutions while also reducing burdens caused by outdated rules and procedures

instruments.name: Water Sector Costing Forecast
instruments.summary: This initiative predicts future costs for each water plant and for each main spending category, such as electricity, chemicals, labor, and maintenance. It helps finance and operations teams plan budgets better, spot unusual cost increases early, and make better decisions on where to control spending. It was developed to improve cost visibility, reduce surprises in future expenses, and support more efficient management of water production assets.

instruments.name: AI for resilient digital  government services (Subnational: Province of Cordoba)
instruments.summary: The Province of Córdoba (Argentina) developed an autonomous AI agent system that monitors, diagnoses, and resolves incidents in the digital infrastructure supporting public services. Operating across government cloud platforms serving 3.8 million citizens, it reduces service disruptions from hours to minutes while creating full audit trails for every automated action. https://infografia-aws-gob-cba.vercel.app/

instruments.name: Horizons: Empowering Educators with Artificial Intelligence (AI) Technologies
instruments.summary: National professional development programme led by the UAE Ministry of Education and delivered in partnership with the Emirates College for Advanced Education to equip teachers and school leaders to integrate AI into teaching, assessment and school practice. It builds practical capability across seven curriculum-aligned AI areas, including AI foundations, data and algorithms, ethical use, classroom applications and innovation. Launched at GITEX Global 2025, scaling to train 5,000 educators.

instruments.name: AI Safety and Security Institute Deutschland
instruments.summary:
AISI Deutschland is a national competence and evaluation center for Frontier AI models. It combines technical, strategic, and security policy expertise within a single central institution. 
AISI Deutschland is intended to enable the Federal Government to
-	identify safety and security-related risks at an early stage,
-	develop evidence-based courses of action,
-	strengthen Germany’s digital sovereignty with regard to AI safety and security, and
-	strategically assess international developments.

instruments.name: Technical Verification for Appropriate Use of Generative AI in Administration
instruments.summary: Japan's Digital Agency ran a pilot from December 2023 to March 2024 testing how text-based generative AI could improve government work. Officials at central ministries and selected local governments used a chat platform with multiple large language models, examining use cases including public comment processing, regulatory drafting, and code generation. The pilot generated practical knowledge on where generative AI delivers efficiency gains and quality improvements in administration.

instruments.name: Integrated Innovation Strategy
instruments.summary: Since 2018, Japan’s Cabinet has approved a new Integrated Innovation Strategy each year, providing an end-to-end plan from basic research to social implementation of AI and science policy. The series operationalises Japan’s multi-year STI Basic Plans and realises Society 5.0 by coordinating AI, quantum, biotech and other technologies across government. It benefits researchers, industry and citizens through sustained investment and governance of emerging technologies.

instruments.name: Council on Social Principles of Human Centric AI
instruments.summary: The Council on Human-Centric AI Social Principles is an advisory body established in 2018 under Japan's Cabinet Office to develop and maintain ethical principles for AI development and deployment. It developed the Social Principles of Human-Centric AI in 2019, which guide Japan's approach to AI based on three core values: dignity, diversity & inclusion, and sustainability. The Council continues to meet annually to review and update guidance in response to technological development.

instruments.name: Orientation, Methodologies and Guides for AI in the Public Service
instruments.summary: A set of guides designed to help public servants and the general public understand and responsibly use AI tools, without requiring prior IT knowledge. They provide an overview of Generative AI, its limits and risks, practical guidance for ethical use in the Brazilian public sector, tips for selecting tools, and best practices for prompt design, demystifying AI and supporting its responsible adoption.

instruments.name: AI Assistants for Supporting Labor Justice Conciliation
instruments.summary: The initiative integrates five specialised AI assistants into Chat-JT, the Brazilian Labor Justice's official tool. They support the entire conciliation cycle: from intelligent screening of high-potential settlement cases to strategic risk and burden-of-proof analysis. The system also enables immediate updates of complex calculations during hearings using the SELIC rate and savings indices, ensuring precision and agility in the judicial process.

instruments.name: Air Travel Complaints Artificial Intelligence Initiative
instruments.summary: The Air Travel Complaints Artificial Intelligence Initiative focuses on improving decision quality and consistency through AI‑enhanced drafting support, automating document and case‑file summarisation to streamline workflows, and accelerating complaint handling to deliver faster, more proportional, and higher‑quality resolutions.

instruments.name: Unified Intelligent Assistant
instruments.summary: The Unified Intelligent Assistant is an AI powered conversational tool developed by the Ministry of Digital Transformation that is integrated into existing websites to help users quickly find reliable information from government portals. It reduces the burden on traditional support channels by automating answers to recurring questions and provides 24/7 access to clear, user friendly information.

instruments.name: Nusuk Card System
instruments.summary: The Nusuk Card System is a comprehensive IoT and AI-driven crowd management initiative designed to facilitate and secure the Hajj journey for over 1.8 million pilgrims. By utilising RFID-enabled smart cards and a network of over 800 surveillance cameras equipped with AI analytics across the Holy Sites, the system tracks pilgrim movements, ensures adherence to scheduling plans, and prevents overcrowding.

instruments.name: ProVerifier
instruments.summary: This initiative develops an AI-powered inspection tool that helps SFDA inspectors verify whether food, pharmaceutical, cosmetic, and medical device products comply with SFDA regulations. Inspectors can photograph or scan a product, and the system automatically extracts key details and checks them against official registration databases and safety standards. The tool was developed to reduce manual inspection time, minimise human error, and strengthen public health protection.

instruments.name: RASID
instruments.summary: RASID is an AI-powered inspection system developed by the Saudi Food and Drug Authority to support inspectors at border checkpoints. The system analyses images of medicines carried by travelers to detect controlled substances and verify compliance with regulatory rules. It improves inspection speed, accuracy, and consistency while protecting public health and preventing misuse of restricted drugs.

instruments.name: Responsible AI Guidance for the Public Service: GenAI
instruments.summary: New Zealand’s Responsible AI Guidance for the Public Service: GenAI is updated guidance to support Public Service organisations and officials to explore generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) systems in ways that are safe, transparent and responsible. The guidance is part of a suite developed by the Government Chief Digital Officer (GCDO) including an AI toolkit, case studies, and other resources to be developed over time.

instruments.name: AI Scribe for Emergency Departments
instruments.summary: New Zealand’s AI Scribe for Emergency Departments is an AI clinical documentation tool used nationwide to support emergency health services. Ambient, generative AI securely transcribes consultations with patient consent and automatically creates quality draft clinical notes, summaries and referral letters. Clinician time is prioritised for more direct patient care with faster documentation enabling more patients to be seen each shift.

instruments.name: AI-Powered Research Support Service (RSS)
instruments.summary: The Research Support Service is an integrated platform leveraging hyper-scale AI to support the entire research process, from topic identification to report writing and dissemination of outcomes. It primarily targets public researchers, including those from the National Research Council for Economics, Humanities and Social Sciences and its 26 affiliated research institutes. It was developed to efficiently analyse vast volumes of policy research data and enhance research quality and productivity.

instruments.name: Enhancing Digital Security and Trust Act, 2024 (Subnational: Ontario)
instruments.summary: In January 2025, Ontario brought the Enhancing Digital Security and Trust Act, 2024 (EDSTA) into force. EDSTA builds a foundation to support the responsible use of AI through: introducing a definition of “artificial intelligence system” in alignment with leading jurisdictions, and creating regulation-making authorities to set accountability, risk management and transparency requirements and technical standards around the use of AI systems for select public sector organisations.

instruments.name: REGi - Regulatory Intelligence (Subnational: Ontario)
instruments.summary: REGi is an internal government AI tool to reduce burden and improving life for people and businesses by making it easier to find red tape and uncover opportunities to modernise laws, regulations, policies and forms. The tool currently uses AI to scan Ontario laws, including regulations, and forms to help identify government rules that businesses and individuals need to follow, including where there may be outdated language and/or overly dense rules.  The tool will evolve over time.

instruments.name: Pakistan Digital Authority (PDA)
instruments.summary: Pakistan Digital Authority (PDA) is a statutory body established under the Digital Nation Pakistan Act 2025 to lead Pakistan’s digital transformation. It develops and implements the National Digital Masterplan and coordinates efforts across government and stakeholders. The PDA also provides oversight, standards, and compliance for data governance, AI, and emerging technologies.

instruments.name: Sindh Cloud First Policy (Subnational: Province of Sindh)
instruments.summary: The Sindh Cloud First Policy is a provincial government policy issued by the Province of Sindh, Pakistan in 2022 to mandate cloud-based infrastructure across all public sector entities. By establishing a Cloud Acquisition Office and shifting ICT procurement toward scalable cloud services, the policy builds the foundational compute layer required for AI adoption and data-driven governance across provincial departments. The policy benefits all government agencies and the citizens they serve.

instruments.name: Roadmap Toward the Development and Ethical Implementation of Artificial Intelligence in Guanajuato (Subnational: Guanajuato State)
instruments.summary: This roadmap helps Guanajuato’s government, universities, businesses, and communities use AI in a responsible way that respects people’s rights. It was created to turn UNESCO’s AI ethics guidance into practical steps that reduce risks and make the benefits of AI reach more people.  It sets out three phases—learning and engagement, deploying useful solutions, and becoming a leader in ethical innovation.

instruments.name: Explorer
instruments.summary: KAŞİF is an AI-based big data risk analysis system developed by TÜBİTAK BİLGEM for the Republic of Türkiye's Ministry of Treasury and Finance. It analyses daily tax and financial data of over four million taxpayers to identify risky behaviour. The initiative was developed to overcome the limits of rule-based audits and enable early detection of tax fraud, fake invoices and unjustified VAT refunds.

instruments.name: Cali ResuelVE Knowledge Library (Subnational: Cali)
instruments.summary: Cali ResuelVE Knowledge Library is an AI-powered tool used in the City’s One-Stop Window to help public servants provide clear and accurate information about procedures and services. It relies on official data to deliver reliable guidance. It was developed to reduce service congestion, improve response quality, and make it easier for citizens to access municipal services.

instruments.name: Chatbot Flora (Subnational: Municipality of Escobar)
instruments.summary: Flora is an AI-powered conversational assistant for the Municipality of Escobar, Argentina, designed to centralise and automate citizen-government interactions. Operating 24/7, it enables residents to manage health appointments, track administrative procedures, and access public services through a single omnichannel interface. By resolving over 570,000 inquiries annually, Flora reduces waiting times, eliminates bureaucratic friction, and optimises municipal resource allocation.

instruments.name: Responsible AI Policy
instruments.summary: The Responsible AI Policy promotes the responsible development and use of AI aligned with ethical principles across the whole AI lifecycle. It shapes the direction for providing clear guidance to manage risks while enabling innovation. It promotes ethical and responsible use as well as mitigating harms such as bias, privacy violations, and misuse, while strengthening trust and accountability in AI systems.

instruments.name: Government AI Offices
instruments.summary: AI has witnessed a rapid development in the past two years. Establishing AI offices in government helps coordinate the adoption of Artificial Intelligence in a structured, safe and strategic way. They create opportunities for innovation, stronger governance, and improved trust in AI-powered government services.

instruments.name: Estishraf
instruments.summary: Estishraf is an initiative by the Saudi Data and Artificial Intelligence Authority that enables evidence-based decision-making across government. It uses advanced analytics and artificial intelligence to analyse integrated government data, simulate policy outcomes, detect patterns and emerging risks, and generate actionable insights for policymakers. The initiative helps government entities better understand economic and social trends, evaluate policy impacts, strengthen national planning.

instruments.name: Generative AI for Engineering Design
instruments.summary: This initiative is an AI-powered tool developed for the Saudi Water Authority that automatically reads and interprets complex engineering diagrams used in water desalination plants. It identifies equipment, classifies plant processes, and allows engineers to ask questions about the diagrams through a chat interface. It was developed to reduce the time and manual effort required to analyse these technically complex documents.

instruments.name: Guidance on Government use of Public Generative AI Tools
instruments.summary: This initiative provides updated guidance to help Australian Government agencies safely use publicly available generative AI tools, such as chatbots that can draft text, summarise documents, or answer questions. The guidance explains how staff can use these tools with government information that is not classified or sensitive while protecting personal and commercial information. The guidance was updated to reflect new information security advice from the Department of Home Affairs.

instruments.name: National Artificial Intelligence Strategy 2026–2030
instruments.summary: Peru’s National Artificial Intelligence Strategy 2026–2030, approved by the Presidency of the Council of Ministers through Ministerial Resolution No. 152-2026-PCM, is a national strategic instrument designed to organise and coordinate State interventions for the development, governance and management of artificial intelligence. It establishes a long-term vision and provides a framework for strengthening AI capabilities, deployment, oversight and public-sector coordination across the country.

instruments.name: Data Center Strategy
instruments.summary: Germany’s Data Center Strategy, published in March 2026, aims to double national data centre capacity and quadruple AI compute and HPC capacity by 2030. The data center strategy identifies three priority areas: energy and sustainability, site availability and land use, as well as technology and sovereignty. These areas are supported by 28 measures to be implemented within the next 12 months.

instruments.name: High-Tech Agenda Germany – Roadmap for AI
instruments.summary: The agenda serves as a guideline for technological and economic objectives. It reflects the common understanding of the measures required to consolidate Germany's position as a nation of technological innovation, ensure technological sovereignty and maintain economic strength. The focus of the agenda is on the further development of six priority key enabling technologies, one of them artificial intelligence, and the strengthening of five research fields.

instruments.name: Strategy for the Use of AI in the Judiciary
instruments.summary: It sets out a comprehensive vision for the use of AI systems in the judiciary, along with the necessary action plans and measures to achieve this vision. The strategy aims to harness the opportunities offered by AI for the judiciary at federal and state levels, while taking due account of the associated risks and limitations. Notably, the strategy anticipates providing forward-looking support for judicial and administrative processes, enhancing access to justice, and promoting innovation in AI.

instruments.name: Guidance on privacy and the use of commercially available AI products
instruments.summary: Provides guidance to make it easier for businesses to comply with their privacy obligations when using commercially available AI products and to assist them with selecting an appropriate AI product. Aims to clarify how Australia’s privacy laws apply to AI and outlines practical steps to follow privacy best practices. Developed in response to growing concerns about the use of their personal information to deploy AI products, and uncertainty among industry around how privacy law applies to AI.

instruments.name: Framework for Governance of Indigenous Data
instruments.summary:
The Framework guides the Australian Public Service (APS) in improving governance practices for data related to Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people and aims to provide Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people greater agency over how their data are governed within the APS.
Recognising the importance of data for self-determination, the Framework provides a stepping stone towards greater awareness and acceptance by APS agencies of the principles of Indigenous Data Sovereignty.

instruments.name: Document Register Agent
instruments.summary: Finance developed the Document Register Agent (DRA) an AI-enabled tool that supports a business area to extract and record key information from documents. It uses AI and automation to extract key information from documents and store it in a consistent format. DRA was developed to improve access to historical records, reduce duplication of work, and address problems caused by broken links, inconsistent document formats and limited searchability.

instruments.name: Microsoft 365 Copilot Trial
instruments.summary: In 2024, the DTA led the 6-month Australian Government trial of Microsoft 365 Copilot – a generative AI assistant embedded in the Microsoft 365 application suite. The trial involved the distribution of over 5,700 Copilot licenses across 56 federal government agencies. Broadly, the trial and evaluation tested whether the anticipated benefits of generative AI capabilities translated into real‑world adoption by workers.

instruments.name: AI Technical Standard
instruments.summary: The standard helps agencies, technical specialists and business owners build AI safely and responsibly by providing practical guidance to design, build and deploy AI systems in ways that uphold fairness, transparency and accountability. The standard reinforces the Australian Government’s AI Ethics Principles into a set of technical requirements and guidelines.

instruments.name: Grant Connect – Web Reporting
instruments.summary: This initiative applies AI to automatically create short, clear summaries of government grant applications published on Grant Connect. It was developed to reduce manual work and errors, and to ensure grant information is accurate, consistent and easy for the public to understand.

instruments.name: AI Consultation Summary
instruments.summary: This initiative used computer tools (including AI tools) to help government staff review and summarise public consultation responses more efficiently. It was developed to manage a large volume of submissions while ensuring every response was still read and checked by people. The approach aimed to save time, improve consistency, and support better advice to government while protecting privacy.

instruments.name: Remote Pilot Program
instruments.summary: The Department uses drones to provide innovative and expert advice grounded in evidence and science, provide regulatory compliance and surveillance activities, provide land management, visitor safety and infrastructure inspection in Commonwealth Parks, engage and partner with First Nations ranger groups and provide staff safety and wellbeing in operational settings.

instruments.name: farmpredict
instruments.summary:
farmpredict is a simulation model of Australian farm businesses. It uses statistical machine learning to predict how Australian farms will be affected by recent and future weather and other factors like changes in commodity prices. 
Outputs from farmpredict support government and other organisations in planning early for supporting farms through drought and other challenges. 
farmpredict can also separate effects of climate from other changes, helping understand the costs of climate change.

instruments.name: AI in Digital Health
instruments.summary: The Digital Health Agency’s AI initiative aims to improve how health information is used to support safer, more connected care for Australians. It helps clinicians and consumers by providing faster insights and reducing manual work. The initiative was created to address growing demand for timely, reliable health information and to ensure emerging AI tools are used safely and responsibly in the health system.

instruments.name: AI-Enabled Government Services Modernisation (Alberta) (Subnational: Alberta)
instruments.summary: The Government of Alberta is deploying AI-supported tools to modernise service delivery, including secure knowledge retrieval, automated application development, and enterprise generative AI. These tools help staff respond faster, work more consistently, and improve service quality for Albertans.

instruments.name: Act on Promotion of Research and Development, and Utilisation of AI-related Technology
instruments.summary: The AI Act and the AI Basic Plan (established in Article 18, para. (1) of the Act) constitute a government-led policy framework designed to promote AI innovation while mitigating risks. It is intended for citizens, business operators, and R&D institutes, aiming to ensure that AI benefits society and supports economic growth. It is necessary to address delays in domestic AI development and public concerns about AI-related risks, while balancing innovation promotion with effective risk mitigation.

instruments.name: AI Utilisation Guidelines on Administrative Procedures Including Those Involving Citizens
instruments.summary: The systematic development of guidelines and key considerations for AI utilisation by government agencies from the perspective of legal frameworks governing administrative procedures including those involving citizens (such as various application processes). This approach aims to prevent any misuse of AI by government agencies that could infringe upon citizens' rights and interests or compromise administrative fairness and transparency, and to not unduly restrict “risk-free” AI applications.

instruments.name: Social Media Analytics for Water Sector Issues
instruments.summary: Social Media Analysis is an AI system that automatically classifies content from X (formerly Twitter) to support the Water Authority’s leadership. It replaces a 4-hour daily manual process with automated sentiment, location, and problem classification. By feeding daily insights into the Observatory Dashboard, it enables higher management to understand citizen feedback and service reports instantly, significantly improving digital transparency and public engagement.

instruments.name: H2O AI Assistant for Water Sector
instruments.summary: H2O AI Assistant is an AI portal for water sector leadership and employees to query our water sector knowledge base via natural language. It empowers executives and managers by providing instant access to unstructured documents and structural databases, streamlining decision-making. Developed to break down information silos and modernise data retrieval, it uses generative AI models to turn complex records into actionable insights, ensuring our leadership remains data-driven and efficient.

instruments.name: AssessorIA: A Multi-Agent Ecosystem for Judicial Intelligence (Subnational: Porto Velho)
instruments.summary: AssessorIA is a pioneering multi-agent ecosystem for the Rondônia Court of Justice, designed to transform legal workflows for judges and staff. By utilising "Specialists" for routine tasks and autonomous agents for complex case analysis, it integrates with judicial systems to solve high caseload challenges. This tool holds immense potential to centralise institutional knowledge and ensure unprecedented speed and precision, delivering a more efficient and ethical justice system.

instruments.name: GaIA: Generative AI for Judicial Intellectual Identity and Strategic Appellate Judgments (Subnational: Porto Velho)
instruments.summary: GaIA is a generative AI assistant that helps appellate judges and court staff draft complex legal documents, such as case summaries and judicial decisions. It was developed to reduce judicial backlog by speeding up the writing process while preserving each judge's unique legal voice and style. This innovation ensures faster legal services for citizens while keeping humans in control of every final decision.

instruments.name: National Office of Information Technologies (ONTI) AI Agents Guidelines
instruments.summary: Standard guide that is being developed by the National Office of Information Technologies to guide the design and sizing of projects incorporating Artificial Intelligence Agents in public administration. It is only aimed at national public administrations seeking to adopt this technology in a planned and responsible manner. Its objective is to disseminate best practices, reduce risks, and ensure secure, effective implementation aligned with State priorities and regulations.

instruments.name: SOPHOS
instruments.summary: SOPHOS is an AI‑enabled language learning tool designed for use across the Government of Canada. It was first developed to support Canadian diplomats by providing adaptive training in more than 15 foreign languages aligned with the Interagency Language Roundtable (ILR) scale. The application is now being expanded to offer English and French training that meets federal official languages requirements, helping public servants across all regions access consistent, affordable learning.

instruments.name: Ulysses - Bill Procedural Routing Analysis
instruments.summary: Ulysses - Bill Procedural Routing Analysis is an AI system incoming legislative bills to identify procedural requirements and committee assignments, then produces a dispatch draft suggesting the bill's processing regime, committee routing order, and consideration procedures. It supports the Clerk’s staff before sending the bill to be discussed in the legislative committees. The Clerk staff are required to make many deep analyses of each incoming bill, which requires a lot of time.

instruments.name: NugepIA: AI-Powered Judicial Precedent Management System (Subnational: Porto Velho)
instruments.summary: NugepIA is an AI tool that organizes repetitive lawsuits to ensure faster and more consistent decisions for citizens. It was developed to replace slow manual processes and spreadsheets that were prone to human error in identifying similar cases. The system now automatically identifies identical cases and extracts dates from documents, making the court’s work more efficient.

instruments.name: Prompting Guide for Public Administration
instruments.summary: The Prompting Guide for Public Administration is a national guidance for professionals working at National Public Administration. It supports the responsible use of generative AI by providing practical instructions, legal safeguards, and human oversight criteria for interacting with large language models. It was developed to strengthen institutional digital capabilities while ensuring data protection, transparency, and accountability in the use of AI tools.

instruments.name: Data EF AI Agent
instruments.summary: GDDE's Data EF AI Agent is a digital assistant that helps Ministry of Economy and Finance staff quickly find and understand open government data. It was designed for making searching, downloading, and analyzing datasets from the Data EF Portal less time-consuming. It enables quicker and more effective decision-making by letting users ask straightforward questions and providing statistics, charts, and summaries.

instruments.name: Ulysses - Consolidated summaries of legislative bills
instruments.summary: Legislative consultants assist parliamentarians by producing consolidated executive summaries of bills, including justifications, amendments, attached bills, and approved substitutes. This process can take hours or days depending on the volume of related documents. The solution employs generative AI tools to help consultants create these summaries, which are then reviewed and supplemented as needed.

instruments.name: Ulysses - Legislative Demand Router
instruments.summary: Ulysses - Legislative Demand Router is an AI solution designed to automatically distribute legislative demands from Members of Parliament (MPs) to appropriate expert groups within the Legislative Consultancy Department. It analyses the demand text and suggests up to three specialist groups based on thematic relevance. The system aims to increase distribution efficiency, reduce bias, and lower staff workload, with demands automatically routed when the AI's confidence exceeds 90%.

instruments.name: Ulysses – Smart analysis on e-Polls
instruments.summary: “Ulysses – Smart analysis on e-Polls” is an AI algorithm that analyses citizens' comments on e-polls about legislative bills available. The algorithm identifies the main arguments for and against each legislative bill in progress, grouping them. As all legislative bills are available for e-polls, there is a huge number of citizens contributing opinions. In addition, quantitative indicators are not sufficient to effectively identify exactly the items of articles accepted or rejection by citizens.

instruments.name: Artificial Intelligence Governance Policy of the Chamber of Deputies
instruments.summary: AI Governance Policy, which is a mandatory standard that covers: a) AI ethical principles; b) rules related to privacy, transparency, accountability, human autonomy, robustness, security, and intellectual property; c) an AI risk management process; d) an AI governance process which that adds an AI Ethics Committee to the IT governance process, with new roles and responsibilities. It is intended to maximise AI benefits and minimise risks in legislative and administrative and legislative dimension

instruments.name: AI Chatbot for Statistical Analyses of Fiscal Data
instruments.summary: The initiative consists in the development of an AI-based chatbot capable of analysing aggregated statistical data. The first chatbot prototype was based on a monolithic assistant, but a multimodal agent is being designed with the support of our technical partner, Società Generale d’Informatica (SOGEI).  The initiative develops an AI-based chatbot designed to analyse aggregates fiscal data and statistical data and support advanced analytical tasks. It addresses the growing volume and complexity

instruments.name: Ulysses chat
instruments.summary: Ulysses chat is an AI assistant developed for the Brazilian Chamber of Deputies. It considers official data and documents as well as the Chamber’s rules before answering questions.

instruments.name: BizData
instruments.summary: BizData is a free, 24/7 digital advisory service developed by Israel’s Ministry of Economy to support businesses and entrepreneurs. The AI‑powered system provides business guidance alongside relevant government and public information, enabling users to access planning, regulatory and market insights through a single, easy‑to‑use interface. Its purpose is to help businesses make informed decisions about establishment, growth and operations without needing to consult multiple sources.

instruments.name: GOV.BR Chatbot
instruments.summary: The Chat GOV.BR is an interface tool that aims to provide and maintain a complete and integrated communication and relationship service with citizens regarding the provision of public services, encompassing multiple channels, digital service, automation, and the use of AI resources, including LLMs, proprietary to the generative IA platform or integrated from third parties, the construction of proactive communication journeys, and integration with government systems.

instruments.name: Transform Paraná Program – Integrated Ecosystem of AI, Automation, and Data Governance (Subnational: Paraná)
instruments.summary: The Transform Paraná Program uses AI to modernize state management and deliver faster, more efficient digital services. It creates a unified data foundation to overcome fragmentation and automate slow manual processes across government agencies. Citizens, rural producers, and safety officials benefit from diverse projects like smart food donation, environmental monitoring, and traffic safety analysis.

instruments.name: CiudadanIA: AI-Powered Citizen Correspondence Processing for the Spanish Prime Minister’s Office
instruments.summary: CiudadanIA uses AI to accelerate the processing of citizen letters addressed to the Spanish President through the “Write to the President” service. Small language models generate summaries of citizen correspondence, enabling faster routing and response. The project also produced open-source tools for testing AI prompts and models at scale, including an LLM-as-a-judge evaluation framework, contributing to trustworthy AI in government.

instruments.name: Aurora – Institutional AI Cognitive Infrastructure (Subnational: State of Rio Grande do Sul)
instruments.summary: Aurora (“Dawn”) is an AI ecosystem developed by the Public Prosecution Service of Rio Grande do Sul (Brazil) to transform justice administration. Active in judicial and extrajudicial domains, it supports prosecutors protect vulnerable groups and collective rights by analyzing large volumes of documents and audiovisual records and integrating AI into legal workflows. With a human-in-the-loop approach, it enhances institutional capacity while preserving accountability and professional judgment.

instruments.name: Khmer Intelligent Document AI Agent (KIDAI-A)
instruments.summary: KIDAI-A is Cambodia’s first sovereign AI agent purpose-built for the Khmer language. It processes Khmer and English text, speech, and image documents, enabling government agencies, businesses, and citizens to query, summarise, and extract information from official documents in their native language. KIDAI-A closes the critical gap left by global AI tools that perform poorly on Khmer, a low-resource language, advancing digital sovereignty and public service efficiency.

instruments.name: ANAC Artificial Intelligence Strategy 2025–2026
instruments.summary: ANAC’s AI Strategy 2025–2026 is the Brazilian Civil Aviation Agency’s roadmap for adopting AI across the organisation in a broad, safe and responsible way. It links governance, capacity-building, risk management and implementation. It was created to improve public services, strengthen decision support and protect data, rights and trust.

instruments.name: ServetIA: AI Research Platform for the Spanish Prime Minister’s Office
instruments.summary: ServetIA is an AI-powered research platform developed for the Spanish Prime Minister’s Office to help government staff conduct faster, more thorough policy research. The tool uses large language models with source verification to provide reliable, evidence-based outputs. It was developed to reduce the time public servants spend on information gathering and improve the quality of briefing materials supporting government decision-making. ServetIA is in Beta.

instruments.name: Taina (Public Service Agent)
instruments.summary: Taína is a public service agent developed by the Government Office of ICT (OGTIC) to help citizens access information about public services and procedures in clear and accessible language. It provides guided assistance through a web interface. The initiative explores how public AI can improve citizen service while remaining ethical, inclusive, and open source.

instruments.name: Khmer eKYC OCR API — AI-Powered Identity Document Recognition for Cambodian Citizens
instruments.summary: Khmer eKYC OCR API uses AI to instantly extract data from Cambodian identity documents in Khmer and English, and already powers CamDigiKey, Cambodia's official government single sign-on application. Available completely free via CamDX to all 45+ registered public and private members, including banks, insurance companies, and government agencies, it requires no integration cost and is open to both public and private CamDX members. It has processed more than Khmer ID card images, as of now.

instruments.name: Santo Domingo Declaration — Third Ministerial Summit and High Authorities on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence in Latin America and the Caribbean
instruments.country: The United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization
instruments.summary: The Santo Domingo Declaration is the outcome document of the Third Ministerial Summit and High Authorities on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence in Latin America and the Caribbean, held on 25–26 June 2026 in Santo Domingo, Dominican Republic. Supported by UNESCO and CAF, it approves a Roadmap f2026–2027 focused on governance and regulation, talent and the future of work, protection of vulnerable groups, environment and sustainability, and infrastructure, building on prior summits in Santiago.

instruments.name: Cartagena de Indias Declaration for Governance, the construction of AI ecosystems and the promotion of AI education in an Ethical and Responsible manner in Latin America and the Caribbean
instruments.country: The United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization
instruments.summary: The Cartagena de Indias Declaration is a regional agreement signed by ministers and high authorities from seventeen Latin American and Caribbean countries in August 2024. Building on the 2023 Santiago Ministerial Summit on AI Ethics, it sets out commitments to strengthen cooperation on building AI ecosystems, promoting ethical AI education, and developing AI governance frameworks that respect human rights, sustainability and gender equity.

instruments.name: UK National AI Infrastructure Roadmap
instruments.summary: The UK Compute Roadmap is a long-term national strategy for expanding the United Kingdom’s computing capacity to support AI research, innovation, and industrial development.

instruments.name: AI Opportunities Action Plan
instruments.summary: The UK Government's central AI strategy document, published in January 2025, setting out a comprehensive national agenda to secure the UK's position as a world-leading AI nation.

instruments.name: Backing your business: our plan for SMEs
instruments.summary: Government support initiative helping SMEs improve productivity and adopt digital technologies.

instruments.name: 7th Basic Plan for the Promotion of Science and Technology
instruments.summary: Japan's national strategic framework for science, technology and innovation, covering the period FY2026–FY2030, which succeeds the 6th Basic Plan. Where the 6th Plan emphasised Society 5.0 as a social vision, the 7th Plan introduces an "actionable science" philosophy and places greater weight on three axes: revitalisation of Japan's basic research capabilities, acceleration of innovation-driven economic growth and integration of science and technology policy with economic security objectives.

instruments.name: R&D Tax Credit System
instruments.summary: Japan's core corporate R&D tax credit system providing a 6–14% tax credit on total R&D expenses, with enhanced rates of 12–17% for SMEs, an open innovation add-on of up to 10%, and a new 40% credit for strategic technologies including AI from FY2026.

instruments.name: Japan AI Safety Institute (AISI Japan)
instruments.summary: A national institute dedicated to evaluating, testing and improving the safety and reliability of artificial intelligence systems.

instruments.name: AI and Semiconductor Industry Strengthening Framework
instruments.summary: A Cabinet-approved comprehensive Japanese policy framework committing over JPY 10 trillion in public support for AI and semiconductor sectors by FY2030, targeting JPY 50 trillion+ in combined public-private investment over the next decade.

instruments.name: DX Investment Promotion Tax Incentive
instruments.summary: A Japanese corporate tax credit providing up to 5% of eligible cloud/AI investment costs (with a ceiling of 20% of annual corporate tax liability) for companies with government-approved digital transformation plans under the Industrial Competitiveness Enhancement Act.

instruments.name: Open Innovation Promotion Tax System
instruments.summary: A Japanese income-deduction / deductible-expense incentive that supports corporate–startup open innovation by allowing eligible corporations to deduct up to 25% of the acquisition cost of qualifying startup shares, subject to conditions and limits.

instruments.name: AI Strategic Headquarters
instruments.summary: Central government body responsible for coordinating Japan’s national AI strategy.

instruments.name: IPA MITOU Program
instruments.summary: A national Japanese talent development programme run by IPA/METI since FY2000, discovering and developing young IT and AI innovators through intensive mentorship, project-based funding, and a Super Creator recognition system.

instruments.name: Law No. 5321/2026 – Measures for the Implementation of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 13 June 2024 (Artificial Intelligence Act), Amendment of Law 4961/2022, and Other Provisions
instruments.summary: Law No. 5321/2026 establishes the national framework for the implementation of the EU ΑΙ Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) in Greece. It designates competent authorities, provides for market surveillance and enforcement, establishes an AI regulatory sandbox, a AI Systems Registry for the public sector and an AI Observatory, and promotes the trustworthy and innovative use of AI. The law further replaces the AI governance provisions previously contained in Law 4961/2022.

instruments.name: EU General-Purpose AI (GPAI) Code of Practice
instruments.summary: A co-regulatory instrument under Article 56 of the EU AI Act, developed through a multi-stakeholder process led by the EU AI Office, which translates the AI Act's obligations for General Purpose AI (GPAI) model providers into specific, operationalisable compliance measures covering transparency, copyright, systemic risk assessment, safety testing, incident reporting and governance.

instruments.name: EU AI Continent Action Plan
instruments.summary: The European Commission's AI strategy adopted in 2025, setting out a multi-pillar framework to make Europe "an AI Continent". The Plan encompasses 5 strategic pillars: computing infrastructure and data, AI research and innovation talent, the regulatory environment, AI adoption across sectors, and European AI sovereignty and global outreach. It serves as the parent strategic framework for InvestAI, the Apply AI Strategy, the AI Factories network, and the EU AI Office's coordination mandate.

instruments.name: EU AI Office
instruments.summary: The European Commission body responsible for overseeing the implementation and enforcement of the EU AI Act at the EU level, with specific responsibility for supervising General Purpose AI (GPAI) models and systemic risk assessment.

instruments.name: EU Scaleup Europe Fund
instruments.summary: The Scaleup Europe Fund is a multi-billion-euro, privately managed and publicly anchored growth capital fund announced by the European Commission in October 2025, aimed at investing in the most promising European companies in strategic deep tech areas, including artificial intelligence, quantum technologies, semiconductors, robotics, energy, space, and biotechnologies.

instruments.name: Frontier AI Initiative
instruments.summary: An EU initiative to coordinate research, infrastructure and governance efforts around frontier artificial intelligence systems and strengthen Europe’s ability to develop and deploy highly capable AI models.

instruments.name: Justice Practical Guide
instruments.summary: The Justice Practical Guide is a digital tool that helps citizens and businesses quickly find clear and simple information about justice‑related services in everyday language. It was created to make access to justice faster and more understandable, reducing the need to visit onsite services and helping navigate common legal situations. It uses AI to provide quick, natural‑language answers, ensuring that anyone - regardless of legal knowledge - can understand the options available to them.

instruments.name: AI-Specific Evaluation Framework for Public Procurement in Korea
instruments.summary: Korea’s Public Procurement Service is developing an AI-specific evaluation framework for public procurement to enable the safe and effective adoption of AI products and services. The initiative introduces new assessment criteria covering AI performance, reliability, transparency, and risk management, addressing the limitations of traditional procurement standards. It aims to support trustworthy AI adoption while fostering innovation and market access for AI suppliers.

instruments.name: The Interministerial AI Assistant
instruments.summary: The AI Assistant is a secure chat tool for public servants, designed to help them write, summarize and find information faster. It was developed to give government teams an easy and trusted way to use generative AI in their daily work. The goal is to improve efficiency while reducing duplicated efforts across ministries.

instruments.name: AI verkstaden - AI node for public administration
instruments.summary: The "AI-verkstaden" is a national initiative that provides public sector organisations with shared, secure environments and ready‑to‑use AI services to help them develop, test, and use AI solutions. It is designed to support government agencies, regions, and municipalities by offering technical tools, guidance, and trustworthy AI services. The initiative was developed to address common challenges such as limited AI competence and  legal uncertainty.

instruments.name: KB Lab
instruments.summary: KB-labb (The KBLab) at the National Library of Sweden is a data-driven infrastructure for research. It provides access to the library’s massive digital collections—including newspapers, books, and radio/TV—for large-scale analysis.

instruments.name: Tampere Pulse – AI-Driven Visitor Flow Forecasting for Smarter Urban Decision-Making (Subnational: City of Tampere)
instruments.summary: Tampere Pulse is an AI-powered predictive analytics service developed by the City of Tampere, Finland, to forecast visitor flows in the urban centre. By leveraging anonymised IoT and machine vision data, it predicts foot traffic up to one month in advance, enabling authorities and businesses to enact smarter decision-making, operational planning, resource allocation, and public services through human-centric, trustworthy AI.

instruments.name: EU Apply AI Strategy
instruments.summary: An EU-wide strategy launched October 2025 to accelerate AI adoption across 11 key industrial and public sectors, with a specific focus on lowering barriers for SMEs through coordination, funding mechanisms, and an 'AI-first' policy culture.

instruments.name: Public Sector AI Community of Practice
instruments.summary: New Zealand’s Public Sector AI Community of Practice is an active professional network of digital government practitioners meeting monthly online for wide knowledge sharing, learning and connection. Online meetings regularly bring together up to 200 practitioners from a wide range of government organisations to share knowledge on a range of AI-related topics and relevant information.

instruments.name: Piano Transizione 4.0 – Tax Credit
instruments.summary: An Italian tax credit scheme for investments in Industry 4.0 tangible capital goods (including AI-integrated machinery) of up to 20% of eligible costs, with a national spending cap of EUR 2.2B for 2025.

instruments.name: OTT2 : Dynamic Data-Driven Personalisation of Employment Services and Counsellor Decision Support
instruments.summary: OTT2 is an AI-powered decision support system that helps Estonia’s Unemployment Insurance Fund prevent long-term unemployment. It combines data from public registries to assess each jobseeker’s employment prospects in real time, enabling counsellors to identify those at highest risk and focus support where it is most needed. With above 98% forecast accuracy, it eliminates laborious and error-prone manual work and it enables a policy pilot to dedicate counselling resource to high-risk customers.

instruments.name: Italy AI Law 132/2025
instruments.summary: Italy's first comprehensive national AI law, entered into force 10 October 2025, establishing governance, sector-specific rules, and fundamental principles for AI use, and authorising up to EUR 1B in state-backed venture capital for AI, cybersecurity and telecommunications companies.

instruments.name: Fondo di Garanzia PMI
instruments.summary: Italy's central public loan guarantee fund providing state-backed guarantees of up to 80% on bank loans to SMEs and innovative startups, directly facilitating AI and technology investment finance without requiring collateral.

instruments.name: Virtual assistant in mObywatel
instruments.summary: The virtual assistant in mObywatel is an AI chatbot, powered by a Polish LLM (PLLuM), available through a national digital citizen app. It was created in order to make information about public services more available to citizens. It is meant to combat digital exclusion and provide a safe and verified alternative to general purpose chatbots in the official context.

instruments.name: Nuova Sabatini Digital
instruments.summary: An Italian government programme subsidising the interest costs on bank or leasing loans taken by SMEs to purchase new capital goods including AI-integrated machinery, hardware, software, and digital 4.0 technologies.

instruments.name: National Data Infrastructure (NDI)
instruments.summary: The National Data Infrastructure (NDI) constitutes a set of norms, policies, architectures, standards, technological tools, and information assets, aimed at promoting the strategic use of data held by the bodies and entities of the Brazilian Federal Executive Branch. The IND enables data discovery, interoperability, access, strategic use, privacy, security, and protection. The objective is to improve public service, empower citizens, and promote economic and social development.

instruments.name: R&D & Innovation Tax Credit 4.0
instruments.summary: A national Italian tax credit scheme established under Law 160/2019 to support business investments in research and development (R&D), technological innovation, design, and digital transformation as part of the Transition Plan 4.0. The scheme provides a 10% tax credit for R&D activities and a 5% tax credit for innovation and design activities, applicable to companies of all sizes operating in Italy.

instruments.name: Voucher Cloud & Cybersecurity
instruments.summary: A ministerial voucher programme to subsidise the purchase/subscription of cloud and cybersecurity services by SMEs and self-employed persons (eligible products explicitly include cloud SaaS with integrated AI features such as productivity/ERP/CRM tools). The measure reduces infrastructure and security barriers for SMEs adopting AI-enabled software.

instruments.name: IT4LIA AI Factory
instruments.summary: A national AI Factory (EuroHPC selected) centred on Italy’s LEONARDO/LISA supercomputers and national AI infrastructure to provide free/discounted access and services to researchers, SMEs, startups and public administrations.

instruments.name: AI Sovereign Compute Infrastructure Program (AI SCIP) / Canadian Sovereign AI Compute Strategy
instruments.summary: Canada's flagship sovereign AI infrastructure investment, comprising three complementary streams: a CAD 705M public supercomputing facility (AI SCIP), up to CAD 700M for private-sector AI data centres (AI Compute Challenge), and CAD 200M in near-term augmentation of existing public compute infrastructure.

instruments.name: Canadian AI Safety Institute (CAISI Canada)
instruments.summary: Canada's national AI safety body established to evaluate advanced AI models for safety risks, develop safety testing methodologies, and contribute to international AI safety coordination through the Bletchley Declaration process and the International Network of AI Safety Institutes.

instruments.name: Sectoral Workforce Solutions Program (AI-focused projects)
instruments.summary: A dedicated CAD 50M federal contribution programme funding sectoral organisations to develop and deliver skills training for workers in industries potentially disrupted by AI, helping them reskill and adapt to an AI-transformed labour market.

instruments.name: MEB Smart Legislation Assistant  (AI-powered Legal Assistant)
instruments.summary: The MEB Smart Legislation Assistant is an AI-powered tool that helps Ministry staff quickly access and understand official legislation. It allows users to ask questions in plain language and receive structured answers supported by official legal sources. The system reduces time spent searching complex legal texts and improves accuracy in administrative decision-making.

instruments.name: Innovative Solutions Canada (ISC)
instruments.summary: A federal innovation procurement programme that challenges Canadian SMEs to develop pre-commercial AI solutions for real government needs, funding proof-of-concept and prototype development, with a pathway to government commercialisation contracts of up to CAD 8M.

instruments.name: BDC Data to AI Program
instruments.summary: A Business Development Bank of Canada programme providing Canadian SMEs with structured advisory services, personalised AI readiness diagnostics and roadmaps, cybersecurity assessments, and flexible term loan financing to adopt AI, automation, and cybersecurity solutions.

instruments.name: Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) Tax Credit
instruments.summary: Canada's largest federal R&D tax incentive programme, providing investment tax credits (ITCs) to businesses conducting eligible scientific research and experimental development in Canada, including AI system development, with enhanced refundable rates for qualifying small Canadian-controlled private corporations (CCPCs).

instruments.name: Scale AI Supercluster (Supply Chains and Logistics Excellence AI)
instruments.summary: Canada's national AI-powered supply chain Global Innovation Cluster, providing co-investment grants to industry consortia developing and adopting AI solutions across supply chain sectors, headquartered in Montréal.

instruments.name: AI for Growth
instruments.summary: A CAD 174 million, three-year Canadian programme to accelerate domestic AI adoption by SMEs, delivered through Canada's National AI Institutes and Global Innovation Clusters.

instruments.name: Vendor Innovation Program (VIP) - Canada Health Infoway
instruments.summary: Funding programme supporting development and implementation of digital health technologies including AI tools.

instruments.name: AI Assist (IRAP)
instruments.summary: A support programme helping SMEs adopt AI technologies (generative AI and deep learning) through advisory services and innovation support.

instruments.name: Regional Artificial Intelligence Initiative (RAII)
instruments.summary: A multi-regional funding programme that supports AI commercialization and adoption projects by businesses across Canada.

instruments.name: AI Compute Access Fund
instruments.summary: A federal programme that provides financial support and compute-credits to Canadian SMEs so they can access high-performance/cloud AI compute needed to train, test and deploy models for commercialisation.

instruments.name: UK AI for Science Strategy
instruments.summary: A national strategy designed to accelerate the application of artificial intelligence across scientific research and discovery in the United Kingdom.

instruments.name: AI Security Institute (formerly AI Safety Institute, AISI)
instruments.summary: The UK's national body for advanced AI safety and security research, model evaluation and international AI safety coordination. Originally established as the AI Safety Institute (AISI) in November 2023, it was renamed the AI Security Institute in January 2025 to reflect a broader mandate encompassing both safety and security risks from advanced AI systems.

instruments.name: TiNAI (Tamil Nadu Land Use Information System) (Subnational: Tamil Nadu State)
instruments.summary: TiNAI (Tamil Nadu Land Use Information System) is an AI-enabled geospatial and Digital Twin platform designed to support evidence-based land-use planning. It uses artificial intelligence to analyse multi-sector data and generate clear insights that help policymakers understand climate, urban, and environmental challenges. The platform was created to address fragmented data and improve coordinated, transparent decision-making across sectors.

instruments.name: AI STRATEGIC WORKFORCE PLANNING
instruments.summary: The Ministry of the Interior is developing a digital workforce planning tool that supports decision-making based on big data and predictive technologies. The tool analyses demographic trends, retirements, skills and operational needs to produce 5–10 year staffing scenarios. It helps policymakers anticipate future needs, identify skill gaps, compare hiring and reskilling options, and better align staff with organisational goals.

instruments.name: PresidencIA: Generative AI Adoption Programme for the Spanish Prime Minister’s Office
instruments.summary: Leveraging on 3 pillars (Community, Applications and Infrastructure), PresidencIA builds AI literacy among staff through workshops, community and best practices, develops custom AI tools for processes in the PM’s Office, and pursues on-premises AI infrastructure for tech sovereignty. It also works to position Spain as a partner for leading AI labs on safety and alignment. The programme addresses the gap between AI’s potential and practical government capacity.

instruments.name: AI Bridging Cloud Infrastructure 3.0 (ABCI 3.0)
instruments.summary: ABCI 3.0 is Japan's national AI computing infrastructure that provides access to supercomputing resources for developing sovereign AI capabilities. Operated by AIST and funded through Japan's METI, it delivers 6.2 exaflops of computing power using 6,128 NVIDIA H200 GPUs. The infrastructure supports industry, academia, and government in developing large language models and advancing generative AI research, with priority given to national research institutes, universities, and startups.

instruments.name: AI Growth Zones
instruments.summary: AI Growth Zones are designated regions in the United Kingdom aimed at accelerating the development of AI infrastructure, including data centres and computing capacity, while fostering AI innovation ecosystems.

instruments.name: AI Research Resource (AIRR)
instruments.summary: A government-led public AI compute capability (suite of AI-optimised supercomputers and gateways) to provide specialised compute to UK researchers, industry and SMEs for ambitious AI R&D.

instruments.name: Patent Box
instruments.summary: A UK tax incentive allowing companies to elect a reduced 10% corporation tax rate on profits derived from qualifying patented inventions, including AI-enabled products and processes, to encourage the commercialisation and retention of intellectual property in the UK.

instruments.name: Merged R&D Tax Relief / ERIS (UK)
instruments.summary: A unified UK corporation tax relief scheme replacing the previous SME and RDEC regimes, providing a 20% above-the-line expenditure credit for all companies, with an enhanced 27% payable credit for R&D-intensive loss-making SMEs (ERIS).

instruments.name: PALOMA: Artificial Intelligence for Early Detection of Unwanted Loneliness in Older Adults (Subnational: Madrid)
instruments.summary: PALOMA is an artificial intelligence system that makes phone calls to people over 75 who live alone to detect situations of unwanted loneliness. It conducts short conversations with a natural sounding voice, identifies risk signals, and offers information or municipal follow up. The project helps reach more people, detect needs earlier, and connect them quickly with social support.

instruments.name: Messina Urban Digital Twin (GDU) – AI-enabled Urban Intelligence Platform (Subnational: Municipality of Messina)
instruments.summary: The Messina Urban Digital Twin (GDU) is an AI-enabled platform that integrates data from IoT sensors, administrative sources and urban systems to support decision-making and scenario simulation. It transforms fragmented urban data into a dynamic and interactive model of the city. The initiative aims to improve planning, resource management and public services through data-driven insights.

instruments.name: Agent MIA (Argentine State's Artificial Intelligence Assistant)
instruments.summary: MIA is integrated into the national government's chatbot (TINA). It was conceived as a support agent for citizen services management based on information security, administrative transparency, and human oversight principles. It offers personalized responses according to each user's needs and context. It is based on LLAMA 4 (Meta) for speed, low operating cost, and open-source nature. Currently in its initial phase with two use cases: SMEs and Mi Argentina (citizens' platform).

instruments.name: IPS Córdoba Assistant — AI Policy Analysis Agent for Social Progress Governance (Subnational: Province of Córdoba)
instruments.summary: The IPS Córdoba Agent is an AI-powered policy tool integrated into the Social Progress Index dashboard for Córdoba’s 427 localities. It analyses quality-of-life data across 12 components and 57 indicators, combining social metrics, trends, and policy literature. More than a chatbot, it provides contextualised analysis and actionable recommendations so mayors and local officials can turn data into informed public policy, targeted investment, and evidence-based decisions.

instruments.name: Guideline for Japanese Government’s Procurements and Utilizations of Generative AI for the sake of Evolution and Innovation of Public Administration
instruments.summary: "Japan's GenAI Procurement & Utilization Guideline" was formulated in 2025 to establish rules for the procurement and use of generative AI across national government.
