The aim of the projects in this funding measure is to research and develop AI-based assistance systems that lead to quantifiable and measurable improvements in clinical processes.

instruments.name: AI-assisted precision surgery in oncology
instruments.summary: Surgical interventions are a core element of multimodal treatment strategies for solid cancers and continue to play a central role in modern oncology. Artificial intelligence is expected to contribute to more personalised and precise approaches to cancer care, supporting clinical decisions before, during, and after surgery. The funding measure seeks to advance the precision of oncological surgery through the development and application of interactive AI technologies.

instruments.name: Data dissemination and management platform (DAGR)
instruments.summary: ​DAGR is a next-generation data exchange and governance platform enabling secure data sharing across government, business, and citizen interactions. It will consolidate all government data sources into a single access point by 2030, streamlining public sector operations and reducing administrative burdens. The platform will also support emerging digital initiatives such as the European Digital Identity Wallet and AI training.

instruments.name: Act on Health Data Use (GDNG)
instruments.summary: The GDNG is a key enabler to facilitate the access to healthcare data for secondary use. Its measures include procedural simplifications on re-using health data across multiple states (Länder). It further provides a legal basis for healthcare institutions to re-use their patients‘ data for research, patient safety and quality assurance, and enables statutory health insurance funds to utilize data to improve the quality of care and to support AI applications.

instruments.name: PariSanté Campus
instruments.summary: Designed as a digital health development center in Paris, PariSanté Campus brings together public institutions, research institutes, and startups to foster innovation in digital health, emphasising AI applications in healthcare.

instruments.name: Development and implementation of the National Digital Platform for Medical Diagnostics
instruments.summary: This platform is designed to improve of diagnostics and treatment of socially important diseases. It is also expected to facilitate communication between healthcare professionals and other relevant stakeholders.

instruments.name: Translate-AD
instruments.summary: The Translate-AD project unites six universities and university hospitals (VUB, UZ Brussel, ULB, Hôpital Erasme, Université Catholique de Louvain (UCL), and Cliniques Universitaires St. Luc) in developing digital platform designed to streamline the exchange patient data among these institutions. Initially tailored to Alzheimer’s patients in Brussels, the platform is envisioned to expand in the long term to other Belgian and international centers.

instruments.name: AI Priority Research Program and Equipment (PEPR)
instruments.summary: Within France’s 2030 strategy, this programme accelerates innovation in key fields, including AI in healthcare. By supporting foundational AI research, it drives advancements in medical imaging, predictive analytics, and therapeutic development. The programme also fosters digital health innovation through AI-powered personalised medicine and diagnostics, while encouraging collaboration between research institutions, healthcare providers, and industry.

instruments.name: Memorandum of Understanding
instruments.summary: Signed by 12 partners during the 5G Techritory event, the MoU aims to establish a partnership for developing Latvia’s semiconductor ecosystem. Coordinated by Riga Technical University and open to international collaborators. Since December 2024, 5 additional partners have signed the MoU. the MoU of a total of 17 partners aims to establish a partnership for developing Latvia’s semiconductor ecosystem. Coordinated by Riga Technical University and open to international collaborators.

instruments.name: Important Project of Common European Interest – Next Generation Cloud Infrastructure and Services (IPCEI-CIS)
instruments.summary: IPCEI-CIS is a significant European initiative involving over 100 companies and research organizations across 12 Member States, with Germany playing a coordinating role. This project aims to establish a decentralized cloud-edge ecosystem that will reduce technological dependencies and foster new data-driven business models. The primary goal of IPCEI-CIS is to create a “Multi-Provider Cloud-Edge Continuum,” which allows for advanced use of data processing resources from cloud-edge environments.

instruments.name: Member of IPCEI Microelectronics, IPCEI Cloud data, and IPCEI Health
instruments.summary: Latvia participates in IPCEI working groups on Microelectronics, Cloud Data, and Health to advance innovative technologies and meet digital and green goals. RRF funding supports these projects.

instruments.name: Health IT Interoperability Governance Ordinance (GIGV) Competence Centre
instruments.summary: Germany has advanced healthcare interoperability through the Digital Act, which expanded the Coordination Office for Interoperability into a Competence Centre. Supported by the Interop Council and expert working groups, it promotes technical, syntactic, and semantic interoperability, with the Health IT Interoperability Governance Ordinance (GIGV) ensuring a holistic, coordinated approach to developing binding guidelines and standards.

instruments.name: National Strategy for Advanced Computing
instruments.summary: Portugal was one of the six pioneering countries to sign the EuroHPC Declaration in March 2017. Through its National Strategy for Advanced Computing, the country aims to establish itself as a European reference point in three areas: an advanced computing services economy, a cutting-edge laboratory environment, and the education and training of specialists in this field.

instruments.name: Strategy of the e-Health Centre – summary 2023-2027
instruments.summary: Strategy for Poland’s e-Health Centre, focused on continuing the development of e-Health services and maximise the potential of digitalisation.

instruments.name: Public Administration Cloud Strategy
instruments.summary: The cloud is a network of remote computers connected by the Internet that allows you to store and manage data, run applications, and provide services. The Cloud Strategy for the Public Administration aims to promote the use of the cloud by public entities.

instruments.name: Clinnova
instruments.summary: Clinnova’s mission is to advance precision medicine by using AI-driven solutions to provide tailored treatments for patients, focusing initially on inflammatory bowel disease, rheumatoid disease, and multiple sclerosis. The initiative aims to bridge biomedical research and healthcare by creating an interoperable infrastructure for federated health data across Europe, driving innovation and supporting Luxembourg's personalised healthcare goals.

instruments.name: Dataspace4Health
instruments.summary: The Dataspace4Health project aims to transform Luxembourg’s healthcare by creating a secure platform for health data sharing, enhancing patient care through improved diagnosis, treatment, and prevention while respecting GDPR and patient rights.

instruments.name: Centre of Excellence for Data Sharing and Cloud (CoE-DSC)
instruments.summary: The CoE-DSC was established to overcome challenges in data sharing, such as building trust, ensuring regulatory compliance, and defining governance structures. It supports the development of "data spaces," which allow organizations to securely exchange data across sectors. These data spaces, such as the Smart Connected Supplier Network and HDN, have the potential to drive innovation and economic growth.

instruments.name: Data-Driven Innovation Strategy for the Development of a Trusted and Sustainable Economy in Luxembourg
instruments.summary: Luxembourg’s strategy to boost a trusted and sustainable data economy through infrastructure, advanced digital technologies, and supportive regulation.

instruments.name: SMEs Innovative: Medical Technology
instruments.summary: To strengthen the innovative capacity of "Made in Germany" medical technology, the Federal Ministry of Education and Research (BMBF) supports SMEs in their research on innovative medical products, in-vitro diagnostics, and digital medical technology solutions. This funding aims to initiate additional research and development activities, boost medical technology research in Germany, enhance networking between SMEs and partners in science and healthcare.

instruments.name: Optimal therapies through data-driven decision and support systems
instruments.summary: In many diseases, choosing the appropriate therapy forms the basis for the subsequent course and success of the treatment. The goal of the funding is to optimize patient care through medical technology solutions in the form of innovative decision and support systems. Data-driven approaches should support healthcare providers at all stages of the care process to achieve better healing or a reduction in side effects.

instruments.name: Invest-NL
instruments.summary: Invest-NL provides financing to promising Dutch companies that contribute to societal transitions, including in deep tech sectors like AI. It focuses on providing equity and debt financing, particularly for SMEs that struggle to secure funding.

instruments.name: Supporting Health Data Access Bodies in Slovenia (SI-SUD)
instruments.summary: The National Institute for Public Health started this project with the objective of enabling secondary use of data by developing four digital capabilities: Data Access Management System, National Metadata Catalogue, Secure Processing Environment and Quality labelling.

instruments.name: Chip Chairs
instruments.summary: Creation of 17 university chairs focused on semiconductor scientific investigation and talent creation; 80 private sector companies involved.

instruments.name: PERTE Chip Semiconductor Ecosystem
instruments.summary: PERTE Chip aims to strengthen the design and production capabilities of the microelectronics and semiconductor industry in Spain and promote national and EU strategic autonomy in this sector, in line with the EU Chip Law. Its 4 strategic axes cover the entire value chain of the industry in different phases: conception, design, production of chips and manufacturing ICT electronic products, so that it acts as a generator of demand for the microchips produced and boosts the semiconductor ecosystem.

instruments.name: Measures to reinforce Spain’s HPC capacity for AI development
instruments.summary: Several measures including: reinforcing capacity at Barcelona Supercomputing Center (BSC-CNS) so the MareNostrum 5 supercomputer exceeds 450 Pflops, making this capacity available to industry actors (objective of 20%), and reinforcing the Spanish HPC network.

instruments.name: Programme to support edge technologies (as part of UNICO IPCEI subsidy programme)
instruments.summary: Subsidies granted to actions aimed at supporting Spain's contribution to Important Projects of Common European Interest (IPCEI), including IPCEI on Next Generation Cloud Infrastructure and Services (IPCEI CIS) - provide competitive and fair access to next-generation cloud and edge capabilities.

instruments.name: Plan to Promote Sectoral Data Spaces
instruments.summary: The Ministry for the Digital Transformation and Civil Service has presented an ambitious Plan for the Promotion of Sectorial Data Spaces. Its objective is to foster innovation and improve competitiveness and added-value in all economic sectors, promoting the deployment of data spaces where data can be securely shared. Thanks to them, companies, and the economy in general, will be able to benefit from the full potential of a European data single market.

instruments.name: Slovenian national strategy in semiconductor technologies and chips until 2030
instruments.summary: The strategy is being conducted under the auspices of the Ministry of Digital Transformation in association with two other ministries – the Ministry of Economy, Tourism and Sport, and the Ministry of Higher Education, Science and Innovation.

instruments.name: IPCEI-CIS project on Cloud Edge
instruments.summary: The first Important Project of Common European Interest on cloud and edge computing, this project targets the development of the first interoperable and openly accessible European data processing ecosystem, the multi-provider cloud to edge continuum. It will develop data processing capabilities, and software and data sharing tools that enable federated, energy-efficient and trustworthy cloud and edge distributed data processing technologies and related services.

instruments.name: Establishment of Edge nodes indicators
instruments.summary: Slovenia is in the process of establishing indicator Edge nodes, in accordance with Article 5(1) of the Decision (EU) 2022/2481 in collaboration with the Agency of communication networks and services of the Republic of Slovenia.

instruments.name: IoT Connectivity Platform
instruments.summary: In 2023 an IoT Connectivity Platform pilot project was implemented, which was intended for users from the state administration. Technically it focuses on a key challenge, i.e. how to connect various IoT end devices like sensors, actuators, meters, dedicated devices,

instruments.name: Support for Slovenian companies involved in IPCEI ME/CT
instruments.summary: This measure of the Ministry of the Economy, Tourism and Sport aims at supporting companies involved in the important project of common European interest in microelectronics and communication technologies (IPCEI ME/CT) in carrying out R&D activities, including the first industrial deployment of pilot solutions, in the framework of R&D projects in the field of microelectronics, semiconductors, microchips and communication technologies.

instruments.name: Support for Slovenian companies involved in the Chips JU
instruments.summary: Slovenia supports research and innovation projects within the tenders of the joint European Chips JU, as part of its measures to promote entrepreneurship from Ministry of Digital Transformation.

instruments.name: Slovenian national Competence centre for chips and semiconductors, and other support as part of the Chips Joint Undertaking (Chips JU)
instruments.summary: As part of the European Chips Joint Undertaking, Slovenia envisages the establishment of a consortium of public RTOs, which will manage the role of the Competence Centre for chips and semiconductors, to be located at the University of Maribor’s Faculty of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science (FERI UM).

instruments.name: DRO Next
instruments.summary: The project "Establishment of Next-Generation Information Infrastructure (DRO Next)" focuses on developing advanced digital infrastructure that will enhance the capabilities for data management and processing at the edge, facilitating the use of edge computing technologies across various sectors, aiming to upgrade the current governmental private cloud.

instruments.name: Data centres in Arnes
instruments.summary: The construction of the data centre in Maribor, spearheaded by the Academic and Research Network of Slovenia (ARNES) is underway, implementing a 2023 action plan for open science, implementing “Measure 6.2: Open science to improve the quality, efficiency and responsiveness of research” within the Resolution on the Scientific Research and Innovation Strategy of Slovenia 2030 (ReZrIS30).

instruments.name: National Competence Centre SLING
instruments.summary: The National Competence Centre SLING helps users and in using High Performance Computing (HPC) to learn, access, use and learn about supercomputing.

instruments.name: Pladenj (System for Standardized Execution of Electronic Data Queries)
instruments.summary: In December 2023, the platform Pladenj, a common central data exchange platform to facilitate seamless data and document exchange across many diverse systems and life events within the public administration, which since 2018 employs advanced AI machine learning techniques (to distribute network traffic for rush hour events between the application servers and their visitors), was upgraded to support cross-border exchanges in alignment with the EU Single Digital Gateway Regulation.

instruments.name: Experimental Regulatory Environments for AI
instruments.summary: The Action Plan of Digital Transformation 2023-2026 includes the development of Experimental Regulatory Environments for AI. The first step of this project involved preparing a feasibility study for establishing an AI sandbox; the study proposed a set of legislative and technical tools, including a legal framework on the AI sandbox, necessary personnel capacities, and technical requirements. Based on this study, the preparatory phase of this pilot project is scheduled for 2025.

instruments.name: Use of AI in Business Intelligence System - Skrinja
instruments.summary: The Ministry of Digital Transformation is planning to introduce AI-based predictive analytics into the Business intelligence system Skrinja (‘box’), which is used by different public authorities to analyse data about their policy area, like public sector salaries, public tenders and administrative procedures, supporting data-driven decisions in real time in public administration.

instruments.name: Virtual civil servants
instruments.summary: Two local communities have introduced 'virtual civil servants'. The creation of this 'civil servant,' based on artificial intelligence, is part of the digitisation process of procedures in the local public administration in Cluj. Galați City Hall also launched a virtual civil servant based on artificial intelligence. The virtual assistant is currently being trained and tested but will soon be able to provide information to citizens on town planning, taxes, fees, and other local revenues.

instruments.name: EDIH AI Boost
instruments.summary:
"One of seven Danish government-approved Research and Technology Organisations (GTS institutes), whose mission is to transfer research-based knowledge to industry and help drive innovation and growth in public and private organisations.
Provides research-based knowledge in the following areas:
•	Artificial intelligence (strong focus)
•	Computer vision
•	Cybersecurity
•	Digital sustainability
•	Digital health
•	IoT and smart products"

instruments.name: Digitalised Yellow Book
instruments.summary: AI-driven project to digitise handwritten complaint reports in the public administration’s Yellow Book, aiming to reduce processing time, enhance evaluation standards, and extend electronic support for complaints. The Yellow Book (Livro Amarelo) is a public administration tool that allows citizens to submit complaints, suggestions, and compliments regarding public services. It serves as a formal channel for feedback, helping to improve the quality and accountability of public administration.

instruments.name: Artificial Intelligence Security Research Centre at the Research and Academic Computer Network
instruments.summary: In December 2024, the NASK announced a transformation of its AI division into the AI Security Research Centre, which will focus on scientific research the field of AI, with an emphasis on cybersecurity.

instruments.name: ARTIQ - AI Centres of Excellence
instruments.summary: In 2023, AGH University won a grant for the ARTIQ through the joint undertaking from the National Science Centre (NCN) and the National Centre for Research and Development (NCBR) to create a highly specialised research team to contribute to increasing Poland's scientific and R&D potential in the field of AI, with a project proposal titled “Integrating Reasoning, Learning, Optimization and Interpretability for accelerated commercialization of next-generation intelligent software systems.

instruments.name: ROBUST
instruments.summary: The ROBUST consortium, initiated in 2022, is a 10-year research project focusing on reliable and trustworthy AI. Comprising 54 partners in AI labs, including knowledge institutions, private companies, and civil society organisations, ROBUST aims to enhance AI systems across five dimensions: accuracy, reliability, repeatability, resilience, and safety. It seeks to formalize AI reliability through contracts and develop methods to foster trust in AI systems.

instruments.name: Innovation Center for Artificial Intelligence (ICAI)
instruments.summary: ICAI aims to position the Netherlands as a leader in AI knowledge and talent development. It aims to create a national AI ecosystem, leverage AI expertise across sectors, nurture academic and industry partnerships, and to ensure the sustainable use of AI resources.

instruments.name: European Digital Innovation Hubs (EDIH) in the Netherlands
instruments.summary: The Netherlands hosts six European Digital Innovation Hubs (EDIHs), with five focusing on private-sector digitalisation and one on public-sector support. These hubs aim to accelerate AI and digital adoption in businesses and public services.

instruments.name: AiNed
instruments.summary: AiNed  is a multi-year public-private initiative that helps Dutch companies and public institutions capitalise on AI's economic and social opportunities. Funded by the National Growth Fund, AiNed focuses on AI investments in Ethical, Legal and Societal Aspects (ELSA) labs, learning communities, innovation labs, and SME innovations. It also supports research grants and the development of a robust AI ecosystem through start-ups and SMEs, aligning with EU AI legislation in a responsible manner.

instruments.name: Smart & Sustainable Investment Grant
instruments.summary: The Smart & Sustainable Investment Grant provides business funding to support investments that lead to more sustainable processes, enhancing the competitiveness of enterprises through the optimisation of resource use in their activities. This includes initiatives such as sustainable digitisation. The service is offered by the DiHubMT.

instruments.name: Innovation Aid for SMEs Scheme
instruments.summary: The Innovation Aid for SMEs Scheme provides grants to SMEs aiming to enhance their innovation performance. This includes projects leading to product, process, and organisational innovation through collaboration with Research & Knowledge-dissemination Organisations and access to innovation advisory and support services. This service is offered by the DiHubMT.

instruments.name: Start-up Finance Scheme
instruments.summary: The scheme provides financial support to innovative start-ups that demonstrate viable business concepts and a commitment to expanding their economic activities. In 2024, it allocated dedicated funding through various grants to support small start-ups undertakings and academic research in AI. The financial support is provided as a repayable advance.

instruments.name: Digital Technologies Programme
instruments.summary: The Digital Technologies Programme led by Xjenza Malta (XM) supports capacity-building efforts related to AI, digital trust, knowledge and data, representation and analysis, technology for sustainability, quantum computing and other emerging technologies. The capacity-building efforts are aimed at researchers, entrepreneurs, and organisations involved in these emerging technologies.

instruments.name: Data Sandbox
instruments.summary: The Data Sandbox managed by the Malta Digital Innovation Authority will provide a secure and controlled environment for organisations to experiment with data-driven technologies while adhering to data protection laws. The initiative will provide guidance on best practices for responsible data use, enabling companies to safely explore new technological applications.

instruments.name: TAKEOFF Seed Fund Award
instruments.summary: The TAKEOFF Seed Fund Award (TOSFA) is a seed funding initiative established in 2014, aimed at fostering innovation by providing financial support to researchers and entrepreneurs. This joint initiative between the University of Malta and the Ministry for the Economy, Enterprise and Strategic Projects (MEEP) supports early-stage technology and start-up development by offering grants ranging from EUR 2 500 to EUR 25 000 per project, with a total allocation of EUR150,000 in 2023.

instruments.name: Luxembourg National Research Fund
instruments.summary: The Luxembourg National Research Fund provides a variety of research funding instruments that, while not exclusively focused on AI, are available to support AI-based projects. These include fellowships, PhD grants, and funding for companies looking to adopt innovative technologies.

instruments.name: Fit 4 Digital – AI
instruments.summary: As of October 2024, an existing digitalisation support for SMEs has been augmented to focus on AI-specific measures. This program provides businesses with the opportunity to collaborate with an experienced AI consultant who will help identify challenges, set objectives, and prioritize development actions. The initiative includes a feasibility analysis of selected AI use cases, supported by a qualitative and quantitative review of internal data.

instruments.name: Digital Vouchers for SMEs
instruments.summary: The goal of this programme is to encourage micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) to improve their digitisation processes. It provides funding for companies to purchase digitisation and technology services.

instruments.name: InoStartas, InoBranda ir InoPazanga
instruments.summary: Under these measures 47 projects are being implemented to develop AI solutions (by the companies in the middle-west region of Lithuania).

instruments.name: Measure for start-ups and spin-offs in the Vilnius region to develop innovative solutions and products in AI, blockchain technology and robotics process automation
instruments.summary: This measure aims to develop innovative solutions and products in AI, blockchain technology and robotics process automation (by the start-ups and spin-offs in the Vilnius region).

instruments.name: SustAInLivWork – Centre of Excellence (CoE) for Sustainable Living and Working
instruments.summary: The CoE will be specialised in the development and application of R&I solutions based on AI in the manufacturing, energy, health and transport sectors and to create an internationally connected Lithuanian AI cluster.

instruments.name: Memorandum with the Artificial Intelligence Center Hamburg (ARIC)
instruments.summary: This partnership between Latvia’s Riga Technical University, RTU Riga Business School, and the Latvian IT Cluster with ARIC aims to enhance digital innovation in the logistics sector through AI. The collaboration focuses on advancing AI applications in supply chain management, automation, and optimisation while strengthening cross-border research and technology deployment.

instruments.name: AiNed – “AI for energy and sustainability”
instruments.summary: AiNed – “AI for Energy and Sustainability” is a public-private programme that explores how AI can accelerate the energy transition. It establishes AI Innovation Labs to develop practical solutions for sustainable energy. The initiative supports the Netherlands’ efforts to achieve climate goals by 2030 and beyond.

instruments.name: MEGALITH project
instruments.summary: The MEGALITH project uses AI models to study and protect Malta’s megalithic temples. The models predict stone degradation under different weather and climate scenarios. This helps preserve these historic sites for future generations.

instruments.name: WinGo Deposit
instruments.summary: The WinGo Deposit facility in Latvia uses machine vision and neural networks to sort recyclable materials, including PET and glass bottles, metal cans, tetra packs, and batteries. It helps improve recycling efficiency and reduce waste contamination. Future plans aim to expand its processing capabilities to additional waste types, such as shampoo bottles.

instruments.name: Latvian National Center for Artificial Intelligence
instruments.summary: The centre aims to advance AI adoption in Latvia by fostering collaboration between the public sector, private sector, and universities. Its objectives include pooling resources to drive AI innovation, supporting high-potential AI initiatives aligned with national interests, enhancing public AI literacy and access, and ensuring ethical, responsible AI use. The centre is expected to play a key role in AI research, education, and policy development.

instruments.name: IT Competence Centre project “Information and Communication Technology Competence Centre for Digitisation”
instruments.summary:
This research-driven initiative aims at advancing AI applications across different sectors. Key projects include: 
i) developing AI-driven governance solutions for software supply chain security;
ii) using AI to optimise retail discounts and stock management; and 
iii) AI/ML-driven analysis and classification of user-generated digital content to improve decision-making in digital environments.

instruments.name: TEF-Health
instruments.summary: TEF-Health is a European Testing and Experimentation Facility supporting AI validation and certification in the healthcare sector. It provides technical and scientific assistance to AI providers and notified bodies, aiming to accelerate AI solution development and market access while ensuring compliance with legal, ethical, quality, and interoperability standards. This initiative involves multidisciplinary teams focused on enhancing healthcare system efficiency, resilience, and sustainability.

instruments.name: European Digital Innovation Hubs
instruments.summary: Latvia is home to two European Digital Innovation Hubs (EDIHs), which focus on accelerating AI adoption: First, Digital Accelerator of Latvia (DAoL) specialises in AI research and digital product development. Second, Latvian Digital Innovation Hub (EDIHLV) has established an Applied AI Knowledge Centre to analyse business processes and model AI implementation benefits. These hubs support AI-driven manufacturing, business process automation, and municipal digital transformation through training

instruments.name: AI Factories Latvia
instruments.summary: AI Factories Latvia aims to drive AI innovation by supporting start-ups and established companies in developing and commercialising new AI products and services. A core focus is the creation of large language models tailored to regional languages to enhance translation, content creation, and communication technologies. Additionally, the initiative supports digital twin projects to strengthen cybersecurity and regional security simulations.

instruments.name: Competence Centres Initiative
instruments.summary: ​Italy's Competence Centres Initiative, launched in 2023, is a strategic programme designed to accelerate the nation's digital and green transformation, building upon the previous Industry 4.0 framework. This initiative establishes a network of eight public-private partnerships, each serving as a hub for expertise in advanced technologies such as AI, the Internet of Things, collaborative robotics, automation systems, big data analytics, blockchain, and cloud computing.

instruments.name: IPCEI on Microelectronics and Communication Technologies (IPCEI ME/CT)/ Project FANFARE
instruments.summary: Investment by the State in Analog Devices Inc.’s Project FAN-FARE. Minister Coveney welcomes the European Commission’s approval of Government supported semiconductor investment.

instruments.name: Disruptive Technologies Innovation Fund (DTIF)
instruments.summary: DTIF is a challenge-based fund established under Project Ireland 2040 and run with administrative support from Enter-prise Ireland. The types of projects that typically receive funding are partnerships to develop, deploy and commercialise disruptive technologies to transform business. AI relevant projects range from health-related applications of AI to technology, gaming and creative industries.

instruments.name: Irish Centre for High-End Computing (ICHEC)
instruments.summary: ICHEC organised the second European Quantum Technologies Conference in 2021. It is also part of the flagship project NEASQC (Next Applications of Quantum Computing), and it participates in the European High Performance Computing project HPCQS (High Performance Computer-Quantum Simulator).

instruments.name: Swiss Latvian Cooperation Programme – Pre-defined Programme Component in ICT and Smart Energy
instruments.summary: The Swiss–Latvian Cooperation Programme supports research and innovation in smart grids and energy storage. AI-enabled tools will be developed for real-time stability assessment of the Baltic electricity grid, alongside improved materials for energy storage and hydrogen production. The initiative involves national research institutions, led by the Institute of Solid-State Physics at the University of Latvia.

instruments.name: I-NERGY
instruments.summary: The I-NERGY tool is an AI-driven platform that supports smart and optimized energy management. It unifies energy-related data and facilitates efficient data exchange. The tool helps improve energy efficiency and enhances predictive capabilities in energy management.

instruments.name: CeADAR Technology Centre and  CeADAR AI EDIH
instruments.summary: CeADAR is Ireland’s National Centre for Applied AI. It is a market-focused technology centre for innovation and applied research in AI, machine learning and data analytics across all industry sectors. Enterprise Ireland is working with CeADAR on its next phase plan to scale up the centre.

instruments.name: Development of a new big data-driven overhead power grid pre-storm damage prediction system
instruments.summary: The Big Data-Driven Overhead Power Grid Pre-Storm Damage Prediction System in Latvia uses AI and machine learning to forecast potential storm damage to power grids. It provides real-time predictions for medium- and low-voltage networks. The system helps grid operators act proactively to prevent power outages.

instruments.name: Technology Voucher Programme for Enterprises
instruments.summary: Scheduled for launch in 2024, this programme provides financial grants covering 60-80% of costs to Hungarian SMEs seeking to implement AI solutions. It aims to support up to 200 SMEs, facilitating the integration of AI technologies into business operations.

instruments.name: Transition 5.0 Plan
instruments.summary: The Transition 5.0 Plan supports Italy’s move toward energy and environmental sustainability. It offers tax incentives for investments in energy-efficient digital infrastructure, smart manufacturing, and AI-driven resource optimisation. The initiative aims to reduce energy consumption while promoting renewable energy adoption.

instruments.name: Euro-Mediterranean Centre on Climate Change and the Cassandra supercomputer
instruments.summary: The Euro-Mediterranean Centre on Climate Change (CMCC) is a research institution in Italy focused on climate variability and its socio-economic impacts. The deployment of the Cassandra supercomputer doubles CMCC’s computational capacity, enabling faster and more detailed climate simulations. This supports AI-driven climate research and strengthens CMCC’s role in tackling climate change challenges.

instruments.name: Next Generation Energy Systems (NexSys)
instruments.summary: The Next Generation Energy Systems (NexSys) project develops pathways toward a net-zero energy system in Ireland. It uses AI in the Cities & Communities hub to analyse geospatial and sensor data for smarter energy use. The project combines big data analysis and citizen science to improve energy efficiency at neighbourhood and city levels.

instruments.name: ATMOSYS Air Quality Management System
instruments.summary: The ATMOSYS Air Quality Management System provides software tools and web applications to monitor and manage air quality in Croatia. It uses machine learning to forecast air quality at national measurement sites. The system was adapted from a Belgian model to meet Croatian regional and urban requirements.

instruments.name: Smart Attica EDIH
instruments.summary: The Smart Attica Digital Innovation Hub (EDIH) helps organisations develop and implement AI solutions for environmental challenges. It provides services such as training, testing technologies before investment, and building innovation networks. The initiative focuses on promoting sustainable and green technologies in Greece.

instruments.name: Smart Cities Projects in Kozani, Trikala, Ioannina, Kalamata, Thessaloniki and Athens
instruments.summary: The Smart Cities Projects in Kozani, Trikala, Ioannina, Kalamata, Thessaloniki, and Athens use AI technologies to improve urban planning and reduce emissions. They help cities optimize energy use, manage traffic, and monitor environmental quality. The projects involve collaboration between municipalities, technology providers, and research institutions.

instruments.name: Programme for Modern Enterprises
instruments.summary: Implemented by the Hungarian Chamber of Commerce and Industry, this programme assists SMEs in their digital transformation by providing resources and guidance on digital tools and technologies, including AI. It offers personalised IT audits, access to accredited IT suppliers, information on funding opportunities, thematic events, and a digital knowledge repository.

instruments.name: OcéanIA Challenge
instruments.summary: The OcéanIA Challenge develops AI and mathematical modeling tools to improve understanding of the ocean. It focuses on the ocean’s structure, dynamics, and role in regulating the biosphere. The initiative also supports efforts to combat climate change.

instruments.name: AI European Digital Innovation Hub (EDIH) Hungary
instruments.summary: This project aims to foster AI-driven innovation across Hungarian SMEs, start-ups, and public sector organisations. It offers comprehensive services ranging from initial awareness-building to prototype development and marketisation, and targets seven priority industries, including manufacturing, healthcare, energy, agriculture, logistics, finance, and public administration.

instruments.name: Inclusion of the climate or environmental dimensions of AI in education and training
instruments.summary: In France, several initiatives integrate climate and environmental aspects of AI into education and training. These include university programmes, MOOCs, and educational content on sustainable digital technologies. The goal is to raise awareness of the environmental impacts of AI and ICT among students and professionals.

instruments.name: Corallia Clusters Initiative
instruments.summary: The Corallia Clusters Initiative implements targeted interventions of sustainable innovation ecosystems focusing on the management of Clusters, Incubators and Entrepreneurship Programmes. It supports SMEs by providing access to resources, mentorship, and networking opportunities.

instruments.name: Signature Projects
instruments.summary: The Signature Projects in Denmark test AI applications in the public sector to improve sustainability and reduce CO2 emissions. AI is applied in areas such as energy management, fleet optimisation, and flood forecasting. The projects aim to make public services more efficient and environmentally friendly.

instruments.name: Call for projects between France and Germany on artificial intelligence technologies for risk prevention, crisis management, and resilience
instruments.summary: France and Germany launched a joint call for AI projects focused on risk prevention, crisis management, and resilience. One funded project, RenovAIte, develops AI-based software to optimise large-scale renovation of housing and roads. The initiative supports decision-making for engineering firms and local authorities.

instruments.name: CONTRAILS project Call for projects between France and Germany on artificial intelligence technologies for risk prevention, crisis management, and resilience
instruments.summary: The CONTRAILS project is a joint French–German initiative using trusted AI methods and physical models to study and predict condensation trails. Its goal is to assess their climate impact and support strategies to reduce contrail formation. The project is part of a binational call on AI technologies for risk prevention, crisis management, and resilience.

instruments.name: LIFE
instruments.summary: The LIFE project focuses on creating climate-resilient, water-efficient, and self-sustainable agri-food systems. As climate change threatens food security, the project emphasises sustainable techniques like hydroponics and locally sourced fertilisers. It transforms animal manure into nutrient solutions for hydroponic farming, with Digital Twin technology optimising this process to increase efficiency and reduce resource consumption.

instruments.name: Athens Center for Entrepreneurship and Innovation (ACEin)
instruments.summary: The ACEin, the incubation & acceleration centre of the Athens University of Economics, among other public-private partnerships, incubators, and accelerators, offers mentorship, resources, and financial support to AI start-ups.

instruments.name: Digital Pilot Farms
instruments.summary: The Digital Pilot Farms project focuses on creating a pilot farm network to test innovative plant protection techniques. It aims to make the use of plant protection products (PPPs) more efficient, safe, and environmentally friendly by using a digital tool that provides targeted advice to farmers. This tool is openly accessible to all in Luxembourg, helping farmers better manage pests and weeds in a sustainable way.

instruments.name: Various projects on decryption of logging sites
instruments.summary: The Lithuanian State Forest Service (2021-2022) and the Environmental Protection Agency have conducted multiple successive projects using AI solutions to identify clear-cut forest areas as a result of logging.

instruments.name: EquiFund & EquiFund II
instruments.summary: This programme aims to boost entrepreneurship and innovation in Greece by providing financing to start-ups. Specific funds under the EquiFund umbrella, such as the Innovation Window and the Early-Stage Window, are designed to support tech start-ups, including those working with AI. These funds provide equity financing to help businesses grow from the seed stage to scaling up. EquiFund II focuses on start-ups in the areas of Life sciences & Healthcare and Sustainability & Social impact.

instruments.name: Forestry 4.0 project
instruments.summary: The objective of the FOREST 4.0 project is to establish a Centre of Excellence to transform the forest environment monitoring, data acquisition, and analysis, and capture value from the collected data.

instruments.name: Control of the metabolic efficiency of selenium and iodine transfer to eggs, using AI technologies and assessment of the bioavailability of these necessary trace elements
instruments.summary: This project, implemented by the KTU Artificial Intelligence (AI) Center, uses AI technologies to assessment of the bioavailability of selenium and iodine in eggs, to assess metabolic efficiency.

instruments.name: High- and Highest-Performance-Computing for the Digital Age
instruments.summary: This initiative by the BMBF aims to enhance Germany’s position in HPC through targeted investments. The SCALEXA programme focuses on developing new methods and technologies for exascale computing, which enables processing at a scale that is orders of magnitude beyond current capabilities. Secondly, the GreenHPC initiative promotes energy-efficient solutions in EuroHPC, addressing environmental sustainability concerns associated with large-scale computing infrastructures.

instruments.name: Smart and Social Home Care
instruments.summary: This initiative is a research and development project, aiming to create an innovative, secure, and privacy-preserving smart home system to support the health and well-being of elderly individuals living independently. By integrating technology, public health, and social sciences, the project addresses challenges such as social isolation and the need for assistance and safety. It adopts an interdisciplinary approach, involving social sciences, software development, smart environments & security.

instruments.name: AiCatalyst
instruments.summary: The Association of Artificial Intelligence – AiCatalyst is private network of industry and academic experts aiming to utilise and democratise AI solutions within an ethical, transparent, and explainable framework while, establishing a network between the academic research and innovative entrepreneurship. It is partnered with the European Institute of Technology’s AI Community and the European Digital Innovation Hub ‘Smart Attica'.

instruments.name: Developing methodologies and recommendations for assessing the impact of AI technologies on sustainable, healthy and smart food ecosystems
instruments.summary: This project implemented will provide a platform and methodology for assessing the progress and maturity of the food ecosystem in its different parts (primary production, processing, distribution and marketing, consumption and waste management). Based on scientific sources and experience, it will identify the criteria needed to determine the level of maturity in the areas of sustainability, health-friendliness and digitalisation/artificial intelligence, creating a platform to assess maturity.

instruments.name: Gauss Centre for Supercomputing
instruments.summary: The Gauss Centre for Supercomputing (GCS) is a collaboration between Germany’s three leading national supercomputing centres: High-Performance Computing Centre Stuttgart (Höchstleistungsrechenzentrum Stuttgart, HLRS), Jülich Supercomputing Centre (JSC), and Leibniz Supercomputing Centre (Leibniz-Rechenzentrum, LRZ) in Garching. GCS provides Germany with HPC resources, supporting a wide range of scientific research and industrial applications.

instruments.name: Microelectronics. Trustworthy and sustainable. For Germany und Europe
instruments.summary: Running from 2021-2024, this framework programme by the German Federal Government focuses on promoting research and innovation in microelectronics with a commitment to trustworthiness, sustainability, and technological sovereignty. It emphasizes the development of secure and reliable microelectronic components, aiming to reduce Europe’s dependence on non-European technologies. The programme also advocates for environmentally friendly manufacturing processes within the microelectronics sector.

instruments.name: WeedBot
instruments.summary: This AI-driven agricultural tool uses high-resolution imaging and laser technology to distinguish crops from weeds. By applying concentrated light or laser beams, the system removes weeds without damaging crops, reducing reliance on chemical herbicides and enabling more sustainable farming practices.

instruments.name: Development and Implementation of Automated Nursery Plant Thinning and Weeding Technology
instruments.summary: This AI-powered smart weeder uses advanced object-recognition technology to identify and remove unwanted plants with precision. The automated solution enhances efficiency, reduces labour costs, and supports sustainable farming by minimising the need for chemical herbicides.

instruments.name: Administrative Cloud Strategy (DVS)
instruments.summary: The Administrative Cloud Strategy (DVS) is part of Germany’s efforts to enhance digital sovereignty in public administration by establishing a standardized, modular federal cloud infrastructure. The strategy aims to enable interoperability across federal, state, and local government levels by creating open standards and interfaces. It seeks to reduce dependence on single providers by fostering a diverse ecosystem of specialized IT service providers.

instruments.name: Bioeconomy Strategy for R&I
instruments.summary: The Investment and Development Agency of Latvia, in collaboration with different stakeholders, is developing a knowledge-intensive bioeconomy strategy for R&I. This strategy integrates aspects of digitalisation within the sector, including the application of AI. The strategy is accompanied by an action plan with defined timelines.

instruments.name: p-NET Competence Center
instruments.summary: Founded in the context of the Competence Centers Act of the General Secretariat for Research and Innovation (GSRI) and backed by both private and public funding, p-NET, a network of twenty-one shareholders from industry leaders, SMEs, academia, research institutions, and consulting firms from Greece’s digital landscape supports innovation, entrepreneurship, and technological advancement in 5G communications and other emerging networks.

instruments.name: Baltic Satellite Service project ML4HealthyForest
instruments.summary: This project develops a fully automated AI-powered service that provides objective forest management and thinning recommendations. By leveraging remote sensing data, machine learning, and automated forest growth models, the system enables data-driven decision-making for sustainable forestry practices.

instruments.name: Support semiconductor ecosystem
instruments.summary: As part of the national strategy on electronics, France supports initiatives aimed at developing advanced semiconductor technologies.

instruments.name: Institutional and Coordination Framework for Digital Transformation
instruments.summary: This governance framework aims to enhance policy coordination, streamline digital transformation efforts, and align Slovakia’s regulatory approach with EU digital regulations.

instruments.name: AI Politeai Lab at the IIT Demokritos
instruments.summary: The AI Politeia Lab, a project of the Institute of Informatics and Telecommunications (IIT), one of five National Centres for Scientific Research (NCSR) “Demokritos”, is an interdisciplinary lab set up to explore how to ensure a responsible and sustainable technology-enabled future by fostering innovative academic and industrial research across domains in a virtual environment.

instruments.name: Slovak Quantum Communication Infrastructure
instruments.summary: The Slovak Quantum Communication Infrastructure project is implemented by institute of Physics of the Slovak Academy of Sciences.

instruments.name: Projects under Food Vision 2030
instruments.summary: Under Food Vision 2030, the Department of Agriculture, Food and the Marine (DAFM) funds innovative agri-food research, including AI-driven projects. Recent AI-focused initiatives include improving productivity in the mushroom sector (MUSHNOMICS), food quality analysis using hyperspectral tech (SPECTROFOOD), AI in slaughterhouse inspections (RIBMINS), smart farming (APP4FARM), food system mapping, and AI-nutrition links in older adults (AMBROSIA).

instruments.name: Important Project on Common European Interest in the field of mictroelectronics, including communication technology (IPCEI-ME/CT)
instruments.summary: Four Slovak companies have been approved by the European Commission to support research, innovation and the first industrial deployment of microelectronics and communication technologies across the value chain.

instruments.name: Archimedes Unit at the Athena Research Center
instruments.summary: The Archimedes Unit at the Athena Research Center, which aims to foster basic and applied research and innovation in AI and data science, algorithms by funding visiting researchers as well as PhD candidates, organising systematic training and educational programmes, and building bridges foreign academic institutions.

instruments.name: Ancient Woodlands Ireland project
instruments.summary: The project builds on an established framework for identifying ancient woodlands. It will notably integrate AI-derived digital mapping of long-established woodlands.  By developing a methodology for integrating AI-derived digital mapping of historic maps and analysis of contemporary satellite imagery, this project can also help understand long-term changes of other land-cover types.

instruments.name: Medresyst
instruments.summary: The MedReSyst initiative seeks to revolutionise network and systems medicine through a holistic approach that considers the patient as a whole. By integrating biological data, exposomics, detailed clinical records, and advanced artificial intelligence (AI), MedReSyst aims to create individualised health profiles. These profiles map risk factors and protective elements unique to each person, enabling precise predictions of disease development and personalised treatment responses.

instruments.name: Powerful Medical cardio mobile app
instruments.summary: Clinical assistant that allows health care professionals to interpret an electrocardiogram (ECG), a recording of the heart's electrical activity, with the precision of a top cardiologist.

instruments.name: Health Data Agency
instruments.summary: The Belgian Health Data Agency (HDA), working with regional and federal partners, is creating a framework to improve access to quality health and healthcare-related data in a uniform, secure, and transparent way. This framework aims to optimise the re-use of data for purposes such as population health management, prevention, and healthcare policy.

instruments.name: Digital Health Slovakia
instruments.summary: Digital Health Slovakia is a non-profit association dedicated to promoting interoperability and standardisation in healthcare within Slovakia. It supports sustainable, patient-centric healthcare by fostering a community of digital health standards users and experts.

instruments.name: HealthHub - Center for Innovative Healthcare
instruments.summary: The Center for Innovative Healthcare, a European Digital Innovation Hub (EDIH), aims to drive structural reforms, innovation, and digital transformation in Slovakia's healthcare sector to enhance quality and efficiency. By 2025, it plans to establish a network of key Slovak companies and public institutions dedicated to modern healthcare solutions, with AI in healthcare as a priority area.

instruments.name: National High-Performance Computing at Universities
instruments.summary: Since 2021, the BMBF, in collaboration with the federal states, has supported HPC at universities, with an annual investment of EUR 62.5 million. This initiative provides the AI community with computing resources, specialised training, and consulting to strengthen research capabilities and advance scientific computing skills within academic institutions.

instruments.name: TEF Health - AI in Medical Imaging
instruments.summary: TEF Health, an initiative by the European Commission, aims to accelerate the adoption of AI and robotics in healthcare. In Slovakia, it focuses on using AI to analyse radiological images, enhancing the speed and accuracy of diagnoses for radiologists.

instruments.name: Crop Optimisation through Sensing, Understanding and Visualisation (CONSUS)
instruments.summary: CONSUS is a collaborative research partnership between UCD and Origin Enterprises PLC that has been supported through the Science Foundation Ireland (SFI) Strategic Partnership Programme. The project investigated digital, precision agriculture and crop science through a strong multi and inter-disciplinary approach that combined the leading expertise of UCD in data science and agricultural science with Origin’s integrated crop management research, systems, capabilities and on-farm knowledge.

instruments.name: Development and construction of a supercomputer
instruments.summary: This project aims to construct high-performance computing capacities, adding to the procurement and operation of publicly accessible national high-performance computing infrastructure, which is set to serve not only the academic community, but also public and state administration institutions, as well as private research and development.

instruments.name: Smart Agro Hub
instruments.summary: The Smart Agro Hub is the competence centre of the Agricultural University with the partnership of 12 other companies, forming an ecosystem of research, practical knowledge and entrepreneurship, contributing to the creation of a more environmentally friendly agricultural production system based on digital technologies.

instruments.name: Methodological Guidelines for Cloud Services
instruments.summary: These guidelines outline best practices and recommendations for integrating cloud services in public administration, supporting the goals of NKIVS, focussing on security, interoperability, and cost-efficiency in using cloud technologies.

instruments.name: Flemish AI Action Plan
instruments.summary: In terms of general AI, the Flemish group is moving ahead and is part of European groups. With an AI plan first created in 2019, it has a knowledge centre for data and society to provide legal advice, an AI board in its AI office, and an AI learning academy.

instruments.name: Lunit INSIGHT MMG
instruments.summary: Lunit INSIGHT MMG is an AI solution for mammography that has been implemented with the private health sector to improve the detection of breast cancer.

instruments.name: The development of genomic research in Romania (ROGEN)
instruments.summary: The initiative aims to create an integrated approach to genomic medical research.

instruments.name: National Genomic Data Infrastructure (GDI) Node and 1+ Million Genome Project
instruments.summary: Romania is working towards a national genome data infrastructure to contribute to the 1+ MG project and share its available genome data.

instruments.name: T2O2 Regulation
instruments.summary: This project focuses on creating a biomass-based combustion control system to reduce pollutants in free-standing room heaters. Developed with industry partners, the T2O2 system applies the energy balance method and aims for market readiness after further optimisation.

instruments.name: Optimization of Data Collection and Control Technology for Biomass Combustion Systems
instruments.summary: DigitalFire aims to improve biomass combustion systems by using advanced data collection, machine learning, and predictive maintenance. The project is aimed at enhancing efficiency and reliability, providing cost-effective solutions for manufacturers and operators.

instruments.name: FAIR Forward Open Data for Agriculture
instruments.summary: The Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (Bundesministerium für wirtschaftliche Zusammenarbeit und Entwicklung, BMZ) promotes environmental sustainability and AI with the FAIR Forward project. It provides partner countries in the Global South with access to climate-smart agricultural advice and includes a practitioner’s guide to green data centres, developed in collaboration with the World Bank, ITU, and GIZ.

instruments.name: AI and Data Accelerator in the Field of Food and Agriculture
instruments.summary: As part of the German AI strategy, KIDA serves as a cross-institutional service centre for AI use cases in the agri-food sector. Led by the Federal Ministry of Food and Agriculture (Bundesministerium für Ernährung und Landwirtschaft, BMEL), it enables AI and big data applications in agriculture, supporting subordinate authorities in handling AI and data cases.

instruments.name: Research programme "Agroecology and ICT: data, agricultural equipment, and genetic resources in the service of the agroecological transition and adaptation to climate hazards"
instruments.summary: The research projects selected and funded should implement multidisciplinary and systemic approaches based on the hybridisation of expertise from agronomy, ecology, genetics, physiology, ethology, digital technology, artificial intelligence, and social sciences (economics, sociology, management sciences, ergonomics). The funded infrastructures and equipment should be structured and provide data and methods for agroecological practices.

instruments.name: Intelligent Digital Economy AlgorithmS (IDEAS) NCBR
instruments.summary: IDEAS is a research and development centre operating in the field of artificial intelligence, whose mission is to support the development of this technology in Poland by creating a platform connecting the academic and business environments.

instruments.name: AI Department and Institute of Digital Games, University of Malta
instruments.summary: The University of Malta has established an AI excellence research centre through its AI Department and the Institute of Digital Games. The department offers specialisations in various AI fields, including Machine Learning, Deep Learning, Digital Games, Virtual Reality, Augmented Reality, Robotics, Fintech, Big Data, Creative Technologies, Text Processing, IoT, Data Science, AI in Education, Generative AI, and Computer Vision.

instruments.name: International accelerator of Startup Lithuania, the national startup ecosystem facilitator, under the auspices the Lithuanian Innovation Agency
instruments.summary: This initiative offers start-up acceleration services and accelerates at least 60 start-ups.

instruments.name: FactoryXChange EDIH
instruments.summary: The FactoryxChange (FXC) consortium is led by Irish Manufacturing Research and also integrates the National Centre for high performance computing (ICHEC), the National Centre for data analytics (INSIGHT).

instruments.name: Research Ireland Frontiers for the Future Programme (FFP)
instruments.summary: FFP provides funding for high-risk, high-reward research. It currently funds ~16 active awards in the field of AI.

instruments.name: Flemish AI Action Plan
instruments.summary: In terms of general AI, the Flemish group is moving ahead and is part of European groups. With an AI plan first created in 2019, it has a knowledge centre for data and society to provide legal advice, an AI board in its AI office, and an AI learning academy.

instruments.name: National Concept of Public Administration Informatization (NKIVS)
instruments.summary: The NKIVS provides the framework for the informatisation of public administration, focusing on digital and data transformations as well as integration of cloud services into public administration processes, promoting the use of next-generation cloud technologies to improve efficiency, accessibility, and security in government operations It includes guidelines on adopting cloud services within public administration, ensuring secure and efficient digital services.

instruments.name: National programme on spintronics
instruments.summary: Programme launched as part of France 2030 to promote frugal, agile and sustainable digital solutions. Spintronics is an emerging technology with multiple potential applications in the context of AI solutions.

instruments.name: EU4Health Program 2021-2027
instruments.summary:
In Romania, the EU4Health programme supports the creation of a National Health Data Observatory to improve how health information is collected and used for policymaking.
It also backs the development of an integrated e-health system, linking hospitals and digital health records across the country.
A further strand strengthens the digital literacy of medical staff, helping them use e-health tools and data securely in daily practice.

instruments.name: xPlain-AI
instruments.summary: xPlain-AI is an educational app on AI-based technologies in the medical field and was funded by the Vienna Chamber of Labor (Arbeiterkammer Wien), which began in 2021 as part of the Artificial Intelligence Mission 2030.

instruments.name: EUCAIM – EUropean Federation for CAncer Images
instruments.summary: The EUropean Federation for CAncer IMages project includes 76 partners across 14 countries including Portugal, bringing information from more than 91.000 patients with cancer. The EUCAIM’s objective is to build a central repository of cancer images, which will be used to develop and validate AI tools to support clinical decision making, diagnosis, and precision medicine.

instruments.name: DeepGreen
instruments.summary: In 2023, DeepGreen project partners launched the first open-source software platform for embedded AI: the Eclipse AIDGE platform.

instruments.name: D4Health Tirol
instruments.summary: Project to integrate the federated secure data infrastructure to link data from hospitals, telemedicine services and Austria's death registry to support the application of machine learning and artificial intelligence in research and routine care.

instruments.name: Research Ireland research infrastructure programme awards
instruments.summary: The Research Ireland Infrastructure Programme supports the research community in building and sustaining essential resources to conduct high-quality, innovative research across all disciplines. This programme recognises that robust research infrastructure is fundamental to advancing knowledge that contributes to Ireland’s cultural, social, environmental and economic development.

instruments.name: Digital Transformation of SMEs initiative
instruments.summary: The goal of this programme is to strengthen the digital maturity of the country's small and medium-sized enterprises operating in a wide range of sectors of the economy programme. It supports investments for the development of new products and services in the IT and communications sector and covers costs related to purchasing software, training staff, and integrating new digital solutions, including AI (via vouchers to SMEs).

instruments.name: Greek satellite in AI-MATTERS
instruments.summary: This network of seven nodes and one satellite aims to increase the resilience and the flexibility of the European manufacturing sector through the deployment of the latest developments in AI and robotics, and intelligent, autonomous systems for flexible production.

instruments.name: Synergies between Digital Agricultural Strategy, AI Strategy, and the Digital Food Strategy
instruments.summary: Hungary’s agricultural and food industry digitisation efforts are underpinned by the Digital Agricultural Strategy, the AI Strategy, and the Digital Food Industry Strategy. Together, these initiatives aim to modernise the sector across three pillars: digitising production technologies, enhancing data-driven decision-making, and streamlining product pathways through digital tools.

instruments.name: MISSION KI
instruments.summary: MISSION KI, established by the Federal Ministry for Digital and Transport (BMDV), focuses on accelerating the transfer of cutting-edge AI research into practice and fostering the growth of outstanding AI innovations. To further advance the development of trustworthy AI by design, the initiative is developing and testing a voluntary AI quality standard and corresponding testing procedures, particularly for low-risk AI systems, in alignment with the EU AI Act.

instruments.name: Fraunhofer Society
instruments.summary: The Fraunhofer Society consists of 76 institutes across Germany and facilitates the transfer of AI research into business applications. Institutes such as Fraunhofer IAIS, IPA, and IAO support companies—especially SMEs—through AI Innovation Centres with PoC projects, training, and advisory services. Over 250 companies have engaged with these services, with 30% deploying operational AI systems.

instruments.name: Projects from the National Institute of Geographic and Forestry Information (IGN)
instruments.summary: The French National Institute of Geographical and Forest Information (IGN) leads several AI-enhanced projects supporting land use, ecology, and agriculture. These include LiDAR HD (3D national mapping), OCS GE (land cover classification), CarHab (habitat modelling), AI4GEO (automated 2D/3D mapping from satellite data), CAP monitoring (with MASA/ASP), and BDForêt (forest reference mapping), advancing data-driven public policy and environmental management.

instruments.name: Acceleration strategy dedicated to the agritech industry
instruments.summary: France's agritech acceleration strategy supports innovation in agriculture through AI-driven projects and targeted funding. Key initiatives include the development of smart farming solutions and data platforms. Notably, France has funded Agdatahub, a secure data intermediation platform designed to enhance data sharing across the agricultural and agri-food sectors.

instruments.name: Company Level Spaces for Learning and Experimentation with AI (KI Lern- und Experimentierräume)
instruments.summary: Part of the New Quality of Work Initiative (Initiative Neue Qualität der Arbeit, INQA), this programme provides SMEs with dedicated spaces to experiment with and learn about AI applications within an operational context. Running from 2019 to 2024, the initiative aimed to demonstrate how AI can enhance workplace practices and benefit SMEs in various industries.

instruments.name: Finnish Bioeconomy Strategy
instruments.summary: The Finnish Bioeconomy Strategy 2022-2035 notably promotes the use of AI and other technologies to enhance the efficiency and sustainability of bio-based industries. It supports the development of new bio-based products and services, contributing to Finland’s goal of becoming climate-neutral by 2035.

instruments.name: EuroCC Cyprus
instruments.summary: The Cyprus NCC hosts activities, strengthens competences and provides services to the Cyprus and regional computational communities in the fields of High Performance Computing (HPC), Machine Learning (ML), Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Data Science (DS) and their application in industry, academia and public sector.

instruments.name: Forest data collection and management
instruments.summary: Building on the Finnish open forest data system, which was launched in March 2018, new solutions are being developed for forest data collection and management. Many of these solutions involve the use of AI. The most recent projects use accurate forest maps and autonomous drones to help improve the harvesting quality. It is also being studied how gamified mobile apps can be used in the collection of forest data. There is also work on digital twins of forests.

instruments.name: AI Professorships
instruments.summary: As part of the national AI strategy, Germany aimed to fund 100 new AI professorships by 2025, a target achieved in 2022 with a total of 150 professorships created by 2023. These include positions supported by various measures, such as the Alexander von Humboldt Professorship for AI, university AI competence centres, the tenure-track programme, DFG projects, and collaborations with non-university research institutions.

instruments.name: NL AIC Working Group on Human Capital
instruments.summary: As part of the NL AIC, the Human Capital Working Group focuses on improving AI education and reskilling efforts in the Netherlands.

instruments.name: Cloud Computing Platform "Vrančić"
instruments.summary: The Cloud Computing Platform "Vrančić" launched by the University Computing Centre (Srce), is an advanced OpenStack-based infrastructure supporting scientific research in Croatia.

instruments.name: NL AIC Training Platform
instruments.summary: The NL AIC launched a platform that provides an overview of over 600 university programmes, both ICT-focused and non-ICT, aimed at incorporating AI into higher education.

instruments.name: Projects focusing on AI-based solutions in agriculture under the research and development programme
instruments.summary: Under the research and development programme “Grønt Udviklings- og Demonstrationsprojekt” (GUDP), there are several examples of projects funded that investigate AI-based solutions in agriculture. GUDP supports the development and demonstration of knowledge and technologies that can make the food sector of the future greener. The second application round in 2025 with a focus on reducing emissions and nitrogen is now open for applications.

instruments.name: Human Capital Agenda ICT
instruments.summary: The Human Capital Agenda ICT, led by the Platform Talent for Technology, addresses the growing need for ICT talent in the Netherlands, including AI specialists.

instruments.name: Programme to Support Applied Research of the Ministry of Agriculture for the period 2024 – 2032
instruments.summary: The Ministry of Agriculture supports the development and implementation of AI within the framework of the Programme to Support Applied Research of the Ministry of Agriculture for the period 2024 – 2032. The programme is implemented in accordance with key strategic documents in the field of research, development and innovation (RDI). AI is supported under the Smart Farming area, which is one of the key areas of this programme.

instruments.name: Cultural AI Lab
instruments.summary: The Cultural AI Lab explores the intersection of AI and the humanities. It focuses on using AI to study cultural artifacts while also ensuring that AI development is informed by public values such as diversity and inclusivity.

instruments.name: AI Innovation Competition
instruments.summary: The AI Innovation Competition, launched by the BMWK, provides funding for exceptional approaches to developing AI-driven platform economies in key sectors of the German economy. The initiative aims to leverage AI methods as catalysts for innovative value creation networks and the development of new products and business models across various industries. Since 2019, three funding calls have been issued, resulting in support for a total of 26 projects to foster the growth of AI ecosystems.

instruments.name: AI for SMEs Grants (KI4KMU)
instruments.summary: The AI for SMEs grants support innovative AI projects led by SMEs in partnership with universities and start-ups. This programme encourages SMEs to explore advanced AI solutions in areas such as automated decision-making, privacy-by-design, and data engineering, with a focus on industry-specific applications like renewable energy, mobility, and manufacturing.

instruments.name: Bura Supercomputer
instruments.summary: Operated by the Centre for Advanced Computing and Modelling (CNRM) at the University of Rijeka, the Bura Supercomputer supports advanced research. Bura enables researchers to solve complex problems and perform advanced simulations across various scientific disciplines. Bura's peak performance is 233.6 teraflops.

instruments.name: European Innovation Partnership Operational Groups
instruments.summary: The European Innovation Partnership Operational Groups in Bulgaria support innovative projects in agriculture, focusing on the integration of technologies such as AI and robotics. The initiative encourages collaboration among farmers, researchers, and SMEs to develop practical solutions that address real-world agricultural challenges.

instruments.name: AgroHub.BG
instruments.summary: AgroHub.BG serves as the country's Digital Innovation Hub (DIH) for agriculture. This platform facilitates communication and collaboration among various stakeholders in the agricultural sector, including farmers, technology providers, and policy institutions. AgroHub.BG aims to democratise access to knowledge and resources in the agrarian industry, enabling the development of innovative solutions to address sector-specific challenges. It is part of the AgroDigiRise project, funded by the EC.

instruments.name: AI for Education pilot project
instruments.summary: The Ministry for Education, Sport, Youth, Research, and Innovation is developing an AI-powered adaptive learning system scheduled for implementation in 2024-2025.

instruments.name: Valbowal
instruments.summary: Valbowal is the Walloon strategic innovation initiative working on forestry. It aims to use AI to develop new construction products allowing a durable carbon capture and storage, but also new conception and production methods.

instruments.name: Towards the Food Factory of the Future
instruments.summary: Towards the Food Factory of the Future is an initiative led by Flanders’ FOOD that aims to drive the digital and sustainable transformation of the agri-food industry in Flanders. By bringing together research institutions, technology providers, and food manufacturers, the initiative fosters collaboration to enhance automation, AI-driven quality control, and energy-efficient production processes. It supports food companies in adopting cutting-edge digital technologies, such as machine learning

instruments.name: Flanders Research Institute for Agriculture, Fisheries and Food (ILVO)
instruments.summary: ILVO conducts various AI-based projects, such as precision farming using data technology, climate-smart agriculture, and robotics for agrifood. It participates in the Testing & Experimentation Facility for AI on Agrifood, co-funded by the Flemish Government.

instruments.name: Course on “Machine Learning and Computer Vision for the Environmental Sciences"
instruments.summary: The University of Malta offers a course focusing on applying Machine Learning and Computer Vision techniques to Geosciences. Students develop practical skills in using AI technologies to address environmental challenges, preparing them for research and professional applications in natural sciences.

instruments.name: Regional/local AI networks
instruments.summary: Several regional and local AI networks have developed in France, with missions including network development, raising awareness of the benefits of AI, and technology demonstration.

instruments.name: Agriculture of the Future Programme
instruments.summary: Digibiocontrol focuses on integrating AI and digital tools into biocontrol solutions for agriculture. The initiative supports farmers in using data-driven strategies to optimise pest and disease management, promoting sustainable and eco-friendly agricultural practices.

instruments.name: Digibiocontrol
instruments.summary: Digibiocontrol focuses on integrating AI and digital tools into biocontrol solutions for agriculture. The initiative supports farmers in using data-driven strategies to optimise pest and disease management, promoting sustainable and eco-friendly agricultural practices.

instruments.name: Supek Supercomputer
instruments.summary: Operated by the University of Zagreb, the Supek Supercomputer is Croatia's first petascale supercomputer, offering energy-efficient, high-performance computing with 1.25 petaFLOPS capacity.

instruments.name: Testing and experimentation facilities
instruments.summary: France participates in the five Testing and experimentation facilities for AI. French players coordinate two of them (PREVAIL and AI MATTERS). France is also coordinating the ALT-EDIC initiative that integrates evaluation activities for advanced AI models.

instruments.name: National Health Data Infrastructure
instruments.summary: With recent legislative updates, the federal government, states, regional health funds, and the umbrella association of social insurance carriers are now required to establish and operate a national platform for the secondary use of health data. This platform, currently in development, aims to enable coordinated secondary use of health data by relevant public health authorities to inform public health policies.

instruments.name: Community of Professional Educators (COPE) sessions
instruments.summary: The COPE sessions are designed to enhance the professional development of teachers in Malta. These sessions aim to provide educators with the necessary tools and knowledge to improve their teaching practices and stay updated with the latest educational trends.

instruments.name: Digital Commons for Generative Artificial Intelligence
