instruments.summary: This call for projects aims to create and make accessible digital commons across the entire generative AI value chain to foster the development of innovative products or services.

instruments.name: PAIDEIA project
instruments.summary: The PAIDEIA project is designed to upskill teachers in the use of AI in education and to develop an AI-related competence framework.

instruments.name: Digital Nose
instruments.summary: The Digital Nose project uses AI to detect stress-induced volatile organic compounds from trees and insect pheromones, combined with image data of typical damage patterns, to develop an early warning system for tree diseases, enabling climate-smart forestry and timely reactions to climate stress in forests.

instruments.name: Luxembourg Tech School (LTS)
instruments.summary: Luxembourg Tech School (LTS) is a digital education initiative allowing students aged 12 to 19 to learn about cutting-edge technologies while gaining business and industry knowledge. As a three-month extracurricular program, LTS uses a project-based approach to develop future digital leaders by involving students in hands-on, team-based projects in fields like coding, game development, fintech, AI, and space.

instruments.name: Cloud research programme (PEPR)
instruments.summary: Scientifically co-piloted by the CEA and Inria as part of the new “Digital, algorithms and software” programme. Its goal is to propose significant advances in the performance, security and frugality of cloud infrastructures and services while emphasising the transfer of innovative solutions from research to the industry.

instruments.name: Skillsbridges
instruments.summary: In the 2024/2025 academic year, Luxembourg's Ministry of Education is launching Skillsbridges, a new short-term professional training program. Aimed at helping adults adapt to evolving technologies and the changing job market, the initiative focuses on both upskilling and reskilling. Skillsbridges target a diverse audience, including both employed individuals and job seekers, addressing labor shortages and supporting professional transitions.

instruments.name: National Competence Center for HPC (EuroCC)
instruments.summary: The National Competence Centre for high-performance computing (HPC) in Croatia serves as the central point of contact for HPC, High-Performance Data Analytics (HPDA), and AI Croatia. The Centre is a consortium led by the University Computing Centre, University of Zagreb, and includes several Croatian institutions such as the University of Zagreb, University of Osijek, University of Split, Ruđer Bošković Institute, and University of Rijeka.

instruments.name: Accelerating the use of generative AI in the economy
instruments.summary: This call for proposals focuses on the downstream part of the generative AI value chain by encouraging the development of advanced integrated generative AI solutions with a short-term adoption horizon. It aims at bringing together developers and users of generative AI solutions and develop demonstrators for potentially replicable and economically viable solutions.

instruments.name: Open Data Government Strategy / Laws
instruments.summary:
Several noteworthy initiatives:
Livre III du code des relations entre le public et l’administration. 
Justice administration :
•	2016 Law for a Digital Republic which lays the foundation of open public data: LOI n° 2016-1321 de 2016 pour une République numérique. 
•	Decree 2023-1199 on automatic per-sonal data treatment.
•	Open data related to court decisions have been publicly available since 2021 for the Supreme Court, and since 2022 for appeal courts in the civil, social and business.

instruments.name: Interministerial framework for data administration
instruments.summary: As part of the public policy on data, algorithms and source codes, this document specifies the interministerial framework for administrations must register and describes the associated service offering. It covers data, algorithms, and source codes.

instruments.name: Chips from the North Strategy
instruments.summary: Initiative by the Technology Industries of Finland that benefits from public sector inputs in different areas, such as funding for RDI, R&D infrastructure, talent and education, and initiatives to attract international investments. The strategy aims to enhance Finland’s capabilities in semiconductor technology and ensure a competitive edge in the global market.

instruments.name: Kvanttinova piloting environment for microelectronics and quantum technology
instruments.summary: Finland will form an RDI environment and business cluster for specialised microelectronics and quantum technology, which will be one of the largest and most significant in Europe. These will enable the scaling of new products and services to an industrial scale. Co-financing of the EU Chips Act in accordance with the Government Programme will be ensured, and Business Finland will implement the chip technology programme. Preparations will be made for the establishment of a chip centre in Finland.

instruments.name: Develop and upscale quantum compute capacity
instruments.summary: Further to the announcement by VTT Technical Research Centre of Finland that they would continue the development of a quantum computer with a minimum of 50 qubits for use in Finland by 2025, in its 2023 budget session, the Government of Finland allocated EUR 70 million to VTT for upscaling the quantum computer to 300 qubit by 2027. HPC will be leveraged through the development of a national quantum computing environment by linking the quantum computer with LUMI.

instruments.name: Transitional study support
instruments.summary: To facilitate the re-skilling of professionals (not only on AI), in 2022, the government introduced the study support, which gives adults aged between 27 and 62 the opportunity to study and broaden their skills. For one year, professionals can receive a study grant equivalent to 80% of their pre-study salary, and for a further year, they can apply for a student loan.

instruments.name: Application Hub for a Circular Economy for Plastic Packaging through AI Methods
instruments.summary: The Application Hub for a Circular Economy for Plastic Packaging uses AI methods to improve recycling and reduce plastic waste. It supports research and innovation to enhance circular economy practices in Germany. The initiative aims to make plastic packaging management more efficient and sustainable.

instruments.name: AI Idea Workshop for Environmental Protection
instruments.summary: The AI Idea Workshop for Environmental Protection in Germany helps NGOs, researchers, start-ups, and individuals develop AI applications for environmental protection. It combines funding, technical expertise, and networking to encourage civil society engagement in AI-driven environmental solutions.

instruments.name: National Real-Time Water Management System
instruments.summary: The National Real-Time Water Management System in Bulgaria uses advanced technologies, including AI, to monitor and manage the country’s water resources. It tracks factors such as precipitation, snowmelt, and river flow in real time. The system aims to improve flood risk assessment and disaster preparedness.

instruments.name: European Master for High Performance Computing (EUMaster4HPC)
instruments.summary: The EUMaster4HPC is a new EU-funded Master’s program aimed at developing a highly skilled workforce in HPC to support Europe’s digital transformation. Coordinated by the University of Luxembourg, the program brings together expertise from European universities, research centres, and industry to create a comprehensive graduate-level curriculum.

instruments.name: Transitional study support
instruments.summary: To facilitate the re-skilling of professionals (not only on AI), in 2022, the government introduced the study support, which gives adults aged between 27 and 62 the opportunity to study and broaden their skills. For one year, professionals can receive a study grant equivalent to 80% of their pre-study salary, and for a further year, they can apply for a student loan.

instruments.name: Elements of AI – Luxembourg
instruments.summary: The Elements of AI course in Luxembourg offers a free, accessible introduction to artificial intelligence, tailored for individuals from all backgrounds.

instruments.name: AI4T
instruments.summary: The Erasmus+ project 'AI4T (AI for and by Teachers)' was a three-year collaboration involving partners from five European countries: France, Ireland, Italy, Luxembourg, and Slovenia. With contributions from ministries of education, universities, research centers, and private companies, the project aimed to develop a professional learning path for secondary school teachers. Its goal was to help teachers better understand the opportunities and risks associated with AI in the classroom.

instruments.name: Women Go Tech
instruments.summary: This mentoring programme, implemented by a non-profit association, supports women’s careers in the spheres of IT and engineering, while promoting gender equality in the workplace.

instruments.name: Analysing the impact of AI on educational programmes
instruments.summary: The government assigned the Swedish Higher Education Authority (UKÄ) the Swedish National Agency for Higher Vocational Education (MYH) with analysing the potential of impact artificial intelligence on the university's or polytechnic's education offerings in relation to the labor market's future skills needs.

instruments.name: ForeSight Project
instruments.summary: The ForeSight Project is a European collaborative initiative that uses AI-powered tools to help civil protection agencies respond to emergencies. It focuses on predicting and managing wildfires and urban incidents. By combining advanced AI algorithms and real-time data, the project enhances safety and emergency response efficiency.

instruments.name: A project for digitally excluded people to improve their digital skills
instruments.summary: The project, implemented by the Information Society Development Committee (ISDC) together with partners Langas į ateitį Association and the Lithuanian National Library Martynas Mažvydas, aims to provide digital literacy training and other activities to help develop the population's ability to make full use of the digital solutions developed. It also aims to enable the most vulnerable social groups to make greater use of e-services.

instruments.name: Priority Research Programme and Equipment (PEPR) on Artificial Intelligence
instruments.summary: As part of the national strategy for AI, it aims to develop breakthrough technologies that can help position France and Europe as leaders in strategic AI fields.

instruments.name: AI Cluster
instruments.summary: The National Strategy has allocated €560 million in 2023 to the initial and continuous training of AI experts and "AI+X" professionals with dual competencies. Within this framework, the AI Cluster initiative is dedicated to excellence in AI training in 9 universities and grandes écoles.

instruments.name: AI-programmes in Business Finland’s Digital Native Finland mission
instruments.summary: The aim of the Digital Native Finland mission is to accelerate digital transformation and create a global competitive advantage for Finnish companies. By increasing digital capabilities, we can increase sustainable customer value and raise the productivity of companies to the next level.

instruments.name: Business Finland campaign on Generative AI
instruments.summary: The main goal of the campaign is to accelerate generative AI-driven innovations for improved productivity and efficiency to strengthen global competitiveness.

instruments.name: SatGrass
instruments.summary: The Copernicus satellites from the European Earth Observation Programme can continuously monitor grassland and its use at the field level with high spatial resolution. The SatGrass project combines remote sensing and weather data into a model, calibrated with regional yield measurements and quality assessments, to analyse vegetation dynamics.

instruments.name: Collaboration for AI in Municipalities and Civil Society
instruments.summary: In this project, a targeted investment is made towards Sweden’s municipalities and civil society organisations. The aim is to provide tailored help and financial support that helps the target groups understand how AI can be used and to get started with their first concrete projects.

instruments.name: Assignment to the Swedish Agency for Digital Government and the Swedish Authority for Privacy Protection to develop guidelines for the use of generative artificial intelligence in public administration
instruments.summary: The government recently tasked two agencies with developing guidelines for generative AI, which are meant to be used to upskill civil servants.

instruments.name: eSam
instruments.summary: 41 government agencies are organized through eSam, a public collaboration mechanism for digitalization of the public sector, which has been implementing seven AI-related initiatives in 2023/2024, including i) use of AI in the creation of public documents, ii) Risks and prerequisites for exchanging models for AI development, iii) a common platform for chatbots, iv) practical application of AI solutions (interpretation), v) generative AI-based services, vi) AI for communication ops.

instruments.name: Incubator of AI solutions for the public administration
instruments.summary: Incubator focused on AI-based solutions for public sector organizations, with a focus on use cases involving generative AI. Although no public announcement had been issued at the time of writing, Spanish authorities report having received more than 300 requests from ministries. A prioritization protocol and development guidelines for the use cases are being developed.

instruments.name: REASSURE
instruments.summary: The REASSURE project develops a data analytics toolkit to improve the reliability of sustainable energy systems. It uses context-aware and predictive models to enhance energy efficiency and system robustness. The initiative helps energy networks adapt to changing conditions and operate more sustainably.

instruments.name: AI use in processing VAT returns
instruments.summary: The Financial Administration of the Republic of Slovenia (FURS) uses advanced artificial intelligence technologies (models for the use of predictive analytics in the implementation of business processes) in the process of acceptance of VAT returns. By using predictive analytics, FURS aims to increase the effectiveness of controls, both in terms of the number and of the additionally identified irregularities.

instruments.name: Creation of a hybrid cloud to combine registers such as AJPES register
instruments.summary: This project aims to create a hybrid cloud that will combine registers such as the AJPES register, the register of the Financial Administration of the Republic of Slovenia and, for example, court registers, with the aim of simplifying procedures for businesses in relation to the Ministry of Economic Development and Technology.

instruments.name: Innocities
instruments.summary: The state has signed long-term agreements with InnoCities on the allocation of RDI funding to strengthen globally competitive ecosystems. InnoCities covers all Finnish university and university consortium cities. The implementation mainly takes place with the financing of sustainable urban development of the EU programme period 2021–2027. The agreements develop close cooperation networks for innovation activity ecosystems, strengthen competence areas and increase the effectiveness of RDI.

instruments.name: Prognostic Health Management and Improving Energy Production of Wind Turbine Parks
instruments.summary: The Prognostic Health Management and Improving Energy Production of Wind Turbine Parks project uses AI for predictive maintenance in wind farms. It aims to optimise energy production, improve turbine reliability, and reduce operational costs. The initiative is part of Belgium’s broader Flanders AI Research Programme supporting AI innovation in the energy sector.

instruments.name: Single Horizontal AI Platform
instruments.summary: The Ministry of Digital Transformation has developed the pilot prototype “Semantični analizator” (Semantic Analyser), an open-source tool using AI techniques to process natural language. Building on these experiences, a single horizontal AI platform is planned for development to facilitate the processing of both public and non-public data. The platform will be modular, flexible, scalable, and upgradeable, ensuring adaptability to the diverse needs and requirements of individual authorities.

instruments.name: SIRIUS Simulator Project
instruments.summary: The SIRIUS Simulator Project, led by Jetpack.AI, develops a decision support system for electricity network operators. It helps Distribution System Operators (DSOs) plan long-term investments and adapt grids to the increasing integration of renewable energy. The project provides data-driven insights to improve sustainable grid management.

instruments.name: Coordination Mechanisms for the Sharing of Energy (COOMEP)
instruments.summary: The Coordination Mechanisms for the Sharing of Energy (COOMEP) project helps households coordinate their energy usage to be more efficient and sustainable. It uses AI proxies—autonomous decision-makers configured by users—to optimise energy sharing and consumption. The initiative encourages collaboration among households to improve overall energy efficiency.

instruments.name: sustAIn.brussels
instruments.summary: sustAIn.brussels is a European Digital Innovation Hub (EDIH) based in the Brussels Capital Region. It helps organisations adopt sustainable and digital innovations, including AI and other emerging technologies. The hub supports businesses in future-proofing operations while addressing economic, social, and environmental challenges.

instruments.name: Climate Change Cockpit
instruments.summary: The Climate Change Cockpit provides a centralised platform for environmental data in Austria’s tourism sector. It consolidates information from multiple sources to give a comprehensive overview of environmental conditions and trends. The initiative helps tourism organisations make better decisions and plan strategically to address climate-related challenges.

instruments.name: Slovakia	Strategic Transport Development Plan of the Slovak Republic until 2030
instruments.summary: The Strategic Transport Development Plan of the Slovak Republic until 2030 focuses on integrating AI technologies into transport infrastructure. It aims to improve traffic management, safety, and efficiency across road, rail, and water transport. The plan supports the development of intelligent transport systems (ITS) and multimodal transport solutions.

instruments.name: DARS AI Initiative
instruments.summary: The DARS AI Initiative introduces artificial intelligence to predict congestion and accidents on Slovenia’s motorways. The initiative uses machine learning models to improve traffic management and road safety. All AI projects are linked to the National Traffic Management Centre to support real-time decision-making.

instruments.name: Digitisation of Railway and Road Infrastructure – Digitisation of Road Traffic
instruments.summary: The Digitisation of Road Traffic project in Slovenia modernises the country’s road infrastructure management using digital technologies. It provides real-time information on traffic conditions and vehicle movement. The initiative aims to improve traffic efficiency, interoperability, and safety.

instruments.name: The National Traffic Management Centre (NTMC)
instruments.summary: The National Traffic Management Centre (NTMC) in Slovenia collects and analyses road and traffic data. It provides services for traffic control, management, and Intelligent Transport Systems (ITS). The NTMC supports safe and efficient traffic operations across the country.

instruments.name: Net Zero Cities
instruments.summary: The Net Zero Cities pilot in Ljubljana, Kranj, and Velenje upgrades urban digital platforms with public transport and traffic data. It integrates multiple data sources and installs new equipment to improve measurement accuracy. The pilot also develops a Mobility-as-a-Service (MaaS) mobile application to enhance sustainable urban mobility.

instruments.name: Support to SRIP ACS+ Strategic Research Innovation Partnership
instruments.summary: The SRIP ACS+ Strategic Research Innovation Partnership in Slovenia supports innovation and R&D in the engineering and automotive sectors. It provides funding and collaboration opportunities for companies, research institutions, and service providers. The ACS+ AV Living Lab offers a real-world environment to test autonomous vehicles and smart mobility technologies.

instruments.name: Sweden	FFI Strategic Vehicle Research and Innovation
instruments.summary: The FFI Strategic Vehicle Research and Innovation programme is a joint initiative between the Swedish state and the automotive industry. It supports research and innovation to promote sustainable road transport. The programme funds R&D activities with around SEK 1 billion per year, shared equally between the state and industry.

instruments.name: Drive Sweden
instruments.summary: Drive Sweden is a national Swedish initiative that develops and tests sustainable, connected, and automated mobility solutions. It brings together over 200 partners from business, academia, and the public sector. By financing innovations, it makes new AI-based transport solutions technically, commercially, and legally feasible.

instruments.name: FFI Traffic Safe Automation
instruments.summary: The FFI “Traffic Safe Automation” programme in Sweden develops innovative solutions to make road safety a driver of vehicle automation. It focuses on safe, connected and automated vehicles that are prepared for sharing, aiming to improve road safety and promote sustainable transport.

instruments.name: Cooperative Streets Project
instruments.summary: The Cooperative Streets Project in Portugal pilots Cooperative Intelligent Transport Systems (C-ITS) in urban areas. It aims to improve road safety, reduce emissions, and encourage public transport use. The project also tests multimodal access, parking management, Mobility as a Service (MaaS), and smart infrastructure solutions.

instruments.name: Strengthening the Digital Skills of Civil Servants
instruments.summary: This programme of the Administrative Academy (under the Ministry for Public Administration) aims to improve the competences of civil servants in core digital skills, including specialised skills on AI. The content of the programme is designed in accordance with the OECD Framework for Digital Talents and Skills in the Public Sector. The implementation of the programme is co-financed by the Republic of Slovenia, the Ministry of Public Administration, and the European Union - NextGenerationEU.

instruments.name: Central Government Guidelines on Cloud Policies
instruments.summary: The Ministry of Finance updated the central government’s cloud guidelines on Cloud policies in 2023. The updated policies emphasise a “Cloud First” strategy, encouraging the use of cloud solutions as the primary option. They also address the handling of public and confidential data in cloud environments, ensuring that data protection and security measures are in place.

instruments.name: Finnish AI Region (FAIR) European Digital Innovation Hub (EDIH)
instruments.summary: This initiative aims to foster collaboration and innovation in AI across various sectors, with a focus on the Helsinki region. It focuses on practical applications and aims to create a world-class AI research and innovation hub by pooling expertise and resources and supporting regional development and networking. Moreover, FAIR provides a range of experimentation and testing platforms and offers the opportunity to test products and services in real-world settings.

instruments.name: Tampere City Lab
instruments.summary: Business Tampere operates several initiatives to support AI testing and experimentation, notably the Tampere City Lab, which is part of the EU-wide Citcom.ai initiative and network of testing and experimentation facilities to help bring AI innovations to market responsibly. It provides a combination of virtual and physical testbeds for smart city and AI-powered solutions and supports the development and testing of AI technologies in real-world urban environments.

instruments.name: Route 25 Project
instruments.summary: The Route 25 project develops autonomous and connected transport systems in Portugal. It invests EUR 80 million and creates 488 new jobs to advance smart, sustainable, and inclusive mobility solutions. The project focuses on research and innovation in autonomous, intelligent, and interoperable transport technologies.

instruments.name: Smart Traffic Analysis and Traffic Safety (STATS)
instruments.summary: The Smart Traffic Analysis and Traffic Safety (STATS) project uses AI to improve traffic safety in urban areas. It applies computer vision and data analysis to monitor traffic patterns and enhance the safety of cyclists and pedestrians. The project aims to reduce accidents and create safer city streets.

instruments.name: A12 traffic forecaster
instruments.summary: The A12 Traffic Forecaster is a machine learning-based application that predicts traffic levels on the A12 motorway. It combines historical data, roadwork schedules, and holiday periods to deliver real-time updates. This helps commuters plan their journeys more efficiently and avoid congestion.

instruments.name: BikeSafeAI
instruments.summary: The BikeSafeAI project uses AI to analyse cyclist behaviour and traffic conditions to identify risky situations. It aims to reduce accidents and improve safety for cyclists in urban and regional settings. The project is a collaboration between multiple universities, government bodies, and mobility organisations in the Netherlands.

instruments.name: Open Government Action Plan
instruments.summary: The Open Government Action Plan 2023-2027 supports the development of data policies that align with the principles of open government. It emphasises transparency, accountability, and citizen participation in government activities. It includes initiatives to enhance data accessibility and promote the use of open data.

instruments.name: Science, Technology and Society university programmes
instruments.summary: The University of Uppsala has complementary programmes in place to educate students of technology-focused subjects to consider the policy/societal impact of technology, while the University of Gothenburg has a research group on the same subject.

instruments.name: Digital Compass/data policy
instruments.summary: Finland’s Digital Compass encompasses data policy, e.g. it outlines the country’s vision and goals regarding data management, sharing, and use.

instruments.name: MIRRI Information hub for artificial intelligence (AI).
instruments.summary: The new website, created in collaboration with the National Artificial Intelligence Platform "AIslovakIA," aims to provide easy access to relevant legislation, documents, and initiatives in the field of AI. It is part of fulfilling the measures of the Action Plan for the Digital Transformation of Slovakia 2023-2026. The platform's main goal is to offer both experts and the general public access to information on AI legislation, events, study programmes related to AI.

instruments.name: Intelligent Transport Systems (ITS)
instruments.summary: The Intelligent Transport Systems (ITS) project in Malta uses AI-driven tools to reduce traffic congestion and improve urban mobility. It optimises traffic re-routing, road closures, and low-traffic zones. The initiative also promotes multi-modal transport for seamless travel.

instruments.name: AI Hub Tampere
instruments.summary: AI Hub Tampere is a research centre dedicated to applied AI hosted by Tampere University and funded by public instruments. Backed by a coalition of 25 professors combining multiple disciplines, AI Hub explores the diverse socio-technical aspects of AI transformation.

instruments.name: AI for traffic management pilot project
instruments.summary: The AI for Traffic Management Pilot Project in Malta integrates AI into traffic control systems and GIS. It aims to reduce congestion and emissions, improve public transport planning, and monitor traffic behaviours. The project provides data-driven insights to support intelligent journey management and traffic enforcement.

instruments.name: 3VisionD
instruments.summary: 3VisionD is an AI-powered video analytics system that detects objects and determines their locations in real-world 3D coordinates. It supports smart city applications such as traffic and parking management, urban planning, and harbour monitoring. The system enables automated parking violation detection, occupancy tracking, and adaptive street lighting based on real-time data.

instruments.name: Smart LED Light
instruments.summary: AI-powered smart lighting solutions are used in Latvian cities to monitor and detect traffic violations. The system records incidents such as red-light running, misuse of public transport lanes, and illegal stopping. The data supports traffic law enforcement and improves urban mobility management.

instruments.name: LMT Traffic Monitoring Tool
instruments.summary: The LMT Traffic Monitoring Tool uses AI-powered video and machine vision to monitor traffic in real time. It detects traffic intensity and common violations, such as running red lights or illegal turns. The system improves road safety and supports traffic management.

instruments.name: Winter Road Maintenance Using AI in Kuldīga Municipality
instruments.summary: The Winter Road Maintenance Using AI initiative in Kuldīga Municipality uses AI to monitor road conditions in real time. It predicts necessary maintenance actions and provides an interactive map for local authorities. The system improves collaboration between municipalities and road maintenance providers, increasing efficiency in winter road upkeep.

instruments.name: AI for Smart Cities Mobility
instruments.summary: The AI-based Smart City Solutions initiative uses artificial intelligence to improve traffic management and public transport. It develops intelligent networks to reduce congestion in high-traffic areas. The programme also supports environmental sustainability goals as part of the broader digital transition.

instruments.name: Urban Mobility Data Integration
instruments.summary: The Urban Mobility Data Integration initiative in Italy establishes a national registry of datasets and models for mobility applications. It supports the development of intelligent transport networks that can dynamically adapt to real-time demand, aiming to enhance urban mobility planning and decision-making.

instruments.name: AI for Policymaking
instruments.summary: The Slovak government is exploring the use of AI for data-driven policymaking. This involves using AI to analyse large datasets to identify trends, predict outcomes, and inform policy decisions. Such initiatives aim to make policymaking more evidence-based and effective.

instruments.name: Sustainable Mobility
instruments.summary: The Sustainable Mobility AI initiative in Italy develops AI applications for transportation to optimise energy use, manage traffic, and reduce emissions. It aims to improve quality of life through smarter and greener mobility solutions. The initiative is part of the Italian Strategy for AI 2024–2026.

instruments.name: Dublin City Council’s Smart Dublin initiative: Project on Using AI-Enabled Cameras to Understand Vehicular Flows
instruments.summary: The AI-Enabled Cameras for Vehicular Flows project uses video streams processed by AI to monitor traffic automatically. It identifies and reports traffic patterns, reducing the need for manual monitoring or storing large volumes of footage. The initiative improves traffic management efficiency.

instruments.name: Dublin City Council’s Smart Dublin initiative: Project on Mapping City Assets from Street Level Imagery
instruments.summary: The Mapping City Assets from Street Level Imagery initiative uses AI to detect urban assets such as traffic signs, bins, and storm drains. Each asset is assigned accurate GPS coordinates, creating a geospatial record. This information supports city planning, operations, and maintenance.

instruments.name: Dublin City Council’s Smart Dublin initiative: Project on Delivery Robots using AI enabled computer vision to solve issues regarding ‘last mile delivery’
instruments.summary: The Delivery Robots Pilot Project uses AI-powered computer vision to improve last-mile delivery. The initiative tests autonomous delivery robots to make logistics faster, safer, and more efficient. It aims to reduce delivery costs and enhance service quality for customers.

instruments.name: Testing authorisation regime and connected vehicle technology pilot
instruments.summary: The Connected and Automated Mobility (CAM) Interdepartmental Steering Group oversees the development of testing rules for connected and automated vehicles on public roads. A pilot project is running until the end of 2024, focusing on on-road connected vehicle technology (C-ITS). Around 1,500 drivers are participating to help test and evaluate these systems.

instruments.name: Investment C1.4 R5-I2 Autonomous Vehicles in Zagreb
instruments.summary: The Autonomous Vehicles in Zagreb initiative focuses on developing self-driving electric vehicles and the infrastructure needed for urban mobility. It aims to make transportation in Zagreb safer, more efficient, and environmentally friendly.

instruments.name: "Digitisation and decarbonisation of mobility" strategy
instruments.summary: The “Digitisation and Decarbonisation of Mobility” strategy in France aims to speed up the use of digital technologies and low-carbon solutions in mobility systems. It supports projects that reduce emissions from passenger and freight transport using “smart”, automated, or connected mobility tools. With public funding, it encourages innovation in logistics, infrastructure, and transport services to make mobility greener and more efficient.

instruments.name: IRT SystemX
instruments.summary: IRT SystemX is a French research institute that works with public and private partners on projects to validate the safety of autonomous vehicles through simulation. Projects such as SVA, 3SA, and SVR develop tools, scenarios, and methods to test autonomous driving systems, shuttles, and robot-taxis. The goal is to ensure these systems are safe, reliable, and can eventually be approved for real-world use.

instruments.name: European Digital Innovation Hubs (EDIHs)
instruments.summary: European Digital Innovation Hubs (EDIHs) in Slovakia play a crucial role in supporting the uptake of AI and other innovative technologies in public sector organisations. These hubs provide resources, expertise, and support for implementing AI-driven solutions to enhance public service delivery.

instruments.name: DigitalLead
instruments.summary: Part of the business promotion system and Denmark's national cluster for digital technologies, serves as a hub for digital innovation – both for companies developing digital solutions and for other sectors in need of innovative digital solutions. The cluster build bridges between businesses, entrepreneurs, and knowledge institutions.

instruments.name: Advanced digital skills training program for civil servants
instruments.summary:
The objective of this investment (under the RRP) is to increase the advanced digital skills of the civil servants, aiming to support the digitalisation of the public services by improving the availability of a qualified workforce for internal IT&C operations. The investment consists of training for advanced digital skills (database management, system management, business analysis, data analysis, programming) for 32,500 civil servants
(out of which 2,500 seniors).

instruments.name: Order no. 234/2022 regarding professional training and development programs for civil servants
instruments.summary: The purpose of this initiative is to train civil servants in ICT and emerging technologies, including AI, as foreseen in the Order of the National Agency of Public Officers no. 234/2022.

instruments.name: ION
instruments.summary: An initiative to support citizen engagement in the public sector, ION, an AI counsellor designed to serve as a link between Romanian citizens and the executive branch of government, leveraging natural language processing and computer vision techniques with the aim of capturing the sentiments of Romanian citizens in real time. This tool was developed with a Bucharest-based company - Humans.ai - in collaboration with Romanian AI researchers and computer science professors.

instruments.name: Caixa Geral de Aposentações AI Virtual Assistant
instruments.summary: The General Retirement Fund has implemented an AI-based virtual assistant on its portal. This virtual assistant is designed to answer frequently asked questions (FAQs), thereby improving user navigation and reducing wait times for responses. It helps users find the information they need more efficiently and enhances the overall user experience on the CGA portal (CGA, 2023[759]). The CGA is a Portuguese institution responsible for managing the social security regime for public sector employees.

instruments.name: Social Security Chatbot
instruments.summary: A chatbot created during the COVID-19 crisis to answer citizens’ frequent questions, with future plans for full integration with the Social Security Portal and the addition of live chat options with human agents.

instruments.name: Digital Croatia Strategy
instruments.summary: A comprehensive national digital transformation strategy that aims to strengthen the Croatian market's investment cycle through additional financial resources for new technologies, including AI and green technologies.

instruments.name: AEXCIA Platform
instruments.summary: Over the next two years, the AEXCIA platform, an AI-powered consumer experience management tool, will automate the handling of citizens’ complaints and information requests while analysing consumer behaviour, particularly on social networks. Designed to enhance efficiency, AEXCIA will support regulatory and supervisory activities by providing insights into consumer satisfaction and company conduct, ultimately improving consumer experience management through advanced AI capabilities.

instruments.name: SME: Digital and Denmark’s Export and Investment fund (EIFO) digitalisation support for small businesses
instruments.summary: Support to SMEs through grants, mainly for the purchase of private advice to identify digitalisation potential (including an AI-dedicated strand) or advice on implementation. Other support measures include subsidies for investments; skills and management development; and guidance on digital development. In addition, since May 2023, the EIFO facilitates access to financing for smaller Danish companies for digitalisation.

instruments.name: PlanAPP Project
instruments.summary: The project is an EU-funded initiative led by the public administration planning, policy, and foresight competence centre. This project focuses on applying AI to enhance regulatory impact assessments. By leveraging AI, PlanAPP aims to improve the quality and efficiency of regulatory analysis at both national and European levels. The project collaborates with Nova Information Management School.

instruments.name: Digital Research Centre Denmark (DIREC)
instruments.summary: DIREC’s research spans ten areas in advanced digital technology. It aims to develop and support research in AI, big data, IoT, and IT Security.

instruments.name: Secure platform for developing transparent Danish language models
instruments.summary: This platform for developing and training language models will be established for Danish companies and authorities to freely access and use and further develop Danish language models for their own contexts. The initiative will be run under the auspices of the Danish Foundations Models – a collaboration between Aarhus University, the University of Southern Denmark, the University of Copenhagen and the Alexandra Institute on research-based development of language models.

instruments.name: Centre for Artificial Intelligence in Society
instruments.summary: The Danish government establish an interdisciplinary centre for research and advice on using AI in society. The centre will work closely with the Pioneer Centre for Artificial Intelligence. The centre will serve as a single point of access to knowledge and advice on how authorities and companies can best use AI in practice and will also conduct independent research and practice-oriented evaluation and monitoring of generative AI.

instruments.name: TWIST
instruments.summary: This initiative, running between 2025 and 2031, is aimed at strengthening innovation within existing companies and adapting to industrial and technological shifts. It emphasises supporting AI research and industrial applications through strategic investments, with a specific focus on AI, quantum technologies, and semiconductors. The first call for projects targets AI R&D.

instruments.name: Technology Incubation Project
instruments.summary: This initiative focuses on developing a network of technology incubation hubs in Czechia to foster the growth of start-ups and spin-offs, especially in innovative AI fields. By 2025, the project aims to support around 250 start-ups with both financial aid and mentoring, helping them bring new AI-driven products and services to market.

instruments.name: Open Data Policy / Open Data Portal
instruments.summary: The Open Data Policy establishes a comprehensive framework for public sector data sharing, aiming to enhance transparency and create economic opportunities. The policy enables unrestricted access to government data for both domestic and international users, including researchers from academia and industry.

instruments.name: RICAIP - Research and Innovation Centre on Advanced Industrial Production
instruments.summary: RICAIP is an international research centre that connects testbeds in Prague, Brno, and Saarbrücken, Germany. It focuses on Industry 4.0 innovations and the application of AI in industrial production, promoting modular, distributed production methods. The centre aims to integrate AI into production processes, making them more adaptive to market needs.

instruments.name: Digital Decade: no one is left behind
instruments.summary: This initiative is aimed at reducing the digital exclusion of the Lithuanian seniors through a multi-year project by the Communications Regulatory Authority (CRA), consisting of a tour across communities of Lithuania to educate seniors on how to use digital services conveniently, how to protect themselves from fraud and what their rights as consumers are.

instruments.name: Business and scientific organisations Platform (S2B)
instruments.summary: The Platform aims to foster effective collaboration in research and innovation between the government, universities, scientific organizations, and businesses.

instruments.name: The Wallenberg AI and Transformative Technologies Education Development Program
instruments.summary: Denmark has started collaborating with NVIDIA in 2024 to establish the centre for AI innovation that will host one of the world’s most powerful AI supercomputers (Gefion). Researchers from Denmark’s public and private sectors will gain access to a state-of-the-art supercomputer optimised for large-scale projects using AI as well as  software platforms, training, and expertise (Novo Nordisk Foundation, 2024).

instruments.name: Developing AI solutions at all education levels
instruments.summary: This reform intends to apply international recommendations in Lithuanian educational institutions and integrate AI solutions into lessons safely, including by providing consultations and training for teachers on AI related issues.

instruments.name: Operation Programme Research, Development and Education
instruments.summary: This programme has been the largest state-funded initiative in AI research and development in Czechia, supporting 23 AI-related projects. Its main focus is on bolstering AI innovation through educational and research efforts, facilitating advancements in both academic and applied AI fields.

instruments.name: Bulgarian Portal for Open Science (BPOS)
instruments.summary: The Bulgarian Portal for Open Science (BPOS) was created by the National Centre for Information and Documentation in line with the EC Recommendation No. 790 of 25 April 2018 on access to and preservation of scientific information, as well as Bulgaria’s commitments to the European Open Science Cloud (EOSC).

instruments.name: Update to the general programme of computer science (classes 1-12)
instruments.summary: This initiative examines AI topics and intends to improve AI literacy skills.

instruments.name: Open Data Portal (Public Sector Data)
instruments.summary: This platform is designed to share a wide range of public sector data, including scientific data.

instruments.name: Urban Data Space
instruments.summary: Led by GATE, the Urban Data Space is the first sectoral data space in Bulgaria. It facilitates data sharing and access between organisations to enable the development of new business products and services.

instruments.name: National center for AI innovation
instruments.summary: Denmark has started collaborating with NVIDIA in 2024 to establish the centre for AI innovation that will host one of the world’s most powerful AI supercomputers (Gefion). Researchers from Denmark’s public and private sectors will gain access to a state-of-the-art supercomputer optimised for large-scale projects using AI as well as  software platforms, training, and expertise (Novo Nordisk Foundation, 2024).

instruments.name: European Digital Innovation Hubs (EDIHs)
instruments.summary: Czechia hosts key European Digital Innovation Hubs (EDIHs) that facilitate the digital transformation of enterprises and public organisations. For instance, EDIH CTU focuses on supporting AI and HPC applications, offering tailored solutions for SMEs and the public sector through expert consultations, training, and access to cutting-edge infrastructure. Another notable hub, EDIH Testbed for Industry 4.0, specialises in advanced manufacturing technologies, helps organisations adopt Industry 4.0.

instruments.name: Digital entrepreneurship programme for schoolchildren in grades 5-8 of the Ministry of Economy and Innovation
instruments.summary: This initiative aims to create a methodology for learning digital entrepreneurship to bring integrated, relevant, creative computer science and entrepreneurship lessons to students in grades 5-8.

instruments.name: European Testing and Experimentation Facility (TEF) Manufacturing
instruments.summary: This TEF project aims to boost the resilience and flexibility of the manufacturing sector by integrating AI and robotics into production. Czechia is represented by three universities collaborating with European partners to implement AI-based automation and intelligent systems for advanced manufacturing.

instruments.name: Web-based advice on AI in education
instruments.summary: The National Agency for Education provides a web-based support tool for teachers, schools leaders and school providers on the risks and opportunities of AI in schools, particularly in view of generative AI-powered chatbots.

instruments.name: A joint project of the education and learning programme "Vedliai" and "Lietuvos Junior Achievement" (LJA)
instruments.summary: This joint project intends to bring integrated, relevant, creative computer science and entrepreneurship lessons for pupils in grades 5-8 to Lithuanian schools.

instruments.name: National Data Governance Reference Framework (NDGRF)
instruments.summary: A framework under development that will establish comprehensive standards for data management across Bulgaria's digital ecosystem. The NDGRF is established by decision of the Minister of Electronic Governance and regards the national public administration as a whole. This framework encompasses standards for data collection, quality assurance, storage protocols, and exchange mechanisms.

instruments.name: National Strategy for Research Data Management
instruments.summary: DeiC is also leading the work to implement the National Strategy for Research Data Management. The strategy targets research institutions and research funding organisations. It defines several principles and areas of action to strengthen the dissemination and financing of good data management practices, resulting in more FAIR research data (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable) in Denmark.

instruments.name: Digital Transformation of Bulgaria Strategy 2024-2030
instruments.summary: The Digital Transformation of Bulgaria Strategy for 2024-2030 is a comprehensive framework that outlines Bulgaria's vision for digital development.

instruments.name: Walloon Export and Foreign Investment Agency (Agence wallonne à l'Exportation et aux Investissements étrangers, AWEX)
instruments.summary: AWEX supports the development of large-scale data centres in Wallonia.

instruments.name: Danish e-infrastructure Consortium (DeiC)
instruments.summary: DeiC is “the collaboration with and between the Danish universities. DeIC coordinates the delivery and development of the national digital research infrastructure. Its “purpose is to ensure that computing power, data storage and network infrastructure are available for Danish research and education”.

instruments.name: Wallonia Undertaking  (Wallonie Entreprendre)
instruments.summary: Wallonie Entreprendre supports strategic investments in large-scale data centres to bolster regional ICT infrastructure and facilitate the growth of Wallonia’s data-driven economy.

instruments.name: Strategic projects for economic recovery and transformation (PERTE) of the new language economy
instruments.summary: The plan, which also covers dimensions beyond AI proper, aims to contribute to AI learning in Spanish and co-official languages.

instruments.name: Vlaams Supercomputer Centrum (VSC)
instruments.summary: The VSC operates Flanders’ Tier-1 and Tier-2 HPC systems, supporting cutting-edge research in AI, machine learning (ML), and computational science.

instruments.name: Transversal Cloud Adoption Plan
instruments.summary: The Transversal Cloud Adoption Plan proposes a unified framework for adopting secure public cloud solutions across federal institutions. It includes capacity-building measures, governance structures, and guidelines for a consistent cloud policy to enhance efficiency and security in the public administration.

instruments.name: SolidLab Flanders
instruments.summary: SolidLab Flanders is a research initiative to advance the use of solid-based personal data vaults for privacy-preserving data management. It works together with Flemish and international data-initiatives to create applications built on the Solid standard.

instruments.name: Wizards (Teachers Lead Tech)
instruments.summary: This programme helps all computer science teachers in grades 1-4 and 5-8 to creatively integrate computer science into their lessons.

instruments.name: National Strategy for Quantum Technology
instruments.summary: In 2022, the Danish Agency for Higher Education and Science published a research mapping on the quantum field. This shows that Danish quantum research is considered to be world-class in a number of fields and enjoys great international recognition. Over the last ten years, the activities of the Danish research institutions within the quantum area have been on the rise. New research groups have been established, and we have succeeded in recruiting several international top researchers.

instruments.name: National Plan on Vulnerable Collectives
instruments.summary: The Spanish government is working towards the development of a National Plan on Vulnerable Collectives. A study on the impact of AI use on vulnerable collectives was expected to be conducted in Q4 2024.

instruments.name: GovCloud
instruments.summary: Cloud service for governmental bodies hosted by the Danish Agency for Governmental IT Services (SIT) on the platform https://www.dmi.dk/frie-data, which is delivered as community cloud for SIT customers and offers data hosting on Danish territory. Used for distributing open meteorological data and for the National Data Portal among others.

instruments.name: School of Computational Thinking and Artificial Intelligence (EPCIA)
instruments.summary: The School of Computational Thinking and AI is an experimental project developed aimed at exploring the possibilities of introducing computational thinking and AI for learning in the classroom. To this end, educational and training resources are created, classroom practices are carried out with students and impact research is developed. Resource on AI in education has also been developed.

instruments.name: State programme for developing, attracting and retaining talent – specific call on AI
instruments.summary: Within the general objective of promoting the consolidation of the professional career of researchers in any thematic area, this call specifically promotes the consolidation of people whose field of research is framed within a strategic theme related to either AI or microelectronics and semiconductors.

instruments.name: Programme for the development of AI skills
instruments.summary: A specific programme for the development of AI skills (under development at the time of writing) will be launched as part of the national plan for digital competency enhancement (Plan Nacional de Competencias Digitales).

instruments.name: Data strategy for local governments
instruments.summary: Since 2001, Denmark's central, regional, and local governments have jointly developed digital strategies, forming the foundation for a future-ready public sector through multi-year agreements on digital direction. In 2022, the association of Danish municipalities published its data strategy for local governments (KL), which notably calls upon municipalities to make standardised data available.

instruments.name: Forma Program for Artificial Intelligence
instruments.summary: The programme will finance up to 80% of the enrollment fee of nearly 8,000 young people studying AI in Spanish universities, both public and private.

instruments.name: Digital for Care: Digital Health Framework 2024-2030
instruments.summary: This framework has been developed to reflect recently established six HSE health regions in Ireland. The mission of the framework is to harness the power of new technologies, digital and data to transform how health and social care services are delivered for its population.

instruments.name: Autonomous mobility projects PRISSMA Project - Research and Investment Platform for the Safety and Security of Autonomous Mobility
instruments.summary: The PRISSMA Project develops a platform for the safety and security of autonomous mobility. It focuses on validating automated road transport systems, including AI components, to ensure safe operation. The project is part of an AI Challenge organised by the Innovation and Industry Fund.

instruments.name: Future Mobility Finland
instruments.summary: Future Mobility Finland is a national initiative that supports sustainable and innovative transport solutions. It promotes the use of AI technologies across public transport, private vehicles, and logistics. The initiative fosters collaboration and knowledge sharing to accelerate the transition to smarter, greener mobility.

instruments.name: Legislative amendments for road transport automation
instruments.summary: The Ministry of Transport and Communications in Finland is preparing legislative changes to enable road transport automation. A public consultation on the proposed amendments was held until 17 May 2024. The ministry aims to submit the government proposal to Parliament in autumn 2025.

instruments.name: Hybrid Cloud Enabling Infrastructure
instruments.summary: Platform providing government entities with suitable data hosting options.

instruments.name: Silicon Economy Ecosystem
instruments.summary: The Silicon Economy Ecosystem project helps logistics companies of all sizes use AI-based tools to automate supply chain processes. It provides open-source data models, interfaces, and software/hardware components free of charge. The initiative aims to increase efficiency and innovation in the logistics sector.

instruments.name: AIAMO Mobility Data Hub & Services
instruments.summary: The AIAMO initiative develops a data-sovereign platform for mobility services to support SMEs and smaller cities. It uses AI applications to simplify data collection and provide insights for environmentally friendly and multimodal traffic management. The project aims to improve reliable mobility options while prioritising climate protection.

instruments.name: AI applications in mobility and logistics
instruments.summary: The AI applications in mobility and logistics initiative in Germany supports the use of AI for analysis, forecasting, and information systems. It aims to improve safety, efficiency, sustainability, and convenience in transport and logistics. The programme also promotes transferable AI concepts that can be applied across the sector.

instruments.name: nxtAIM
instruments.summary: Funded by the Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Climate Action (BMWK), this joint project develops and trains generative AI methods for autonomous driving. It seeks to remove barriers to the deployment of automated and autonomous vehicles. For the first time, participating companies are sharing proprietary datasets to jointly train foundation models.

instruments.name: Mobility Innovation Hub
instruments.summary: The Mobility Innovation Hub in Czechia is part of the National Technology Incubation framework. It connects start-ups, businesses, and research institutions to develop sustainable mobility and transportation technologies. The Hub accelerates innovation in urban transport, electrification, autonomous vehicles, and smart mobility.

instruments.name: TRANSPORT 2030
instruments.summary: The TRANSPORT 2030 programme supports applied research and innovation in the transport sector in the Czech Republic. It emphasises AI, automation, digitalisation, and advanced transport technologies across all modes of transport. The programme brings together research organisations, private companies, and public entities to develop next-generation transport solutions.

instruments.name: Ethics Commission for the Assessment of Automated and Autonomous Vehicles
instruments.summary: The Ethics Commission for the Assessment of Automated and Autonomous Vehicles provides guidance on the ethical aspects of researching, testing, and deploying automated mobility, including AI-related systems. Established in 2020, it issues guidelines to ensure autonomous vehicle development follows ethical standards.

instruments.name: Public Administration Data Strategy
instruments.summary: The Public Administration Data Strategy 2023–2027 is a cornerstone of Malta’s digital transformation in public administration, both from a technological and a governance standpoint.

instruments.name: Training scholarships
instruments.summary: The program grants 374 training scholarships lasting four years in the field of AI and related areas such as massive data and information processing technologies; high performance computing; cloud computing; cybersecurity; biotech, medical devices, medical imaging; robotics or quantum technologies.

instruments.name: Danish Data Portal
instruments.summary: www.datavejviser.dk aims at enabling access to available data from the public sector and engaging in dialogue with users on their demand for further access to data so that future investments in quality and availability of public sector data is demand-driven.

instruments.name: Training of Professional and Managerial Staff in Education
instruments.summary: The Ministry of Education launched a public call for training of professional and managerial staff in education to strengthen competences for sustainable development and financial literacy as well as digital competences, which includes the field of AI.

instruments.name: Digital Transformation of Education EdTech
instruments.summary: This initiative promotes the use of state-of-the-art educational technologies in the education sector by training teachers and supporting digital content and solutions for teaching methods, through an educational technology testing platform (testbed).

instruments.name: Smart Data Sciences Market Consultation
instruments.summary: The Smart Data Sciences Market Consultation, conducted by FPS Policy and Support from 2022 to 2023, aimed to create intelligent data services by maximizing the re-use of government data.

instruments.name: Requalification of Women in ICT Professions
instruments.summary: As part of the National Strategic Plan for the Digital Decade, the Ministry of Digital Transformation has launched an initiative aimed at requalifying women over the age of 18 in the field of information and communication technologies (ICT).

instruments.name: Skills for entrepreneurs
instruments.summary: This initiative provides training for micro, small, medium, and large enterprises to help businesses acquire digital transformation competencies.

instruments.name: Smals
instruments.summary: Smals provides advanced IT and data centre solutions tailored to the needs of government, social, and healthcare organizations.

instruments.name: Improving access to data (strategy for digitalisation)
instruments.summary: One of the key areas covered by the national strategy for digitalisation, "A strong, ethical, and responsible digital foundation", includes the objective of improving access to data.

instruments.name: Research on artificial intelligence systems and discrimination aspects
instruments.summary: This research study examines the risks of AI-related discrimination and the adequacy of Latvia’s legal and regulatory framework in addressing algorithmic bias.

instruments.name: Imec’s Participation in PREVAIL
instruments.summary: Imec’s involvement in the PREVAIL project facilitates the development of AI hardware through a multi-hub European network.

instruments.name: Latvian Employers for Green and Digital Transition
instruments.summary: This initiative, implemented by the Employers' Confederation of Latvia (LDDK) in collaboration with BusinessEurope, supports businesses in adapting to digitalisation and the green transition.

instruments.name: Baltic first AI Hackathon
instruments.summary: This hackathon brought together students from various fields to work on generative AI solutions aimed at addressing challenges in education, social inclusion, sustainability, and public services.

instruments.name: Reform of Higher Education for a Green and Resilient Transition to Society 5.0
instruments.summary: This reform supports the digital transformation of education by improving digital skills and teaching practices in higher education. It includes pilot projects in AI, cybersecurity, and other advanced technologies, as well as training for educators. It also introduces micro-credentials to quickly meet changing skill needs.

instruments.name: HPC “Lucia”
instruments.summary: "Lucia" is a state-of-the-art supercomputing facility in Wallonia designed to meet the region's research and innovation needs. It includes advanced GPU nodes for AI applications and supports academic research and business projects in areas such as energy, health, and advanced manufacturing.

instruments.name: HPC “CÉCI”
instruments.summary: “CÉCI” is a Tier-2 supercomputing initiative integrating multiple smaller clusters to support advanced computational research.

instruments.name: AI-related training courses in the State Employment Agency’s Reskilling and Upskilling training programmes
instruments.summary: This initiative provides AI-related training courses as part of Latvia’s broader reskilling and upskilling efforts. Training options include online courses via Google AI Basics, ICT training programmes based on DigComp Level 4, and short AI-focused courses ranging from 8 to 80 hours. The programme targets unemployed individuals, job seekers, and people at risk of unemployment, aiming to improve their employability through the development of digital and AI skills.

instruments.name: Flemish Data Strategy
instruments.summary: The Flemish Data Strategy aims to transform governance by fostering collaboration between local and regional authorities to enable data-driven decision-making.

instruments.name: Federal Data Strategy
instruments.summary: The Federal Data Strategy, coordinated by FPS Economy, focuses on creating a robust data ecosystem across sectors such as mobility, energy, manufacturing, and health.

instruments.name: EuroCC Belgium
instruments.summary: EuroCC Belgium serves as the National Competence Centre for HPC, high-performance data analytics (HPDA), and AI.

instruments.name: Cloud Strategy for the Flemish Administration
instruments.summary: The Cloud Strategy for the Flemish Administration provides a phased roadmap to modernise public ICT infrastructure by adopting a “public cloud first” approach.

instruments.name: Belgium’s Participation in EuroHPC Joint Undertaking
instruments.summary: Belgium is participating in the EuroHPC Joint Undertaking, which aims to develop world-class HPC infrastructure across Europe.

instruments.name: Athumi
instruments.summary: The three agencies Austria Wirtschaftsservice GmbH (aws), the Aus-trian Research Promotion Agency (FFG) and the Austrian Science Fund (FWF) offer funding for basic research, applied research and its entrepreneurial implementation under the title ‘AI Mission Austria’ (AIM AT).

instruments.name: AI-Empowered Teaching: Unlocking the Future of Digital Education for Teachers (AI-EmpaTe)
instruments.summary: This international project aims to enhance the AI-related competencies of educators by developing online training modules tailored for teacher education students and professional development programmes for primary and secondary school teachers.

instruments.name: AI in social sciences
instruments.summary: This study course is designed for educators and aims to introduce them to the fundamentals of AI and its applications in the fields of humanities and education.

instruments.name: National Data Strategy
instruments.summary: Austria has published its first national data strategy in October 2024 (Federal Chancellery of Austria, 2024).

instruments.name: Pumice
instruments.summary: The Ministry of Digital Transformation co-funds the project, the goal of which it is to develop educational content and examples of AI’s use in various subjects and activities in primary and secondary schools, with a focus on practical demonstrations of AI’s usefulness in teaching subject content, e.g. Slovenian language, history, chemistry, biology, art.

instruments.name: Data Intelligence Offensive
instruments.summary: The Data Intelligence Offensive (DIO) aims to advance and promote business models for data exchange and monetisation, adhering to the highest ethical and legal standards.

instruments.name: Training for children and young people to strengthen digital competences and to promote natural sciences and technical professions
instruments.summary: The Ministry of Digital Transformation co-funds training for children and young people to strengthen digital competences and encourage and promote science and technology careers. The 2023-2024 project included AI content in part B: Advanced digital technologies. A further public call was launched in Q3 2024 with a special lot dedicated to AI.

instruments.name: Digital Competences and Basic Knowledge of Computer and Information Science
instruments.summary: The Ministry of Education has run two public tenders to carry out experimental projects for the development and verification of digital competences and basic knowledge of computer and information science in innovative departments or groups at educational institutions.

instruments.name: INNOAIR
instruments.summary: The INNOAIR Project in Sofia, Bulgaria, uses AI and sustainable transport solutions to improve urban mobility and cut air pollution. Supported by the Urban Innovative Actions programme, it optimises public transport routes based on real-time demand. Key innovations include an on-demand electric minibus service connecting underserved areas to Sofia’s metro system.

instruments.name: CitCom.ai TEF
instruments.summary: CitCom.ai is an EU test and experimentation facility that provides both physical and virtual environments where AI and robotics solutions can be validated under real smart-city conditions. It helps innovators with services like algorithm validation, ethics and compliance guidance, and impact assessment. The goal is to support the creation and deployment of AI solutions that are safe, effective, and aligned with regulations.

instruments.name: Using generative artificial intelligence for and in education
instruments.summary: The Ministry of Education has published this public call for proposals with regard to the use of generative artificial intelligence for and in education, including content development for primary and secondary school, in line with the with the Recovery and Resilience Plan (RRP) within the development area of Smart, Sustainable and Inclusive Growth.

instruments.name: NAVAJO
instruments.summary: The NAVAJO pilot project introduces an autonomous shuttle service in Ottignies-Louvain-la-Neuve, Belgium. It tests and validates autonomous transport technologies for use in urban mobility systems. The project is financed through Digital Wallonia’s “Intelligent Territories” call for projects to support smart mobility solutions.

instruments.name: Flemish Task Force on Automated Driving
instruments.summary: A task force initiated by the Flemish Departments of Economy, Science, and Innovation (EWI) and Mobility connects research, innovation, and mobility stakeholders. It aims to build an ecosystem for shared automated road mobility and speed up the development of autonomous driving technologies in Flanders.

instruments.name: Proloog Mobilidata 2
instruments.summary: The Proloog Mobilidata 2 programme supports development of mobility technologies including remote driving. In spring 2024, it held a “Remote Driving Test Week” to evaluate safety, efficiency, and real-world feasibility. The initiative is designed to test advanced vehicle operation under actual conditions.

instruments.name: Austrian Scientific Computing (previously Vienna Scientific Cluster)
instruments.summary: The Vienna Scientific Cluster (VSC) is a collaboration of several Austrian universities that provides supercomputer resources and technical support to their users. The current flagship systems of the VSC family are VSC-4 and VSC-5, currently the fastest supercomputers in Austria. Both systems are powering science and research at the leading academic institutions in Austria and fulfil the demand for high computing power in the areas such as physics, chemistry, meteorology and life sciences.

instruments.name: AI-specific programmes
instruments.summary: Twenty-two degree programmes in artificial intelligence are now offered at six Slovak universities. These programmes benefit students interested in studying AI and related fields. The initiative addresses growing demand for AI skills in education and the tech job market.

instruments.name: Quantum Austria
instruments.summary: On behalf of the Federal Ministry of Education, Science and Research (BMBWF) and funded by the European Union under the Development and Resilience Plan (2020-2026), the Austrian Research Promotion Agency (FFG) and the Austrian Science Fund (FWF) are implementing the Quan-tum Austria Funding Initiative. Part of the funding is provided for research infrastructure in the fields of next generation HPC, quantum computing as well as their interconnection.

instruments.name: DiTEdu
instruments.summary: The goal of the national project “Support for the Digital Transformation of Education” (DiTEdu) is to create innovative teaching methodologies for preschools, primary schools, and secondary schools that will reflect the latest trends in digitalisation.

instruments.name: "AI Essentials" courses for women
instruments.summary: This beginner-friendly course, developed by Google.org and implemented by Riga TechGirls, aims to help women harness AI to enhance productivity and efficiency in their daily tasks. The course provides practical AI tools and knowledge, enabling participants to integrate AI into their professional and personal activities.

instruments.name: The swedish Digitalisation Strategy 2025–2030
instruments.summary: AI is part of the cross-cutting themes throughout the entire strategy and are integrated across all five strategic areas - digital skills, private sector, public administration, public welfare, and connectivity.

instruments.name: National IT Academy project on the creation of study materials for new and innovative subjects in the field of artificial intelligence
instruments.summary: A project of the National IT Academy has focused on creating study materials for new and innovative subjects in the field of artificial intelligence at higher education institutions. These subjects included topics such as introduction to neural networks, neural networks, artificial intelligence, and programming languages for artificial intelligence.

instruments.name: National Funding Call “Mobility Transition 2024/1 – Mobility Technologies and Components”
instruments.summary: The AI for Mobility Technologies funding initiative supports the development of AI-driven solutions for sustainable mobility. It focuses on projects that help avoid, shift, and reduce environmental impact in transport. The programme encourages innovation that contributes to the mobility transition in line with national climate and environmental goals.

instruments.name: Mistra Digital Forest
instruments.summary: Mistra Digital Forest is a research programme that uses digital technologies to support sustainable forestry. It develops digital tools and automation techniques to make use of large amounts of forestry data. The initiative aims to improve decision-making and sustainability in the forestry sector.

instruments.name: Testbed Digitalized Agriculture
instruments.summary: The RISE Test Bed for Digitised Agriculture allows companies and researchers to develop new technologies and data-driven innovations for agriculture. It focuses on making farming more sustainable, climate-smart, and profitable. The test bed supports collaboration and experimentation in real-world agricultural environments.

instruments.name: The Knowledge Hub for the Digitalization of Agriculture
instruments.summary: The National Knowledge Hub for Digitisation in Agriculture in Sweden helps the agricultural sector understand and use digital technologies. It collects, refines, and shares knowledge to support modern farming practices. The hub is led by Linköping University on behalf of the Swedish Board of Agriculture.

instruments.name: Agrifood TEF
instruments.summary: The Agrifood TEF initiative in Spain promotes innovation in AI and robotics for the agri-food sector. It supports the development and adoption of smart technologies to improve efficiency and productivity. The programme fosters collaboration between research centres, companies, and technology providers.

instruments.name: Technological and Territorial Network Project for forest monitoring and reduction of environmental disasters as levers for the development of the forest bioeconomy (RetechFOR)
instruments.summary: The RetechFOR project is a regional consortium in Spain that applies AI to forest monitoring and disaster reduction. It aims to support the sustainable management and development of the forest bioeconomy. The initiative helps prevent environmental disasters while promoting the productive use of forest resources.

instruments.name: Cross-cutting platform of artificial intelligence applied to the agri-food sector
instruments.summary: The Proyecto PAN in Spain is a platform that applies artificial intelligence (AI) to the agri-food sector. It supports the adoption of disruptive technologies to improve productivity and innovation. The initiative encourages collaboration across regions and stakeholders in the sector.

instruments.name: AgrarIA: AI applied to the value chain ​​of agricultural production 2050
instruments.summary: This project explores the use of AI and other technologies to develop new agricultural production methods. It investigates solutions such as natural pest control, collaborative robotics, quantum computing, and digital twins. The goal is to make agricultural production more efficient, sustainable, and innovative.

instruments.name: Strategic plan for the common agricultural policy for the 2023–2027 period
instruments.summary: Slovenia’s Strategic Plan for the Common Agricultural Policy 2023–2027 supports the use of AI and digital technologies in agriculture. It funds modern machinery, IT solutions, and precision farming practices, especially in fruit and vegetable production. The initiative aims to increase efficiency, productivity, and innovation in the agricultural sector.

instruments.name: e-Farming, Food and Forestry Project under RRF
instruments.summary: The Slovenia e-Farming, Food and Forestry Project is a digitalisation initiative under the Recovery and Resilience Plan (RRF). It aims to modernise agriculture, food, and forestry sectors through technology and digital solutions. The project includes the establishment of the National Food Institute to support research and innovation.

instruments.name: Component 7, Reform 1 of the curriculum reform of the Slovak education system
instruments.summary: The Slovak education system is preparing to improve skills related to AI, primarily through curriculum reform and textbook reform for primary and secondary education as well as vocational training. These topics are included in the areas of computer literacy, digital society, media literacy skills, and exploration of traditional and modern technical environments.

instruments.name: BrAIn - BRinging Artificial INtelligence towards SMEs
instruments.summary: The BrAIn – Bringing Artificial Intelligence towards SMEs project is part of the Interreg DANUBE transnational programme. It aims to boost the competitiveness of SMEs in the Danube Region by transferring AI knowledge and technologies to sectors such as manufacturing, agri-food, and healthcare. In Slovenia, the ITC – Innovation Technology Cluster manages activities related to the agri-food area.

instruments.name: Area Monitoring System (AMS)
instruments.summary: The Area Monitoring System (AMS) uses satellite images and machine learning algorithms to track and assess agricultural land in Slovenia. Managed by the Agency for Agricultural Markets and Rural Development, it provides up-to-date information on land use and conditions. In 2024, the Ministry of Agriculture launched a project group to explore further digitisation and AI applications in agriculture.

instruments.name: Green.Dat.AI
