instruments.summary: GREEN.DAT.AI is a Horizon Europe project that develops energy-efficient, large-scale data analytics services for use in industrial AI systems. It aims to reduce the environmental impact of data management while demonstrating new analytics services in sectors such as energy, agriculture, mobility, and banking. In Slovenia, the Innovation Technology Cluster (ITC) coordinates pilots on smart farming and smart water management.

instruments.name: Smart Specialization Technologies for Agro-ecology and Forestry (PNRR) in the context of the National Forest Strategy 2030
instruments.summary: The National Forest Strategy 2030 in Romania supports the creation of innovation and technology centres in the smart specialisation area of agro-ecology and forestry. Its main investment is the development of an integrated IT system to monitor forest integrity, wood transport, and biodiversity. This system will also connect to SUMAL 2.0, Romania’s new wood traceability system.

instruments.name: Agriculture and Rural Development - ADER 2026
instruments.summary: The Sectoral Plan for Research and Development in Agriculture and Rural Development 2023–2026 (ADER 2026) funds projects to build a smart, resilient, and diversified agricultural sector. It supports research on climate change adaptation, natural resource management, biodiversity conservation, innovative technologies, and digitalisation in agriculture and forestry.

instruments.name: Adoption and Exploitation of AI in Agriculture
instruments.summary: The Adoption and Exploitation of AI in Agriculture programme supports the use of AI-driven automation in agriculture and industry. It funds R&D projects, including EU-supported initiatives, to promote digitalisation in agriculture and food sectors. The initiative aims to increase efficiency and innovation in farming and agri-food operations

instruments.name: Data-Driven Agriculture course
instruments.summary: The Data-Driven Agriculture course helps agricultural companies adopt digital and precision agriculture techniques. It teaches skills in data collection, governance, analysis, and technological solutions. The course is a collaboration between CAP and NOVA IMS, supporting the digital transformation of the agricultural sector.

instruments.name: AGRISPACE
instruments.summary: The Portuguese AGRIculture Data SPACE consortium was created to support the digitalisation of agriculture in Portugal. It focuses on developing a Data Space to collect, manage, and share agricultural data. The initiative helps improve efficiency, decision-making, and innovation in the agricultural sector

instruments.name: Action Plan for the Sustainable Bioeconomy
instruments.summary: The Portuguese Action Plan for the Circular Bio-economy promotes the transition of the economy toward sustainable and circular practices. It uses advanced technologies, including AI, robotics, and big data, in sectors like agriculture and forestry. The plan supports innovation and resource-efficient growth.

instruments.name: Clean Forest Project
instruments.summary: The Forest Fire Protection AI Project uses AI and augmented reality to monitor forest fire protection zones. It aims to reduce the risk and impact of forest fires. The project combines automatic and participatory surveillance for more effective forest safety.

instruments.name: COMPETE 2030 Program
instruments.summary: The programme provides funding for research and innovation projects in agriculture, including the development of AI solutions. Projects focus on areas such as precision agriculture and data analytics to improve productivity and decision-making. It supports collaboration between researchers, companies, and other stakeholders in the agricultural sector.

instruments.name: Agricultural scenario-pilot to develop AI models2-
instruments.summary: The AI4EOSC project expands the European Open Science Cloud (EOSC) to include AI, machine learning, and deep learning services. It develops AI models for agriculture, helping to assess crop disease and pest risks and track plant growth. The initiative supports data-driven decision-making in the agricultural sector.

instruments.name: Satellite Crop Monitoring System
instruments.summary: The S2MUR project provides detailed monitoring of agricultural crops and forecasts adverse weather events that may cause crop losses. It generates maps and reports to estimate crop damage and support decision-making. The project uses satellite, meteorological, soil, and statistical data, combined with machine learning models, to improve agricultural risk management.

instruments.name: NXTGEN High-Tech – Agri-Food
instruments.summary: NXTGEN develops autonomous agricultural machinery and smart production lines to improve efficiency and safety in the agrifood sector. It uses AI, robotics, and automation to reduce waste and optimise resource use. The initiative promotes collaboration between technology experts and the farming industry.

instruments.name: National Living Lab for Precision Agriculture (NPPL)
instruments.summary: The National Precision and Productivity Lab (NPPL) helps farmers use precision farming techniques, including AI-driven tools for crop monitoring and irrigation. By leveraging open weather and soil data, it promotes sustainable agriculture. The initiative also provides insights that support policy development.

instruments.name: Knowledge and Innovation Agenda for Agriculture, Water and Food (KIA LWV)
instruments.summary: The KIA LWV programme develops key technologies, including AI, for the agriculture, horticulture, and water sectors. It aims to make systems more efficient, intelligent, and environmentally friendly. The programme uses tools such as sensors, robots, and digital twins to support sustainability goals.

instruments.name: AI in Animal and Terrestrial systems - WUR
instruments.summary: This initiative applies AI in agriculture to improve sustainability and efficiency. It includes projects that enhance livestock management and land-use optimisation. The research supports farmers and agricultural stakeholders in making data-driven decisions.

instruments.name: Action Program Digitalisation (ADP)
instruments.summary: The Action Program Digitalisation (APD) supports the digital transformation of agriculture in the Netherlands. It funds training and the development of AI systems for smart farming, autonomous greenhouses, and precision agriculture. The programme helps make food production more efficient and sustainable.

instruments.name: Fruit and vegetable price monitoring and forecasting
instruments.summary: The Malta Food Agency is developing a project to monitor and forecast fruit and vegetable prices. The initiative uses AI and advanced technologies to analyse market data and predict price trends. This will help stakeholders make better decisions in the food supply chain.

instruments.name: Agricultural Research and Innovation Hub (AgriHub)
instruments.summary: The AgriHub brings together researchers, innovators, and farmers to improve farming practices in Malta. It focuses on developing the country’s first Integrated Pest Management programmes for key crops. AI-enabled monitoring systems and remote data collection support more efficient and sustainable pest management.

instruments.name: Méi Weed
instruments.summary: The Méi Weed initiative adapts a grass growth prediction model to Luxembourg’s soil and climate conditions. Delivered through a digital tool, it helps farmers manage pastures more effectively, respond to climate change, and improve both economic efficiency and sustainability.

instruments.name: AI Excellence Centres
instruments.summary: Italy has created several centres of excellence to advance AI research and applications. These include the Italian Institute of Artificial Intelligence for Industry (AI4I) in Turin, the ELLIS Unit in Milan, and the Alma Mater Research Institute for Human-Centred AI in Bologna. Together they strengthen AI innovation, fundamental research, and human-centred applications.

instruments.name: AI-related university courses
instruments.summary: Under Italy’s AI Strategy 2024-2026, Italian universities are expanding their AI research and teaching capacities. Over 53 universities now offer more than 160 AI-related courses, equipping students with essential AI skills.

instruments.name: AI in Primary and Secondary school
instruments.summary: As part of Italy’s AI Strategy 2024–2026, the Ministry of Education has launched the “AI in Primary and Secondary Education” initiative. Starting in 2024–2025, 15 schools across Calabria, Lazio, Tuscany, and Lombardy will pilot AI-integrated lessons. The programme aims to give students foundational digital and AI skills and help teachers deliver personalised learning experiences.

instruments.name: SOLAS Skills to Advance and eCollege ICT Development Pathways
instruments.summary: SOLAS, the Irish state agency for further education and training, is developing a suite of digital upskilling micro-qualifications such as Introduction to AI, Cloud Computing, and Big Data. Its eCollege platform offers self-paced, tutor-supported online courses in Digital Skills and ICT.

instruments.name: Skillnet Ireland
instruments.summary: Skillnet Ireland Business Networks provides digital skills programmes to support SMEs and develop specialised talent in new and emerging technologies. Several networks focus on AI training, including Technology Ireland ICT Skillnet and Tech Industry Alliance Skillnet. New academic programmes in AI, such as MSc and PhD degrees, further strengthen Ireland’s AI talent pipeline.

instruments.name: Human Capital Initiative (HCI) and Springboard+
instruments.summary: The Springboard+ and Human Capital Initiative (HCI) programmes in Ireland provide AI-focused training courses to support reskilling and upskilling. In 2023–2024, these initiatives offered courses in AI, including AI in Medicine, with several hundred training places available. These programmes help workers gain skills for AI-related roles.

instruments.name: AI and academic integrity guidelines
instruments.summary: The National Academic Integrity Network provides guidance for educators on the use of generative AI in education. It also offers resources for handling academic misconduct cases. The initiative helps ensure ethical and responsible use of AI in academic settings.

instruments.name: AI in Schools (various initiatives)
instruments.summary: Ireland participated in the AI4T Erasmus+ project to explore the use of AI in education and generate practical policy recommendations. Oide Technology in Education provides an AI Hub with resources, a one-hour online course, and guidance for teachers and school leaders. Post-primary teachers engaged in workshops and pilots to develop practical AI use cases in schools.

instruments.name: Digital Culture Curriculum
instruments.summary: The Digital Culture Curriculum in Hungary introduces students in grades five and eleven to the foundational concepts of AI. It builds a basic understanding of the technology from an early age. Teacher training programmes support this effort by equipping educators with the skills to effectively deliver AI education.

instruments.name: AI Challenge
instruments.summary: The Hungary AI Challenge is an introductory programme to raise awareness and understanding of AI. It is part of Hungary’s National AI Strategy. The programme aims to engage citizens, students, and professionals in learning about AI concepts and applications.

instruments.name: ReGeneration Initiative
instruments.summary: Under the Hellenic Ministry of Digital Government, Microsoft and ReGeneration run Greece’s largest programme to upskill young people in digital and soft skills. The initiative, “The ReGeneration Initiative: Upskilling Greek Youth for the Digital Era powered by Microsoft,” offers extensive training in AI and other emerging technologies. Its goal is to prepare young people for modern job market demands.

instruments.name: Pioneers in AI
instruments.summary: The project “Students of Natural Sciences: Pioneers in Artificial Intelligence” offers an online AI course designed for science students. Developed under the “Science For You – SciFy” initiative with support from the Education Office of NCSR “Demokritos”, it includes videos, exercises, and other interactive materials to make AI learning accessible.

instruments.name: Panhellenic Educational Robotics Competition
instruments.summary: The National Competition on Educational Robotics introduces robotics and STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics) into the official school system. It helps students develop 21st-century skills and promotes STEM as a core teaching methodology in compulsory education.

instruments.name: Supply of robotics and STEM equipment for education
instruments.summary: This programme funds the provision of robotics kits to primary and secondary schools across the country. Each kit combines building blocks and software so students can both construct and program their own projects. It aims to promote STEM learning and digital skills from an early age.

instruments.name: National Artificial Intelligence Competition (NAIC)
instruments.summary: The ARCHIMEDES Unit of the Athena Research Center, together with key Greek AI and education organisations, organises the National Artificial Intelligence Competition (NAIC) for middle and high school students. The competition introduces students to AI techniques such as machine learning, computer vision and natural language processing. Winners represent Greece at the International Olympiad in Artificial Intelligence.

instruments.name: A central AI Educational Platform
instruments.summary: This flagship project under the Blueprint for Greece’s AI Transformation aims to create a shared virtual space where AI experts from academia and industry can develop educational material. Its goal is to build a dynamic and sustainable ecosystem for AI education in Greece.

instruments.name: A world-class AI Research and Educational Institute
instruments.summary: Under Greece’s Blueprint for AI Transformation, a flagship project plans to create a new graduate school and research centre focused on artificial intelligence. The centre will conduct research and deliver training programmes to build national AI capacity.

instruments.name: Konrad Zuse Schools of Excellence in AI
instruments.summary: The Konrad Zuse Schools of Excellence in AI in Germany attract international master’s and PhD students to high-quality English-language programmes. They combine teaching and research with close links to industry, connecting top scientists and industry fellows. The initiative is funded by the German Federal Ministry of Education and Research (BMBF) through the German Academic Exchange Service (DAAD).

instruments.name: Funding Programme  for Female AI Junior Scientisits
instruments.summary: The Federal Ministry of Education and Research (BMBF) in Germany funds a programme to support female-led junior research groups in AI. It aims to increase the share of qualified women in leadership positions within German AI research. The programme also considers family–work balance in its funding criteria.

instruments.name: Digital Pact for Schools
instruments.summary: The Digital Pact for Schools supports Germany’s federal states in integrating AI technologies into education. It funds digital learning materials, adaptive learning systems, and student support to strengthen digital and AI-related skills. The initiative invests EUR 92 million in AI-related educational media infrastructure across nine cross-state projects.

instruments.name: Competence Centres for Digital and Digitally Supported Teaching in Schools and Continuing Education
instruments.summary: The Federal Ministry of Education and Research (BMBF) in Germany funds centres to improve digitalisation-related teacher training. These centres support research, innovation, and knowledge transfer until 2026. AI-supported systems are used to enhance teaching practices in schools.

instruments.name: Choose France programme
instruments.summary: The ChooseFrance talent programme is designed to attract and support international AI professionals in France. It is led by the IA Cluster initiative and the National Research Programme on Artificial Intelligence (PEPR IA). The programme helps connect talent with research and industry opportunities in AI across the country.

instruments.name: LaborIA
instruments.summary: LaborIA is responsible for analysing and addressing reskilling needs arising from AI developments. It helps workers and organisations adapt to changes in the labour market caused by AI. Other initiatives, such as IA Clusters and AMI CMA projects, also support continuing education and reskilling.

instruments.name: Promotion of inclusion and diversity in AI ecosystems
instruments.summary: The “Women in AI” and “Inclusive AI” initiatives in France aim to promote diversity in AI education and careers. They support women and underrepresented groups in entering and thriving in the AI sector. Additional projects, such as TechPourToutes, are being developed to further strengthen inclusion in AI.

instruments.name: Call for expressions of interest for Skills and professions of the future
instruments.summary: The AMI-CMA programme in France supports the development of digital and AI training curricula across all education levels, from secondary school to PhD. It aims to train 400,000 individuals per year by 2030 and adapt curricula to the evolving professional use of digital tools. Selected projects, such as MACMIA and AISorb, create specialised training to enhance employability in AI-related fields.

instruments.name: Attracting and retaining AI-related talent
instruments.summary: The Ministry of Education and Culture in Finland provides funding to universities to pilot new practices in doctoral education, including support for 1,000 doctoral researchers. The Finnish Doctoral Programme Network in AI is among the recipients. The Work in Finland programme helps Finnish companies, including AI firms, attract and retain international talent.

instruments.name: Re- and up-skilling initiatives
instruments.summary: The digital service bundle for continuous learning and the Digivisio 2030 programme provide online tools and courses to help individuals develop skills and make informed career choices. AI is used to personalise learning and support guidance in higher education and workforce development. The Service Centre for Continuous Learning and Employment (SECLE) connects labour market needs with training, helping SMEs and academic institutions strengthen AI skills.

instruments.name: Recommendations on AI in education, teaching and training
instruments.summary: Finland’s Ministry of Education and Culture and the National Agency for Education are developing recommendations on AI in education. The guidance aims to help teachers and learners use AI safely and responsibly. It also seeks to ensure that all students have equal opportunities to benefit from AI in learning.

instruments.name: “Digital problem solving” in Preparatory Adult Education (FVU)
instruments.summary: As of January 2024, the FVU (Preparatory Adult Education) programme in Denmark includes new learning objectives on digital problem solving. The curriculum introduces basic concepts of generative AI, its uses, limitations, and practical applications in everyday life. It helps adults develop digital skills relevant to employment, education, and personal life.

instruments.name: Strengthen and retain specialised IT talent and skills
instruments.summary: Denmark’s national IT education strategy aims to strengthen continuing and further education in IT, enhance professional Master’s programmes, and retain international students in the Danish job market to meet the growing demand for specialised IT competencies.

instruments.name: Compulsory training in digital skills across subjects (Act on Upper Secondary Education)
instruments.summary: The Act on Upper Secondary Education in Denmark mandates that students develop digital competencies across subjects, including AI-related skills, enabling them to critically assess digital content and participate effectively in digital communities.

instruments.name: Technology Comprehension in traditional subjects
instruments.summary: As part of a 2024 political agreement on quality in Danish primary and lower secondary education, Technology Comprehension will be integrated into traditional subjects. The goal is to ensure students can critically reflect on and competently use new digital technologies, with an expert group deciding the subjects and grade levels for implementation.

instruments.name: Recommendations on AI based tools for examinations in primary, lower and upper secondary school
instruments.summary: In 2023, the Ministry of Children and Education in Denmark established an expert group to issue recommendations on the use of AI-based tools in school examinations. Published in April 2024, the recommendations emphasise diverse testing methods and the need for students to use and critically reflect on digital tools, shaping the Ministry’s future policies in this area.

instruments.name: RRF 3.1 Innovation in education in the context of digitization
instruments.summary: The AIDIG project, implemented by the National Pedagogical Institute of the Czech Republic, helps schools integrate the European framework for teachers’ digital skills (DigCompEdu). Funded by the National Recovery Plan (NPO 3.1), it trains teachers in emerging technologies such as AI, cybersecurity, digital well-being, and media literacy to improve students’ digital competencies.

instruments.name: prg.ai Minor
instruments.summary: The prg.ai Minor is a specialised AI education programme created and managed by the NGO prg.ai in collaboration with Prague universities. It provides students from different disciplines with foundational AI knowledge and skills, combined with lectures and networking sessions with top technology companies, to help them apply AI across diverse fields.

instruments.name: Allowance for the payment of digital training courses
instruments.summary: As part of the Recovery and Resilience Facility (RRF), the Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs (MoLSA) provides financial support to individuals for enrolling in digital training courses, including AI-focused ones. The initiative covers up to 82% of course costs (up to about EUR 2,000 per person over three years), making digital upskilling more accessible through the “I’m in a Course” platform.

instruments.name: AI for Children
instruments.summary: The “AI for Children” initiative promotes the integration of AI concepts into primary and secondary education, providing teachers and schools with resources and guidance to help young learners develop digital literacy and a practical understanding of AI technologies.

instruments.name: “I’m in a Course” Initiative
instruments.summary: The online platform developed by the Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs (MoLSA) serves as a national gateway for retraining and further education opportunities, with a strong emphasis on digital skills including AI programming and usage.

instruments.name: HRDA AI courses
instruments.summary: The Human Resource Development Authority of Cyprus (HRDA) offers a range of training courses related to artificial intelligence, aimed at equipping the Cypriot workforce with the skills needed for a technology-driven economy.

instruments.name: Adult Education Act Implementation Programme
instruments.summary: The Ministry of Science and Education runs a programme to encourage unemployed persons’ inclusion in the labour market, with a strong focus on digital skills development and lifelong learning, as part of its active employment policy measures.

instruments.name: National Competence Centre for Semiconductors and Microelectronics
instruments.summary: The National Competence Centre acts as a one-stop-shop for research and development, prototyping, testing, and training in advanced semiconductor technologies, fostering innovation and skills development in a strategically important sector.

instruments.name: NRRP Labour Market and Social Protection Component
instruments.summary: The Ministry of Labour in Croatia offers a voucher scheme for digital skills improvement, including AI-related skills. The programme supports lifelong education, focusing on competencies needed for the green and digital transition.

instruments.name: Croatian Association for Artificial Intelligence (CroAI)
instruments.summary: CroAI is a business community initiative in Croatia bringing together over 300 members, including AI enterprises, start-ups, universities, and enthusiasts. It offers introductory AI courses and facilitates connections between leading companies and start-ups in the AI ecosystem.

instruments.name: University of Zagreb University Computing Centre (SRCE) ICT Education Programme
instruments.summary: The University Computing Centre (SRCE) at the University of Zagreb provides ICT training and educational activities for both the academic/research community and the general public. Courses are self-paced and integrated into the E-citizens portal, making digital education widely accessible across Croatia.

instruments.name: INSAIT Research Programmes
instruments.summary: The INSAIT Research Programmes at Sofia University advance research in computer science and AI, hosting over 20 international researchers. They provide competitive internships for students worldwide and focus on areas such as AI, machine learning, robotics, and computer vision.

instruments.name: Adult Learning Platform
instruments.summary: This comprehensive digital platform in Bulgaria aims to democratise access to digital and AI skills training. It aims to provide digital clubs and tailored support for disadvantaged groups, along with certification pathways to validate skills and enhance career opportunities in the digital sector.

instruments.name: Operation “New Skills”
instruments.summary: Operation "New Skills" is a Bulgarian training programme designed to enhance the competencies of 53,200 employees. It focuses on digital skills and other employer-requested competencies, helping workers improve employability and adaptability in a rapidly evolving job market.

instruments.name: Operation “Digital Skills”
instruments.summary: Operation "Digital Skills" is a Bulgarian training programme aimed at improving employability by equipping unemployed and inactive individuals with essential digital skills. The initiative seeks to reduce digital divides and prepare participants for the AI-driven economy.

instruments.name: GATE’s Internship Programme
instruments.summary: The GATE Centre of Excellence internship programme offers hands-on experience in Big Data and AI for students and young professionals. Interns work on interdisciplinary research projects, developing skills in data management, analytics, and visualisation under the guidance of experienced researchers.

instruments.name: International AI Olympiad
instruments.summary: An international AI competition for high school students, launched in 2024 in Bulgaria, brings together young talent to develop AI models and solutions. The inaugural event attracted over 200 participants from around 40 countries, fostering innovation and early engagement in AI education.

instruments.name: GATE Master’s Programme “Big Data Technologies”
instruments.summary: This advanced Master’s programme, jointly offered by GATE Institute and Sofia University’s Faculty of Mathematics and Informatics, provides specialised training in Big Data and AI applications. Launched in the 2023–2024 academic year, it prepares graduates for professional roles in data science and AI.

instruments.name: INSAIT Explorer Programme
instruments.summary: The INSAIT Explorer Programme is a fellowship initiative by INSAIT at Sofia University targeting talented high school students. It combines a four-year Bachelor’s degree with research opportunities in AI, machine learning, robotics, and quantum computing, aiming to cultivate Bulgaria’s top tech talent.

instruments.name: AI Programmer Vocational Education
instruments.summary: AI Programmer Vocational Education is a specialised vocational training programme that integrates the “Programmer with AI” profession into high school curricula. In the 2023/2024 academic year, it engaged 580 students across 13 schools, equipping them with practical AI programming skills and preparing them for careers in AI and technology.

instruments.name: Short-term Teacher Training Programme
instruments.summary: A specialised programme in partnership with “Prof. Asen Zlatarov” University in Bulgaria focuses on enhancing teachers’ digital competencies. It aims to train 225 teachers in the use of augmented and virtual reality (AR/VR) software for educational purposes, helping them create more engaging and interactive learning experiences.

instruments.name: AI Guidelines for Education System
instruments.summary: The Ministry of Education and Science of Bulgaria has released guidelines for the use of AI in schools. These guidelines are designed to help teachers, school administrators, and students integrate AI ethically and effectively into educational processes and programmes.

instruments.name: Women in Digital
instruments.summary: Belgium’s national and intersectoral strategy “Women in Digital 2021–2026” aims to increase women’s representation in the digital sector by tackling cultural and systemic barriers. Coordinated by the FPS Economy, the five-year plan sets out concrete actions to boost women’s participation and retention in digital education and careers, challenge stereotypes, and bridge the gender gap in specific target groups.

instruments.name: Women Award in Technology and Science
instruments.summary: This Innoviris initiative aims to inspire young women in Brussels to pursue STEM careers. Each year, a EUR 10 000 award is granted to a Science Ambassadress, who organises events and workshops to encourage girls and young women to engage with science and technology, addressing gender imbalances in the STEM field.

instruments.name: Technocité
instruments.summary: Technocité is a regional competence centre in Belgium offering training in ICT, creative, and cultural industries. It addresses digital skill gaps by providing tailored programmes for individuals and businesses, emphasising digital inclusion and equipping participants with the skills needed to thrive in a tech-driven economy.

instruments.name: Smart Education @ Schools
instruments.summary: An Imec-led initiative integrates digital tools and AI technologies into classroom settings to enhance learning. It provides funding and resources for innovative educational projects, helping schools incorporate smart technologies into their curricula.

instruments.name: Interface3
instruments.summary: Interface3 is a Belgian training centre that promotes digital inclusion, with a special focus on women. It offers comprehensive training programmes in ICT, including coding, digital tools, and technology careers, aiming to empower underrepresented groups and close the digital skills gap in the workforce.

instruments.name: Innoviris’ Funding Programmes on STEM
instruments.summary: Innoviris, the public research and innovation institute of the Brussels-Capital Region, funds and supports initiatives to spark interest in science, technology, and AI among youth and other groups. Programmes include coding training, interdisciplinary academies combining technology and art, and robotics competitions that cultivate digital and STEM skills.

instruments.name: InnoVET
instruments.summary: InnoVET is a programme supporting innovation in vocational education and training (VET). It equips learners with digital and technological skills aligned with labour market needs and fosters closer collaboration between education providers and industry.

instruments.name: e-cl@sses
instruments.summary: e-cl@sses is a Walloon initiative providing digital education resources for teachers and students. It offers interactive lessons, educational content, and tools for primary and secondary education, supporting digital literacy and the integration of AI in learning.

instruments.name: DigiSkills Platform
instruments.summary: DigiSkills Belgium is a national platform that promotes reskilling and upskilling in AI and digital competencies. It connects learners with training opportunities across sectors to help close skill gaps and enhance employability in AI-driven industries.

instruments.name: #BeDigitalTogether
instruments.summary: Belgium’s #BeDigitalTogether programme promotes inclusion and diversity in the digital sector, including AI. It seeks to reduce barriers for underrepresented groups and ensure equitable access to opportunities in technology careers.

instruments.name: Schoolpackage AI
instruments.summary: Schoolpackage AI is an Austrian government initiative aimed at enhancing AI knowledge in primary and secondary education. It targets both teachers and students, promoting the use of AI tools, including generative AI, through pilot programmes in selected schools.

instruments.name: National Competition for AI
instruments.summary: The Austrian National Competition for AI is a programme for students aged 14 to 19, encouraging them to explore and develop skills in artificial intelligence. The competition fosters young talent and innovation in AI, and its third edition was held in 2023.

instruments.name: AI Radar
instruments.summary: AI Radar is an Austrian project offering reskilling and upskilling programmes in AI for the tourism sector, mainly through online webinars and workshops. It tracks AI innovations, recognises trends, and helps tourism professionals strengthen their skills and develop prototypes.

instruments.name: European Digital Innovation Hubs (EDIHs)
instruments.summary: Sweden has co-financed four European Digital Innovation Hubs (EDIHs) approved by the European Commission and continues to support five additional hubs through the EC’s “Seal of Excellence”. The creation and operation of these hubs is a joint effort between Vinnova (the Swedish Innovation Agency) and Tillväxtverket (the Swedish Agency for Economic and Regional Growth).

instruments.name: Start your AI journey
instruments.summary: “Start Your AI Journey” is a Swedish initiative designed to help SMEs adopt artificial intelligence. Managed by Vinnova, it funded 51 small projects with grants of around EUR 43,000 (SEK 500,000) each to support companies in exploring and starting their AI transformation.

instruments.name: AI-specific research and innovation programme administered by Vinnova, Sweden’s innovation agency
instruments.summary: Since 2009, Vinnova—Sweden’s innovation agency—has supported over 800 AI-related projects. Its current programme, “Advanced digitalisation – future solutions in Swedish industry”, includes funding calls for start-ups and SMEs with AI-specific themes, such as “AI from research to innovation”, “AI in the service of the climate” and “AI for Advanced Digitalization”. Most of the funding has gone to SMEs as providers or users of AI solutions.

instruments.name: Edge Learning Lab of AI Sweden
instruments.summary: Sweden offers a broad network of test facilities for AI systems and applications, including dedicated environments specifically built for AI. One example is the Edge Learning Lab at AI Sweden, which allows researchers to explore decentralised and edge learning.

instruments.name: Wallenberg AI, Autonomous Systems and Software Program
instruments.summary: The Wallenberg AI, Autonomous Systems and Software Program (WASP) is Sweden’s largest research programme, focusing on artificial intelligence, autonomous systems, and software. It supports strategically motivated basic research, education, and international faculty recruitment to establish Sweden as a global leader in these areas.

instruments.name: Research and innovation bill
instruments.summary: In 2024, Sweden adopted its largest-ever research and innovation bill, allocating substantial funding to strengthen excellent research, higher education, research infrastructure, and groundbreaking technologies (including AI).

instruments.name: Initiatives to help SMEs adopt digital or novel technologies including AI
instruments.summary: Spain offers several national digitalisation support programmes for companies, including SMEs. Key initiatives include Digital Kit, Kit Consulting, Activa Startups, and Generación Digital Pymes, which provide guidance, training, and funding to promote digital transformation and innovation. While not exclusive to AI, these programmes also support AI adoption.

instruments.name: Initiatives to help start-ups and/or scale-ups access financing
instruments.summary: Spain supports innovation and technology adoption—including AI—through a range of national funding programmes. These include large-scale funds such as Next Tech Fund, FOCO, INNVIERTE, Fond-ICO Global, ENISA participatory loans, and Women’s Digital Entrepreneurs, providing billions of euros in financing for start-ups, scale-ups, and SMEs.

instruments.name: RETECH IA
instruments.summary: Spain’s Territorial Networks of Technological Specialisation (RETECH) IA bring together 13 flagship projects to promote artificial intelligence across Spanish regions. The initiative strengthens interregional cooperation and supports the development and deployment of AI solutions.

instruments.name: AI4ES (Network of Excellence in AI)
instruments.summary: AI4ES is a Spanish network of excellence created to strengthen the country’s data- and AI-based economy. It brings together four leading technological centres to transfer AI capabilities, results, and technologies to industry.

instruments.name: Spain Neurotech
instruments.summary: Spain has signed an agreement to create the National Center for Neurotechnology (Spain Neurotech) on the campus of the Autonomous University of Madrid. The centre will focus on neuroscience, brain science, and artificial intelligence, acting as a national hub for research and innovation in these fields.

instruments.name: Financing of cooperative research plans in the area of ​​AI developed by interdisciplinary research groups
instruments.summary: Spain is creating 15 sectorial networks of excellence to strengthen research and innovation in artificial intelligence. These networks cover areas such as theoretical challenges, cognition, advanced algorithms, physics, human–computer interaction, social and environmental challenges, quantum, and new AI applications. The selection of participating organisations is being finalised.

instruments.name: The National AI Policy
instruments.summary:
The Rwanda AI policy aims to achieve the following national objectives:
• Positioning Rwanda as Africa's AI Lab and Responsible AI Champion
• Building 21st Century Skills and AI Literacy
• Creating an Open, Secure, Trusted Data Ecosystem as an Enabler of the AI Revolution
• Driving Public Sector Transformation to Fuel AI Adoption
• Accelerating Responsible AI Adoption in the Private Sector

instruments.name: Slovene Early Stage Innovation Fund
instruments.summary: The Slovene Enterprise Fund equity financing scheme provides equity capital to innovative micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). It supports companies that contribute to the green and digital transition and promotes the growth of globally oriented start-ups and scale-ups.

instruments.name: High-tech equity financing programme
instruments.summary: The SID Bank programme provides equity financing to innovative and high-tech start-ups and scale-ups in Slovenia. It offers seed capital and convertible loans to support early-stage development, product commercialisation, and scaling of technology-driven businesses.

instruments.name: P4D grants for digital transformation
instruments.summary: The Ministry of Economy, Tourism and Sport, in cooperation with the Slovene Enterprise Fund, provides grants of up to €100,000 to support the digital transformation of SMEs. The programme also encourages adoption of advanced technologies, including artificial intelligence, to modernise business operations.

instruments.name: P2 subsidies for start-ups
instruments.summary: The P2 programme, managed by the Ministry of Economy, Tourism, and Sport and implemented via the Slovene Enterprise Fund, co-finances innovation-driven start-ups. It supports the development and commercialisation of innovative products, including solutions based on artificial intelligence.

instruments.name: Digital transformation incentives programme of the Slovene Enterprise Fund
instruments.summary: The Slovene Enterprise Fund provides grants and blended financing to micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) through its Digital Transformation incentives. The programme supports investment in digital technologies and skills, helping SMEs modernise operations and increase competitiveness.

instruments.name: European Digital Innovation Hubs (EDIHs)
instruments.summary: Slovenia hosts two European Digital Innovation Hubs (EDIHs) with dedicated services to support AI start-ups and scale-ups in accessing financing and advancing digital transformation. These are: Smart, Resilient and Sustainable Communities (SRC-EDIH) and DIGI-SI.

instruments.name: Digital Innovation Hub Slovenia
instruments.summary: Slovenia’s national Digital Innovation Hub (DIH Slovenia) serves as a one-stop shop supporting the digitalisation of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). It provides financial and advisory support through vouchers that help companies strengthen their digital skills, develop strategies, improve digital marketing, and enhance cybersecurity.

instruments.name: Pilot demonstration projects
instruments.summary: Slovenia funded 21 consortia to run pilot projects supporting the circular economy as part of its National Energy and Climate Plan (NEPN). These projects aim to test and demonstrate innovative solutions that reduce environmental impact and improve resource efficiency. Three of the projects apply artificial intelligence to advance sustainability goals.

instruments.name: R&D projects for ICT and specific economic purposes
instruments.summary: In 2022, Slovenia’s Ministry of the Economy, Tourism and Sport co-funded 95 R&D projects led by consortia of companies, with 18 of these projects explicitly based on AI. The initiative supports innovation aligned with green transition, productivity growth, and competitiveness, with AI integrated into the ICT programme and other sectoral priorities.

instruments.name: Artificial Intelligence in the Financial Sector – Interim Report of the Inter-Agency Task Force on the Use of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning in Israel's Financial Sector
instruments.summary: This initiative aims to improve financial services, reduce costs, and boost innovation. It promotes responsible AI use while addressing risks like bias, data misuse, and lack of transparency. The initiative focuses on flexible, sector-specific regulation. Policymakers and regulators are working together to ensure fair, safe, and effective AI integration that benefits consumers and supports sustainable financial growth.

instruments.name: Legal Guide for Designing Regulatory Sandboxes
instruments.summary: This guide was written for Israeli regulators to support the design of a responsible, innovation-friendly regulatory framework. It introduces the "regulatory sandbox" tool, explains its use in Israel, outlines its advantages and disadvantages, and provides examples from Israeli law to support better rulemaking.

instruments.name: National Multi stakeholder consultation forum for AI policy and regulation
instruments.summary: The expert forum will assist in developing a governmental strategy and policy for promoting the safe use of artificial intelligence, aiming to encourage innovation and maximize the technology’s social and economic benefits.

instruments.name: R&D projects for smart specialisation and specific economic objectives
instruments.summary: Slovenia supports R&D projects at TRL 3–6 in line with its Sustainable Smart Specialisation Strategy for Advanced Technologies. The initiative funds applied research and prototype development in strategic technology areas, including AI, to foster innovation and strengthen the national research ecosystem.

instruments.name: Gravity and Strategic projects
instruments.summary: The Gravity Projects initiative funds four major research consortia in Slovenia, each focusing on a high-impact technology area: AI, semiconductors, language technologies, and quantum technologies. Co-funded by the Ministry of Higher Education, Science and Innovation and the Ministry of Digital Transformation, the projects support research from early-stage concept (TRL 1/2) to validated prototypes (TRL 4/5).

instruments.name: PoVejMo
instruments.summary: The PoVejMo programme supports research on adaptive natural language processing using large-scale language models. It funds collaborative projects through a public call from the Ministry of Higher Education, Science and Innovation. The programme aims to advance AI-driven language technologies in Slovenia.

instruments.name: COFUND SMASH project
instruments.summary: The SMASH programme brings together leading Slovenian universities, research institutes, and public bodies to attract 50 outstanding postdoctoral researchers from around the world, including Slovenians abroad. Using machine learning, AI, and the Vega supercomputer, researchers will work across multiple scientific and humanities fields. The initiative strengthens Slovenia’s role in global research while supporting the return of local talent.

instruments.name: AI for Science Moonshot
instruments.summary: The national program’s Scientific Advisory Committee, the PBC is happy to launch a new Call for Proposals: AI for Science Moonshot. The term "Moonshot" is used here to describe an ambitious and groundbreaking project aimed at achieving a goal perceived as difficult or nearly impossible, but which has the potential to revolutionize a given domain with far-reaching implications for technological and overall progress.

instruments.name: EUROPEUM-EDIC
instruments.summary: The European Blockchain Partnership and European Blockchain Services Infrastructure (EBSI) EDIC brings together EU countries to build secure and interoperable blockchain services. Its goal is to support cross-border cooperation between public authorities and ensure blockchain solutions work seamlessly with other technologies like AI, cloud, and data spaces. The initiative also creates better conditions for innovation in decentralised technologies.

instruments.name: CitiVERSE
instruments.summary: The Connected Local Digital Twins for CitiVERSE (LDT CitiVERSE EDIC) links digital twins of cities across Europe to form a shared CitiVERSE. These virtual city models use AI and data to simulate real-world conditions and improve decision-making. The initiative helps cities test solutions for issues like traffic, air quality, and urban planning, while also enhancing citizen engagement through interactive tools.

instruments.name: Establishment of a Moonshot AI Applied Research Consortium
instruments.summary: The Israel Innovation Authority invites proposals for the establishment of an applied research consortium dedicated to the development of groundbreaking technologies in the field of artificial intelligence (AI). These technologies should be at the forefront of global R&D and have the potential to provide Israeli industry with a competitive edge in the international market.

instruments.name: Increasing the number of AI experts from overseas in Israeli industry (returning residents, new immigrants, foreign experts)
instruments.summary: Shortage in AI experts with graduate-level academic qualifications constitutes a barrier to the local high-tech industry’s ability to fulfil its potential for AI-driven innovation. Some 300-400 advanced degree graduates complete their studies each year and join the high-tech industry in research roles. Yet the demand for such experts is much higher. Attracting foreign talent into the Israeli high-tech eco system serves to expand and diversify the local expert pool.

instruments.name: European Digital Innovation Hubs (EDIHs)
instruments.summary: Slovakia hosts several European Digital Innovation Hubs (EDIHs) that support digital transformation across sectors. These hubs assist SMEs, hospitals, companies, and public institutions in adopting advanced digital technologies, including AI. Their implementation is coordinated by the Ministry of Investment, Regional Development, and Informatization.

instruments.name: Alliance for Language Technologies - European Digital Infrastructure Consortium (ALT-EDIC)
instruments.summary: Slovenia is a member of the European Digital Infrastructure Consortium for Language Technologies (ALT-EDIC). This initiative seeks to build shared European infrastructure for language technologies and create large language models for European languages. The goal is to strengthen Europe’s AI capabilities while preserving linguistic diversity.

instruments.name: AI Competence Center
instruments.summary: Slovenia is planning to establish a national Competence Center for Artificial Intelligence, led by the Ministry of Digital Transformation. The center will advance AI research, innovation, and practical applications across industries and public services. It will also act as a one-stop-shop to help SMEs adopt AI solutions.

instruments.name: Strategic materials of the Ministry of Investment, Regional Development and Informatisation of the Slovak Republic (MIRRI)
instruments.summary: The Slovak government has introduced measures to strengthen digital skills in small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). These include training programmes to help companies understand and integrate artificial intelligence into their daily operations. The aim is to boost competitiveness and support digital transformation.

instruments.name: Slovak Center for Artificial Intelligence Research (AISlovakIA)
instruments.summary: The Slovak Center for Artificial Intelligence Research (AISlovakIA) was created in 2019 as Slovakia’s national AI platform. It connects researchers, students, businesses, government, and international partners to advance AI research and adoption. Its goal is to build a collaborative environment that fully develops Slovakia’s AI potential.

instruments.name: Regional AI Hubs at universities
instruments.summary: InnovAIte Slovakia brings together regional universities and local industries to advance research and innovation in artificial intelligence. Universities have established dedicated AI research hubs focusing on practical applications. The initiative fosters collaboration and supports the development of AI solutions tailored to Slovakia’s economic and social needs.

instruments.name: Aid scheme for the digitalisation of SME
instruments.summary: Under Romania’s National Recovery and Resilience Plan (NRRP), a dedicated investment supports the digitalisation of SMEs. It provides grants both for developing advanced digital technologies and for helping SMEs adopt them. Eligible areas include AI, cloud computing, blockchain, IoT, cybersecurity, and other key digital tools.

instruments.name: European Digital Innovation Hubs (EDIHs)
instruments.summary: Romania hosts seven European Digital Innovation Hubs (EDIHs), five of which have a strong focus on artificial intelligence. These hubs support SMEs and public organisations in adopting digital and AI technologies. They are co-funded by the European Commission and the Romanian Government to drive digital transformation across the country.

instruments.name: AI Innovative Lab
instruments.summary: The AI Innovative Lab focuses on building advanced research and development capacity in artificial intelligence. Its mission is to develop skills and applications in areas such as bioinformatics, computer vision, and natural language processing. The lab also advances research in deep learning and other AI subfields to generate innovative solutions.

instruments.name: AI Research Institute (ICIA)
instruments.summary: The AI Research Institute (ICIA) at Cluj-Napoca Technical University was inaugurated in 2024 as part of the Romanian AI Hub. Equipped with high-performance computing systems and advanced research facilities, it focuses on developing innovative AI-driven solutions across multiple sectors. Its work spans areas such as smart cities, robotics, e-health, e-agriculture, and cybersecurity.

instruments.name: ICIINNOLAB
instruments.summary: The ICIINNOLAB project at ICI Bucharest created eight innovation laboratories focused on emerging and disruptive technologies, including AI, cybersecurity, and blockchain. These labs provide facilities and resources to support advanced research, talent development, and practical applications. The goal is to strengthen institutional performance and foster innovation in Romania’s digital ecosystem.

instruments.name: Research in areas of strategic interest
instruments.summary: The “Research in Areas of Strategic Interest” programme, part of Romania’s National RDI Plan (2022–2027), supports participation in international scientific initiatives. Its AI subprogramme funds research, development, and innovation projects that apply artificial intelligence across different sectors. The goal is to strengthen Romania’s AI ecosystem and promote the use of advanced technologies in society and the economy.

instruments.name: Romanian AI Innovation Hub for AI (HRIA)
instruments.summary: The Romanian Hub of Artificial Intelligence (HRIA) is a national project that brings together universities and companies to strengthen Romania’s AI ecosystem. Its goal is to advance research, create new AI products and services, and transfer knowledge to industry and society. Running from 2025 to 2029, the hub aims to position Romania as an active player in the European AI landscape.

instruments.name: Institute for AI Mihai Drăgănescu
instruments.summary: The “Mihai Drăgănescu” Research Institute for Artificial Intelligence in Bucharest carries out advanced research in artificial intelligence and related fields. Its work covers areas such as machine learning, natural language processing, robotics, and intelligent systems. The institute contributes to both fundamental research and practical applications that support technological progress.

instruments.name: Start-up Hub Portal
instruments.summary: The Start-up Hub Portal in Portugal is an online platform that maps the country’s start-up ecosystem. It gathers information on start-ups, incubators, investors, and support programmes, offering a real-time view of the sector. The portal makes it easier for entrepreneurs, investors, and institutions to connect and collaborate.

instruments.name: National Test Beds Network
instruments.summary: The National Test Beds Network in Portugal helps companies and researchers test and apply new AI and digital technologies. It provides access to real environments, equipment, and infrastructure for safe experimentation. The initiative supports collaboration across business, academia, and research to speed up digital transformation in key sectors.

instruments.name: Attract Digital Innovation Hub
instruments.summary: As part of the network of EDIH, the Attract Digital Innovation Hub for AI and HPC supports SMEs and public entities in their digital transformation through the full exploitation of the synergetic potential between AI and HPC.

instruments.name: National Digital Innovation Hubs (DIHs) Network
instruments.summary: The national network of European Digital Innovation Hubs (DIHs) in Portugal focuses on the adoption of advanced digital technologies such as AI, HPC, cloud computing, and cybersecurity. These hubs are supported by the National Innovation Agency (ANI) and the Testing Experimental Facility for AI.

instruments.name: RNCA Supercomputers and Cloud Access
instruments.summary: A call from the Portuguese Foundation for Science and Technology to facilitate access to the National Network for Advanced Computing (RNCA) for AI-related projects. These projects will benefit from RNCA’s HPC and cloud infrastructure, significantly supporting advanced AI research in Portugal. This call started in 2020 and has been renewed every year.

instruments.name: Centre of Excellence for AI R&D
instruments.summary: The Centre of Excellence for AI R&D in Portugal is currently under development.

instruments.name: European Digital Innovation Hubs
instruments.summary: There are 22 Digital Innovation Hubs in Poland, 11 of which are funded under the Digital Europe programme.

instruments.name: TEFs
instruments.summary:
Poland is participating in two TEFs for AI:
agrifoodTEF – Test and Experiment Facilities for the Agri-Food Domain: Innovation and co-creation of sustainable agriculture tools. 
The Warsaw University of Technology is a partner in the project TEF Smart Cities & Communities: project “CitCom”.

instruments.name: Priority 1 of the EU Funds for Smart Economy 2021–2027
instruments.summary: Within the programme, Priority 1 aims at directly supporting companies, with special focus on small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). As an incentive to investment in research and development, entrepreneurs have the ability to apply to a flexible combination of modules that include green and digital transition, R&D business infrastructure, internationalisation and support to skills in enterprises.

instruments.name: AI4MSP
instruments.summary: This online tool, administered by the Future Industry Platform Foundation (Fundacja Platforma Przemysłu Przyszłości) and created as a cooperation between the Ministry of Digital Affairs and Global Partnership on AI, connects startups, micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) looking for artificial intelligence (AI) solutions with providers of AI solutions.

instruments.name: Start in Poland, edition II - Acceleration Programs
instruments.summary: This programme of the Polish Development Fund (PFR) programme aims to create a favourable environment for start-ups, by supporting start-up acceleration programmes. The accelerators in the competition are required to choose min. 25% of startups operating from the following areas: Space Technologies, Fintech, Artificial Intelligence (AI), Smart Plastics, Microelectronics, Industrial Internet of Things/Augmented reality, Smart city, Cybersecurity, Bioeconomy, Pharmaceutical Biotechnology.

instruments.name: PFR Ventures
instruments.summary: This project of the Polish Development Fund (PFR) provides venture capital to VC firms as well as innovative companies, including AI start-ups.

instruments.name: BRIdge VC - TDJ Pitango Ventures fund
instruments.summary: This programme, building on the “Bridge VC” programme of the National Centre for Research and Development (NCBR) to support commercialisation of Polish R&D projects, and the Polish-Israel venture capital fund TDJ Pitango Ventures, helps technology start-ups access financing for R&D, and offers management and consulting assistance. So far, especially AI-focused companies have profited from this programme.

instruments.name: Alliance for Language Technologies EDIC
instruments.summary: Poland participates in in the Alliance for Language Technologies EDIC, which concentrates on usage of AI for large language models. Polish institutions will participate in calls devoted to support ALT-EDIC activities.

instruments.name: Fast Track
instruments.summary: This competition of the National Centre for Research and Development: (NCBIR) is aimed at entrepreneurs, consortia of enterprises, scientific and industrial consortia which conduct industrial research and/or experimental development projects that result in the development of an innovative solution that can be implemented in businesses and companies. Several projects utilizing artificial intelligence have been supported.

instruments.name: INFOSTRATEG
instruments.summary: This strategic programme of the National Center for Research and Development (NCBR) support on scientific research and development in the area of “Advanced information, telecommunications and mechatronic technologies”. In the first quarter of 2025, the NCBR also plans to announce another, eighth competition in the INFOSTRATEG strategic programme, with the goal to develop the Polish AI potential.

instruments.name: PLLuM
instruments.summary: A consortium of six institutions, led by the Wrocław University of Science and Technology (PWr), have launched a project to develop the Polish Large Language Universal Model (PLLuM). The model is intended to be open source and free to use, and for it to form the basis of a Polish-speaking intelligent assistant that can help provide public services.

instruments.name: GenAI Team at the CaMiNO
instruments.summary: The University of Lodz has established Poland’s first university team dedicated to generative artificial intelligence at the Centre for Analysis, Modelling and Computational Science (Centrum Analiz, Modelowania i Nauk Obliczeniowych - CaMiNO), which pursues an interdisciplinary research approach in biology, maths, data analysis, finance, economics.

instruments.name: Artificial Intelligence & Data Analysis Centre (AIDA)
instruments.summary: The Artificial Intelligence & Data Analysis Centre (AIDA) is one of our four management centres of the public research centre NASK, focusing on coordinating, initiating and developing projects involving artificial intelligence applications, taking into account the needs of the administration, cybersecurity, education and the media. The goal of AIDA is to become a Central European centre of excellence specialising in artificial intelligence.

instruments.name: LEAP
instruments.summary: LEAP, organized annually in Riyadh, is one of the worlds largest tech events, bringing together global leaders to showcase innovation and address challenges, with SDAIA powering the AI-focused DeepFest.

instruments.name: Artificial Intelligence Mission
instruments.summary: Artificial Intelligence Mission AI.M aspires to stimulate a comprehensive system of innovation in the field of artificial intelligence and contribute to strengthening the Kingdom's leadership role regionally and globally in artificial intelligence within the next 5 years.

instruments.name: Global Artificial Intelligence Assembly
instruments.summary: ICESCO, SDAIA, and the UN organized the Global Artificial Intelligence Assembly in Riyadh to explore AI's potential in driving sustainable development and global collaboration.

instruments.name: Global Smart City Forum
instruments.summary: The Global Smart City Forum in Riyadh is a global platform where the world's distinguished experts in the fields of AI and smart city building gather to discuss important topics related to the future of these cities and their impact on human communities.

instruments.name: Data Sharing Policy
instruments.summary: The initiative seeks to establish guidelines for secure and responsible data sharing to protect privacy and confidentiality.

instruments.name: Open Data Datathon
instruments.summary: SDAIA launches the Open Data Datathon to develop talent and skills in data science, foster innovation, and address real-world challenges using open data.

instruments.name: AI Scholarship Program
instruments.summary: The Program aims to contribute to achieving the objectives of the National Strategy for Data & AI and position the Kingdom among the leading countries in AI by providing external scholarships for national competencies and fostering global competition.

instruments.name: Cloud Computing services provisioning regulations
instruments.summary: The Cloud Computing Regulatory Framework (CCRF) by the Saudi Communications, Space, and Technology Commission (CST) provides guidelines to ensure secure, efficient, and transparent cloud computing services in Saudi Arabia.

instruments.name: One Million Saudi in Artificial Intelligence
instruments.summary: In September  2024, Minister of Education Yousef bin Abdullah Al-Benyan and Saudi Data and AI Authority (SDAIA) President Abdullah bin Sharaf Alghamdi launched the "One Million Saudi in AI" initiative , aiming to empower 1 million Saudis in artificial intelligence (AI).

instruments.name: The International Center for Artificial Intelligence Research and Ethics (ICARE)
instruments.summary: ICAIRE is an international centre established in Riyadh and it is the lighthouse for ethical AI. The centre has a legal personality, and financial and administrative independence to advance AI Research and Ethics worldwide.

instruments.name: SDAIA - KAUST Summer Program
instruments.summary: SDAIA and KAUST Launch the Summer Program for AI to Equip Saudi High School Students with the Knowledge of Artificial Intelligence.

instruments.name: Joint Research Center for Artificial Intelligence
instruments.summary: The centre aims to establish the Kingdom as a global leader among data-driven economies by conducting and supporting research and innovation in AI.

instruments.name: Centre for Artificial Intelligence in Precision Medicines
instruments.summary: A leading global innovation center for developing precise therapies using artificial intelligence and emerging technologies.

instruments.name: Global AI Summit
instruments.summary: The Global AI Summit is the leading platform for advancing the global discussion on AI, where visionary experts, academics, corporates, and policymakers converge from every part of the world to shape the future of artificial intelligence for the good of humanity

instruments.name: International AI Olympiad
instruments.summary: Saudi Arabia is hosting here the inaugural International AI Olympiad (IAIO), spearheaded by the Saudi Data and Artificial Intelligence Authority (SDAIA), a global event aiming to boost ties among technology and software experts, as well as AI educators from various countries.

instruments.name: The National Olympiad for Programming and AI (ATHKA)
instruments.summary: The National Programming and Artificial Intelligence Olympiad is a national competitive competition for middle and high school students from different regions of the Kingdom, where distinguished male and female students compete on an individual basis to solve issues and refine their information skills, which is centred on discovering the skills of using computers to solve issues that depend on  designing learning-based algorithms, structuring data and programming with AI.

instruments.name: Personal Data Breach Incidents Procedural Guide
instruments.summary: Data breaches are to be notified to SDAIA in accordance with the conditions set forth in the Regulations, along with notifying the Data Subjects if this incident conflicts with their rights or interests.

instruments.name: National Platform of Technologies and Semiconductors
instruments.summary: A National Platform of Technologies and Semiconductors has been launched in December 2024 as a priority project aiming to bring together and consolidate the R&D capacities in the area of semiconductors.

instruments.name: EuroHPC JU
instruments.summary: Romania participates in the European High-Performance Computing Joint Undertaking (EuroHPC JU). The Romanian partner is the National Institute for Research and Development in Informatics – ICI Bucharest. Such capacity is primarily used for scientific and research purposes, and the demand for AI-specific uses has grown particularly in recent years and this infrastructure could be further leveraged to support AI start-ups and SMEs.

instruments.name: America's AI Action Plan
instruments.summary: The Action Plan sets forth policy goals for near-term execution by the Federal government and articulates policy recommendations in line with the President’s vision for US leadership in AI. It is articulated around three main pillars: innovation, infrastructure, and international diplomacy and security.

instruments.name: AI Competence for Sweden
instruments.summary: AI Competence for Sweden is an initiative where ten universities collaborate with the goal to elevate the competence about AI in academia and in industry.

instruments.name: Research Institutes of Sweden (Rise)
instruments.summary: RISE combines AI research with interdisciplinary research, a wide range of test beds, inspiring innovation hubs, educational programmes, digital platforms and extensive experience in software. More than 75 AI projects are currently underway at RISE, conducted by over 60 active AI researchers. RISE has established a center for applied AI and possess a wealth of experience in working with practical applications as well as the situations that arise there from.

instruments.name: Guidelines for the use of generative AI in the public administration
instruments.summary: The authorities shall develop guidelines with the aim of promoting the effective, safe and ethical use of generative AI in public administration. The guidelines shall serve as guidance and support for the use of generative AI for employees of state authorities, municipalities and regions from a legal, security and ethical perspective. The guidelines will also serve as methodological support and provide guidance for the activities' assessments of whether and how generative AI should be used.

instruments.name: Quantum Spain
instruments.summary: Quantum Spain promotes and funds a competitive quantum computing infrastructure to strengthen Spain’s scientific and technological base in quantum computing and its AI applications. It supports the national ecosystem with essential tools and resources. In 2023, Spanish authorities announced that Southern Europe’s first quantum computer would be installed in Barcelona.

instruments.name: Language Strategic Project for the Economic Recovery and Transformation
instruments.summary: The plan supports AI learning in Spanish and co-official languages and goes beyond AI alone (Presidencia del Gobierno, 2023\[15]). It is partly implemented through the National Plan on Language Technologies, which includes initiatives to advance language technologies and AI in these languages. A key action is the creation of linguistic corpora composed of diverse texts such as novels, plays, film scripts, and press materials, helping train and improve AI language models.

instruments.name: AI Regulatory Sandbox
instruments.summary: The AI Regulatory Sandbox, developed in collaboration with the European Commission, is a digital space that seeks to connect competent authorities with AI development companies to jointly define best practices when implementing future European AI regulation, and ensure its application. The AI Sandbox will be implemented by two focus groups and they will work on the publication of initial guidelines. The initiative will include a quality label.

instruments.name: University-Business Chairs on AI
instruments.summary: Three ENIA chairs focus on AI and agriculture/rural development: University of Murcia, University of Cordoba, University of Oviedo. Two of the ENIA chairs focus on the intersection between AI and climate and the environment:  Sustainability and Decarbonised society (Polytechnic University of Catalunya) and Green Algorithms (University of La Coruña).

instruments.name: Transformation of work because of AI
instruments.summary: Analysis of the transformation of the labour market, employment relations, working conditions and organisation, job profiles and jobs in different sectors in Slovenia that have the potential to be replaced or changed as a result of the introduction of AI, including from a gender perspective, over a 10-year period.

instruments.name: Advanced Computing Portugal 2030
instruments.summary: ACP.2030 is a science, innovation and growth strategy to foster Advanced Computing in Portugal in the European context, oriented towards building a high-performance computing world-reference network infrastructure. The centre aims to play a crucial role in supporting research and higher education by providing state-of-the-art computing resources. A new 500m² science data centre is being developed for the National Centre for Advanced Computing.

instruments.name: Analysis and prediction of patterns in the utilization of emergency services and medical services
instruments.summary: The development of mechanisms to analyze patterns in the utilization of medical services, particularly in emergency services, is relevant to the management of healthcare entities in the National Health Service (SNS). To this end, the use of microdata from medication prescriptions by healthcare professionals from healthcare institutions and medical services is proposed.

instruments.name: R&D programme on data science and AI in Public Administration
instruments.summary: The programme was specifically designed and implemented in order to develop and attract talent in projects involving Public Administration organisations. It aims to leverage data science and AI to improve decision-making and public policy.

instruments.name: Govtech Justice AI Project
instruments.summary: The Govtech project in the justice sector is part of a broader government initiative under the RRP. This project aims to integrate innovative products and services to enhance the efficiency and agility of justice services. One of the key innovations is an AI-based tool designed to automatically validate documents in nationality application processes. This tool helps streamline the process, reducing the time and effort required for manual validation, and improving overall service delivery.

instruments.name: Amsterdam's AI Register
instruments.summary: Amsterdam and Helsinki have launched open AI registers that track how algorithms are being used in the municipalities.

instruments.name: Malta Digital Innovation Authority`s Technology Assurance Sandbox
instruments.summary: The Technology Assurance Sandbox managed by the MDIA offers a secure environment for individuals or companies to test solutions based on innovative technologies such as blockchain and AI. The sandbox ensures that solutions meet recognised standards for safety and security.

instruments.name: The Pathfinder MDIA Digital Scholarship
instruments.summary: The scholarship, established by the MDIA, aims to support postgraduate education and PhD level studies in fields such as AI, information security, quantum computing, machine learning, neural networks, and robotics.

instruments.name: European Digital Innovation Hub
instruments.summary: The European Digital Innovation Hub (EDIH) in Malta is another example which support collaboration and cooperation at an international level. By facilitating networking and collaboration with other EDIHs through the DiHubMT platform, AI opportunities in the public and private sectors will be fostered.

instruments.name: MDIA Applied Research Grant
instruments.summary: The Applied Research Grant is an initiative by the MDIA to support capacity-building efforts in AI research in Malta. The grant aims to advance AI research capacity, foster AI R&D investments and promote collaboration between academia and commercial entities. The grant supports projects in various areas, including AI, digital trust, knowledge and data representation, technology for sustainability, quantum computing, and other emerging technologies. Applications for this grant are open annually.

instruments.name: Future Innovators Summer School
instruments.summary: The Future Innovators Summer School and Future Innovators Plus are initiatives by the MDIA, in collaboration with the University of Malta, the Malta College of Arts, Science and Technology (MCAST), the Malta Innovation Forum, and Malta’s Interactive Science Centre, Esplora. These programs include two summer schools and bootcamps and one winter bootcamp, aimed at introducing young students to digital innovation, including AI.

instruments.name: Skills Development
instruments.summary: The scheme supports business undertakings to provide training to develop and update the skills and knowledge of their workforce and to train new employees for them to acquire the necessary skills and knowledge to perform effectively

instruments.name: Digital Tech Fund
instruments.summary: The Digital Tech Fund, part of the Digital Luxembourg initiative, is a seed fund designed to support ICT start-ups and strengthen the country's tech ecosystem. It operates as a joint public-private partnership, with contributions from the government, Société Nationale de Crédit et d'Investissement (SNCI), the University of Luxembourg, and other key stakeholders. The fund focuses on investing in areas such as cybersecurity, fintech, big data, digital health, media, or next-generation comms.

instruments.name: AI: A Strategic Vision for Luxembourg
instruments.summary: This strategic vision for AI in Luxembourg articulates the activities, ambitions and intentions related to the role of AI, both in Luxembourg and across the EU and is a government-approved strategic document.

instruments.name: MELUXINA Supercomputer
instruments.summary: Luxembourg’s national supercomputer MeluXina launched was launched as part of the EU’s EuroHPC initiative. Operated by LuxProvide, it delivers HPC capabilities to support innovation in sectors such as finance, healthcare, research, and manufacturing. MeluXina is designed to handle large-scale data processing, simulations, and AI applications, playing a key role in Luxembourg’s push to become a leader in digital transformation and data-driven innovation.

instruments.name: Supercomputers
instruments.summary:
"Italy hosts five of the world’s 500 most powerful supercomputers in the world: 1. HPC6 (Pavia) deployed in 2024 (most powerful in Italy,  5th globally); 2. LEONARDO (Bologna) deployed in 2022; 3. Marconi-100 (Bologna) deployed in 2020; 4. Davinci-1 (Genova) in 2020; 5. Cassandra (Lecce) in 2024. 

The initiative has the following objective: To develop top-of-the-range exascale supercomputers for processing big data, based on European technology.

instruments.name: Future Artificial Intelligence Research (FAIR) Centre
instruments.summary: Research network to address research aspects, methodologies, models, technologies, and ethical and legal rules for building human centric AI systems. It includes four research institutions and 14 universities.

instruments.name: Italian Institute for AI
instruments.summary: The Italian Institute for Artificial Intelligence is a research and technology transfer structure able to attract first class talents from the international market and, at the same time, become a flagship initiative for the development of Al in Italy.

instruments.name: Ireland's Research Centres and Research Projects
instruments.summary: A listing of past and current research projects and research centres directed to AI.

instruments.name: Proposals and Report for an Italian Strategy on AI
instruments.summary: Proposals for an Italian strategy for AI have been developed by the Expert Group on artificial intelligence selected by the Ministry of Economic Development and published in July 2020.

instruments.name: National Digital Research Centre
instruments.summary: The National Digital Research Centre (NDRC) is a publicly funded early investor in digital technology start-ups.

instruments.name: SFI Research Centres and Spokes Programme
