instruments.summary: The Research Centres Programme, launched in 2012, aims to develop a set of world-leading, large-scale research centres on a themed basis in order to align this major investment to areas which can generate maximum economic and societal benefit for Ireland.

instruments.name: AI Use Cases in the Public Sector in Ireland
instruments.summary: A series of use cases of AI in the Irish public sector.

instruments.name: National AI Laboratory
instruments.summary: Established in 2020 under the Ministry for Culture and Innovation, this laboratory serves as a central hub for AI research and development. It unites numerous research centers and receives government funding, positioning itself as a foundational pillar in advancing the country's AI capabilities.

instruments.name: European Digital Innovation Hubs (EDIHs) in Greece
instruments.summary: Greece participates in the EDIH network, which aims to support SMEs in their digital transformation. There are seven EDIHs in Greece, including Innovation hub for Artificial Intelligence in Energy and Environment, Supply chain and mobility, Culture and Tourism, aims to increase the digital maturity of Greek businesses and local authorities through increased AI uptake. The Hubs are based on existing clusters and EU-wide initiatives, making it a valuable policy-support instrument.

instruments.name: AI factory - Pharos
instruments.summary: This flagship project under the Blueprint for Greece’s AI Transformation is one of seven EU AI Factories, aiming to accelerate AI innovation by serving as a hub for academia, research, the public sector and private enterprises aiming to develop innovative AI-driven services, spanning sectors of health, Greek language and culture, and sustainability and energy (including climate adaptation). The project will leverage the high-performance computing infrastructure of the “DAEDALUS” supercomputer.

instruments.name: DAEDALUS Hypercomputer
instruments.summary: This project includes the development of a new supercomputing system through the procurement of new hardware and infrastructure. The action forms part of the strategy to strengthen the country's public digital infrastructure through the Recovery Fund, as set out in the Digital Transformation 2020-2025 Paper. It will be implemented in the framework of the National Recovery and Resilience Plan "Greece 2.0" with funding from the European Union - Next Generation EU.

instruments.name: Plattform Lernende Systeme - Germany's Platform for AI
instruments.summary: Founded by the BMBF in 2017, this expert network fosters interdisciplinary dialogue on AI, involving around 200 members from academia, business, and civil society. It develops guidance on responsible AI use, including resources like the AI Roadmap for SMEs, which provides practical advice for AI adoption in firms.

instruments.name: Green AI Hub mid tier
instruments.summary: The Green AI Hub Mittelstand is an initiative launched by the BMUV to support German SMEs in adopting AI technologies for environmental protection and climate action. The hub aims to empower SMEs to integrate AI solutions that enhance energy efficiency, reduce resource consumption, and minimize environmental impact. It offers a range of resources, including technical guidance, funding access, and training opportunities to facilitate the development and implementation of AI-driven proposals.

instruments.name: Application Laboratory for AI and Big Data (AI Lab)
instruments.summary: Managed by the German Environment Agency, this lab specialises in leveraging AI and big data to advance environmental enforcement, research, and the sustainable use of AI technologies. As part of the Federal Government’s economic stimulus and future technologies package, it is funded until 2025. The lab generates data-driven insights to inform policy decisions and raise public awareness on environmental issues, while also promoting a modern and efficient approach to public administration.

instruments.name: German Mobility Data Space
instruments.summary: The German Federal Ministry for Digital and Transport (BMDV) is funding the Mobility Data Space (MDS), a platform designed to facilitate the legally secure exchange of sensitive data. Within this space, private sector data can be voluntarily shared and traded while ensuring full respect for data sovereignty. The MDS operates as a non-profit joint venture and is managed by Datenraum Mobilität GmbH, established in May 2021.

instruments.name: Lighthouses of AI for Environment, Climate, Nature, and Resources
instruments.summary: The programme provides funding for AI-driven solutions aimed at addressing environmental challenges and strategically advancing AI applications for environmental and climate protection. This includes areas such as energy efficiency, resource efficiency, biodiversity conservation, nature protection, species preservation, water management, sustainable consumption, and eco-friendly mobility. The focus is on application-oriented research and development projects.

instruments.name: GAIA-X
instruments.summary: Gaia-X was announced in October 2019 as a collaborative effort led by Germany and France to create a secure, federated data infrastructure for Europe. Its goal is to facilitate decentralized data exchange across businesses and research institutions, ensuring interoperability and data sovereignty. Gaia-X is designed to support a wide range of industries, enabling participants to share data and access services on a large scale while retaining control over their data.

instruments.name: GAIA-X
instruments.summary: In 2019, ministers from France and Germany formally launched Gaia-X, an EU cloud initiative that aims to establish an interoperable data exchange through which businesses can share data under the protection of European laws.

instruments.name: Centres of Excellence for AI Research
instruments.summary: Objectives:To build an AI research ecosystem and bring AI research in Germany to a globally leading level.To secure long-term research expertise in Germany.

instruments.name: Automated and Connected Driving
instruments.summary: Safe AI Engineering, funded by the BMWK under the New Vehicle and System Technologies programme, aims to enable comprehensive verification of AI safety for autonomous vehicles, paving the way for their reliable and secure use. The funding guidelines titled “Ensuring a Viable and Sustainable Mobility System through Automated Driving and Connectivity” aimed to support developments in the fields of automated and connected driving as integral components of the future mobility system.

instruments.name: Research on AI Technologies in Agriculture, Health Nutrition, Food Chain, and Rural Areas
instruments.summary: To foster research on AI technologies to optimise the industries of agriculture, health nutrition, food chain, and rural areas.

instruments.name: Advisory Center for AI
instruments.summary: The Federal Ministry of the Interior and Community’s (Bundesministerium des Innern und für Heimat, BMI) BeKI initiative is creating a central advisory and coordination hub for AI in the federal administration. It aims to standardise AI initiatives across federal agencies by offering guidance on legal, ethical, and technical aspects of AI use. BeKI also collaborates with other specialised centres like the Federal Ministry of Finance’s AI Competence Centre.

instruments.name: AI Booster
instruments.summary: AI Booster supports SMEs willing to obtain advice on data-diagnostics and development of relevant AI use cases (Ministère de l'economie, des finances et de l'industrie, 2023).

instruments.name: AI Standardisation Initiative
instruments.summary: The French government intends to support French players in the field of AI by creating, through the influence of voluntary standardization, the conditions for access to and success of trusted solutions and products in France and internationally.

instruments.name: Cloud Strategy: Infrastructures for the Data and AI Economy
instruments.summary: A National Strategy supported by EU initiatives for levelling the playing field of French cloud providers in the path of a European sovereign cloud.

instruments.name: Jean Zay Supercomputer and Support Team
instruments.summary: Jean Zay is a supercomputer of the National Center for Scientifical Research (CNRS) dedicated to academic research and firms. Later initiatives include the extension of Jean Zay’s capability in response to generative AI needs and improve access for AI start-ups. The associated teams of support engineers have also been further strengthened.

instruments.name: Finnish Centre for AI (FCAI)
instruments.summary: FCAI is among the Research Council of Finland’s flagships. It hosts a community of AI experts in artificial intelligence in Finland, initiated by Aalto University, University of Helsinki, and VTT Technical Research Centre of Finland. FCAI hosts ELLIS Unit Helsinki, a node in the pan-European ELLIS network.FCAI is implemented through a large project portfolio. Research Council of Finland’s FCAI flagship funding is a small share of the total funding (about 3% in 2019–2020).

instruments.name: LUMI Supercomputer
instruments.summary: Finland hosts the EuroHPC supercomputer LUMI, which is located in CSC’s data center in Kajaani. In March 2024, Finland made a funding commitment of up to EUR 250 million in the context of an upcoming call for new top-level EuroHPC supercomputers. As of mid-2021, LUMI (Large Unified Modern Infrastructure) will be a top-of-the-range pre-exascale supercomputer, capable of executing more than 375 petaflops or more than 375 million billion calculations per second.

instruments.name: Digital Task Force for AI
instruments.summary:
To accelerate the roll-out of AI in the public sector, the government, together with Local Government Denmark and Danish Regions, have established a Digital Taskforce for Artificial Intelligence.
The Task force shall promote a structured and coordinated initiative to to identify and address barriers to the use of AI and promote large-scale deployment of AI solutions across the public sector.

instruments.name: Pioneer Centre for Artificial Intelligence
instruments.summary: The Pioneer Centre for Artificial Intelligence supports top-level research to develop AI that benefits people and society. It brings together leading Danish universities and foundations to explore both technical and ethical aspects of AI. The centre aims to solve real-world challenges through responsible and innovative AI research.

instruments.name: Regulatory Sandbox for AI
instruments.summary: Denmark's Regulatory Sandbox for AI helps businesses and public authorities develop AI projects by offering expert advice on data protection and AI rules. It aims to support safe and legal AI use while speeding up project development. This initiative reduces uncertainty about laws, helping more AI solutions reach the market responsibly. Part of the Danish strategy for digitalisation, the sandbox is open to public and private organisations.

instruments.name: National AI Strategy of the Czech Republic 2030
instruments.summary: The Digital Economy and Society (DES) strategy is part of the Czech government's Digital Czech Republic program. It aims to prepare economic and social sectors for digital transformation by supporting the development of artificial intelligence across various industries. This initiative helps businesses and society adopt AI technologies to improve efficiency and innovation.

instruments.name: GATE (Big Data for Smart Society)
instruments.summary: The Big Data for Smart Society Institute (GATE) serves as Bulgaria's first Centre of Excellence for Big Data and AI research while also functioning as the country's International Data Spaces Association (IDSA) Hub . The institute integrates research excellence with practical innovation across four strategic areas: Future Cities, Intelligent Government, Smart Industry, and Digital Health.

instruments.name: HPC Supercomputer
instruments.summary: The European High Performance Computing Joint Undertaking (EuroHPC JU) has launched a call for tender for the procurement of a petascale supercomputer capable of executing more than 4 Petaflops, 4 million billion calculations per second and located in Sofia, Bulgaria.

instruments.name: Innovation Strategy for Smart Specialisation 2021-2027
instruments.summary: The ISSS (2021-2027) is a comprehensive policy framework designed to enhance Bulgaria's competitiveness and innovation capacity. It focuses on developing research and innovation infrastructure, improving enterprises' technological capabilities, and fostering human resource skills. The strategy identifies five key thematic areas for smart specialisation, including informatics and ICT, mechatronics, and clean technologies. It aims to promote the adoption of Industry 4.0 technologies, including AI.

instruments.name: Prospective Research Programme
instruments.summary: Through its Prospective Researchprogramme, Innoviris is financing projects led by academic researchers at a Brussels university or college which focus on the future and cover areas of importance to the Brussels Capital Region.

instruments.name: DIGITALWALLONIA4AI
instruments.summary: Digital Wallonia 4 Edu's initiatives aim to enhance digital literacy and inspire interest in STEM among students. These actions include collaborations with educational institutions, creating digital learning resources, and organising workshops and events. Students receive hands-on experience in coding, robotics, and other STEM areas, equipping them with skills for a digital economy (Digital Wallonia, 2024).

instruments.name: Flemish Policy Plan AI
instruments.summary: Flanders has made available EUR 32 million per year for an AI-impulse program that will be centered around three main pillars: basic research, technology transfer and industrial applications, and supporting activities.

instruments.name: AI Expertise Center
instruments.summary: The AI Expertise Center supports and guides the use of artificial intelligence within the Flemish government and local authorities to improve the efficiency, effectiveness and innovation of their (digital) services. The AI Expertise Center takes on the role within the Flanders Digital agency of providing the framework, supporting the knowledge sharing and stimulating the innovative application of AI in government.

instruments.name: IMEC Core Funding
instruments.summary: Imec is a globally renowned research centre based in Flanders, specialising in semi-conductors, digital innovation, and AI technologies. It plays a pivotal role in advancing hardware solutions for edge AI and quantum computing. Imec collaborates with industry and academia to drive innovation and technological leadership in the global semi-conductor field (Imec, 2024[21]).

instruments.name: AI-Ready Flemish Public Administration
instruments.summary: This project aims to enhance the capacity of AI governance within Flemish public administrations through a comprehensive approach that includes organizational, policy, and human capacity building. Through the implementation of UNESCO's Readiness Assessment Methodology (RAM) as well as related measures, the Flemish public administrations are assisted in adapting their AI governance frameworks and in swiftly implementing current and upcoming digital legislation, particularly the AI Act.

instruments.name: AI Directory
instruments.summary: The project aimed to create a comprehensive overview of all AI systems used in federal public administration in 2023. The survey data will help identify challenges and risks related to AI in the public sector. Over five months, 31 AI-related projects were identified across various ministries: 17 operational AI systems, 10 AI research projects, 3 chatbots, and 1 guideline for AI in public administration. This project also serves as preparatory work for the AI Map (KI-Landkarte) initiative.

instruments.name: Clusters of Excellence
instruments.summary: The Clusters of Excellence “Bilateral AI” will advance basic research at the highest scientific level in the forward-looking fields of research on aging and AI (BilateralAI, 2024[18]). Under the coordination of the Johannes Kepler University Linz, the ‘Bilateral AI’ research project combines two important strands of research in the field of AI to date, namely sub-symbolic AI (machine learning) and symbolic AI (knowledge representation and reasoning).

instruments.name: AI Mission Austria 2030
instruments.summary: The three agencies Austria Wirtschaftsservice GmbH (aws), the Austrian Research Promotion Agency (FFG) and the Austrian Science Fund (FWF) offer funding for basic research, applied research and its entrepreneurial implementation under the title ‘AI Mission Austria’ (AIM AT). The funding initiative was implemented for 2022 and 2023 with funds from the Fonds Zukunft Österreich (FZÖ) (FFG, 2024[16]).

instruments.name: FAIR-AI - Fostering Austria's Innovative Strength and Research excellence in Artificial Intelligence
instruments.summary: FAIR-AI addresses the research gap created by dealing with society-related risks in the application of AI.

instruments.name: Automated Driving Regulation
instruments.summary: This Regulation allows for testing of automated vehicles and associated technologies on public roads, but only for a specific set of use cases (lane-changing assistants, self-driving minibuses, and self-driving military vehicles).

instruments.name: AI implementation plan for 2024 and the following years
instruments.summary: The AI implementation plan 2024 is a supplement to the national AIM AT 2030 strategy and at the same time a first interim report on it. The AI Implementation Plan 2024 further operationalises these goals, outlining concrete actions for all 12 ministries, ensuring that AI development aligns with sectoral priorities across various domains such as education, healthcare, and public administration.

instruments.name: Digital Skills Initiative
instruments.summary: Austria has established a “Digital Skills Initiative” (Digitale Kompetenzoffensive) as an intersectional cooperation between five federal ministries (BKA, BMKOES, BMAW, BMF and BMBWF). The initiative focuses on the development and coordination of measures for digital literacy and skills. Under the umbrella of the initiative, the Digital Competencies and Skills strategy outlines how Austria is going to achieve increased digital competencies among the citizens.

instruments.name: AI Strategy for the Austrian PES
instruments.summary: The AI strategy will align the use of AI with company goals and corporate objectives. It will provide guidance for implementation projects and ensure a standard process for AI projects and initiatives within the AMS.

instruments.name: Resolution on Civil Law Rules on Robotics and AI
instruments.summary: In February 2017 the European Parliament called upon the Commission to table a legislative proposal laying down a set of civil law rules on robotics and artificial intelligence.

instruments.name: National Program for Artificial Intelligence
instruments.summary: The National Program for Artificial Intelligence is a multi-year program, budgeted at about NIS 1 billion so far. It relies on a central directorate and on theimplementation capabilities of its member organizations. Its operations include coordinating the work of all relevant governmental entities. The Program is intended tomaintain Israel's global leadership on AI including Research, Infrastructure, Talent, Data, Regulatory Environment, and AI Adoption

instruments.name: New Supercomputer
instruments.summary: The Colombian government plans to invest 1.5bn pesos (US$330,000) to convert an underused datacenter into the country's most robust supercomputer.

instruments.name: Ai Skills Accelerator for Young Women on Artificial Intelligence
instruments.summary: The programme aimed to benefit young women aged between 18-25 years by providing them with the necessary digital, ethical, and managerial skills to become content creators, and to boost creativity and innovation in solving challenges at the community level using AI.

instruments.name: Digitising European industry
instruments.summary: This resolution welcomes the Commission's communication on digitising European industry.

instruments.name: National Digital Strategy
instruments.summary: The NDS 2023 “ 2026 is the instrument that consolidates and coordinates all the public policy initiatives of the national government related to connectivity and digital transformation for the coming years, providing Colombia's vision regarding access, use and appropriation of data and digital technologies. Additionally, this strategy includes a component (axis) associated with Artificial Intelligence with specific actions to be developed in terms of public policy.

instruments.name: IndiaAI Compute Capacity
instruments.summary: Under the IndiaAI Compute Pillar, the Mission is developing a scalable AI computing ecosystem to support India's growing AI startup and research community.

instruments.name: Instructions Regarding the Processing of Personal Data and Artificial Intelligence
instruments.summary: These are the instructions issued by the Colombian Data Protection Authority to Data Controllers and Processors to consider when processing personal data within Artificial Intelligence systems.

instruments.name: Communication Artificial Intelligence for Europe
instruments.summary: Communication from the Commission to the European Parliament, the European Council, the Council, the European Economic and Social Committee and the Committee of the Regions on Artificial Intelligence for Europe.

instruments.name: AI Start-up Hub
instruments.summary: Creation of the AI market: Colombia will become a laboratory for the creation of an AI market in which designers, suppliers, intermediaries and consumers of this technology interact. This market will become the dynamic centre of the nascent 4IR ecosystem in the country.

instruments.name: AI Startup Fund
instruments.summary: Algeria's state-owned telecom company Algerie Telecom has announced a 1.5 billion dinar ($11 million) investment fund to support startups in artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, and robotics.

instruments.name: National Artificial Intelligence Centers
instruments.summary: Considering the progress made in Colombia concerning the adoption of AI systems and the contribution they can make to accelerate accurate decision-making based on data and evidence, as well as the priorities established by the National Government on this issue, it has been proposed that the country will be able to adopt and the creation of artificial intelligence centers. These Centers will be essential articulators for the strategy of digital ecosystems being consolidated at the national level.

instruments.name: European Coordinated Plan on Artificial Intelligence
instruments.summary: Adoption of Conclusions on the Coordinated Plan on artificial intelligence.

instruments.name: Investment Support Fund
instruments.summary: Decree 182 has been widely praised by experts as a landmark initiative reflecting the government's commitment to attracting world-class high-tech businesses to invest in Vietnam.

instruments.name: Centre for the Fourth Industrial Revolution (C4IR) Network
instruments.summary: C4IR is focused on developing advanced and smart regulation, research, and policy design for emerging technologies such as AI, blockchain, and IoT.

instruments.name: National Programme for Transparency and Protection of Personal Data in the Use of Artificial Intelligence
instruments.summary: This program fosters analytical processes and enhances capabilities to ensure the responsible development and use of artificial intelligence. It targets both public and private entities that deploy automated decision-making systems, focusing on safeguarding citizens' privacy while encouraging transparency and clarity. The initiative comprises three key components: an artificial intelligence observatory, governance and social engagement, and capacity building.

instruments.name: Resolution on a Comprehensive European Industrial Policy on Artificial Intelligence and Robotics
instruments.summary: This resolution concerns the impact of AI on industrial policy and was initiated by the Committee on Industry, Research and Energy (ITRE), which calls to maximise the benefits and minimise the risks for society and ensure a safe, equitable development of AI.

instruments.name: Data Public Innovation Center
instruments.summary: The Digital Public Innovation Center is an initiative from the ICT Ministry that uses innovation methods to stimulate the use of technology (including AI) to boost the digital transformation of the State. Our goal is to foster the generation of new citizen services based on AI and help public innovators to generate public value through the use and implementation of AI solutions.

instruments.name: Finance Act 2024
instruments.summary: On 27 July 2024, Mauritius enacted the Finance (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 2024, introducing new tax incentives and exemptions for companies specialising in AI products and services.

instruments.name: Comprenhensive National Artificial Intelligence Program in Justice
instruments.summary: A traves del Sistema Argentino de Informacin Jur­dica, el Ministerio de Justicia implement el Programa Nacional Integral de IA para modernizar el sistema jur­dico argentino optimizando los procesos judiciales y procesos administrativos. Sumar¡ m¡s eficacia y transparencia sin da±ar derechos colectivos e individuales ya que se respeta el uso etico de datos. Queremos beneficiar a los profesionales del derecho y la ciudadan­a en general.

instruments.name: Autonomous Driving in European Transport
instruments.summary: The resolution recognises the benefits of connected and autonomous vehicles, urges for further regulatory reform in this area, and calls for future EU policies and legislation to cover all modes of connected and automated transport (not just road transport).

instruments.name: AI.GOV Website
instruments.summary: The Presidency of the Republic of Colombia has spearheaded and developed the first Colombian government-oriented AI website. The webpage allows for the consolidation of the Colombian's Government commitment to the implementation of an active and trustworthy AI ecosystem for the advancement of the country's AI agenda. The website can be found both in Spanish and English.

instruments.name: Scientific and Technological R&D Tax Incentive Guidelines
instruments.summary: Companies undertaking scientific and technological R&D in the Republic of South Africa can qualify for a 150 per cent tax deduction for the operational R&D expenditure in terms of section 11D of the ITA, if their R&D activities are approved by the Minister of Science and Technology.

instruments.name: Guidance for Public and Private Entities on Transparency and Personal Data Protection for Responsible Artificial Intelligence
instruments.summary: This guide is for public and private entities to develop and use artificial intelligence in a responsible way, guaranteeing the right to transparency and the protection of citizens' personal data.

instruments.name: Resolution on Automated Decision-making Processes
instruments.summary: On 12 February 2020 the European Parliament adopted a resolution on automated decision-making processes: ensuring consumer protection and free movement of goods and services.

instruments.name: Strategic Plan for Knowledge Transfer in AI
instruments.summary: This initiative is a plan to promote the transfer of knowledge in AI in the scientific sector, for Colombia to surpasse the world technological frontier. The plan establishes the steps for technical “ scientific knowledge to be adapted by the countrys companies and become an input to the AI market.

instruments.name: India AI Datasets Platform
instruments.summary: This platform aims to streamline access to high-quality non-personal datasets for AI innovation.

instruments.name: Council Conclusions on Regulatory Sandboxes
instruments.summary: In November 2020, the Council of the European Union adopted a set of conclusions on the role of regulatory sandboxes and experimentation clauses in an innovation-friendly, future-proof, sustainable and resilient EU regulatory framework.

instruments.name: Law for the Promotion of AI Technology and Entrepreneurship
instruments.summary: The purpose of this Law is to establish a regulatory framework that encourages entrepreneurship, as well as the growth, consolidation, and sustainability of companies, to increase social welfare and generate equality. The framework is designed to be implemented through a regionalized approach in accordance with the socioeconomic realities of each region.

instruments.name: OpenThaiGPT
instruments.summary: OpenThaiGPT, built upon the cutting-edge LLM opensource models, is a pioneering open-source Large Language Model tailored for Thai language interactions.

instruments.name: Assuring a Responsible Future for AI
instruments.summary: This report combines analysis from a large-scale industry survey, deep-dive interviews with industry experts, focus groups with members of the public and an economic analysis to reflect on the state of the UK AI assurance market.  It surveys the market and its future potential, and sets out targeted actions the government is taking - both to maximise assurance market growth and ensure the safe and equitable development and deployment of AI in Britain.

instruments.name: Resolution on Intellectual Property Rights for the Development of Ai Technologies
instruments.summary: This European Parliament Resolution stresses the key importance of intellectual property rights (IPRs) protection in relation to AI technologies.

instruments.name: Cybersecurity Policy for AI Deployment
instruments.summary: The CONPES 3995 or the NATIONAL POLICY ON DIGITAL TRUST AND DIGITAL SECURITY, aims to establish measures to expand digital trust and improve digital security, to establish Colombia as an inclusive and competitive society in the digital future.

instruments.name: Copyright and Artificial Intelligence: Open consultation
instruments.summary: This consultation seeks views on how the UK government can ensure the UK's legal framework for AI and copyright supports the UK creative industries and AI sector together. It commenced on 17 December 2024 and will close on 25 February 2025.

instruments.name: CurrentAI
instruments.summary: Current AI was set up to reshape the existing AI landscape by developing and supporting large-scale initiatives that serve the public interest.

instruments.name: Resolution on AI: Questions of Interpretation and Application of International Law
instruments.summary: The European Parliament drafted a report entitled Artificial intelligence: questions of interpretation and application of international law in so far as the EU is affected in the areas of civil and military uses and of state authority outside the scope of criminal justice.

instruments.name: Dashboard for the Implementation of AI Ethical Principles
instruments.summary: The Dashboard for monitoring the Ethical Framework for Artificial Intelligence provides an overview of AI projects from public entities and how they are implementing ethical principles and tools in their projects. Entities will need to report: the tools they are using to implement ethical principles, how they are insuring non - discrimination, and an analysis from ethical risks in the project and the mechanisms to mitigate them.

instruments.name: Kenya Agricultural Data-sharing Platform
instruments.summary: As a digital public good that empowers organizations across the agricultural landscape to seamlessly share, integrate, and leverage valuable data for the greater good, KADP offers more customized services to farmers, fosters collaboration, enhances data accessibility and promotes sustainable agricultural practices.

instruments.name: AI Upskilling Fund
instruments.summary: The AI Upskilling Fund will support small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) by match-funding AI skills training for their employees.

instruments.name: EU Cloud Initiative
instruments.summary: Since 2016, the EU has been developing a blueprint for cloud-based services and world-class data infrastructure.

instruments.name: Standards for the Implementation of Inclusive AI Systems
instruments.summary: Document establishing the guidelines, strategies, and standards related to the implementation of inclusive AI systems

instruments.name: Airawat
instruments.summary: India's AI supercomputer AIRAWAT, ranked No. 75 globally in the Top 500 Supercomputing List (ISC 2023), showcases a significant advancement in AI and computational research.

instruments.name: Invest 2035: The Uk's Modern Industrial Strategy
instruments.summary: The UK government's new industrial strategy, Invest 2035, is a robust 10-year plan designed to provide the stability and certainty that businesses require to invest in high-growth sectors. Its aim is to attract a larger share of global investment in key areas and encourage domestic companies to increase their investments and expand, which is vital for achieving sustainable, inclusive, and resilient economic growth.

instruments.name: Declaration of Cooperation on AI
instruments.summary: Addressing this emerging trend, on 10 April 25 European countries signed a Declaration of cooperation on AI.

instruments.name: Sandbox on Privacy by Design and Default in AI
instruments.summary: Colombia has released its sandbox on Privacy by Design and Default in artificial intelligence (AI) projects.

instruments.name: fAIr LAC

instruments.name: Office for AI
instruments.summary: The UK Government has a dedicated "Office for AI" unit which collaborates with multiple departments, organisations and other stakeholders to drive responsible and innovative uptake of AI technologies for the benefit of everyone in the UK. It has now evolved into the AI Policy Directorate within the Department for Science, Innovation and Technology (DSIT).

instruments.name: AI Council
instruments.summary: The UK government created a senior AI Council as an independent expert committee to advise on how to stimulate the adoption of AI, promote its ethical use, and maximise its contribution to economic growth. The Council consisted of leaders from business, academia and civil society.

instruments.name: Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Serbia – Centre for Digital Transformation (National Project for Digital Transformation of Business)
instruments.summary: CDT is the main driving force for coordinating and implementing digital transformation in all industries within the private sector, with a special focus on small and medium-sized enterprises.

instruments.name: Recovery, Transformation, and Resilience Plan
instruments.summary: This plan states the post-COVID recovery plan, which puts AI in the heart of several initiatives.

instruments.name: Notice 15/V - 113 ("Notice on the Authorization to Test Automated Driving Systems")
instruments.summary: Notice 15/V was published for the authorization to test automated driving systems on road traffic.

instruments.name: Digital Rights Charter
instruments.summary: This charter presents a set of digital rights to be followed by institutions using digital technologies in their work.

instruments.name: Centre for Data Ethics and Innovation
instruments.summary: The Centre for Data Ethics and Innovation will have an explicit and unique mandate to advise the government on the measures which are needed to ensure safe and ethical innovation in data and AI. The Centre will not, itself, regulate the use of data and AI - its role will be to help ensure that those who govern and regulate the use of data across sectors do so effectively.

instruments.name: Responsible Technology Adoption Unit
instruments.summary: The Responsible Technology Adoption Unit (RTA), formerly the Centre for Data Ethics and Innovation (CDEI) leads the UK government's work to promote the trustworthy development and deployment of data-driven technology, including AI. The RTA sits within the Department for Science, Innovation and Technology (DSIT), and supports DSIT's broader mission to drive responsible innovation that changes lives and sustains economic growth.

instruments.name: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia
instruments.summary: Project financing is implemented in a manner that ensures competitiveness, quality, practical value, transparency, and the functionality of the results. Programs of the Science Fund support the professional development of researchers, integration into the international scientific and technological projects, and cooperation with the scientific diaspora and industry. Additionally, the programs ensure the protection of property rights for research results, protection of intellectual property,

instruments.name: Algorithmic Data in a Labor Environment
instruments.summary: Detailed guidelines outlining the rights and obligations of employees and employers in the context of algorithmic decision making in the workplace.

instruments.name: Autonomous Driving test Bed
instruments.summary: This regulation is envisaged by the latest amendments to the Law on Traffic Safety and Roads (hereinafter: ZOBS) and will provide a clear and predictable procedure for persons who want to test vehicles with an automated driving system in real traffic.

instruments.name: Alan Turing Institute
instruments.summary: Founded in 2015 as the UK's national institute for data science and AI, The Alan Turing Institute is an integral part of the UK government's approach to advancing safe, secure, and trustworthy AI, which was set out in the AI Sector Deal as part of the country's Industrial Strategy.

instruments.name: National Data Strategy
instruments.summary: The National Data Strategy will help ensure that people, businesses and organisations trust the data ecosystem, are sufficiently skilled to operate effectively within it, and can get access to data when they need it.

instruments.name: UNDP Support for AI
instruments.summary: In 2019, the Serbian government adopted a Strategy for the Development of  AI for the period 2020-2025. Through a dedicated project, UNDP has been actively supporting the government's ambitious AI agenda, which has included things like establishing the AI Institute and adopting an Ethical framework for Responsible AI Development. Despite substantial progress, there is still a need for ongoing dialogue regarding the possible benefits and risks associated with rapidly advancing technology

instruments.name: Industrial Strategy: Building a Britain Fit for the Future (White Paper)
instruments.summary: This document sets out the UK Government's plan to create an economy that boosts productivity and earning power throughout the UK.

instruments.name: National AI Strategy
instruments.summary: This Strategy builds on the UK's strengths but also represents the start of a step-change for AI in the UK, recognising the power of AI to increase resilience, productivity, growth, and innovation across the private and public sectors.

instruments.name: Government Technology Innovation Strategy
instruments.summary: This Strategy sets out the foundations needed for government to innovate through emerging technologies. It provides a framework for departments to use as they make plans for digital, data and technology ahead of the next spending review.

instruments.name: Serbian AI Society
instruments.summary: Gathering parts of the ecosystem with the aim of collaborating among participants-experts from different fields, sharing of ideas, developing skills and creating the best possible AI ecosystem.

instruments.name: AI Master Programmes
instruments.summary: The University of Novi Sad (Faculty of Technical Sciences and Faculty of Sciences), the University of Kragujevac, and the University of Ni (Faculty of Sciences and Mathematics and Faculty of Electronics) will offer master's degree programs in artificial intelligence for the first time in 2021.

instruments.name: Eleventh Development Plan
instruments.summary: The Eleventh Development Plan presents a long-term perspective based on the vision of stronger and more prosperous Turkey that produces more value added and shares more fairly. Over the Plan period, through a human centric, participatory, inclusive, accountable, transparent and efficient approach, it will be ensured that the objectives and goals set out in the Plan are bought in by all sections of the society and fundamental steps are taken to achieve the Plan's vision.

instruments.name: Plan for the Digitalisation of Public Administration
instruments.summary: This Plan for the Digitalization of Public Administrations represents a decisive leap forward in improving the effectiveness and efficiency of the Public Administration, transparency and the elimination of administrative obstacles through the automation of management. It places a greater focus on the personalisation of services and user experience, as well as acting as a catalyst for technological innovation in Spain from the public sphere.

instruments.name: KOBIGEL - SME Development Support Programme
instruments.summary: KOBIGEL is an enterprise development, growth and internationalisation support programme to increase the share and contribution of SMEs in the economy and to support the SME projects for improving their competitive power and the added value that they provide.

instruments.name: Spanish Agency for the Supervision of AI
instruments.summary: The Agency will be in charge of creating measures to protect citizens from possible risks arising from this technology, both with regard to their physical safety and that of their fundamental rights.

instruments.name: Spain's AI Advisory Council
instruments.summary: This initiative serves as an advisory body for analysis, advice, and support to the Spanish Government in the field of AI.

instruments.name: Turkish Brain Project
instruments.summary: This project will serve as a decision support system by offering the artificial intelligence algorithms considered to pave the way for many other practices in Turkey to the service of world of medicine.

instruments.name: Artificial Intelligence Ecosystem Call 2023
instruments.summary: This support model aims to facilitate collaboration between companies seeking artificial intelligence solutions and relevant stakeholders. The model encourages companies to form a consortium comprising a technology provider, a university research laboratory/center or a public research center/institute with expertise in artificial intelligence, and the Scientific and Technological Research Council of Turkiye Artificial Intelligence Institute.

instruments.name: Tubitaks RDI Support in AI
instruments.summary: TUBITAK has been publishing calls for project proposals on AI within its mission oriented support programmes since 2012, as well as in the scope of bottom up programs.

instruments.name: AI Education and Awareness Project
instruments.summary: Union of Chambers and Commodity Exchanges of Turkiye (TOBB) and Global AI Hub are collaborating for the AI Education and Awareness Project. It aims to increase qualified human resources and contribute to the AI ecosystem with the training to be given within the scope of the project.‹

instruments.name: COVID-19 Detection with AI
instruments.summary: Within the scope of this project, the estimates made by AI models (developed by the Presidency Digital Transformation Office), the reasoning behind these predictions were presented to relevant physicians, and the AI-model results are in accordance with the concept of explainability of artificial intelligence.

instruments.name: Twelfth Development Plan (2024-2028)
instruments.summary: The Twelfth Development Plan covers all areas of Turkiye development for the next four years from a holistic perspective and whole-of-government approach. One of the main priorities of the plan is digital technologies including AI.

instruments.name: Trustworthy AI Trust Stamp
instruments.summary: We have initiated to work on developing a trust stamp that indicates that trustworthy AI was used in the AI-enabled products to enhance customer trust. In this regard, studies on determining criteria and metrics continue with the Turkish Standards Institute. Expert group meetings are held and methodology determination activities are carried out by examining international studies.

instruments.name: Breast Cancer Detection With AI
instruments.summary: The benign and malignant anomalies in mammography images are labelled by radiologists using the labelling tool developed within the Presidency Digital Transformation Office. AI-models will continue to be developed with open source data sets.

instruments.name: Turkish Academy of Sciences Information Technologies and Communication Working Group
instruments.summary: Turkey Academy of Sciences (TUBA) has established the Working Group, drawing attention to the academic perspective needed a multi-dimensional approach has established a multi-disciplinary structure and the social problems as well as the economic benefits of technological developments.

instruments.name: The Medium Term Program (2024-2026)
instruments.summary: The Medium Term Program, which initiates the budget process, is a main policy document that covers macro policies, principles, the Government's macroeconomic targets, revenue and expenditure forecasts for the next three years, budget balance and debt levels, and appropriation ceilings for public administrative bodies.

instruments.name: The Digital Youth Artificial Intelligence Ecosystem
instruments.summary: The Digital Youth Artificial Intelligence Ecosystem was created to bring together student clubs related to artificial intelligence (AI) at universities affiliated with Y–K. The aim is to support the development of a qualified workforce in these fields through practice-based training, competitions, and post-training career awards.

instruments.name: Teknofest Aerospace and Technology Festival
instruments.summary: TEKNOFEST is Turkiye's's first and only aerospace and technology festival organized with the partnership of numerous organizations that play a crucial role in the development of national technology in Turkiye.

instruments.name: Ministry of Health Digital Strategy Framework and Roadmap
instruments.summary: The Ministry of Health Digital Strategy Framework and Roadmap aims to transform healthcare delivery in Saudi Arabia through digital health solutions, aligning with Vision 2030 and transitioning the Ministry to a regulatory and supervisory role.

instruments.name: SAFIR Depo Cloud Storage Software
instruments.summary: Safir Depo is a cloud computing-based, secure cloud storage software.

instruments.name: Innovation Fund Serbia
instruments.summary: The vision of the Fund is to, as a key state actor in the development of Serbia's innovation system, contribute to the country's economic growth by supporting innovation, strengthening the link between science and economy, establishing new and strengthening existing companies with innovative potential, through various financial instruments. The Fund's mission is to support the development of innovation through appropriate financial, technical and advisory support instrument

instruments.name: Digital Innovation Cooperation Platform
instruments.summary: The cooperation platform serves as a dynamic nexus, uniting public institutions, organizations, industrial entities, and R&D infrastructures engaged in the research, development, application, and dissemination of Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, Robotics, and related technologies. Its overarching mission is to expedite the implementation of multidisciplinary projects, leveraging national resources and opportunities to drive the creation of economic, technological, and social value.

instruments.name: Digital Government Strategy 2023-2030
instruments.summary: The Digital Government Strategy (2023-2030) defines the Kingdom's aspirations, vision, objectives, initiatives, and roadmap. Most strategic initiatives are geared towards achieving the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and the Saudi Vision 2030. The Strategy is also guided and aligned with the Saudi Vision 2030 goals and strategic objectives.

instruments.name: Türkiye Open Source Platform
instruments.summary: Established under the auspices of the Ministry of Industry and Technology, with the partnership of IT Valley and the Scientific and Technological Research Council of Turkiye Turkish Management Sciences Institute, the "Turkiye Open Source Platform" continues its activities to develop the open-source ecosystem with its stakeholders consisting of public and private sector companies, NGOs, universities, educational institutions, and communities.

instruments.name: National Intellectual Property Strategy (NIPST)
instruments.summary: The National Intellectual Property Strategy (NIPST) of Saudi Arabia is aimed at establishing a robust intellectual property ecosystem to drive innovation, competitiveness, and economic growth, in alignment with Vision 2030.

instruments.name: National AI Platform
instruments.summary: In accordance with the goals and measures of the Strategy for the Development of AI in the Republic of Serbia for the Period 2020-2025. In 2021, the Government of the Republic of Serbia provided the National Platform for AI (AI Platform), which is located in the State Data Center in Kragujevac.

instruments.name: National Biotechnology Strategy
instruments.summary: The National Biotechnology Strategy outlines Saudi Arabia's roadmap to becoming a global leader in biotechnology by 2040, aiming to enhance healthcare, boost economic growth, create jobs, and promote sustainability.

instruments.name: National Data Dictionary
instruments.summary: There are currently ongoing efforts to launch a National Data Dictionary (NDD) in order to solve a number of problems such as the challenges of integrating information systems of public institutions and organizations, duplicate and conflictive data, lack of a common language in information systems and unknown data ownership. The NDD has started the process of standardizing data, and a Data Dictionary Portal has been established under the auspices of the Digital Transformation Office.

instruments.name: National Data and AI Strategy
instruments.summary: Saudi Arabia revealed its National Strategy for Data & AI (NSDAI) which aims to make the country a global leader in Artificial Intelligence by 2030.

instruments.name: Turkish Natural Language Processing Project
instruments.summary: With this project, it is aimed to prepare the user-friendly and high-performance libraries and data sets required for the processing of Turkish texts and to establish the distribution infrastructure of the clusters, and to provide the data and tools.

instruments.name: AI Institute
instruments.summary: The Institute for Artificial Intelligence of Serbia's vision is to foster the development of creative leaders in the field of artificial intelligence, as well as to establish Serbia as a global center of excellence in scientific research and technology transfer related to machine learning and AI. The  Institute for AI for Serbia is to establish a distributed research and development organization that can utilize all available AI research resources in both Serbia and overseas.

instruments.name: National Framework for Artificial Intelligence in Digital Learning (AIDL)
instruments.summary: The "National Framework for Artificial Intelligence in Digital Learning in Saudi Arabia" serves as a strategic guide for integrating AI in education, emphasizing ethical and responsible AI use to enhance digital learning experiences.

instruments.name: AI Education Programme in Public Administration
instruments.summary: By implementing the training programme, and along with using modern forms and methods of work on professional devlopment, the Academy improves the competencies of employees working in public administration, required for good quality of business as usual. This ensures constant improvement of quality of the services provided by public administration to the citizens and business subjects.

instruments.name: Turkish National E-science E-infrastructure
instruments.summary: TRUBA, which has more than 1900 researchers from 114 different universities, provides direct service to contribute to scientific studies, carries out joint projects with different public institutions and research institutes and took part in 13 European Union Framework Programme Projects since its establishment, is an e-Infrastructure of strategic importance in the national sense.

instruments.name: AI In Secondary Education
instruments.summary: From 2021, students in the 7th and 8th grade of elementary schools have AI as part of two subjects in schools and an elective subject in high schools.

instruments.name: Data and Privacy Regulatory Sandbox Guidelines
instruments.summary: SDAIA's Data and Privacy Sandbox is a first of its kind regulatory Sandbox within the region to help position the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia as a leader for data and privacy compliance, innovation and experimentation by supporting entities who are creating products and solutions that utilize personal data in innovative and safe ways.

instruments.name: AI In Primary Education
instruments.summary: The Strategy for the Development of Artificial Intelligence in the Republic of Serbia from 2020 to 2025 defines the introduction of content on artificial intelligence into our educational system. As part of the curriculum in the seventh grade, the subjects Engineering and Technology and Informatics and Computing are compulsory.

instruments.name: Data and AI Glossary
instruments.summary: The project involves developing a comprehensive Data & AI Glossary, designed to standardize terminology and concepts, ensuring clear and consistent communication across the field of data science and artificial intelligence.

instruments.name: EUROHPC JU Marenostrum5 Supercomputer
instruments.summary: The European High Performance Computing Joint Undertaking (EuroHPC JU) has launched a call for tender for the procurement of a pre-exascale supercomputer. The system, called MareNostrum5, will be hosted by the Barcelona Supercomputing Center (BSC) and will be capable of executing at least 205 Petaflops, or at least 205 million billion calculations per second. Turkey jointly applied to the Precursors to Exascale call and obtained direct access to the supercomputer MareNostrum 5.

instruments.name: Cloud Computing and Big Data Research Laboratory
instruments.summary: The cloud computing and Big Data Research Laboratory - B3LAB, an affiliate of TUBITAK BILGEM - Institute of Information Technologies, is the research and development (R&D) laboratory in charge of cloud, big data and AI pillars of RDI ecosystem in Turkey.

instruments.name: Easy Export Platform Centre of Excellence of Data Analytics
instruments.summary: Users can identify and clean up data, increase data quality, make short-term and long-term forecasts, automate manual operations, use relationship dashboards to data scope, become data scientists, and minimise manpower. This system also helps policymakers to observe the statistics and changes easily.

instruments.name: Law on Protection of Personal Data
instruments.summary: The Law on the Protection of Personal Data No. 6698 was published in the Official Gazette on 7 April 2016. The Turkish Data Protection Authority was established under the same Law in Ankara.

instruments.name: National Occupational Standard Framework for Data and Artificial Intelligence (NOSF)
instruments.summary: National Occupational Standards are determinants of performance level that an individual must achieve when performing key job roles, including this performance's requirements of experience, knowledge and abilities that this particular individual needs to continue working at this occupational standard.

instruments.name: Emerging Technologies Regulatory Sandbox
instruments.summary: the Communications and Information Technology Commission (CITC) launched the Emerging Technologies Regulatory Sandbox to support investors and companies interested in the Kingdom's emerging tech field. The Regulatory Sandbox aims to increase investment, foster innovation, and maintain adequate consumer protection.

instruments.name: Human-centred Artificial Intelligence for Human Resources: A Toolkit for Human Resources Professionals
instruments.summary: Turkey collaborated closely with the WEF on the Human-Centred Artificial Intelligence for Human Resources project, contributing to the development of the report and toolkit. As the project leader for the Centre for the Fourth Industrial Revolution Turkey, Turkish experts from various public and private sectors, along with research institutions, played a significant role in the report. Additionally, Turk Traktor and Mercedes Benz Turk hosted pilot projects.

instruments.name: The implementing regulation of the Personal Data Protection Law
instruments.summary: The document is an executive regulation outlining the rules for implementing the Personal Data Protection Law in Saudi Arabia.

instruments.name: Focus Group on AI - Assembly of Turkish Scientist Abroad
instruments.summary: The Assembly plays an important role in bringing together the members of the Turkish science diaspora and the researchers working in Turkey, the event included a foresight study on AI in 2019.

instruments.name: Standard Contractual Clauses for Personal Data Transfer
instruments.summary: The Regulation on the Transfer of Personal Data Outside the Kingdom ("Transfer Regulation") sets out the provisions to be followed upon transfer, including the Clauses applied in cases where Controllers are exempted from the requirements to comply with the level of protection and the minimum level of transfer of Personal Data .

instruments.name: Romania's National Strategy on Artificial Intelligence (SN-IA) 2024–2027
instruments.summary: By Government Decision, an Inter-ministerial Commission for the Coordination of the Implementation of the strategy has been set up, made up of representatives of 34 central public institutions, whose meetings are chaired by a high-ranking representative of the Ministry. The Commission is responsible for monitoring and facilitating the implementation of the Strategy. The central public institutions are required to implement the action plan specific to their respective fields of action.

instruments.name: Regulation on Personal Data Transfer Outside the Kingdom
instruments.summary: Outline the provisions and procedures concerning the transfer of personal data outside the Kingdom to ensure an appropriate level of protection for personal data and the data subject's privacy.

instruments.name: Open Data Regulations
instruments.summary: The regulations set out the regulatory frameworks for open data, which is a subset of public information.

instruments.name: Action Plan on Human Rights
instruments.summary: The Action Plan on Human Rights sets certain aims, goals and activities in accordance with this background and framework. The Plan's point of origin is the state's obligation to protect, in all of its affairs and acts and with all of the state institutions and organisations, the physical and moral integrity and the honour and dignity of individuals.

instruments.name: Freedom of Information Regulations
instruments.summary: The regulations outline the fundamentals and guiding principles of data freedom and apply to requests made by individuals to access or obtain unprotected public data generated by public entities.

instruments.name: Data Classification Regulations
instruments.summary: The Regulations set the framework for classifying the data received, produced, or dealt with by public entities, regardless of their source, form, or nature.

instruments.name: 2023 Industry and Technology Strategy
instruments.summary: The Ministry of Industry and Technology published the 2023 Industry and Technology Strategy, which aims to carry out a program that covers the fields of industry and technology with a holistic approach and designed specifically according to the dynamics of the country, provides wide participation and mobilizes the society. The Strategy consists of five main pillars: High Technology and Innovation, Digital Transformation and Industry Move, Entrepreneurship, Human Capital and Infrastructure.

instruments.name: The Saudi Academic Framework for AI Qualifications Education Intelligence
instruments.summary: This initiative aims to be a guide for the development, evaluation, and accreditation of higher education programs in AI, serving as a reliable, primary reference recognised in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.

instruments.name: Y–K 100/2000 PhD Scholarship
instruments.summary: In order to meet the need of human resource in the priority areas of Turkiye, Council of Higher Education  offers a Ph.D. scholarship program to support students studying in doctoral programs in the state universities.

instruments.name: Guidance on Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) technologies based Medical Devices
instruments.summary: This guidance applies to Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) technologies that diagnose, manage or predict diseases by analyzing medical data.

instruments.name: Humane-AI-Net
instruments.summary: The HumanE AI Net brings together top European research centers, universities and key industrial champions into a network of centers of excellence that goes beyond a narrow definition of AI and combines world-leading AI competence with key players in related areas such as HCI, cognitive science, social sciences and complexity science. he researchers in HumaneAI are coming from53 institutions across 20 European countries.

instruments.name: Digital Government Regulatory Framework
instruments.summary: The Digital Government Regulatory Framework categorized as an organizational tool based on international best practices. With this framework, the main components of designing and strategically executing the digital government policy are created, and it works on unifying the concept of policies, standards, and guidelines of digital government.

instruments.name: Open Data Project
instruments.summary: Open Data Portal is a data sharing project that generates value from anonymized and private data to be offered to individuals and scientific community.

instruments.name: Deepfakes Guidelines
instruments.summary: This document provides comprehensive guidelines to address the implications of deepfake technologies and mitigate their associated risks by focusing on privacy, transparency, accountability, and social benefits.

instruments.name: Safe Schooling and Distance Education Project
instruments.summary: The project aims to enhance the capacity of the education system to provide e-learning equitably to school-age children during and following the COVID-19 pandemic and future shocks. In cooperation with the World Bank Group, within the education policies of the country, it is aligned to Turkey's Education Vision 2023, MoNE's Strategy Paper 20119-2023, and the 11th Development Plan.

instruments.name: National Strategy for Research, Innovation and Smart Specialisation 2021-2027
instruments.summary: To find niches (e.g. AI for health) during the entrepreneurial discovery process.

instruments.name: Maker Labs (Deneyap)
instruments.summary: The main purpose of Maker Labs is to equip young individuals with high technology skills. Secondary and high school students are trained for 36 months (free of charge) on several topics such as Design and Production, Robotics and Coding, Electronic Programming and the Internet of Things, Nanotechnology and Materials Science, and Aviation and Space Technologies at Maker Labs. We established 66 Maker Labs in 55 provinces of Turkiye by now.

instruments.name: AI Mirror Committee
instruments.summary: To effectively oversee the standardization efforts within the field of artificial intelligence and ensure that our country's perspectives and evaluations are duly incorporated, a Mirror Committee has been established. This committee brings together representatives from the public sector, private sector, academia, and NGOs.

instruments.name: Education Information Network
instruments.summary: EBA is a distance education platform prepared by the Ministry of National Education within the scope of the F.A.T.I.H. Project, which has been recently renewed and adapted to distance education during COVID-19.

instruments.name: Türkiye's Membership in Global Partnership on AI
instruments.summary: The Global Partnership on Artificial Intelligence (GPAI) is a multi-stakeholder initiative which aims to bridge the gap between theory and practice on AI by supporting cutting-edge research and applied activities on AI-related priorities. Built around a shared commitment to the OECD Recommendation on Artificial Intelligence, GPAI brings together engaged minds and expertise from science, industry, civil society, governments, international organisations and academia for international cooperation.

instruments.name: Centre for Fourth Industrial Revolution Türkiye
instruments.summary: C4IR Turkiye aims to implement a new vision that supports member companies in their transition to Industry 4.0 while fulfilling its traditional role as an industry association. The Centre is crucial in shaping national strategies for the Fourth Industrial Revolution and fostering public-private collaborations. Our primary focus areas include the Internet of Things, Robotics, Smart Cities, AI, and ML. Currently, we are working on projects to enhance the impact of Industrial IoT in SMEs.

instruments.name: AI Ethics Principles
instruments.summary: A practical guide to incorporating AI ethics throughout the AI system development life cycle.

instruments.name: National Strategic Framework in the Field of Artificial Intelligence 2023-2027
instruments.summary: The objective of the project implemented by the Authority for the Digitalization of Romania and University of Cluj-Napoca was to align international strategies for the use of innovative technologies in public administration with the national context and develop strategic directions for 2021–2027. These aimed to contribute to Romania’s future strategy regarding the adoption of digital technologies in the economy and society, while respecting human rights and promoting excellence and trust in AI.

instruments.name: Vision 2030 Program
instruments.summary: This initiative delivers an economic reform plan to stimulate new industries and diversify the economy, facilitate public-private business models and, ultimately, reduce the country's dependence on oil revenues. Vision 2030 views digital transformation as a key means to develop the economy by leveraging data, AI and industrial automation.

instruments.name: Freedom of Information Policy
instruments.summary: The policy and the regulations outline the fundamentals and guiding principles of data freedom and apply to requests made by individuals to access or obtain unprotected public data generated by public entities.

instruments.name: Data Classification Policy
instruments.summary: The Policy set the framework for classifying the data received, produced, or dealt with by public entities, regardless of their source, form, or nature.

instruments.name: HE Impact Of ICT and AI On the Evolution of Man and Society
instruments.summary: Institutional funding for public research

instruments.name: Digital Government Policy
instruments.summary: Create a comprehensive digital government ecosystem focused on beneficiaries.

instruments.name: AI Use Cases in the Public Sector
instruments.summary: This initiative groups several AI use cases in the Tunisian public sector.

instruments.name: National AI Strategy
instruments.summary: The National Artificial Intelligence Strategy has been prepared in line with the Eleventh Development Plan and the Presidential Annual Programs. The strategy reveals the measures that will put our country's work in the field of artificial intelligence (AI) on the common ground between the years 2021-2025 and the governance mechanism that will be established to implement these measures.

instruments.name: Personal Data Protection Law
instruments.summary: Saudi Arabia introduced a new standalone data protection law that addressed the regulation of privacy across the board.

instruments.name: Open Data Policy
instruments.summary: This initiative sets out the regulatory frameworks for open data, which is a subset of public information.

instruments.name: Public Procurement for Innovation
instruments.summary: A national roadmap to facilitate access to markets to start-ups.

instruments.name: National Data Index (NDI)
instruments.summary: The NDI is built to satisfy the data ecosystem requirements of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia (KSA) specifically. This comprehensive framework serves as a reliable metric and an influential indicator, aiding the realization of Vision 2030's objectives by contributing to becoming a smart nation and building a thriving economy, a vibrant society, and an ambitious nation.

instruments.name: Start-up Act
instruments.summary: The Start-up Act is a law enacted on 17 April 2018 that created a favorable framework for entrepreneurs, investors and start-ups structured around a "label" of merit.

instruments.name: Law On The Protection Of Personal Data
instruments.summary: Organic Law No. 2004-63 dated July 27, 2004 on the protection of personal data.

instruments.name: The Rules Governing the National Register of Controllers Within the Kingdom
instruments.summary: These rules aim to determine and understand the extent to which Controllers are obligated to register in the National Data Governance Platform.

instruments.name: Open Data Policy
instruments.summary: The 2016 access to information law is the baseline from which the Tunisian government started working on open data. The law was implemented as a result of the efforts and advocacy civil society in Tunisia.

instruments.name: Tunisia AI Roadmap
instruments.summary: This Roadmap states objectives and proposes an action plan for the development of AI in Tunisia.

instruments.name: Intellectual Property Policy for AI
instruments.summary: Draft amendment of the intellectual property law allowing the protection of algorithms.

instruments.name: Regulating Public Mas Media With Respect to AI Generated Content
instruments.summary: Media law is in the process of adopting special provisions to regulatealso use of AI in media, daling with miss- and diss- information, transparency, responsiblitiy and copyright.

instruments.name: Personal Data Processing Activities Records Guideline
instruments.summary: This guideline aims to assist entities in preparing records of personal data processing activities.

instruments.name: Personal Data Disclosure Cases Guideline
instruments.summary: Saudi Data & AI Authority (SDAIA) has issued this Guideline to assist entities in determining the cases and restrictions of personal data disclosure. This Guideline also provides clarifications regarding the restrictions on personal data disclosure. The terms and phrases used in this Guideline shall be construed in accordance with the definitions provided in the Law and its Implementing Regulations.

instruments.name: Personal Data Destruction, Anonymization, and Pseudonymisation Guideline
instruments.summary: This initiative aims to assist entities in determining the cases where personal data should be destroyed or anonymized. This Guideline also provides examples of techniques to aid in the destruction, anonymization and Pseudonymisation of personal data.

instruments.name: Minimum Personal Data Determination Guideline
instruments.summary: This initiative aims to provide the minimum personal data determination guidelines.

instruments.name: Guidelines for Binding Common Rules (BCR) for Personal Data Transfer
instruments.summary: The Regulation on the Transfer of Personal Data Outside the Kingdom ("Transfer Regulation") sets out the provisions to be followed upon transfer, including the Rules applied in cases where Controllers are exempted from the requirements to comply with the level of protection and the minimum level of transfer of Personal Data.

instruments.name: Bangkok Statement on the Ethics of Science and Technology and Sustainable Development
instruments.summary: The Statement was developed by participants of the Conference on the Ethics of Science and Technology and Sustainable Development held on 6 July 2019 in Bangkok, Thailand. It seeks to encourage regional economic communities, governments, academic institutions and professional associations, the private sector, civil society, and international organizations - especially UNESCO - to adhere to ethics of science and technology and sustainable development.

instruments.name: 12th National Economic and Social Development Plan
instruments.summary: The 12th NESDP aims to develop Science, Technology, Research, and Innovation to enhance the nation's economy and quality of life for its people.

instruments.name: Ethics Guidelines for AI
instruments.summary: Thailand's Ministry of Digital Economy and Society (DES) has drafted the country's first AI ethics guidelines and approved by cabinet in February 2021.

instruments.name: Guide to the Saudi Personal Data Protection Law for Controllers and Processors
instruments.summary: The Saudi Personal Data Protection Law (PDPL) outlines the rules for handling personal data to protect privacy, ensure data security, and enhance transparency, particularly for data controllers and processors‹.

instruments.name: Guide to the Saudi Personal Data Protection Law
instruments.summary: The Saudi Personal Data Protection Law (PDPL) sets out regulations for the protection of personal data and privacy, ensuring compliance with transparency, security, and legal obligations in data processing.

instruments.name: Generative Artificial Intelligence Guidelines Public
instruments.summary: The guidelines outline the benefits of using Generative AI, how to comply with AI Ethics Principles and the risks of Generative AI and ways to mitigate them.

instruments.name: AI Governance Guideline for Executives
instruments.summary: Practical AI governance guideline for organization executives to consider when implementing AI application within their organizations.

instruments.name: Generative Artificial Intelligence Guidelines for Government
instruments.summary: The guidelines for the Government offer regulatory guidance for Government employees regarding the responsible use and processing of Government data using generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools.

instruments.name: Elaboration and Developing Privacy Policy Guideline
instruments.summary: The Privacy Policy Guideline provides a framework for organizations to develop and implement privacy policies in compliance with the Saudi Personal Data Protection Law, ensuring transparency and protecting individuals' personal data.

instruments.name: AI Adoption Framework
instruments.summary: The AI adoption framework is a guiding reference that provides a comprehensive approach for AI adoption across all sectors. It aims to establish directions, guidelines, and identify key steps in according with best practices. The AI adoption framework helps ensure achievement of desired goals through the optimal and responsible use of AI

instruments.name: National Ethics Committee of Science and Technology
instruments.summary: The National Ethics Committee of Science and Technology was established to encourage the advancement of ethical science and technology for sustainable development.

instruments.name: Amendments to Personal Data Protection Law
instruments.summary: The Personal Data Protection Law (PDPL) of Saudi Arabia (KSA) was recently amended pursuant to Royal Decree No. M/148, dated 05/09/1444H (corresponding to 27 March 2023G) (Amended PDPL). These amendments were preceded by a public consultation launched by the Saudi Data and Artificial Intelligence Authority (SDAIA) in late 2022.

instruments.name: National Data Index Operational Excellence
instruments.summary: The National Data Index Operational Excellence document outlines the metrics and methodology for measuring the efficiency and effectiveness of data management operations across government entities in Saudi Arabia.

instruments.name: National Centre for AI
instruments.summary: The NCAI was established in August 2019, with its main mission to drive Saudi advancement in AI innovations by orchestrating AI research and solutions development, providing AI strategic advisory to the government, and promoting AI education and awareness.

instruments.name: ELEVATE Program
instruments.summary: This program, in cooperation with Google Cloud, aims to train 25,000 women globally on data and artificial intelligence (AI) domains.

instruments.name: Thailand National AI Strategy and Action Plan (2022 “ 2027)
instruments.summary: Vision: Thailand has an effective ecosystem to promote AI development and application to enhance the economy and quality of life within 2027.3 Goals:1) To develop human capacity and Technology2) To create economic growth3) To create social and environmental impact

instruments.name: European Lighthouse on Secure And Safe AI
instruments.summary: The "European Lighthouse on Secure and Safe AI" (ELSA) project networks excellent researchers from 26 top research institutions and companies in Europe to pool their expertise in the field of AI and machine learning.

instruments.name: Rules for Appointing Personal Data Protection Officer
instruments.summary: These rules clarify the cases in which a personal data protection officer must be appointed at controller to the application of the provisions of the personal data protection law and its implementing regulations, and the minimum requirements for appointment.

instruments.name: Interdepartmental Working Group on AI
instruments.summary: Within the framework of its "Digital Switzerland" strategy, the Swiss Federal Council established a working group within the federal administration on the subject of AI.

instruments.name: Digital Society Initiative
instruments.summary: Initiative housed at the University of Zurich to help shape the digital transformation of society and science through research, education, and public outreach.

instruments.name: Saudi Data and AI Authority
instruments.summary: The Saudi Data and Artificial Intelligence Authority (SDAIA) was established in 2019 as the owner of Saudi Arabia's national and artificial intelligence agenda, mandated with unlocking the value of data and AI to elevate Saudi Arabia as a pioneering nation among the elite league of data-driven economies. Addressing data, innovation and capability-building, SDAIA serves to foster the digital ecosystem while also supporting the suite of values-based G20 AI Principles.

instruments.name: National Data Management Office (NDMO)
instruments.summary: This initiative aims to establish data policies and standards, develop data governance mechanisms, and monitor compliance with these policies and standards, while also enhancing data management and protection capabilities.

instruments.name: Guidelines on AI
