instruments.summary: The guiding framework consists of the following seven guidelines:- Putting people at the heart of the matter- Conditions conducive to the development and use of AI- Transparency, traceability, and explainability- Liability- Security- Involvement of all relevant actors at national and international level

instruments.name: Swiss Supercomputer
instruments.summary: The Swiss National Supercomputing Centre, Hewlett Packard Enterprise, and NVIDIA are developing a new supercomputer, which will have seven times more powerful AI capabilities than the current leading system in the world.

instruments.name: Digital Switzerland Strategy
instruments.summary: The "Digital Switzerland" Strategy provides the guidelines for government action and indicates where and how authorities, academia, the private sector, civil society and politics must work together in order to shape the transformation process for the benefit of everyone in Switzerland.

instruments.name: VEGA HPC Super Computer
instruments.summary: With the HPC RIVR VEGA project, Slovenia is setting up supercomputer centre at PETA scale level. Project has clear orientation towards research that includes fields of artificial intelligence, processing big data (smart cities, IoT...), medicine, new materials, mechanical engineering and all other advanced science areas.

instruments.name: Mechanisms for Attracting Foreign and Returning Domestic Experts to Strengthen Slovenia's Position in Global Digitisation Trends
instruments.summary: Mechanisms for attracting foreign and returning domestic experts to strengthen Slovenia's position in global digitisation trends

instruments.name: Interministerial Working Group for Council of Europe Convention on Ai
instruments.summary: Interministerial working group includes representatives of the ministries of the Government of Slovenia.

instruments.name: Interministerial Working Group for AI Regulation
instruments.summary: Working group consistes of representatives of all involved ministries of Government of Slovenia and external experts

instruments.name: Establishing Protocols for the Use of Text and Speech Resources for the Development of Speech and Semantic Technologies, Taking Into Account Privacy and the Protection of Personal Data
instruments.summary: Establishing protocols for the use of text and speech resources for the development of speech and semantic technologies, taking into account privacy and the protection of personal data

instruments.name: Definition of a Model of Indicators for Monitoring the Potential of Ai Deployment in Slovenia
instruments.summary: Definition of an indicator model and methodology for assessing and monitoring the uptake of AI in the private and public sectors in Slovenia, with an overview of the situation in Slovenia (including an overview of stakeholders in Slovenia - public and private sector) and an analysis of the factors influencing the pace of AI uptake.

instruments.name: Demonstration of the Use of Artificial Intelligence for Teaching Different Subjects in Primary and Secondary Schools
instruments.summary: Developing educational content and examples of the use of artificial intelligence (AI) in various subjects in primary and secondary schools (e.g. Slovenian language, foreign languages, history, physics, chemistry, biology, fine arts), with an emphasis on practical demonstration of the usefulness of AI in teaching the content of these subjects.

instruments.name: Slovenian AI Society
instruments.summary: SLAIS (Slovenian Artificial Intelligence Society) is an association of researchers and practitioners in the field of Artificial Intelligence in Slovenia.

instruments.name: Defining a Framework to Ensure Public Trust in Ai Solutions Based on Different Socio-technological Factors
instruments.summary: Defining a framework for ensuring public trust in AI solutions based on socio-technological factors, based on the interaction between the technological characteristics of AI technologies, methodologies for developing and deploying AI solutions, standardisation, the use of different licensing modalities (open source, proprietary software), on the one hand, and ethical and legal principles, cultural and social characteristics and social status, on the other hand.

instruments.name: Slovenian AI Observatory
instruments.summary: Slovenian AI observatory, monitoring AI research, innovation and uptake status in Slovenia for monitoring implementation of NpUI.

instruments.name: NpUI Government working group
instruments.summary: Working group is the decision making group for implementation of National AI programme - NpUI.

instruments.name: International Research Centre for AI under the auspices of UNESCO
instruments.summary: The Centre would add focus and expertise on AI to UNESCO's programmes, particularly to leverage the power of AI for the sustainable development goals (SDGs).

instruments.name: National AI programme of Slovenia
instruments.summary: On 27 May 2021, the Slovenian government adopted its National AI programme.

instruments.name: Digital Uzbekistan - 2030
instruments.summary: Digital Uzbekistan - 2030 is a national strategy to use digital technologies to improve government services and daily life for all citizens. It aims to connect more people to fast internet, make online services widely available, and help the country become more modern and competitive. The initiative was created to reduce inequality, increase efficiency, and prepare Uzbekistan for the digital future.

instruments.name: Resolution About Measures for Creation of Conditions for the Accelerated Implementation of Technologies Of AI
instruments.summary: Uzbekistan adopted its first-ever decree on AI titled On measures to create conditions for the accelerated introduction of AI technologies," which outlines the creation of domestic ecosystem in the field of AI as well as the necessary regulatory and legal steps for its development.

instruments.name: Research Institute for the Development of Digital Technologies and AI
instruments.summary: The Research Institute for the Development of Digital Technologies and Artificial Intelligence has been established in Tashkent under the Ministry for the Development of Information Technologies and Communications of Uzbekistan.

instruments.name: AI Use Cases in the Public Sector
instruments.summary: This initiative lists different AI use cases in Uruguay's public sector.

instruments.name: Data Science and ML Roadmap
instruments.summary: A middle term roadmap for data science and ML development in Uruguay.

instruments.name: Data Policy and Strategy for Digital Transformation
instruments.summary: The Data Policy and Strategy establish the fundamental principles of government data as well as the organisational ecosystem to carry out a national data strategy, which promotes and develops specific projects in the matter. In order to make better use of the States data, it is important to advance in the establishment of a data strategy that establishes the bases of the initiative.

instruments.name: Public Sector Artificial Intelligence Observatory
instruments.summary: The Public Sector AI Observatory promotes the ethical and safe use of AI in Uruguay's government. It provides information on AI projects, shares clear guidelines for public institutions, and creates spaces for collaboration across sectors. The Observatory also monitors progress on national AI and data strategies to ensure responsible development.

instruments.name: National Artificial Intelligence Strategy 2024–2030
instruments.summary: Uruguay's AI Strategy promotes the safe and responsible use of artificial intelligence to benefit people and all sectors of society. It sets rules for how AI should be developed and used, builds national skills and infrastructure, and supports innovation. The goal is to use AI for inclusive growth, better public services, and sustainable development.

instruments.name: AI Strategy for the Digital Government
instruments.summary: This AI Strategy for the Digital Government presents the first actions to be carried out, through an open construction process, and shares what has been elaborated with different stakeholders to obtain their vision and contributions, both nationally and internationally.

instruments.name: Government of Uganda-Huawei Facial Recognition System
instruments.summary: In East Africa, the Republic of Uganda is partnering with China technology giant Huawei to launch a facial recognition surveillance system that uses AI to identify and log the identities of people walking around in public spaces.

instruments.name: Pulse Lab Kampala
instruments.summary: Pulse Lab Kampala combines traditional data sources with new technologies to gain greater insight into how to better serve people living on the African continent.

instruments.name: Expert National Task Force on the Fourth Industrial Revolution
instruments.summary: Uganda has set up a national task force to advise government on domesticating technological advance from the fourth industrial revolution to fast track the country's economic development.

instruments.name: Launch of the Artificial Intelligence (AI) Institute of South Africa and AI Hubs (University of Johannesburg and Tshwane University of Technology)
instruments.summary: South Africa is launching the Artificial Intelligence Institute to support digital innovation and skills. It is a partnership between the government and two universities”UJ and TUT”to help prepare the country for the future. This initiative follows expert recommendations to make South Africa a leader in new technologies.

instruments.name: Consensus Study on the Ethical, Legal, and Social Implications of Genetics and Genomics in South Africa
instruments.summary: Academy of Science of South Africa (ASSAf) undertook a consensus study on the ethical, legal and social implications of genetics and genomics work, as they relate to research, health service provision and forensic applications (medical and legal) in South Africa.

instruments.name: Presidential Commission on the Fourth Industrial Revolution
instruments.summary: Presidential Commission on Fourth Industrial Revolution consists of leaders from academia, business and civil society.

instruments.name: Centre for the Fourth Industrial Revolution South Africa
instruments.summary: The South African hub of the WEF C4IR network advances smart regulation for emerging technologies such as AI and blockchain, through collaboration with government regulators and the technology industry in South Africa.

instruments.name: Poland-Taiwan Scientific Co-operation
instruments.summary: Poland-Taiwan scientific co-operation is based on the agreement between the National Centre for Research and Development and the Ministry of Science and Technology of the Republic of China (originally established as the National Science Council of Taiwan) and consists in joint funding of scientific and R&D projects and organisation of scientific seminars, among others.

instruments.name: Policy for AI Development in Poland
instruments.summary: The Polish AI strategy supports the country's digital and economic growth by promoting AI development across society, business, science, education, international cooperation, and the public sector. It aims to prepare citizens and companies for a data-driven economy and improve digital skills. The strategy addresses challenges of AI adoption and sets goals for short, medium, and long-term progress to benefit all Poles.

instruments.name: National AI Policy: Call for Contributions
instruments.summary: The National Information Technology Development Agency (NITDA) is seeking the contributions of stakeholders to enable the development of the National Artificial Intelligence Policy (NAIP).

instruments.name: National Centre for AI and Robotics
instruments.summary: The National Centre for Artificial Intelligence and Robotics (NCAIR) is one of NITDA's special purpose vehicles created to promote research and development on emerging technologies and their practical application in areas of Nigerian national interest.

instruments.name: Mauritius AI Council
instruments.summary: The METC has four main strategic objectives:Boost the digital ecosystem, focusing on emerging technologiesSupport innovation with emerging technologiesAdvise the government on policies related to emerging technologiesCraft industry partnerships

instruments.name: Mauritius Artificial Intelligence AI Strategy
instruments.summary: The Mauritius AI Strategy outlines how AI could support key sectors like agriculture, health, FinTech, transport, and manufacturing. It identifies national challenges and opportunities through SWOT analysis. The strategy aimed to guide future development, though it lacked detailed implementation plans and was only partially followed up by the creation of the Mauritius Emerging Technologies Council.

instruments.name: Pilot Project on AI for Cancer Treatment
instruments.summary: The Healthcare Ministry of Kazakhstan and IBM have launched a pilot project on the use of artificial intelligence in health care, particularly in the field of oncology.

instruments.name: Road Map, Focused on the Development of Competencies
instruments.summary: Roadmap aimed the development of competencies in the field of smart technologies, artificial intelligence, integration of cyber-physical systems, energy of the future, design and engineering.

instruments.name: PhD Research and Training Grant Program
instruments.summary: Grants are awarded to projects addressing strategic issues related to the future of Kazakhstan in priority areas of scientific and technological development defined by Higher Scientific-Technical Commission under the Government of the Republic of Kazakhstan.

instruments.name: "Digital Kazakhstan" Government Programme
instruments.summary: Digital Kazakhstan is a programme aiming to elevate the living standards of each resident in the country using digital techniques. One key aspect of the program is "innovative ecosystem formation".

instruments.name: Project on Fostering Productive Innovation
instruments.summary: The Project on Fostering Productive Innovation is a partnership between Kazakhstan's government and the World Bank. It aims to support innovative projects and technology start-ups by improving national innovation institutions. The project helps create market-based support and encourages private sector involvement to boost innovation and economic growth.

instruments.name: Artificial Intelligence Research and Development Support Fund
instruments.summary: The Fund was created to attract the worlds leading manufacturers of artificial intelligence solutions to the Republic of Kazakhstan.

instruments.name: Smart Data UKIMET
instruments.summary: Smart Data Ukimet is a set of tools to monitor economic growth and implementation of government programs

instruments.name: National AI Strategy
instruments.summary: Indonesia's National AI Strategy from 2020 to 2045, now known as Stranas KA (Strategi Nasional Kecerdasan Artifisial), has been published.

instruments.name: National Laboratory for AI
instruments.summary: An AI co-operation declaration signed in 2020 seeks to explore the possibilities of establishing a national laboratory in Costa Rica.

instruments.name: Improvements in the Efficiency of Public Spending Through the Appropriate Use of Digital Technologies in the Costa Rican Public Sector
instruments.summary: The Central Administration is ordered and the Decentralized Administration is instructed to take the necessary technical and financial measures that allow them to plan, specify and implement technological solutions in accordance with the national reality.

instruments.name: The Development of the Digital Government of the Bicentenary
instruments.summary: A directive for the project formulation, articulation of actions, inter-institutional collaboration, and transversal generation of digital government capacity.

instruments.name: Regulation and Standardisation of Technology Acquisitions and/or Development of Management Support Computer Systems
instruments.summary: Guidelines to rationalize the use of public resources, especially those destined to the acquisition of electronic equipment, as well as those aimed at the development of computer programs and / or developments of computer systems to support its management.

instruments.name: Implementation of Accessible Websites in the Costa Rican Public Sector
instruments.summary: This guideline is meant to implement accessible websites in the Costa Rican public sector.

instruments.name: Creation of a High-Level Commission for Digital Government of the Bicentennial
instruments.summary: The optimization of processes and their interoperability, through the construction and implementation of new solutions that facilitate and expedite procedures and services.

instruments.name: Digital Transformation Strategy: The Bicentennial of Costa Rica
instruments.summary: This Strategy helps Costa Rica to build on and benefit from two major developments shaping productive processes and the quality of life of persons: the fourth industrial revolution and knowledge societies.

instruments.name: Taxonomy of Driving Automation for Vehicles
instruments.summary: China's six-level standards, called Taxonomy of Driving Automation for Vehicles, provides official definitions for self-driving cars from level zero (L0), which relies largely on human drivers, to L5 that achieves full driving automation.

instruments.name: National Standards for Autonomous Vehicle Testing
instruments.summary: China has issued a set of national standards for testing smart autonomous cars on roads. In 2021, new standards were published to replace old one.

instruments.name: Autonomous Driving Standards
instruments.summary: China has published its first national standards for grading autonomous driving, which will come into force in March 2022, providing a benchmark for carmakers to develop the futuristic technology.

instruments.name: Governance Principles for New Generation AI – Developing Responsible AI
instruments.summary: This initiative highlights the theme of developing responsible artificial intelligence, emphasizing the eight principles of harmony, friendliness, fairness, inclusiveness, respect for privacy, security and controllability, shared responsibility, open collaboration, and agile governance.

instruments.name: Ethical Norms for New Generation AI
instruments.summary: The following document, issued by a state AI governance committee, lays out ethical norms for the use of AI in China.

instruments.name: Chinese Association for AI
instruments.summary: The Association was established to support research on AI in China.

instruments.name: White Paper on Trustworthy AI
instruments.summary: The following White Paper co-authored by a PRC state think tank describes the importance and difficulty of improving the "trustworthiness" of AI systems.

instruments.name: Trustworthy Facial Recognition Applications and Protections Plan
instruments.summary: The CAICT is working with China's AI Industry Alliance, a government-sponsored industry body, to test and certify different kinds of AI systems.

instruments.name: Beijing Consensus on AI and Education
instruments.summary: The Beijing Consensus guides countries on how to use AI in education to improve learning and teaching. It helps schools, teachers, and students benefit from AI while ensuring fairness, ethics, and equal access. The initiative was created to support better education policies and skills development for the AI era.

instruments.name: Guiding Opinions on Strengthening Overall Governance of Internet Information Service Algorithms
instruments.summary: Nine agencies published objectives for regulating algorithms in Internet services, emphasizing business responsibility and party-state priorities.

instruments.name: Guiding Opinions on Strengthening Ethical Governance of Science and Technology
instruments.summary: In July 2021, MOST published guidelines that called for universities, labs, and companies to set up internal review committees to oversee and adjudicate technology ethics issues.

instruments.name: AI Innovation Action Plan for Institutions of Higher Education
instruments.summary: The action plan lays out a number of objectives designed to significantly enhance China's cadre of AI talent and its university AI curricula by 2030.

instruments.name: National New Generation AI Innovation and Development Pilot Zone
instruments.summary: The Zone will focus on exploring an innovative system to develop the AI technology and launching platforms for AI application through co-ordinating efforts of the government, academia, and the industry, aiming to develop AI-related theories, ideas, and talent.

instruments.name: National Engineering Laboratory for Deep Learning
instruments.summary: The laboratory was established to accelerate research related to AI.

instruments.name: National New Generation AI Promotion Office
instruments.summary: This Office is in charge of executing the Next Generation AI Development Plan and realising innovation with AI. It was established by the Ministry of Science and Technology and 14 other government agencies.

instruments.name: National New Generation AI Governance Specialist Committee
instruments.summary: The National New Generation AI Governance Specialist Committee is a Chinese expert advisory body established to guide the responsible development and use of AI. It brings together experts from academia, industry, and government to provide recommendations on ethical, legal, and governance issues. The initiative was launched to address growing concerns around AI safety, fairness, and social impact.

instruments.name: National Governance Committee for New Generation AI
instruments.summary: This Committee was established to research policy recommendations for AI governance and identify areas for international co-operation.

instruments.name: Three-Year Guidance for Internet Plus AI Plan
instruments.summary: China's Three-year Guidance for Internet Plus Artificial Intelligence Plan (2016-2018)' focuses on: i) enhancing AI hardware capacity, ii) strong platform ecosystems, iii) AI applications in important socioeconomic areas, and iv) AI's impact on society.

instruments.name: National New Generation AI Plan
instruments.summary: The Plan involves initiatives and goals for R&D, industrialization, talent development, education and skills acquisition, standard setting and regulations, ethical norms, and security.

instruments.name: Enterprise Incubator Foundation
instruments.summary: Enterprise Incubator Foundation (EIF) is one of the largest technology business incubators and IT/High-Tech development agencies in the region, operating in Armenia.

instruments.name: Armenia Digital Agenda – 2030
instruments.summary: The developers have explored the possibility for implementing digitization reforms in 6 key areas: infrastructure; digital management; digital transformation of the private sector; promotion of digital skills; development of the institutional system and cyber security.

instruments.name: Plans for Regional Diffusion of AI
instruments.summary: The government supports AI innovation to boost regional economies, especially outside the capital area. This initiative connects regional AI policies and projects to reduce the gap between capital and non-capital regions. It aims to help local industries grow and recover from challenges like COVID-19 through AI-driven solutions.

instruments.name: Implementation Strategy for Trustworthy AI
instruments.summary: The Implementation Strategy for Trustworthy AI aims to build social trust in AI by addressing risks like bias and privacy concerns. It supports the growing AI industry by setting clear ethical standards and guiding the private sector to use AI responsibly. Developed by the government, this initiative helps ensure AI innovation benefits society while minimizing potential harms.

instruments.name: Regulatory Sandbox
instruments.summary: Objectives:To test out new technologies and services in the real market.To allow the government to improve related regulations based on real-life data.

instruments.name: The National Guidelines for AI Ethics
instruments.summary: The South Korean government and the National Information Society Agency (NIA) have established the Ethics Guidelines for the Intelligent Information Society to establish a new code of ethics to proactively respond to the social and cultural impacts and dysfunctions of intelligent information technologies such as AI.

instruments.name: Human-Centered National Guidelines for AI Ethics
instruments.summary: The Human-Centered National Guidelines for AI Ethics set government standards to ensure AI technology is used responsibly and fairly. It aims to protect people from risks like bias, discrimination, and privacy violations while supporting AI innovation. This initiative benefits society by promoting trustworthy AI that improves quality of life and industry productivity.

instruments.name: AI Open Innovation Hub
instruments.summary: AI Hub is an AI integration platform that anyone can utilize and participate in by supporting AI infrastructure (AI data, AI SW API, and computing resources) necessary for the development of AI technologies and products and services.For users of the AI hub, we provide infrastructure services for development and utilization and services for AI activation.

instruments.name: Presidential Committee on the Fourth Industrial Revolution
instruments.summary: The Presidential Committee on the Fourth Industrial Revolution (PCFIR) helps guide Korea through rapid technological changes like AI. It supports businesses by creating a safe space for innovation and learning from trial and error. This initiative aims to boost Korea's global competitiveness and help industries adapt to new digital challenges.

instruments.name: National Strategy for AI
instruments.summary: While machines replaced manual labour of humans during the industrialization in the past, artificial intelligence now is developing beyond automation to a level that can perform intelligent tasks that could only be done by humans. As AI is causing a paradigm shift not only in terms of technology but one that encompasses all sectors including humanities, Korea is preparing for the shift on national and social levels.

instruments.name: Mid- to Long-Term Government R&D Investment Strategy
instruments.summary: It is necessary to break down high-cost and low-efficiency structures lacking qualitative outcomes relative to the high R&D investment ratio and secure a driving force for new growth. In line with the changes in the policy environment such as the arrival of the Fourth Industrial Revolution and the increased social importance of science and technology, the focus of the national R&D system needs to shift from economic growth to people and society

instruments.name: Korean New Deal
instruments.summary: The Korea New Deal aims to boost the economy and create jobs by focusing on digital and contact-free industries. It was developed to respond to the COVID-19 crisis and speed up digital transformation in Korea. This initiative benefits businesses and workers by improving data infrastructure and expanding high-speed internet access.

instruments.name: Data & AI-Driven Economy Promotion Plan
instruments.summary: South Korea's initiative aims to improve the data and AI ecosystem by addressing shortages of quality data and skilled AI researchers. It supports better data sharing and stronger use of AI across industries and society. This effort helps businesses, researchers, and policymakers benefit from advanced AI technologies and a connected data market.

instruments.name: AI R&D Strategy
instruments.summary: AI is a core technology of the Fourth Industrial Revolution, which will revolutionize the entire economy and society. In this context, this initiative has been developed to come up with a national strategy for securing national competitiveness in AI.

instruments.name: 6th National Informatisation Master Plan for an Intelligent Information Society
instruments.summary: Korea's 6th National Informatization Master Plan aims to accelerate digital transformation and improve public services using intelligent technologies. It was developed to address fragmented e-government systems and limited use of data and smart technologies. The plan benefits citizens, businesses, and government by promoting innovation, building trust, and creating a human-centered digital society.

instruments.name: Plan to Respond to the Fourth Industrial Revolution for Innovative Growth (I-Korea 4.0)
instruments.summary: This initiative is the current Administrations grand S&T strategy or policy direction to respond to the Fourth Industrial Revolution.

instruments.name: Al-Khwarizmi Program
instruments.summary: The Al-Khwarizmi Program is a national Moroccan initiative that supports research in artificial intelligence and big data. It funds 45 projects from 15 universities to solve real-life problems in areas like health, agriculture, and education. The goal is to boost innovation and help different sectors benefit from new technologies.

instruments.name: Strategy for Developing an AI Ecosystem
instruments.summary: Establishing a strategy and a national roadmap for developing an AI Ecosystem.

instruments.name: Technological sandbox on the use of exponential technologies in selection procedures for the contracting of goods, services, and execution of works, in a scalable manner for the members of the National Digital Transformation System
instruments.summary: Use of technologies that allow massive processing of all available contracting information, to automate and forecast, identify patterns, and detect anomalies that help identify possible irregular practices through innovative algorithms based on Big Data and AI.

instruments.name: Public-private regulatory sandbox regarding the use of unmanned vehicles reliably for members of the National Digital Transformation System, with emphasis on the public and private sectors
instruments.summary: The project covers: improving the integration between the different modes of transport (administrative, regulatory, or value-added), providing a benefit to citizens who use these services (quality, availability, cost reduction, or safety), increasing the effectiveness and efficiency of operators, or advance in aspects linked to sustainability, social inclusion or emissions reduction.

instruments.name: National Center for Innovation and Artificial Intelligence
instruments.summary: It is a national center of excellence in artificial intelligence, in response to the need for human talent and with the aim of accelerating the development and adoption of AI, which will carry out research, development, socialization and innovation by adopting Artificial Intelligence, coordinating its activities with the national and international academic sector, the private and public sectors, considering the sectors where Peru has competitive advantages, whether due to biodiversity, key econo

instruments.name: COVID-19 Use of AI
instruments.summary: This initiative lists AI innovation during Covid-19 in Peru.

instruments.name: Law 31814, Law that promotes the use of artificial intelligence in favor of the economic and social development of the country
instruments.summary: It is a law to promote the safe, transparent, responsible, and respectful use of human rights of artificial intelligence, which establishes the Presidency of the Council of Ministers, through the Secretariat of Government and Digital Transformation (PCM-SGTD) as the technical-regulatory authority at the national level in charge of directing, evaluating and supervising the use and promotion of the development of AI.

instruments.name: Draft Regulation of Law No. 31814, Law that promotes the use of artificial intelligence in favor of the economic and social development of the country
instruments.summary: Proposed Regulation of Law 31814 that develops measures to promote the safe, ethical, sustainable, transparent, replicable, and responsible use and development of artificial intelligence.

instruments.name: Digital Trust Framework, approved by Urgent Decree N. 007-2020
instruments.summary: Article 12.2 provides that public entities and private sector organizations ensure the ethical use of artificial intelligence.

instruments.name: Check Your Plan-telecommunication Services Price Comparison Tool
instruments.summary: Digital tool that allows users to compare telecommunication services prices and characteristics in a simple and friendly way; includes data (GB)/internet speed calculator and chatbot.

instruments.name: National Network of Open Access Digital Repositories of Science, Technology and Innovation
instruments.summary: A national network for open access repositories connecting 49 institutions and providing access to close to 50,000 publications and datasets.

instruments.name: Open-source artificial intelligence algorithm service is provided continuously for the Members of the National Digital Transformation System, with emphasis on public entities at the three levels of government
instruments.summary: Continuous service enabled for public institutions that, through the use of algorithms based on AI, seeks to expedite the national and international comparative analysis of regulation in digital technologies and the development of regulatory projects.

instruments.name: National Open Data Platform
instruments.summary: The National Open Data Platform publishes government data produced, processed, stored and / or collected on digital platforms from all public entities of Peru.

instruments.name: Punku - Open Data Portal
instruments.summary: Open data site with a computing tool that allows users to obtain statistical reports of the main indicators in the telecommucation markets (economic and financial performance, and user complaints).

instruments.name: NSF Program on Fairness in AI
instruments.summary: NSF and Amazon are partnering to jointly support computational research focused on fairness in AI, with the goal of contributing to trustworthy AI systems that are readily accepted and deployed to tackle grand challenges facing society.

instruments.name: National Robotics Initiative
instruments.summary: The Initiative supports research that promotes integration of robots to the benefit of humans, as well as human safety and independence.

instruments.name: National AI R&D Strategic Plan: 2019 Update
instruments.summary: This Plan this 2019 Update to the National AI R&D Strategic Plan is, by design, solely concerned with addressing the R&D priorities associated with advancing AI technologies.

instruments.name: National AI R&D Strategic Plan
instruments.summary: This purpose of this Plan is to convey a clear set of R&D priorities that address strategic research goals, focus Federal investments on those areas in which industry is unlikely to invest, and address the need to expand and sustain the pipeline of AI R&D talent.

instruments.name: Big Data to Knowledge
instruments.summary: The Big Data to Knowledge (BD2K) program supports the R&D of innovative and transformative approaches and tools to maximise and accelerate the utility of big data and data science in biomedical research.

instruments.name: "AI Next" Campaign
instruments.summary: In September 2018, DARPA announced a multi-year investment of more than $2 billion on AI R&D in a portfolio of some 50 new and existing programs collectively called the AI Next campaign.

instruments.name: Quad Principles on Technology Design, Development, Governance, and Use
instruments.summary: The Quad countries (Australia, India, Japan, and the United States of America) affirm that the ways in which technology is designed, developed, governed, and used should be shaped by our shared democratic values and respect for universal human rights.

instruments.name: Proposed Regulatory Framework for Modifications to AI/ML-Based Software as a Medical Device
instruments.summary: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is considering a total product lifecycle-based regulatory framework for AI/ML technologies that would allow for modifications to be made from real-world learning and adaptation, while still ensuring that the safety and effectiveness of the software as a medical device is maintained.

instruments.name: Unmanned Aircraft Systems Integration Pilot Program
instruments.summary: The Program promotes the safe operation of unmanned aircraft systems (UAS) and enables the development of UAS technologies for use in agriculture, commerce, emergency management, human transportation, and other sectors.

instruments.name: AI Researchers Portal
instruments.summary: To connect AI researchers to Federal resources that can support their AI work “ from grant funding and datasets to computing and testbeds.

instruments.name: White House Summit on AI in Government
instruments.summary: On 9 September 2019, the White House hosted its Summit on AI in Government.

instruments.name: White House Summit on AI for American Industry
instruments.summary: The Summit brought together over 100 senior government officials, technical experts from top academic institutions, heads of industrial research labs and American business leaders who are adopting AI technologies to benefit their customers, workers, and shareholders.

instruments.name: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2022
instruments.summary: The NDAA is an annual bill that Congress passes specifying the budget, expenditures, and policies of the U.S. Department of Defense (DOD).

instruments.name: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021
instruments.summary: The NDAA established the National AI Initiative to co-ordinate the ongoing AI research, development, and demonstration activities among stakeholders.

instruments.name: U.S. Patent and Trademark Office Report on Public Views on AI and Intellectual Property Policy
instruments.summary: The Report takes a comprehensive look at a wide variety of stakeholder views on the impact of AI across the intellectual property (IP) landscape, including patent, trademark, copyright, and trade secret policy, as well as developing issues about database protection.

instruments.name: Request for Information and Comment on Financial Institutions' Use of AI, Including ML
instruments.summary: The agencies are gathering information and comments on financial institutions'use of AI, including ML.

instruments.name: Plan for Federal Engagement in Developing Technical Standards and Related Tools
instruments.summary: The Plan recommends that the Federal government commit to deeper, consistent, long-term engagement in activities to help the U.S. speed the pace of reliable, robust, and trustworthy AI technology development.

instruments.name: NITRD-NAIIO Supplement to the President's FY2022 Budget
instruments.summary: In response to the National AI Initiative Act (NAIIA) of 2020, the FY2022 Supplement provides the status of R&D investments and activities in support of the NAIIA, including details of the National AI Research Institutes.

instruments.name: NITRD Supplement to the President's FY2020 Budget
instruments.summary: The NITRD Supplement to the President's FY2020 Budget outlines federal priorities for research in networking and information technology, including AI. It helps coordinate funding and goals across multiple government agencies. The initiative aims to advance innovation, security, and economic growth through strategic investment in emerging technologies.

instruments.name: NIST Principles for Explainable AI
instruments.summary: The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) developed a draft report intended to stimulate a conversation about what NIST should expect of decision-making devices, as part of a broader NIST effort to help develop trustworthy AI systems.

instruments.name: National Security Commission on AI
instruments.summary: This is an independent Commission to consider the methods and means necessary to advance the development of AI, ML, and associated technologies to comprehensively address the national security and defense needs of the U.S.

instruments.name: Memorandum to Heads of Agencies on Regulatory and Non-Regulatory Approaches to AI
instruments.summary: This Memorandum sets out policy considerations that should guide, to the extent permitted by law, regulatory and non-regulatory approaches to AI applications developed and deployed outside of the Federal government.

instruments.name: Government by Algorithm: AI in Federal Administrative Agencies
instruments.summary: The Administrative Conference of the United States (ACUS) commissioned this report, which includes: a rigorous canvass of AI use at the 142 most significant Federal departments, agencies, and sub-agencies; a series of in-depth but accessible case studies of specific AI applications at seven leading agencies covering a range of governance tasks; and a set of cross-cutting analyses of the institutional, legal, and policy challenges raised by agency use of AI.

instruments.name: Defense Innovation Board AI Principles
instruments.summary: The leadership of the Department of Defense (DoD) tasked the Defense Innovation Board (DIB) with proposing AI Ethics Principles for the Department for the design, development, and deployment of AI for combat and non-combat purposes.

instruments.name: Request for Information for Identifying Priority Access or Quality Improvements for Federal Data and Models for AI R&D and Testing
instruments.summary: Under the Executive Order on Maintaining American Leadership in AI (Section 5.a.i), the Office of Management and Budget is inviting the public to identify needs for additional access to - or improvements in the quality of - Federal data and models that would improve the Nation's AI R&D and testing efforts.

instruments.name: U.S. AI COVID-19 Response
instruments.summary: The United States is leveraging AI technologies - including increased access to data and computing resources - to respond to the COVID-19 pandemic.

instruments.name: Automated Vehicles 3.0: Preparing for the Future of Transportation
instruments.summary: Automated Vehicles (AV 3.0) introduces guiding principles and describes the Department's strategy to address existing barriers to safety innovation and progress.

instruments.name: Joint AI Center
instruments.summary: The U.S. Department of Defense established the JAIC to seize upon the transformative potential of AI technology for the benefit of America's national security.

instruments.name: Department of Defense AI Strategy
instruments.summary: The Department of Defense (DoD) AI Strategy directs the Department to accelerate the adoption of AI and the creation of a force fit for our time.

instruments.name: Next-Generation Non-Surgical Neurotechnology Programme
instruments.summary: The U.S. Defence Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) has officially funded a programme to develop a brain-to-machine interface “ in the form of a headset designed to let military personnel control weapons through brain activity alone.

instruments.name: Explainable AI Program
instruments.summary: The Explainable AI (XAI) Program in the United States was launched by the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) to make AI systems more understandable and trustworthy. It aims to help humans better interpret and use AI decisions, especially in high-stakes areas like defense or healthcare. The initiative addresses the problem of black box AI systems that provide results without clear explanations.

instruments.name: Federal 5-Year STEM Education Strategic Plan
instruments.summary: This document presents the Federal government's five-year strategic plan for STEM education, based on a vision for a future where all Americans will have lifelong access to high-quality STEM education and the U.S. will be the global leader in STEM literacy, innovation, and employment.

instruments.name: NSF Funding Opportunities with Special Emphasis on AI
instruments.summary: The National Science Foundation (NSF) provides funding opportunities in the following areas: AI and Society (supported jointly with the Partnership on AI); Fairness, Ethics, Accountability, and Transparency; NSF Program on Fairness in AI in Collaboration with Amazon; and Real-Time ML.

instruments.name: Local, State, and Federal Regulations on Facial Recognition Technologies
instruments.summary: The U.S. has started implementing regulation on facial recognition technologies at the local, state and federal level.

instruments.name: Face Recognition Vendor Test
instruments.summary: The Face Recognition Vendor Test includes a series of large-scale independent evaluations for face recognition systems.

instruments.name: Accelerating Medicines Partnership
instruments.summary: The Accelerating Medicines Partnership (AMP) program is a public-private partnership between the National Institutes of Health (NIH), the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA), multiple biopharmaceutical and life science companies, non-profit, and other organizations to transform the current model for developing new diagnostics and treatments.

instruments.name: Voluntary Commitments
instruments.summary: The United States encourages AI companies to commit voluntarily to high standards for safety, security, and transparency. This initiative helps ensure AI technology is developed responsibly without risking people's rights or safety. It benefits everyone by promoting trustworthy and secure AI that supports innovation while protecting the public.

instruments.name: PCAST Generative AI Working Group
instruments.summary: The PCAST Generative AI Working Group advises the President on the safe and fair use of generative AI technology. It helps identify risks and opportunities to guide responsible development and deployment. This initiative benefits the public by promoting AI that is trustworthy and used fairly.

instruments.name: NIST AI Public Working Groups
instruments.summary: This working group builds on the success of the NISTAI Risk Management Framework to address rapidly advancing AI technologies. The PublicWorking Group on Generative AI will help address the opportunities and challenges associatedwith AI that can generate content, such as code, text, images, videos and music. The publicworking group will also help NIST develop key guidance to help organizations address the specialrisks associated with generative AI technologies.

instruments.name: Artificial Intelligence and Algorithmic Fairness Initiative
instruments.summary: The Equal Employment Opportunity Commission has launched an agency-wide initiative to ensure that the use of AI complies with American anti-discrimination laws.

instruments.name: New York, Electronic Monitoring Bill
instruments.summary: New York passes law requiring every private-sector employ of its electronic monitoring practices

instruments.name: National AI Initiative Act of 2020
instruments.summary: The National AI Initiative Act of 2020 (DIVISION E, SEC. 5001) became law on 1 January 2021, providing for a co-ordinated program across the entire Federal government to accelerate AI research and application for the Nation's economic prosperity and national security.

instruments.name: Maryland Facial Recognition Law
instruments.summary: Maryland requires employers to secure consent to the use of facial recognition services during interviews

instruments.name: Illinois Artificial Intelligence Video Interview Act
instruments.summary: Illinois enacted a law that requires employers to disclose the use of AI analysis in video interviews.

instruments.name: Delaware Electronic Monitoring Law
instruments.summary: Delaware state law requires employers to provide electronic notice of monitoring employees' telephone calls, electronic mail, and Internet usage

instruments.name: Connecticut Electronic Monitoring Law
instruments.summary: Connecticut law requires employers to give advance written notice before monitoring their electronic notice

instruments.name: CHIPS for America Act
instruments.summary: This bill establishes investments and incentives to support U.S. semiconductor manufacturing, R&D, and supply chain security.

instruments.name: Automated Employment Decision Tool Law
instruments.summary: New York City law places compliance obligations on employers in New York City that use AI tools.

instruments.name: AI Training for the Acquisition Workforce Act (Bill S-2551)
instruments.summary: This Bill requires the Director of the Office of Management and Budget to establish or otherwise provide an AI training program for the acquisition workforce and for other purposes.

instruments.name: Federal Trade Commission Consumer Protection and Competition Investigations (Bias in Algorithms and Biometrics)
instruments.summary: In 2021, the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) designated eight key areas of focus for enforcement and regulatory action, one of which directly implicate investigations in unfair, deceptive, anticompetitive, collusive, coercive, predatory, exploitative, or exclusionary acts or practices relating to algorithms and biometrics.

instruments.name: Declaration of U.S.-UK Co-operation in AI R&D
instruments.summary: Building on the U.S.-UK Science and Technology Agreement signed in September 2017, this Declaration communicates the U.S. and the UK's intention to advance their shared vision and work towards an AI R&D ecosystem.

instruments.name: National Artificial Intelligence Research Resource Pilot
instruments.summary: The NAIRR pilot brings together computational, data, software, model, training and user support resources to demonstrate and investigate all major elements of the NAIRR vision first laid out by the NAIRR Task Force.

instruments.name: Materials Genome Initiative
instruments.summary: The Materials Genome Initiative is a multi-agency initiative designed to create a new era of policies, resources, and infrastructures for materials research.

instruments.name: State Department Guidance on Products or Services With Surveillance Capabilities
instruments.summary: This guidance is a tool intended to provide practical and accessible human rights guidance to U.S. businesses seeking to prevent their products or services with surveillance capabilities from being misused by government end-users to commit human rights abuses.

instruments.name: Policies That Regulate FinTech Innovation
instruments.summary: The increased use of data and ML algorithms in financial products and services can empower the American people by helping them make more informed decisions about their short-term and long-term financial goals.

instruments.name: Federal Automated Vehicles Policy
instruments.summary: This Policy has been issued as agency guidance rather than in a rulemaking in order to speed the delivery of an initial regulatory framework and best practices to guide manufacturers and other entities in the safe design, development, testing, and deployment of highly automated vehicles (HAVs).

instruments.name: Executive Order on the Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence
instruments.summary: President Biden is issuing a landmark Executive Order to ensure that America leads the way in seizing the promise and managing the risks of artificial intelligence (AI). The Executive Order establishes new standards for AI safety and security, protects Americans' privacy, advances equity and civil rights, stands up for consumers and workers, promotes innovation and competition, advances American leadership around the world, and more.

instruments.name: Executive Order on Maintaining American Leadership in AI
instruments.summary: This Executive Order outlined the policy of the U.S. government to sustain and enhance the scientific, technological, and economic leadership position of the U.S. in AI R&D and deployment through a co-ordinated Federal government strategy, the American AI Initiative.

instruments.name: AI Clause in Executive Order on Advancing Racial Equity and Support for Underserved Communities Through the Federal Government
instruments.summary: Among other requirements, the Order places new equity obligations on federal agencies that deploy AI systems, and directs agencies to "prevent and remedy discrimination, including by protecting the public from algorithmic discrimination.

instruments.name: AI/ML-Based Software as a Medical Device Action Plan
instruments.summary: The Action Plan is a direct response to stakeholder feedback to the April 2019 discussion paper, Proposed Regulatory Framework for Modifications to AI/ML-Based Software as a Medical Device (SaMD)," and builds on the Agency's longstanding commitment to support innovative work in the regulation of medical device software and other digital health technologies.

instruments.name: R&D Workforce Training
instruments.summary: Federal departments and agencies that invest in AI R&D have defined AI as a priority area within Federal fellowship, training, and service programs.

instruments.name: Addition of Software Specially Designed to Automate the Analysis of Geospatial Imagery to the Export Control Classification Number 0Y521 Series
instruments.summary: In this interim final rule, the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) amends the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) to make certain items subject to the EAR and to impose a license requirement for the export and re-export of those items to all destinations, except Canada.

instruments.name: Strategy for Augmenting Intelligence Using Machines
instruments.summary: The Augmenting Intelligence Using Machines (AIM) Strategy provides the framework for the incorporation of AIM technologies to accelerate mission capability development across the Intelligence Community.

instruments.name: Executive Order on Promoting the Use of Trustworthy AI in Federal Government
instruments.summary: On 3 December 2020, President Donald J. Trump signed the Executive Order on Promoting the Use of Trustworthy Artificial Intelligence in the Federal government, which establishes guidance for Federal agency adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI).

instruments.name: National AI Research Institutes
instruments.summary: Led by NSF, and in partnership with the U.S. Department of Agriculture National Institute of Food and Agriculture, the U.S. Department of Homeland Security, Google, Amazon, Intel and Accenture, the National AI Research Institutes will act as connections in a broader nationwide network to pursue transformational advances in a range of economic sectors, and science and engineering fields ” from food system security to next-generation edge networks.

instruments.name: Human Interpretable Attribution of Text Using Underlying Structure Program
instruments.summary: The goal is for HIATUS to be multilingual and capable of differentiating authors based on stylistic features such as word choice, sentence phrasing, and organization of information.

instruments.name: Centers of Excellence in Regulatory Science and Innovation
instruments.summary: The Food and Drug Administration's(FDA) Centers of Excellence in Regulatory Science and Innovation (CERSIs) are collaborations between FDA and academic institutions to advance regulatory science through innovative research, training, and scientific exchanges.

instruments.name: Department of Energy AI and Technology Office
instruments.summary: The vision behind the AI and Technology Office is to transform the U.S. Department of Energy into a world-leading AI enterprise by accelerating the research, development, delivery, and adoption of AI.

instruments.name: National AI Research Resource Task Force
instruments.summary: The Task Force will write the road map for expanding access to critical resources and educational tools that will spur AI innovation and economic prosperity in the U.S.

instruments.name: National AI Initiative Office
instruments.summary: In January 2021, the White House established the National AI Initiative Office to implement a national AI strategy, co-ordinating AI research and policymaking across government, industry and academia.

instruments.name: Chief Digital and AI Office
instruments.summary: Stood up in February 2022 by integrating the Joint Artificial Intelligence Center (JAIC), Defense Digital Services (DDS), the Chief Data Officer, and the enterprise platform Advana into one organization, the CDAO is building a strong foundation for data, analytic, and AI-enabled capabilities to be developed and fielded at scale.

instruments.name: AI R&D Interagency Working Group
instruments.summary: AI R&D IWG was formed in 2018 to co-ordinate Federal AI R&D across 32 participating agencies and to support activities tasked by both the Select Committee on AI and the Machine Learning and AI Subcommittee (MLAI-SC).

instruments.name: U.S.-EU Trade and Technology Council
instruments.summary: The United States and European Union affirm their willingness and intention to develop and implement AI systems that are innovative and trustworthy and that respect universal human rights and shared democratic values.

instruments.name: Select Committee on AI
instruments.summary: The Select Committee on AI, created in June 2018, advises the White House on interagency AI R&D priorities and improving the co-ordination of Federal AI efforts to ensure continued U.S. leadership in this field.

instruments.name: National AI Advisory Committee's Subcommittee on Law Enforcement
instruments.summary: As directed by the National AI Initiative Act of 2020 (DIVISION E, SEC. 5104e), the National AI Advisory Committee will establish a subcommittee that will consider matters related to the use of AI in law enforcement.

instruments.name: National AI Advisory Committee
instruments.summary: The NAIAC is tasked with providing an independent assessment of the Initiative and making recommendations to the President and the NAIIO on topics related to AI R&D, ethics, standards, education, technology transfer, commercial application, security, and economic competitiveness.

instruments.name: ML and AI Subcommittee
instruments.summary: MLAI-SC serves as the operations and implementation arm of the Select Committee on AI, and is responsible for fulfilling tasking from the Select Committee.

instruments.name: American Workforce Policy Advisory Board
instruments.summary: The Board is part of a government initiative to help bridge the skills gap that is widening in the modern economy due in part to the rise of automation and the increasing need for high-tech skills.

instruments.name: Protecting the U.S. Advantage in AI and Related Critical Technologies
instruments.summary: The National Security Strategy and the National Defense Strategy both address how the United States plans to maintain its competitive advantage.

instruments.name: National Strategy for Critical and Emerging Technologies
instruments.summary: The National Strategy for Critical and Emerging Technologies encourages unity of effort across the U.S. government and provides a framework from which deliberate actions will affect multiple technology areas in a co-ordinated manner.

instruments.name: Federal Data Strategy
instruments.summary: The Federal Data Strategy (FDS) encompasses a 10-year vision for how the Federal government will accelerate the use of data to deliver on its mission, serve the public, and steward resources while protecting security, privacy, and confidentiality.

instruments.name: National Artificial Intelligence Authority
instruments.summary: The Presidency of the Council of Ministers, through the Secretariat of Government and Digital Transformation, was assigned as the national technical-regulatory authority responsible for directing, evaluating and supervising the use and promotion of the development of artificial intelligence and emerging technologies at national level.

instruments.name: High Level committee by a Digital, Innovative and Competitive Peru
instruments.summary: The High Level Committee for a Digital Peru is an strategic body dependent on the Presidency of the Council of Ministers. It means it is in the high policy level domain.

instruments.name: National AI Strategy
instruments.summary: This first draft aims to present some key aspects of the development of AI in Peru and seek for external contributions.

instruments.name: Digital Agenda for Norway
instruments.summary: Government white paper setting out the Governments policy on how Norway can exploit ICT in the best interest of society

instruments.name: Report No. 22 (2020–2021) to the Storting – Data as a Resource: The Data-Driven Economy and Innovation
instruments.summary: White paper to parliament on the data economy and data-driven innovation.

instruments.name: Regulatory Sandbox on AI
instruments.summary: The Government has established a regulatory sandbox for data protection in AI under the remit of the Norwegian Data Protection Authority.

instruments.name: Fee for Illegal Storage and Use of Employee IP Addresses
instruments.summary: The Norwegian Data Protection Authority fined an employer for unnecessarily storing IP addresses and later using them to identify an employee for leaking internal information.

instruments.name: Act on Testing Self-Driving Vehicles
instruments.summary: Since 2017, Norway has allowed the testing of self-driving vehicles.

instruments.name: AI and Privacy Report
instruments.summary: The Norwegian Data Protection Authority published a report on the regulation of privacy and AI.

instruments.name: National Data Catalogue
instruments.summary: The National Data Catalogue “ data.norge.no “ is a public website providing an overview of descriptions of datasets, concepts, APIs and information models. The content is supplied by various establishments, both public and private.

instruments.name: Health Data Programme
instruments.summary: Program to ensure better utilisation of health data for secondary use, including through a health data analysis platform

instruments.name: Changes in the Health Register Act
instruments.summary: Change to the health register act to allow for the establishing of a platform for analysis of healt data.

instruments.name: Guidance on the Development and Use of AI in the Public Sector
instruments.summary: Guidance in the etichal and trustworthy development and use of AI in the public sector

instruments.name: Norwegian Resource Centre for Sharing Data
instruments.summary: The Norwegian Resource Centre for Sharing of Data works to promote the sharing and use of data by sharing knowledge and contributing to the development of legislation that promotes digitalisation.

instruments.name: Strategy for the Digital Transformation of Public Administration
instruments.summary: he TIC2021-26 and corresponding Transversal Action Plan , both to be launched in 2021, are the guiding documents for the digital transformation of the Portuguese public administration, encompassing 6 lines of action: i) Digital public services; ii) Valorization of Data; iii) Reference Architectures; iv) ICT skills; v) ICT infrastructure and services; vi) Security and Trust.

instruments.name: Report: The Boss Sees You? Monitoring and Control of Employees' Digital Activities
instruments.summary: Report from the Norwegian Data Protection Authority on the control and monitoring of employees' digital activities.

instruments.name: Research Council of Norway's ICT Research Programmes
instruments.summary: About 40 per cent of funds allocated to ICT research through the Research Council of Norway go to AI research (AI, data science, robotics).

instruments.name: The Norwegian Data Inspectorate
instruments.summary: The Norwegian Data Protection Authority (DPA) is a public authority and independent body set up to protect the individual right to privacy.

instruments.name: Inter-Ministerial Working Party on AI
instruments.summary: The inter-ministerial working party discusses policy initiatives and provide overview and input from the sectors on AI.

instruments.name: AI Portugal 2030 – National Strategy for AI
instruments.summary: The AI Portugal 2030 strategy aims to foster a collective process mobilizing citizens at large and key stakeholders in particular, towards building-up a knowledge intensive labour-market with a strong community of forefront companies producing and exporting AI technologies supported by research and innovation communities involved in excellent high level research.

instruments.name: National Strategy for AI
instruments.summary: The Norwegian national strategy for artificial intellgence (AI).

instruments.name: Council for Information and Communication Technologies in Public Administration
instruments.summary: CTIC is the coordination structure responsible for operationalizing the ICT Strategy 2020 in the Public Administration

instruments.name: Norwegian participation in HORIZON Europe
instruments.summary: Horizon Europe is a large European Framework programme for research

instruments.name: Norwegian participation in Digital Europe Programme
instruments.summary: The Digital Europe Programme (DIGITAL) is a new EU funding programme focused on bringing digital technology to businesses, citizens and public administrations.

instruments.name: Norwegian National Research Ethics Committees
instruments.summary: The Norwegian National Research Ethics Committees are independent agencies for questions regarding research ethics, and investigation of misconduct, within all subject areas.

instruments.name: Norwegian Biotechnology Advisory Board
instruments.summary: The main tasks of the Norwegian Biotechnology Advisory Board is to evaluate the social and ethical consequences of modern biotechnology and to discuss usage which promotes sustainable development.

instruments.name: Data Factory
instruments.summary: The Data Factory of AI Sweden aims to accelerate research and innovation by making data available in an enabling way. It does so by building resources, knowledge and capabilities that horizontally are of value to partners and the ecosystem.

instruments.name: AI Sweden
instruments.summary: AI Sweden is a national centre for AI-related research, innovation, and education, which aims to enhance Sweden's research in and adoption of AI. In addition to the national centre at Lindholmen Science Park in Gothenburg, there are several nodes around Sweden. AI Sweden is a private initiative supported by Swedish government agencies.

instruments.name: Artificial Intelligence in Incentive Verification
instruments.summary: improve the evaluation and risk management of companies applying for public incentives

instruments.name: Government Assignment To Promote The Public Administration's Ability To Use AI
instruments.summary: The Government assigns four national agencies (Swedish Public Employment Service, Swedish Companies Registration Office, Swedish Agency for Digital Government, and Swedish Tax Agency) to promote the public administration's ability to use AI.

instruments.name: Government Assignment on SMEs and Data as a Strategic Resource
instruments.summary: Government assignment to promote SMEs ability to use data as a strategic resource. Swedish Agency for Economic and Regional Growth is assigned to map conditions for SMEs to use data as a strategic resource.

instruments.name: Location Recommendation Engine for New Investments Based on AI
instruments.summary: he investor will be able to choose the relevant factors for their location decision from a comprehensive list of criteria, including, among others: 1 - Availability of infrastructure or land for construction2 - Type of required infrastructure (e.g., factory vs. office) and areas3 - Requirements for adjacent infrastructure (roads, ports, railways, IT, etc.)4 - Available human resources5 - Installation costs6 - Regulatory requirements (such as environmental licenses)

instruments.name: Big Data Analysis
instruments.summary: Government assignment to map the use of AI and big data analysis, with the aim to produce a wide statistical material of AI use cases and analysis of big data in enterprises, public administration (government agencies, municipalities, and regions), and universities in Sweden.

instruments.name: Committee for Technological Innovation and Ethics (KOMET)
instruments.summary: The Committee continuously delivers policy proposals to the Government and, where relevant, also survey the need to adapt regulatory frameworks. A reference group, including representatives from Government agencies, businesses, and organisations experienced in policy development, is assisting the Committee.

instruments.name: Digital Excellence
instruments.summary: Government assignment to the Swedish Agency for Economic and Regional Growth and the Swedish Higher Education Authority to enhance competencies of digital excellence in society and more specifically in the labour market.

instruments.name: Location Recommendation Engine for New Investments Based on AI
instruments.summary: The investor will be able to choose the relevant factors for their location decision from a comprehensive list of criteria, including, among others: 1 - Availability of infrastructure or land for construction2 - Type of required infrastructure (e.g., factory vs. office) and areas3 - Requirements for adjacent infrastructure (roads, ports, railways, IT, etc.)4 - Available human resources5 - Installation costs6 - Regulatory requirements (such as environmental licenses)

instruments.name: Evaluation of Risk Behavior in Gambling
instruments.summary: The SRIJ receives approximately 2,000,000 records daily in its database, which map all activities carried out by online players on licensed national websites. The majority of these records are related to the gambling activity of these players, providing detailed information about all bets made on a daily basis by each active player.

instruments.name: Swedish National Digitalisation Council
instruments.summary: The renewed Digitization Council aims to hold workshops and take other measures to support the government's work in developing a future digitization strategy that aims to be ready in 2024. The council consists of leading experts from universities, private and public sectors under the leadership of the Minister of public administration with responsibility for digital development in Sweden.

instruments.name: AI Research Investments
instruments.summary: Funding for AI research is allocated through several MBIE-administered mechanisms. E.g., AI is one of six priorities in the Catalyst Fund, and Data Science is one of ten platforms funded in the Strategic Science Investment Fund.

instruments.name: AI Commission
instruments.summary: The AI Commission's purpose is to enhance Sweden's AI capabilities. The AI Commission's work will be instrumental in identifying priority actions. In 2024 the AI Commission has presented proposals to the Swedish Government for measures to help strengthen the development and use of AI in Sweden. The AI Commission presents a total of 75 different proposals for measures including new inquiries, assignments to government agencies and expanded central government funding commitments.

instruments.name: Principles for Safe and Effective Use of Data and Analytics
instruments.summary: The Privacy Commissioner and the Government Chief Data Steward have jointly developed six key principles to support safe and effective data analytics.

instruments.name: Cross-Agency Work Programme on AI (2023–)
instruments.summary: A cross-portfolio work programme on AI has been developed, encompassing the public sector and wider NZ economy, addressing governance and economic and social development objectives, and national security considerations. Within this work programme, NZ will produce a national AI Strategy and Responsible AI Guidance for businesses.

instruments.name: Analysis of Tourism Information
instruments.summary: Allow the control the stay of foreigners in national territory that stay at hotels, complementary accommodation facilities, or tourist resorts.

instruments.name: Algorithm Charter for Aotearoa New Zealand
instruments.summary: The Algorithm Charter commits government agencies to improve transparency and accountability in their use of algorithms over the next five years.

instruments.name: Work on Upcoming Swedish Digitalisation Strategy Incl. AI
instruments.summary: Sweden is currently developing a Digitalisation Strategy - with tangible goals and measures for digitalisation with AI as a horizontal objective.

instruments.name: The Algorithm Impact Assessment (AIA) Toolkit
instruments.summary: A series of tools for agencies to use to help them understand and assess the potential impacts of the algorithms they create or use.

instruments.name: Strategy for Increased Access to Data
instruments.summary: For Sweden as a nation to continue to be successful in global competition, an increased ability to share and use data, a faster development of data markets, and a dynamic policy that can be adapted to the rapid technological development are required.

instruments.name: Digital Economy Partnership Agreement (New Zealand, Singapore, Chile, and South Korea)
instruments.summary: The Digital Economy Partnership Agreement (DEPA) between New Zealand, Singapore, Chile and South Korea will help establish new rules and practices for digital trade, and promote ongoing discussion on issues like digital inclusion, inclusive trade and support for small and medium enterprises (SMEs) in the digital economy.

instruments.name: National Approach to AI
instruments.summary: The purpose of this document is to identify an overall direction for AI-related work in Sweden and lay the foundation for future priorities.

instruments.name: Centre for Data Ethics and Innovation
instruments.summary: A team under the Government Chief Data Steward that supports government agencies to maximise the opportunities and benefits from new and emerging uses of data while responsibly managing potential risk and harms.

instruments.name: Analysis of Mortality Patterns in Portugal
instruments.summary: Information on mortality is fundamental knowledge about population health, central to all areas of health planning. The combination of data on deaths by age group and sex, along with the cause of death coded according to the rules of the World Health Organization, provides invaluable information for public health administration and planning for emerging diseases and disasters.

instruments.name: Callaghan Innovation
instruments.summary: Government agency tasked with supporting business innovation in New Zealand, especially for frontier firms.

instruments.name: AI Agenda for Sweden
instruments.summary: The AI Agenda is a collaborative and stakeholder-driven approach to suggest and formulate a national roadmap to accelerate the AI uptake in Sweden.

instruments.name: Taxpayer Characterization Model - Taxpayer's Perspective
instruments.summary: Assessing the risk of non-compliance (missed reporting obligations, frequency of payment infractions.

instruments.name: Action Plan for Digital Transformation of Slovakia
instruments.summary: Action plan for the transformation of Slovakia into a successful digital country and development of the digital single market. The action plan offers a set of concrete steps on how to start building a sustainable and human centric, and trustworthy AI ecosystem.

instruments.name: Data Ethics Advisory Group
instruments.summary: The Data Ethics Advisory Group helps maximising the opportunities and benefits from new and emerging uses of data, while responsibly managing risks and harms.

instruments.name: Self-Service Dashboard for City Councils
instruments.summary: The sharing of analytical information with Local Administration Entities through a solution that enables the creation of dashboards by Local Entities in an easy, fast, and intuitive manner

instruments.name: State R&D Programs, State R&D Infrastructure Development Programs and SRDA Programs
instruments.summary: State R&D programs, state R&D infrastructure development programs and SRDA programs.

instruments.name: Government Chief Digital Officer Leadership on AI in Public Sector
instruments.summary: The GCDO will provide leadership on AI across the NZ public service.

instruments.name: Accelerated Initiative for Artificial Intelligence
instruments.summary: IPOS' Accelerated Initiative for Artificial Intelligence, AI2 , complements Singapore's shift towards a digital economy and supports innovative enterprises that are looking to bring their AI products faster to the market. It also underscores Singapore's commitment to nurture and protect high-value innovation such as AI technologies. AI2 will be launched on 26 April 2019.

instruments.name: Google for Startups Accelerator: AI-First
instruments.summary: Google for Startups Accelerator: AI First Singapore to nurture and support globally-oriented innovators that use gen AI as the core technology to build their products.

instruments.name: Predictive Analytics in the Court System
instruments.summary: Uses data-driven tools to support and enhance judicial decision-making.

instruments.name: AI Trailblazers
instruments.summary: A Generative AI (Gen AI) innovation sandbox to accelerate development of solutions across Government and Industry.

instruments.name: Chartered AI Engineer (TM)
instruments.summary: Chartered AI Engineer (CAIE) is a professional qualification programme to recognize and award credentials to working professionals in AI-related engineering roles of their competencies and work experiences.

instruments.name: Predictive Analysis from Open Data in Justice and Information Sources from Different Areas
instruments.summary: Using open data, generate multidimensional analyses with predictive behaviours.

instruments.name: AI Grand Challenges
instruments.summary: AI Grand Challenge looks at important issues and problems faced by Singapore and the world that can be effectively addressed with AI technologies and innovation.

instruments.name: AI Apprenticeship Programme
instruments.summary: The AIAP is a full time 9-month programme where we train and groom local Singaporean AI talent. This is in line with the nation's focus in deepening national capabilities in AI, not only in terms of technology, but also skillsets and talents. The AIAP is a deep skilling programme and successful applicants to the AIAP are expected to have prior knowledge in AI and Machine Learning. During the duration of the programme the apprentice is paid a stipend of between SGD$3500 - $5500 per month.

instruments.name: Portugal Guidelines on Telework Monitoring
instruments.summary: Guidance from the Portuguese data protection authority (CNPD) on employee monitoring in the telework context.

instruments.name: AI Research Programme
instruments.summary: AI Research Programme seeds high quality research efforts aimed at developing fundamental AI novel techniques, algorithms and adjacent technologies that will eventually significantly contribute to the other pillars of AI Singapore. The AI Singapore Research Programme will also encourage national research collaborations and nurture local AI talents.

instruments.name: 100 Experiments
instruments.summary: 100E is AI Singapore's flagship programme to solve industries' AI problem statements and help them build their own AI team.

instruments.name: Privacy Enhancing Technologies x Privacy Sandbox
