instruments.summary: The Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA) and Google are helping developers and businesses tap into innovations to build a privacy-first digital ecosystem. The IMDA-Google: PET x Privacy Sandbox provides a safe environment and testing ground for pilot projects.

instruments.name: Privacy Enhancing Technologies Sandbox
instruments.summary: The PET Sandbox provides opportunities for companies to work with trusted PET digital solution providers to develop use cases and pilot PETs, to facilitate experimentation with PETs.

instruments.name: Generative AI Evaluation Sandbox
instruments.summary: The Sandbox will bring global ecosystem players together through concrete use cases, to enable the evaluation of trusted AI products. The Sandbox will make use of a new Evaluation Catalogue, as a shared resource, that sets out common baseline methods and recommendations for Large Language Models (LLM).

instruments.name: Road Traffic (Autonomous Motor Vehicles) Rules 2017
instruments.summary: Singapores Road Traffic (Autonomous Motor Vehicles) Rules expanded the definition of "motor vehicle" in the Road Traffic Act to include "autonomous motor vehicle".

instruments.name: National Multimodal Large Language Model Programme
instruments.summary: Funded by the National Research Foundation, Singapore (NRF), the new S$70 million Initiative will develop Singapore's research and engineering capabilities in multi-modal Large Language Models.

instruments.name: Prompt Engineering Playbook
instruments.summary: This playbook is designed to help public officers navigate the new ways of interacting with the LLM-powered AI through what we now call prompt engineering.

instruments.name: Principles to Promote Fairness, Ethics, Accountability and Transparency in the Use of Artificial Intelligence and Data Analytics in Singapore's Financial Sector
instruments.summary: The FEAT Principles document contains a set of generally accepted Principles for the use of artificial intelligence and data analytics in decision-making in the provision of financial products and services.

instruments.name: Luxembourg Future Fund
instruments.summary: Investment and co-investment fund targeting innovative SMEs.

instruments.name: Model AI Governance Framework for Generative AI
instruments.summary: This framework expands on the existing Model Governance Framework that covers Traditional AI, last updated in 2020. It covers nine dimensions for generative AI which should be looked at in totality - (a) accountability; (b) data; (c) trusted development and deployment; (d) incident reporting; (e) testing and assurance; (f) security; (g) establishing content provenance; (h) safety and alignment research & development; and (i) AI for Public Good.

instruments.name: SpaceResources.lu
instruments.summary: Within the SpaceResources.lu initiative, the country's overall framework, including but not limited to the legal regime, supports any space companies as well as bolstering global security and stimulating emerging sectors such as robotics and artificial intelligence.

instruments.name: Digital Luxembourg
instruments.summary: Consolidating Luxembourgs position in the ICT fields in the longer term.

instruments.name: Law on Road Traffic Safety (Self-Driving Cars)
instruments.summary: Lithuania adopted a law that allows operation of self-driving cars without a driver being present.

instruments.name: Guidelines for Unbiased Algorithms
instruments.summary: Guidelines for unbiased algorithms are being developed to assist developers and C level managers in assuring that their AI products do not discriminate women, disabled persons, other disadvantaged and excluded groups.

instruments.name: LT.AI - Fostering AI and the Creation of Lithuanian Language Technological Resources for AI
instruments.summary: LT.AI is a EUR 17 million financial measure to boost the Lithuanian AI ecosystem.

instruments.name: Model AI Governance Framework
instruments.summary: The voluntary Model AI Governance Framework was first released in January 2019 and updated in January 2020 as a living document that provides detailed and readily implementable guidance to private sector organisations to address key ethical and governance issues when deploying AI solutions.

instruments.name: Lithuanian Artificial Intelligence Strategy: A Vision of the Future
instruments.summary: In 2019, Lithuania launched an AI strategy to become a regional leader and boost its economy by using AI in key areas like healthcare, farming, and energy. The plan helps create good conditions for AI development and ensures it is used ethically. A 2023“2026 action plan supports this by promoting AI innovation and use across all sectors, including government services.

instruments.name: Implementation and Self-Assessment Guide for Organisations
instruments.summary: A companion to the 2nd Edition of Model AI Governance Framework released in January 2020, this Implementation and Self-Assessment Guide (ISAGO) aims to help organisations assess the alignment of their AI governance processes and practices with the Model AI Governance Framework.

instruments.name: AI Use Cases in the Public Sector
instruments.summary: This initiative lists different AI use cases in the Mexican public sector.

instruments.name: The Administrative Provisions of a General Nature for the Preparation, Submission, and Assessment of Impact Assessments on the Protection of Personal Data
instruments.summary: These current administrative provisions will apply to the preparation, presentation and evaluation of personal data protection impact assessments, as well as the corresponding provisions in state legislation on this matter

instruments.name: Compendium of AI Use Cases
instruments.summary: The Compendium demonstrates how local and international organisations across different sectors and sizes implemented or aligned their AI governance practices with all sections of the Model AI Governance Framework.

instruments.name: Towards an AI Strategy in Mexico: Harnessing the AI Revolution
instruments.summary: White paper to lay the foundations for a National AI Strategy.

instruments.name: ASEAN Guide on AI Governance and Ethics
instruments.summary: The ASEAN Guide on AI Governance and Ethics is a practical guide for organisations in the region that wish to design, develop, and deploy traditional AI technologies in commercial and non-military or dual-use applications.

instruments.name: Memories of the Privacy Route: Artificial Intelligence—Perspectives and Prospects from the Right of Personal Data Protection and Privacy
instruments.summary: Editorial product that consists in the compiling of essays regarding AI from the perspective and prospective from the right of personal data protection and privacy, that seeks to present the expert voices who accompanied the INAI during the activities of the initiative of the Privacy Route.

instruments.name: AI Ethics and Governance Body of Knowledge
instruments.summary: The Body of Knowledge (BoK) is based on the Infocomm Media Development Authoritys (IMDA) Model AI Governance Framework and it is tailored for practical issues related to human safety, fairness and the prevailing approaches to privacy, data governance and general ethical values.

instruments.name: Optimization of Digital Services Provided by the Tax and Customs Authority
instruments.summary: streamline digital services to help taxpayers and businesses to interact with the tax authorities.

instruments.name: AI Singapore
instruments.summary: AI Singapore (AISG) is a national AI programme launched by the National Research Foundation (NRF) to anchor deep national capabilities in Artificial Intelligence (AI), thereby creating social and economic impacts, grow the local talent, build an AI ecosystem and put Singapore on the world map.

instruments.name: Recommendations for the Processing of Personal Data Regarding the Use of Artificial Intelligence
instruments.summary: Recommendations regarding the fulfilment of the data protection principles and duties when applying AI, also in different sectors (education, public security, health, etc).

instruments.name: Increase in the Use of Portuguese Ports in the Entry and Exit of Goods
instruments.summary: To be determined

instruments.name: Singapore Conference on AI for the Global Good
instruments.summary: The Singapore Conference on AI for the Global Good (SCAI) brought together 42 global AI experts to articulate the most critical problems of AI development and deployment - critical questions of AI that, if answered systematically, would enable the harnessing of AI for the global good.

instruments.name: Principles and Impact Analysis Guide for the Development and Use of Systems Based on Artificial Intelligence in the Federal Public Administration
instruments.summary: In order to strengthen the responsible and ethical use of Artificial Intelligence for the common good, this guide was developed.

instruments.name: Guideline for the Elaboration of Privacy Impact Assessments
instruments.summary: The Guideline offers a series of recommendations based on international standards and best practices in information security that may be applicable depending on the nature of the data, the purposes of processing, and the technical and economic capabilities of the data processors.

instruments.name: Digital Forum of Small States
instruments.summary: The Forum of Small States (FOSS) is an informal and non-ideological grouping of small states that was established by Singapore in 1992 to discuss issues of mutual concern. Digital FOSS was launched in October 2022 to enable deeper conversations on digital issues of relevance to small states, including AI.

instruments.name: Guide for the Preparation and Submission of Personal Data Protection Impact Assessments
instruments.summary: The Guide aims to promote a culture of personal data protection within the data controllers' organizations by incorporating this topic in everyday language that is understandable regarding the various concepts and figures that are indispensable for impact assessments

instruments.name: Asia Tech x Artificial Intelligence
instruments.summary: ATxAI, as part of IMDA's Asia Tech x Singapore (ATxSG) flagship tech event, is a global conference on AI governance that convenes respected visionaries, experts, and policymakers in a series of discussions to share insights on building trustworthy AI, governing cutting-edge AI technologies, and leveraging them for the benefit of the digital economy.

instruments.name: General Recommendations for Data Processing in AI of the Ibero-American Data Protection Network
instruments.summary: The recommendations have a preventive focus and assume that the best way to protect the human rights involved in the processing of personal data is to prevent their violation.

instruments.name: Computational Data Analysis Exception of the Copyright Act 2021
instruments.summary: A new exception under the amended Copyright Act 2021 permits the copying of copyright works specifically for the purpose of computational data analysis, e.g. sentiment analysis, text and data mining, and training machine learning. To protect the commercial interests of copyright owners, this exception is subject to certain conditions and safeguards, which the user must comply with.

instruments.name: Specific Guidelines for Compliance with the Principles and Rights that Govern the Protection of Personal Data in Artificial Intelligence Projects
instruments.summary: The guidelines were enacted due to the progress of emerging technologies in today's technological landscape entails diverse and innovative approaches to handling personal data. These approaches are under scrutiny and regulation by global data protection authorities to ensure that technological advancements align with the preservation of individuals' freedoms.

instruments.name: Services & Digital Economy Technology Roadmap and Services 4.0
instruments.summary: SDE TRM is an important component of the Digital Economy Framework for Action to guide IMDA's industry development plans and regulatory approaches for the Infocomm and Media (ICM) sector.

instruments.name: National Ecosystem of Open Innovation
instruments.summary: Social development through open innovation with an enviromental perspective and involvment of all economic actors.

instruments.name: Discussion Paper on Generative AI - Implications for Trust and Governance
instruments.summary: IMDA and Aicadium have published a discussion paper to share Singapore's approach to building an ecosystem for trusted and responsible adoption of Generative AI, in a way that spurs innovation and tap on its opportunities.

instruments.name: Website for Personal Data Protection Impact Assessments
instruments.summary: The website wants to foster a culture of safeguarding personal data within the data controller's organization.

instruments.name: Digital Economy Framework for Action
instruments.summary: The Digital Economy Framework for Action provides a guide to help businesses and workforce in Singapore to prepare and embrace digital transformation and embrace the possibilities brought about by such transformation.

instruments.name: Program for the Development of the Software Industry and Innovation
instruments.summary: The Ministry of Economy supports two innovation centers in Mexico that use artificial intelligence (AI) to help businesses and schools work together. These centers develop new AI technologies and train experts, boosting local industries. The goal is to improve skills and create smart products, making Mexico more competitive in modern technology.

instruments.name: Bilateral AI Collaborations
instruments.summary: Singapore has pursued collaboration in Artificial Intelligence on a bilateral basis with a number of countries, to complement existing digital agreements, support the development and deployment of AI for collective benefit, and promote the responsible use of AI.

instruments.name: AI Verify Foundation
instruments.summary: The AI Verify Foundation will harness the collective power and contributions of the global open source community to develop AI testing tools for the responsible use of AI. It will look to boost AI testing capabilities and assurance to meet the needs of companies and regulators globally.

instruments.name: Southeast Asia Languages in One Network Model
instruments.summary: SEA-LION is an open-source large language model introduced by AI Singapore, tailored to reflect the cultural contexts and linguistic subtleties of Southeast Asia. It is designed to be smaller, more flexible, and faster than many prevalent LLMs available today. This makes it a cost-effective and efficient choice for organizations, particularly those in Southeast Asia that are budget-conscious and face throughput constraints, allowing them to seamlessly integrate AI into their operations.

instruments.name: 10G Nationwide Broadband Network
instruments.summary: Upgrade Nationwide Broadband Network to 10Gbps with up to S$100mil to support future innovations and opportunities brought by artificial intelligence, immersive digital experiences and autonomous systems.

instruments.name: Identification of Patterns Leading to the Minimization of Illegal Fishing
instruments.summary: This initiative aims to identify behavioral and operational patterns to help minimize illegal fishing in Portugal.

instruments.name: National Alliance of Artificial Intelligence
instruments.summary: A strategy that seeks to recognise and strengthen the AI ecosystem in Mexico to maintain an open dialogue on AI and its impacts, with a comprehensive, plural, and multidisciplinary perspective, and with the participation of the different stakeholders and society in general; having as main objective: "AI for the benefit of humanity and as a transversal axis for the sustainable development of Mexico".

instruments.name: Towards Trustworthy AI: Malta's Ethical AI Framework 2019
instruments.summary: A strong ethical AI framework as a supplement to the current legal and regulatory system is a core component of Malta's AI strategy to ensure that AI development is ethically aligned, transparent and socially responsible.

instruments.name: AI Certification Programme
instruments.summary: A set of guidance notes aimed at assisting Service Providers and AI-ITA Applicants when approaching the Malta Digital Innovation Authority (MDIA) for registration and certification respectively.

instruments.name: AI Compute
instruments.summary: Invest up to S$500mil to avail high-performance compute to support AI innovation and capability building.

instruments.name: Circular on the Use of Large Language Models in the Public Sector
instruments.summary: An internal circular to inform Ministries, Organs of State, Departments and Statutory Boards in the Singapore Government of the policy positions for the use of Large Language Models (LLMs) in the public sector, and the subsequent standards for Agencies' adherence.

instruments.name: AI in Healthcare Guidelines
instruments.summary: To support patient safety and improve trust in the use of AI in healthcare, the Ministry of Health (MOH), the Health Sciences Authority (HSA), and the Integrated Health Information Systems (IHiS) co-developed the MOH Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare Guidelines (AIHGle)

instruments.name: TRANSCRIBE
instruments.summary: Transcribe is a Speech-to-Text (STT) platform with auto-transcription technologies and localised STT services across various speech models and data classification.

instruments.name: Identification of Patterns in the Rustic Property in Portugal
instruments.summary: Systematic analysis and processing of structured and unstructured data available in the databases of the Public Administration concerning the knowledge of boundaries and ownership of rural territory

instruments.name: SupportGoWhere
instruments.summary: SupportGoWhere is a one-stop portal for Singaporeans to find and apply for social services and government support programmes. It has been upgraded with AI-powered functionalities.

instruments.name: Mexican National AI Agenda
instruments.summary: An agenda created from the plurality of leadership, voices and sectors in Mexico.

instruments.name: PAIR
instruments.summary: Pair is a suite of applications and infrastructure designed to allow officers and agencies to use large language models productively and safely in their work.

instruments.name: Get Qualified Scheme
instruments.summary: This is an initiative that supports the personal development of individuals for the achievement of qualifications and certifications required by industry. The incentive is applicable to individuals following a course of studies leading to a certification, diploma, degree or post-graduate degree courses. Upon successful completion the student will benefit from a tax credit enabling them to recover part of the costs incurred.

instruments.name: The Digital Skills for Artificial Intelligence
instruments.summary: A free online programme to cover key digital skills for the workplace in the age of the AI Revolution.

instruments.name: National AI Programme in Health
instruments.summary: The National AI Programme in Health aims to build deep AI capabilities within Singapore's healthcare sector for clinical decision support, personalised risk score, and personalised treatment.

instruments.name: Key Employee Initiative
instruments.summary: Malta's Key Employee Initiative helps skilled workers from outside the EU in AI roles get faster work and residence permits. It supports companies by bringing in talent needed to boost AI innovation and digital growth. This program was created to attract experts who can help Malta stay competitive and aligned with global AI standards.

instruments.name: MSO OneService Chatbot
instruments.summary: MSO OneService chatbot enables citizens to easily lodge a case and provide additional, crucial information about the complaint through commonly used social messaging apps, such as WhatsApp and Telegram.

instruments.name: JUMPSTART
instruments.summary: The JumpStart platform ingests datasets from across Government to build data science models, and then deploys them as machine learning microservices which products can tap on to improve job search.

instruments.name: Research Programme On Governance Of AI And Data Use
instruments.summary: Set up at the Singapore Management University (SMU) School of Law, this five-year Research Programme on the Governance of AI and Data Use will conduct scholarly research on policy, legal, regulatory, governance, ethics and other issues relating to AI and data use.

instruments.name: Tech Skills Accelerator Initiatives
instruments.summary: Singapore is scaling up our TeSA initiatives, which includes Company-Led Training programmes, to support fresh and mid-career professionals who have the aptitude and attitude to work in AI, with the aim of tripling our AI practitioner pool to 15,000.

instruments.name: Development of algorithms that Enable the Analysis and Control of Waste Management, Using Pattern Analysis and Artificial Intelligence
instruments.summary: To be determined

instruments.name: SMES Go Digital
instruments.summary: Launched in 2017 to support SMEs at various stages of their digitalisation journey. This includes the Industry Digital Plans (IDPs), which provides sector-specific, step-by-step solutions and training programmes to equip employees with the right skillsets at each stage of their digitalisation journey, including the use of AI in some sectors.

instruments.name: Public Sector AI Playbook
instruments.summary: This playbook provides public officers, especially non-technical officers, a guide on how AI can be adopted in their area of work and shares a range of AI projects implemented throughout the public service.

instruments.name: Guide to Job Redesign in the Age of AI
instruments.summary: Under the guidance of the Advisory Council of the Ethical Use of AI and Data, the Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA) and the PDPC have collaborated with the Lee Kuan Yew Centre for Innovative Cities (LKYCIC), Singapore University of Technology and Design to launch the Singapore's first guide that helps organisations and employees understand how existing job roles can be redesigned to harness the potential of AI, so that the value of their work is increased.

instruments.name: Start-up Residence Programme
instruments.summary: The Malta Start-up Residence Programme grants a 3-year residence permit, extendable for an additional 5 years, during which beneficiaries are able to reside in Malta while launching their startup venture.

instruments.name: Tax Credit on Higher Educational Qualifications
instruments.summary: This is an initiative that supports the personal development of individuals who were not yet 40 years of age on the date of commencement of the course, and who graduate with Postgraduate Diploma, Masters Degree or a PhD. Upon successful completion the student will benefit from a tax credit enabling them to recover part of the costs incurred.

instruments.name: Technology Assessment Recognition Framework
instruments.summary: The Technology Assessment Recognition Framework (TARF) by the MDIA is a tiered framework designed to provide varying degrees of recognition to a wide range of technologies, from emerging technologies to traditional, including Artificial Intelligence.

instruments.name: Masters in Artificial Intelligence
instruments.summary: The faculty of ICT of the University of Malta has launched a Master programme in Artificial Intelligence to support the growing ICT industry in Malta. The programme is offered in full-time and part-time modes.

instruments.name: Qualifying Employment in Innovation & Creativity (Personal Tax)
instruments.summary: This measure facilitates employment of non-residents in roles which are currently not addressed by the local labour market by temporarily easing the tax expenses incurred by such individuals through a fiscal incentive.

instruments.name: xPloring Intelligence “A Bootcamp on Us and Tech/Tech Trek“ a Teen Tech Adventure
instruments.summary: The bootcamp is an opportunity for children aged 11- 12 years and Tech Trek for  12-14 years to delve into the area of technology on a deeper level, increase their knowledge on AI through theoretical and practical sessions , and pave their way for a career in these sectors.

instruments.name: Malta Digital Innovation Authority
instruments.summary: MDIA is is the regulatory authority for emerging technologies and is responsible for promotion of governmental policies related to the regulation and promotion of digital technological innovation in Malta.

instruments.name: The Ultimate AI Launchpad: A strategy and vision for Artificial Intelligence in Malta 2030
instruments.summary: Malta's AI Strategy 2030 aims to make the country a leader in artificial intelligence by encouraging investment, innovation, and use of AI in both public and private sectors. It supports six pilot projects in areas like health, education, and traffic to improve services and quality of life. This initiative helps businesses and citizens benefit from smarter, more efficient solutions.

instruments.name: Non-formal AI Coordination Network
instruments.summary: List of persons from public, private sector and academia for information exchange, share experience and opinions.

instruments.name: Digital Transformation Guidelines
instruments.summary: Digital transformation of society, including private and public sectors

instruments.name: Information Report on the Development of Artificial Intelligence Solutions (Project)
instruments.summary: Latvia's AI initiative outlines a three-year strategy to guide the use of artificial intelligence in government and the economy. It aims to raise awareness and assess how AI can improve public services. The plan helps prepare the country for digital transformation and supports smarter decision-making across sectors.

instruments.name: Declaration on AI in the Nordic-Baltic Region
instruments.summary: In May 2018, the Ministers responsible for digital development from Denmark, Estonia, Finland, the Faroe Islands, Iceland, Latvia, Lithuania, Norway, Sweden, and the …land Islands released a Declaration on AI in the Nordic-Baltic Region. The countries agreed to collaborate in order to develop and promote the use of artificial intelligence to serve humans.

instruments.name: Latvia's National AI Strategy
instruments.summary: In February 2020, the Latvian government released its National AI Strategy on Developing Artificial Intelligence Solutions.

instruments.name: AI Use Cases in the Public Sector
instruments.summary: This initiative groups several projects using AI in Kenya's public sector.

instruments.name: Kenya's Digital Economy Strategy
instruments.summary: This Strategy aims at developing the digital economy in Kenya. It focuses on six pillars (Digital Government, Digital Business, Infrastructure, Innovation and Entrepreneurship, Digital Skills and Values and Digital Inclusion) as well as the following cross-cutting themes: An Integrated Ecosystem, Data, Emerging Trends, Green ICT, Security and, Policy and Regulatory Framework.

instruments.name: Kenya's Digital Economy Blueprint
instruments.summary: The Blueprint sets clear outcomes, identifies opportunities and areas that need further focus in the Kenyan digital economy ecosystem, while outlining corresponding plans of action for Government, private sector and the citizens. The Blueprint identifies the five pillars of the digital economy: Digital Government, Digital Business, Infrastructure, Innovation-Driven Entrepreneurship and Digital Skills and Values.

instruments.name: Emerging Digital Technologies for Kenya - Exploration and Analysis
instruments.summary: This initiative is part of Kenya's government Blockchain and AI Taskforce, and explores the different ways these technologies can contribute to addressing the country's challenges.

instruments.name: Blockchain and AI Task Force
instruments.summary: The Kenyan government created a Blockchain & Artificial Intelligence task force in February 2018.

instruments.name: Kenya's Digital Literacy Programme (DigiSchool)
instruments.summary: The programme introduces primary school children to the use of digital technology and communications. It is targeted at learners in all public primary schools in Kenya.

instruments.name: AI Utilisation Guidelines
instruments.summary: These Guidelines are intended to encourage the voluntary consideration of AI users, especially those who provide AI services to others (AI service providers) and those who use AI systems (business users).

instruments.name: AI R&D Guidelines
instruments.summary: These Guidelines are prepared as a basis for international discussions at G7 and OECD regarding matters expected to be considered in R&D activities for promoting the benefits and reducing the risks of AI.

instruments.name: AI Governance Guidelines for Implementation of AI Principles Ver. 1.1
instruments.summary: This Guideline summarizes what to do to put the Social Principles of Human-Centric AI (decided by the Council for Integrated Innovation Strategy) into practice.

instruments.name: Governance Innovation: Redesigning Law and Architecture for Society 5.0
instruments.summary: An expert group in a wide variety of fields, including law, economics, technologies and businesses, has held discussions on the need for new governance models to pursue both the promotion of innovation and the achievement of social value, as well as ideal approaches thereto as Japanese society is facing dramatic changes brought about by big data, IoT, AI and other digital technologies.

instruments.name: Guidebook on Introducing AI to SMEs
instruments.summary: This Guidebook shows how we can introduce AI to SMEs.

instruments.name: Advanced Integrated Intelligence Platform Project
instruments.summary: To gather top researchers and promote R&D for innovative fundamental technology and also promote implementation.

instruments.name: Social Principles of Human-centric AI
instruments.summary: The Principles contain the fundamentals of what each stakeholder should keep in mind in order for AI to be accepted and properly used by society.

instruments.name: ML Quality Management Guideline
instruments.summary: This Guideline establishes a basis for quality goals for ML-based products/services utilizing AI.

instruments.name: Quad Principles on Technology Design, Development, Governance, and Use
instruments.summary: The Quad countries (Australia, India, Japan, and the United States of America) affirm that the ways in which technology is designed, developed, governed, and used should be shaped by our shared democratic values and respect for universal human rights.

instruments.name: Guidelines on Assessment of AI Reliability in the Field of Plant Safety
instruments.summary: This Guideline provides the methodology to fulfill AI's desired quality in terms of safety and productivity enhancement, in order to promote the usage of AI in the field of plants where safety is considered vital.

instruments.name: Contract Guidelines on Utilizing AI and Data (Version 1.1)
instruments.summary: This Guideline is reference for businesses that explains approaches to concluding [i] contracts for utilization of data or [ii] contracts for the development and utilization of software using AI technology.

instruments.name: The Conference Toward AI Network Society
instruments.summary: This multi-stakeholder (industry, academia, consumer organisation and government) conference body discusses issues that the development and deployment of AI network may bring to the society.

instruments.name: Tentative Summary of AI Issues
instruments.summary: A compilation of issues to be addressed due to the advent of generative AI, while maintaining the basic strategies and principles that have already been established.

instruments.name: Governance Innovation Ver. 2 - a Guide to Designing and Implementing Agile Governance
instruments.summary: This report aims to tackle the concept of agile governance and analyse how it can be implemented into the Japanese society.

instruments.name: AI Governance in Japan 1.1
instruments.summary: This report provides the result of discussion of ideal approaches to AI governance in Japan for the purpose of operationalizing the Japanese AI Principles by the Expert Group on How AI Principles Should be Implemented (former the Expert Group on Architecture for AI Principles to be Practiced), organized by the METI.

instruments.name: Agile Governance Update: How Governments, Businesses, and Civil Society Can Create a Better World by Reimagining Governance
instruments.summary: This report is written how governments, businesses, and civil society can create a better world by reimagining governance.

instruments.name: Trilateral French-Japanese-German Research Projects on Artificial Intelligence
instruments.summary: The Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft (DFG, German Research Foundation) together with the French National Research Agency (ANR, France), and the Japan Science and Technology Agency (JST, Japan) is announcing the first trilateral call for research proposals on Artificial Intelligence (AI).

instruments.name: High Performance Computing Infrastructure Project
instruments.summary: Supercomputer "Fugaku" as a central core, construct high-speed network among universities and public research sectors for various uses.

instruments.name: Global Communication Plan 2025
instruments.summary: The Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications (MIC) has formulated the Global Communication Plan 2025 in order to promote the further sophistication of multilingual translation technologies, such as the realization of concurrent interpretation by AI in 2025.

instruments.name: AI Bridging Cloud Infrastructure (ABCI)
instruments.summary: AI Bridging Cloud Infrastructure (ABCI) is the world's first large-scale Open AI Computing Infrastructure, constructed and operated by National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology (AIST).

instruments.name: AI Guidelines for Business Ver1.0
instruments.summary: This Guidelines are intended to encourage all AI-related stakeholders to take voluntary effort (e.g. build internal AI governance systems)

instruments.name: Road Traffic Act
instruments.summary: The Japanese Road Transport Vehicle Act was revised after consideration of automated driving vehicles operating on public roads.

instruments.name: Act on the Protection of Personal Information
instruments.summary: This Act prescribes how covered entities should handle personal information including in the context of development and operation of AI systems.

instruments.name: AI Japan R&D Network
instruments.summary: The AI Japan R&D Network is a consortium established by National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology (AIST), the Institute of Physical and Chemical Research (RIKEN) and the National Institute of Information and Communications Technology (NICT).

instruments.name: Practical Guidebook on Providing Data for Employee Development in AI and Data Science
instruments.summary: This Guidebook focuses on employee development in AI and data science and summarizes issues in four categories based on increasing benefit and risk reduction for businesses.

instruments.name: AI Strategy Council
instruments.summary: Council of experts to discuss issues related to AI

instruments.name: AI Strategy of Japan
instruments.summary: This Strategy describes measures that Japan should immediately take to overcome issues Japan faces by leveraging Japan's strengths and to open up opportunities for the future.

instruments.name: Personalised Virtual assistant - National Institute for Social Security (INPS)
instruments.summary: Virtual assistant based on Generative AI. The virtual assistant helps users to improve the search experience on the INPS website. Also, in its beta version, the virtual assistant can help users to submit specific questions relating to "Opzione Donna (Option Woman), a social securitymeasure for women only.

instruments.name: Corporate Venture Capital Fund for AI start-ups to develop solutions for the public sector
instruments.summary: Investment fund backed by state lender Cassa Depositi e Prestiti (CDP) to promote startups investing in Artificial Intelligence (AI), including generative AI. Use of direct and indirect investments to promote the development of all players in the innovation chain.

instruments.name: Fund for the development of AI, blockchain and internet of things (IoT) technologies and applications
instruments.summary: A dedicated fund for enterprises, including SMEs. It supports projects involving the implementation of industrial research and innovation for developing AI, including generative AI, blockchain, and IoT technologies applications.

instruments.name: AI, Blockchain, IOT Technologies and Applications Development Fund
instruments.summary: From September 2022, companies and research centers can benefit from tax incentives to carry out innovation and research projects related to artificial intelligence, blockchain and internet of things technologies and applications.

instruments.name: Italian AI Employment Case Law
instruments.summary: Documentation of existing AI case law in the employment context.

instruments.name: Support Program for Emerging Technologies Based on 5G
instruments.summary: The Program aims at developing the use of emerging technologies within the national territory, by creating centers for research in the cities with an ongoing 5G trial and co-financing projects.

instruments.name: Blockchain, AI, and Internet of Things Fund
instruments.summary: Fund to finance experimentation and testing activities of the above mentioned emerging technologies.

instruments.name: Cineca Supercomputing Centre
instruments.summary: CINECA is a not-for-profit consortium, made up of the Italian Ministry of Education, the Italian Ministry of Universities and Research, 69 Italian universities and 21 Italian National Institutions.

instruments.name: National Phd in AI
instruments.summary: The Italian National PhD Program in Artificial Intelligence is made of 5 federated PhD courses that bring together 61 universities and research institutions. The 5 PhD courses share a common basis in the foundations and developments of AI (including generative AI), and each one has an area of specialisation in a strategic sector of AI application (Health and life sciences; Agrifood and environment; Security and cybersecurity; Industry 4.0; Society).

instruments.name: AI Strategic Program
instruments.summary: Strengthening skills and attracting talents to develop an Artificial Intelligence ecosystem in Italy; increasing funding for advanced research in Artificial Intelligence; and incentivizing the adoption of Artificial Intelligence and its applications both in public administrations and in the private sector.

instruments.name: Data Science Initiative
instruments.summary: The Council for Higher Education has established a program to support data science research within Israeli universities, including new research centers, an inter-university coordination mechanism, a dedicated fund within the Israel Science Foundation, and scholarship programs.

instruments.name: Public Call for Applications to Support AI Implementation Projects in the Government
instruments.summary: Israel has opened a public call to support AI projects in government. The goal is to improve digital services, increase efficiency, and enhance decision-making. Projects are chosen based on feasibility, impact, planning, and ethical risk management, helping government provide better services to citizens.

instruments.name: Investment in Localized NLP Infrastructure
instruments.summary: In 2021 the Israeli National Forum for R&D Infrastructure (TELEM in Hebrew) recommended on investing in NLP capabilities in Hebrew and Arabic. Those recommendations were later adopted by the government as part of resolution 212, allocating a total of 180M NIS over a period of 3 years for the creation of corpora, model and tools that are to be made widely accessible to the IL R&D eco-system.

instruments.name: Government Resolution No. 212: Promoting Innovation, High-tech Sector, and Technological Leadership
instruments.summary: The resolution lists a series of actions and corresponding funding, aiming to promote innovation, continued growth of the high-tech sector and Israeli technological leadership

instruments.name: Government Resolution No. 173: Strengthning Israel's Global Technological Leadership
instruments.summary: Further to Government Resolutions No. 212 of August 1, 2021 (hereinafter - Resolution212), No. 2118 of October 22, 2014, No. 4398 of December 23, 2018 and No. 218 ofAugust 1, 2021 and in light of the importance of technological innovation as the growthengine of the Israeli high-tech sector, and in order to support the continued prosperityof the Israeli innovation industry and its leadership in the global innovationcompetition

instruments.name: Project Nimbus - National Cloud Infrastructure
instruments.summary: Project Nimbus is Israel's national cloud initiative to provide secure and efficient cloud services for government agencies. Major providers like Google and AWS set up local data centers to support this effort. The project helps improve government technology infrastructure, ensuring faster and safer digital services for citizens.

instruments.name: National Initiative for Secured Intelligence Systems
instruments.summary: The National Initiative for Secured Intelligent Systems: A National Strategy for Israel in the Field of AI (Report to the Prime Minister)

instruments.name: Legal Opinion: Uses of Copyrighted Materials for Machine Learning
instruments.summary: A legal opinion addressing the question of "whether ML enterprises can make unauthorized use of copyrighted materials to train Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems"

instruments.name: Israel's Policy on Artificial Intelligece Regulation and Ethics
instruments.summary: In December 2023, Israel introduced its first policy on AI regulation and ethics. The policy aims to ensure AI is used responsibly, protecting people from risks like bias and privacy issues. Developed by several ministries and experts, it supports innovation while promoting fairness, safety, and transparency for all sectors using AI.

instruments.name: Guiding Principles for the Development of Machine-learning Based Technologies in Healthcare
instruments.summary: Principles for good machine learning practices in development of healthcare technologies, addressing the balance between ethical guidelines and technological advancement

instruments.name: AI Strategy Recommendations by TELEM - the National Governmental Forum for R&D Infrastructure
instruments.summary: A cross-governmental team was set up to devise recommendations for a policy plan to promote AI R&I activities in Israel.

instruments.name: Establishing Local AI & HPC Compute Infrastrcuture
instruments.summary: In 2021, Israel recommended building local computer systems to support artificial intelligence (AI) and high-performance computing (HPC). The government allocated funds to create infrastructure for AI model training, support startups developing AI hardware and software, and provide computing power for scientific research. This initiative helps researchers, startups, and industries improve AI capabilities and innovation.

instruments.name: Future Jobs Ireland
instruments.summary: Future of Jobs Ireland aims to prepare the Irish workforce for technological change.

instruments.name: Data Sharing and Governance Act
instruments.summary: The Act comes as a regulatory adaptation to safeguard privacy and data protection when it comes to new data sharing and collecting practices.

instruments.name: Enterprise Digital Advisory Board
instruments.summary: As per the Irish National AI Strategy 2021, the Advisory Board (with membership drawn from Industry) will work with and advise Government in the adoption of AI by Irish enterprise.

instruments.name: Irish National AI Strategy 2021
instruments.summary: This strategy aims to provide a high-level direction to the development, adoption and implementation of AI in Ireland.

instruments.name: AI Use Cases in the Public Sector
instruments.summary: Estonia has implemented a great number of AI projects across the public sector and has a database of the use cases.

instruments.name: Burokratt - Government AI Virtual Assisstant
instruments.summary: Burokratt is an interoperable network of virtual assistants on the websites of public authorities that allows people to obtain information from these authorities through a chat window. It provides users with the opportunity to access public and information services through a network of virtual assistants.

instruments.name: AI COVID-19 Response
instruments.summary: Estonia implemented an AI powered chatbot SUVE which helped people to acquire information regarding the state of play.

instruments.name: Privacy Enhancing Technology Action Plan
instruments.summary: Privacy Enhancing Technologies aim to protect and minimise personal data use and improve data processing possibilities

instruments.name: Open-source AI Components
instruments.summary: Open-source AI components are being made available for reuse by interested parties in the public and private sectors.

instruments.name: Declaration on AI in the Nordic-Baltic Region
instruments.summary: In May 2018, the Ministers responsible for digital development from Denmark, Estonia, Finland, the Faroe Islands, Iceland, Latvia, Lithuania, Norway, Sweden, and the …land Islands released a Declaration on AI in the Nordic-Baltic Region. The countries agreed to collaborate in order to develop and promote the use of artificial intelligence to serve humans.

instruments.name: Estonian Open Data Portal
instruments.summary: Open Data Portal gives everyone the opportunity to consume and visualize open data, it includes use cases that are based on open data.

instruments.name: Data Governance and Open Data Competence Centre
instruments.summary: Data governance and open data competence centre provides support related to data governance related areas. These include helping with data access, open data, data quality, metadata management, data preparation and privacy enhancing technologies.

instruments.name: Estonian Catalogue of Public Sector Information Systems
instruments.summary: RIHA serves as a catalogue for the Estonian state's information system.

instruments.name: AI & Robotics Estonia
instruments.summary: AI & Robotics Estonia supports Estonian industrial companies in adopting smart digital solutions in the field of artificial intelligence and robotics.

instruments.name: AI Support Portfolio
instruments.summary: AI Support Portfolio includes support services (e.g. data sandbox, AI seminars and workshops, consulting services, deep dives) provided to public sector institutions to facilitate the uptake of trustworthy and human-centric AI in the public sector.

instruments.name: AI Task Force Report
instruments.summary: This report includes proposals for applying artificial intelligence within Estonia on a wider scale.

instruments.name: Research Integrity Working Group
instruments.summary: The Group supports the implementation of existing principles and codes, and contributes to the consolidation of a normative framework in practice in Europe.

instruments.name: Estonia's AI Task Force
instruments.summary: The AI Task Force was initially formed as a collaboration initiative between the Estonian Government's Ministry of Economic Affairs and Communications and Government Office, but has included over time participants from the private and public sectors, as well as academics.

instruments.name: National AI Strategy 2.0
instruments.summary: The AI Strategy is a continuation of Estonia's previous national AI Strategy implemented in the period of 2019“2021.

instruments.name: National AI Strategy 1.0
instruments.summary: The Strategy is a sum of actions that Estonian government will take to advance the take-up of AI in both private and public sector, to increase the relevant skills and research and development (R&D) base as well as to develop the legal environment. This strategy is also Estonian national AI strategy in the European Union's coordinated AI action plan context, synchronised with and supporting relevant EU-level activities.

instruments.name: Estonia's Digital Agenda 2030
instruments.summary: Estonia's Digital Agenda 2030 includes a vision and an action plan concerning the development of the Estonian economy, state and society with the help of digital technology in the next decade.

instruments.name: Personal Data Protection Law
instruments.summary: Egypt launched in 2020 a personal data protection law to emphasize the country's commitment to the responsible use and governance of data.

instruments.name: Egyptian Charter for Responsible AI
instruments.summary: The Egyptian Charter for Responsible AI is a guide to help Egypt develop and use AI in a safe and fair way. It adapts global ethical principles to Egypt's needs, ensuring AI benefits people and society. This initiative supports policymakers and organizations in managing AI responsibly while protecting rights and promoting trust.

instruments.name: Applied Innovation Center
instruments.summary: Egypt launched an Applied Innovation Center for creating applications in different emerging technologies including AI.

instruments.name: National Council for AI
instruments.summary: The Council is the governance arm for Egypt's AI Strategy.

instruments.name: African Working Group on AI
instruments.summary: The AI Working Group (AIWG) is a pioneering platform which aims to develop a unified AI strategy for Africa.

instruments.name: Arab AI Working Group
instruments.summary: The Arab AI Working Group aims to develop a common Arab strategy.

instruments.name: AI for Industry
instruments.summary: AI4I is a training programme to equip participants with basic AI and data competency skills.

instruments.name: AI for Everyone
instruments.summary: AI4E is a 3-hour workshop to introduce anyone to modern AI technologies and applications so that they can be savvy consumers of AI products and services.

instruments.name: Independent Research Fund Denmark
instruments.summary: Independent Research Fund Denmark supports AI research through a new funding call in 2025, with a focus on responsible and ethical use of AI. The initiative funds projects based on researchers' own ideas and promotes scientific progress across all fields. It aims to strengthen Denmark's position in AI by encouraging high-quality, independent research.

instruments.name: Transforming Education Through Technology Masterplan 2030
instruments.summary: The Masterplan outlines how schools in Singapore can better leverage technology, including AI, to enhance teaching and learning.

instruments.name: AI VERIFY
instruments.summary: An AI governance testing framework and toolkit for companies.

instruments.name: SME:DIGITAL
instruments.summary: A co-ordinated scheme to support the digital transformation of Danish SMEs, which can benefit their ability to innovate in AI.

instruments.name: AI Governance Testing Framework Minimum Viable Product (MVP)
instruments.summary: The Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA) and the Personal Data Protection Commission (PDPC) are working with like-minded partners to develop a credible Minimum Viable Product (MVP) that will allow industry to achieve greater transparency around AI systems, and enable organisations to deploy AI systems in a trusted manner.

instruments.name: Law on the Disclosure of Data Ethics Policy
instruments.summary: The Danish government has adopted law on the disclosure of its Data Ethics Policy. The law affects Denmark's largest companies and how they conduct their annual reporting.

instruments.name: Digital Hub Denmark
instruments.summary: A platform aiming at developing public-private collaboration models. It helps bringing together private businesses, researchers, tech-entrepreneurs, and students to foster the development of new digital products.

instruments.name: Working Group on AI Governance Under the Asean Digital Senior Officials' Meeting
instruments.summary: The 4th ASEAN Digital Ministers' Meeting (ADGMIN) has accepted a recommendation to set up a new Working Group under the ASEAN Digital Senior Officials' Meeting (ADGSOM) on AI Governance, including initial work on generative AI.

instruments.name: Digital Platform SPROGTEKNOLOGI.DK
instruments.summary: A joint public sector collaboration was initiated to develop a Common Danish language resource.

instruments.name: Danish Road Directorate
instruments.summary: The Danish Road Directorate has been amended to take into account driverless cars. According to the amended Act, any company that wishes to carry out testing with self-driving cars must apply to the Ministry of Transportation for a permit.

instruments.name: Advisory Council on the Ethical Use of AI and Data
instruments.summary: The Advisory Council on the Ethical Use of AI and Data was set up to advise Singapore Government on issues arising from commercial deployment of AI that may require policy or regulatory intervention.

instruments.name: Innovation Fund Denmark
instruments.summary: Innovation Fund Denmark supports research and innovation projects to help businesses and institutions develop new technologies, including AI. In 2024, it dedicated 100 million DKK to AI projects to boost growth and solve important challenges. This initiative helps create smarter solutions that benefit society and the economy.

instruments.name: National AI Strategy 2.0
instruments.summary: Amid recent advances, especially in Generative AI, we refreshed our National AI Strategy in 2023. Guided by the vision AI for the Public Good, for Singapore and the World, our second National AI Strategy outlines how we will achieve our vision for Singapore to be a place where AI serves as a force for good, and where we harness AI to uplift and empower our people and businesses.

instruments.name: National AI Strategy 1.0
instruments.summary: In 2019, we unveiled our first National AI Strategy, outlining plans to deepen the use of AI to transform our economy. By 2023, our early investment in AI led to the establishment of about 150 teams working on research and development, and 900 startups exploring new ideas with AI.

instruments.name: Centre for Public Private Innovation
instruments.summary: The goal of CO-PI is to strengthen public-private collaboration on innovation.

instruments.name: Danish Data Ethics Council
instruments.summary: In 2019, the Danish government launched an independent Data Ethics Council.

instruments.name: Strategic Approach to Artificial Intelligence “A more robust foundation for the responsible development and use of AI in Denmark"
instruments.summary: The Danish government's vision is that developing and using AI should always be citizen-centric. Danish companies must be globally competitive, and Denmark should be a world leader in using AI in the public sector. The strategic Approachsets up three guiding principles and initiate four new national initiatives for the usage and development of responsible AI.

instruments.name: Catalogue of Autonomous Vehicle Testing Areas on Public Roads
instruments.summary: This initiative offers a free digital map of Czech public roads designed for testing autonomous vehicles safely. It helps developers and engineers test vehicle systems virtually before real-world use, reducing risks and costs. The tool uses advanced scanning and modeling to create realistic road simulations, supporting better development of self-driving technologies.

instruments.name: National Supercomputer National Centre - IT4INNOVATIONS
instruments.summary: IT4Innovations National Supercomputing Centre operates powerful computers to support research and innovation. It provides access to supercomputers and develops AI technologies to help solve complex problems in science and industry. This initiative aims to advance AI research and make high-performance computing tools available to researchers and businesses.

instruments.name: Digital Czech Republic
instruments.summary: Digital Czech Republic is a national strategy that supports the country's transition to the digital age. It focuses on digital public services, education, the economy, and cooperation within the EU. The initiative aims to improve digital skills, modernize public administration, and boost economic growth through digital technologies.

instruments.name: Innovation Strategy of the Czech Republic
instruments.summary: The initiative was presented by the Prime Minister and Minister for Industry and Trade (who is in charge of the implementation). The strategy summarizes the ambitions of the Czech Republic to become a leader in the technological development.

instruments.name: Chilean Participation Process on AI
instruments.summary: The Science, Technology, Knowledge, and Innovation Ministry launched a process to collect the vision, perceptions, opinions, and concerns of people and organisations regarding the use and development of AI in Chile.

instruments.name: AI Observatory and Forum
instruments.summary: The AI Observatory and Forum (AIO&F) was launched in February 2020 to track and assess how artificial intelligence is developing, especially its legal and ethical impacts. It brings together independent experts to monitor AI research, social effects, and regulation trends. The initiative supports informed policymaking and public understanding of AI.

instruments.name: National Challenges
instruments.summary: Documents that contain a series of strategic guidelines to contribute to the consistency and planning of a public policy on science, technology, knowledge and innovation to address the country's challenges, with a view to comprehensive, inclusive, and sustainable development.

instruments.name: AI Use Cases in the Public Sector
instruments.summary: This initiative lists different AI use cases in the Chilean public sector.

instruments.name: National Open Data Portal
instruments.summary: The National Open Data Portal is an API interface that provides access to a large data repository of the public administration. The main objective of the data.gov.cy is to offer the user the ability to easily and quickly find and access processed or unprocessed public sector data, with a view to their reuse and exploitation beyond their original destination, for the development of innovative services / products with added value. This both promotes economic growth and ensures transparency.

instruments.name: Digital Talent
instruments.summary: This initiative integrates companies, training institutions, and the government to develop new capacities in people, in tune with the demands of the digital economy, generating more opportunities to access quality jobs. It aims to connect the demand for talent, the supply of training and job placement.

instruments.name: Smart Job Retraining
instruments.summary: Design and build a web platform that allows smart job retraining.

instruments.name: Digital Economy Partnership Agreement
instruments.summary: The Digital Economy Partnership Agreement (DEPA) between Chile, Singapore, and New Zealand will help establish new rules and practices for digital trade, and promote ongoing discussion on issues like digital inclusion, inclusive trade, and support for small and medium enterprises (SMEs) in the digital economy.

instruments.name: National AI Research Center
instruments.summary: Center of investigation which will develop cutting-edge research on AI.Part of the Center of Excellence from Ministry of Science, Technology, Knowledge, and Innovation.

instruments.name: Guidelines for Ethical Application of AI in Education
instruments.summary: As AI becomes embedded into every aspect of our lives, including education, there is a need for both teachers and students to know about AI, to know how to use AI, to know how AI uses their data and to ensure that the way that use AI is both ethical and safe.

instruments.name: AI subject curricula: Artificial Intelligence - From Theory to Practice
instruments.summary: The AI curriculum has already been developed for primary and secondary schools and is set to be implemented at the start of the 2024/25 school year.

instruments.name: Data Observatory
instruments.summary: Public-private academic foundation aiming to manage the complexity of global value datasets to make them widely available and easier to work with, enabling their use by industry, government, academia, and society to create value in a very broad sense, from talent formation and big data capacity building to training ML algorithms.

instruments.name: PhD Scholarships for Technological Revolution and Digital Transformation
instruments.summary: The National Research and Development Agency (ANID) is awarding scholarships to Chileans and foreigners with permanent residence in Chile to start or continue studies in topics such as digital transformation, artificial intelligence and data science.

instruments.name: National Digital Languages Plan
instruments.summary: This initiative aims to promote the digital transformation of the country by training teachers in the use of tools that contribute to promoting the teaching of computational thinking and programming in the classroom. In this way, the Plan will leave capacities installed in the schools.

instruments.name: AI National Policy
instruments.summary: The Chilean AI Policy 2021-2030 covers three pillars: (1) enabling factors, (2) development and adoption of AI (3) ethics, regulatory aspects and socio-economic impacts.

instruments.name: Detection of Marine Litter and Control of Its Dispersal
instruments.summary: To be determined

instruments.name: Detection of fraud in sick leave in the Education sector
instruments.summary: Detection of fraud in sick leave in the Education sector

instruments.name: U.S. - India Artificial Intelligence Initiative
instruments.summary: The IUSSTF U.S. - India Artificial Intelligence (USIAI) Initiative provides a framework to strengthen the strategic partnership by focusing on AI cooperation in critical areas that are priorities for both countries. USIAI will serve as a platform to discuss opportunities for bilateral AI R&D collaboration, share ideas for developing an AI workforce, and recommend modes and mechanisms for catalyzing the partnerships.

instruments.name: National Strategy on Artificial Intelligence
instruments.summary: The Strategy is focused on leveraging AI for inclusive growth in line with the Government policy of "Sabka Saath Sabka Vikas" to develop the research ecosystem, promote adoption and address AI skills in the population. The strategy also flags issues such as ethics, bias and privacy issues relating to AI, and envisions the government promoting research in technology to address these concerns. The strategy focuses on agriculture, health and education, where public investment would be necessary.

instruments.name: Strategic Action Plan for AI
instruments.summary: The Strategic Action Plan for AI describes the course that the Netherlands wants to take. It is a first step towards initiating concrete measures to achieve the intended acceleration and national profiling. To achieve its goals, the government cooperates with the Dutch AI Coalition. Here, companies, government agencies, knowledge institutions and educational institutions will work together to implement new AI actions that help the specific domains and sectors.

instruments.name: AI Use Cases in the Public Sector
instruments.summary: AI use cases in the public sector in the Netherlands.

instruments.name: Dutch Digitalisation Strategy 2021
instruments.summary: The 2021 DDS provides an overview of the current state of digitalisation in country, identify future trends and analyses the past digitalisation progress.

instruments.name: Dutch Digitalisation Strategy 2020
instruments.summary: Update the report on the existing Dutch Digitalisation strategy 2020.

instruments.name: National Guidelines for Gene Therapy Product Development and Clinical Trials
instruments.summary: This initiative aims to provide advice and directions regarding regulatory requirements for preclinical studies and clinical translation.

instruments.name: Knowledge and Innovation Agenda Ict
instruments.summary: The national agenda for ICT knowledge and innovation (2016-2019) is the framework for PPP-programmes for high end solutions, based on digital technologies 1) big data, 2) artificial intelligence, 3) blockchain, 4) cyber security and 5) Communication technologies (5G).

instruments.name: Knowledge and Innovation Agenda
instruments.summary: HTSM has established a thematic framework with five grand societal challenges: climate (including energy and water), sustainability(including circular economy and food), health, security, and mobility.

instruments.name: Knowledge and Innovation Covenant
instruments.summary: The covenant describes the cooperation between many stakeholders in the Netherlands on key technologies, including AI.

instruments.name: Experimental Law on Self-driving Vehicles
instruments.summary: With effect from 1 July 2019, public road tests involving self-driving vehicles without drivers present are allowed under certain conditions.

instruments.name: Non-discrimination by Design
instruments.summary: Establishes guidelines for the development and application of algorithms.

instruments.name: Vision on Generative AI
instruments.summary: As one of the first EU Member States, the Dutch government has presented a vision on generative AI. In this vision, the government emphasizes the urgent need to take action in light of the opportunities and challenges presented by this disruptive yet promising technology. The vision aligns with a series of investments worth millions of euros already made by research institutions, private enterprises, and the government, all aimed at AI, including generative AI, in the Netherlands.

instruments.name: AI Coalition of the Netherlands
instruments.summary: More than 400 parties from the business community, government, education and research institutions and social organizations have joined the Dutch AI Coalition that launched in 2019. The Dutch AI Coalition (NL AIC) is a public-private partnership that functions as the catalyst for AI in The Netherlands. All parties work in an ongoing multidisciplinary effort to develop transformative technologies in the Netherlands.

instruments.name: AI for the Netherlands
instruments.summary: AINED is the result of a Dutch coalition of industry and academia, it published goals and actions for a national AI plan.

instruments.name: National Education Lab AI
instruments.summary: NOLAI is the National Education Lab AI where teachers, school leaders, school administrators, teacher trainers and people from business work together with academics to improve the quality of primary and secondary education using smart technology.

instruments.name: Egypt National AI Strategy
instruments.summary: The National AI Strategy is a key priority for helping achieve Egypt's sustainable development goals.

instruments.name: Algorithm Supervision Body
instruments.summary: The Dutch government has created an algorithmic supervisory body at the country's data protection regulator.

instruments.name: National Ethical Guidelines for Biomedical and Health Research Involving Human Participants
instruments.summary: This initiative provides general guidelines that are applicable to all biomedical, social and behavioural science research for health conducted in India involving human participants, their biological material and data.

instruments.name: Leveraging Artificial Intelligence and Big Data in Telecommunication Sector
instruments.summary: This initiative aims to ensure the development of responsible Artificial Intelligence (AI) in India to adopt a regulatory framework.

instruments.name: Biological Data Storage, Access and Sharing Policy of India
instruments.summary: These guidelines for the sharing of data generated by scientists in India using modern biotechnological tools and methods provide broad guidelines with specific insights into modern high-throughput, high-volume data.

instruments.name: Approach Document for India: Part 3 - Adopting Framework - A use case approach on facial recognition technology
instruments.summary: This initiative aims to develop governance and regulatory frameworks to reduce the possible hazards of AI.

instruments.name: Approach Document for India: Part 2 - Operationalizing Principles for Responsible AI
instruments.summary: This initiative consolidates several best practices to ensure that AI solutions are socially conscious and travel beyond the digital divide. The strategy builds upon previous approaches to bring under its ambit an accountable and utility-maximising approach to deploying AI solutions.

instruments.name: Approach Document for India: Part 1 - Principles for Responsible AI
instruments.summary: This initiative proposes principles for the responsible management of AI systems that may be leveraged by relevant stakeholders in India, derived from the Constitution of India, among others.

instruments.name: National AI Strategy: Key Action for Promoting the Integration and Development of AI in Cyprus
instruments.summary: A revised/updated strategy was prepared in 2020 with an action plan

instruments.name: National Artificial Intelligence Resource Portal
instruments.summary: This initiative aims to promote R&D in the field of artificial intelligence (AI) through a cloud-based computation platforms.

instruments.name: INDIAai Portal: National AI Portal
instruments.summary: This initiative aims to serve as single-stop portal for information relating to Artificial Intelligence in India.

instruments.name: National Plan for the Development of AI
instruments.summary: The Croatian government is currently working on a National Plan for the Development of AI. This section will be updated with more information as soon as it is published.

instruments.name: The Digital Personal Data Protection Act
instruments.summary: An Act to provide for the processing of digital personal data in a manner that recognises both the right of individuals to protect their personal data and the need to process such personal data for lawful purposes and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.

instruments.name: Genome Canada
instruments.summary: Genome Canada is a not-for-profit corporation dedicated to accelerating the development of Canadian research capacity in genomics and strengthen international partnerships in this field.

instruments.name: STEM Cell Network
instruments.summary: The Stem Cell Network (SCN) is a national not-for-profit corporation dedicated to enabling the translation of stem cell research into clinical applications, commercial products and public policy.

instruments.name: Ontario Working for Workers Act
instruments.summary: The Province of Ontario passed an act that requires employers to notify employees of electronic employee monitoring policies.

instruments.name: Canada's Directive on Automated Decision-making
instruments.summary: The Directive provides a risk-based approach to ensuring the transparency, accountability, legality, and fairness of automated decisions that affect Canadians. The Directive is accompanied by the Algorithmic Impact Assessment, which governs the use of AI systems and including generative AI within the federal public service.

instruments.name: AI Source List
instruments.summary: The Government of Canada has created an AI Source List with 73 pre-approved suppliers to provide Canada with responsible and effective AI services, solutions and products. The framework allows government agencies to expedite procurement from firms that have demonstrated that they are capable of providing quality AI goods and services.

instruments.name: Voluntary Code of Conduct on the Responsible Development and Management of Advanced Generative AI Systems
instruments.summary: The code identifies measures that should be applied in advance of binding regulation pursuant to the Artificial Intelligence and Data Act by all firms developing or managing the operation of a generative AI system with general-purpose capabilities, as well as additional measures that should be taken by firms developing or managing the operations of these systems that are made widely available for use, and which are therefore subject to a wider range of potentially harmful or inappropriate use.

instruments.name: Guide on the use of Generative AI
instruments.summary: This document provides preliminary guidance to federal institutions on their use of generative AI tools. This includes instances where these tools are deployed by federal institutions. It provides an overview of generative AI, identifies challenges and concerns relating to its use, puts forward principles for using it responsibly, and offers policy considerations and best practices.

instruments.name: Canada's Digital Charter
instruments.summary: Canada's Digital Charter lays a foundation of trust and encourages continued growth across the digital- and data-driven economy.

instruments.name: Algorithmic Impact Assessment
instruments.summary: The AIA is a questionnaire designed to help policymakers and other officials assess and mitigate the risks associated with deploying an automated decision system.

instruments.name: Canada-U.S. Innovation Partnership
instruments.summary: The U.S.-Canada Innovation Partnership will work together to increase cross-border collaboration, foster ideas to develop the workforce of the future, and cultivate a shared values-based approach utilizing policy tools where possible to promote the adoption and acceleration of emerging technologies, innovations, and research.

instruments.name: Innovation Superclusters Initiative
instruments.summary: The Innovation Superclusters Initiative (ISI) invites industry-led consortia to lead and to invest in bold and ambitious proposals that will supercharge regional innovation ecosystems. The program supports new partnerships between large firms, SMEs, and industry-relevant research institutions, promoting the development of globally competitive technology. A small number of high-value, strategic investments will be made to build on shared private sector commitment, demonstrated through matched ind

instruments.name: Quebec AI Forum
instruments.summary: The mission of the Forum IA Quebec is to make AI a lever of economic and social development for Quebec.

instruments.name: National Research Council of Canada's AI for Design and Scientific Discovery Challenge Program
instruments.summary: The application of ML and AI to assist engineers and scientists in accelerating the innovation process.

instruments.name: Advisory Council on AI
instruments.summary: The Advisory Council on AI advises the Government of Canada on building Canada's strengths and global leadership in AI, identifying opportunities to create economic growth that benefits all Canadians, and ensuring that AI advancements reflect Canadian values.

instruments.name: Pan-Canadian AI Strategy
instruments.summary: The Government of Canada is providing the Canadian Institute for Advanced Research (CIFAR) with a contribution of $125 million (in Canadian dollars) to launch a Pan-Canadian Artificial Intelligence Strategy to retain and attract top academic talent, and to increase the number of post-graduate trainees and researchers studying AI. Strategy focused on investments in talent, research capacity, commercialization and standardization of (generative) AI.

instruments.name: Development of Common Standards in the Use of Artificial Intelligence in the Digitization Process in Order to Ensure Guarantees of Equal Access and Respect for Human Rights
instruments.summary: Development of common standards in the use of artificial intelligence in the digitization process in order to ensure guarantees of equal access and respect for human rights.

instruments.name: Concept for the Development of AI in Bulgaria Until 2030
instruments.summary: The Bulgarian government approved on 16 December 2020 its national AI strategic document, while also preparing specific policy reports focusing on education, training, and research.

instruments.name: Framework on Ethical Guidelines
instruments.summary: Innoviris, the regional institute for research and innovation in Brussels, is currently working on a framework of ethical guidelines, which would help orienting the regional R&D strategy, including a regional AI strategy, towards an ethical and responsible R&D policy.

instruments.name: Brussels Region AI Policy
instruments.summary: Policies to support AI-related research and innovation.

instruments.name: Declaration on AI in the Nordic-baltic Region
instruments.summary: Collaboration on:1. Improving opportunities for skills development.2. Enhancing access to data.3. Developing ethical and transparent guidelines, standards, principles, and values.4. Developing standards for hardware and software that enable privacy, security, and trust.5. Ensuring AI gets a prominent role in European discussions of the Digital Single Market.6. Avoiding unnecessary regulations.7. Using the Nordic Council of Ministries to facilitate policy co-operation.

instruments.name: Plan Next Tech Brussels
instruments.summary: This plan aims to boost ICT entrepreneurship in the Brussels capital region.

instruments.name: Research Platforms
instruments.summary: The program Research platforms, a program previously known as Bridge, supports collaborative and multidisciplinary academic projects that guarantee the transfer of knowlegde to industry, the non-profit sector, or the public sector.

instruments.name: Data Protection Authority
instruments.summary: To act as the supervisory data authority in Iceland.

instruments.name: R&D Projects (Industrial Research)
instruments.summary: The R&D projects (Industrial research) program (previously: Explore) enables companies or research institutes to acquire scientific knowledge in order to achieve a predetermined industrial or commercial goal. The result of this project leads to the development of a proof of business or a prototype.

instruments.name: Iceland's AI Strategy (Forthcoming)
instruments.summary: A prioritized list of actions for Iceland to meet the societal and economic changes brought by new technology, specifically AI.

instruments.name: R&D Projects (Experimental Development)
instruments.summary: Experimental development may be defined as the activity which targets the application of the results of industrial research in the form of prototype products, processes, or services, which may not be used for commercial purposes before the end of the project.

instruments.name: Joint R&D Project
instruments.summary: The Joint R&D project call (previously known as Team-up) involves an active participation of both academic units and industrial teams with an aim of strengthening knowledge, transferring IP from academic research to the industry and turning it into prototypes that lead to new business opportunities.

instruments.name: Action Plan for Iceland in the Fourth Industrial Revolution
instruments.summary: Objectives:A prioritized list of actions for Iceland to meet the societal and economic changes brought by new technology, specifically AI.

instruments.name: Campaigns and Projects for the Dissemination of Knowledge
