instruments.summary: The Flemish Government aims to provide advice and raise awareness to stimulate the diffusion of knowledge on AI.

instruments.name: Action Plan AI
instruments.summary: The Flemish Region of Belgium launched an action plan on artificial intelligence (AI).

instruments.name: Autonomous Vehicles - Code of Practice for Testing in Belgium
instruments.summary: Belgian Federal Public Service Mobility and Transport published a "code" for companies that want to test driverless cars in the country.

instruments.name: Knowledge Centre for Data and Society
instruments.summary: As part of the Flemish Action Plan AI, the Knowledge Centre Data & Society (Kenniscentrum Data & Maatschappij) was created to focus on the interplay between data, artificial intelligence and society.

instruments.name: Conversational Robot to Support Entities in the Local Government Sector
instruments.summary: Implementation of a chatbot to assist entities in the Local Administration Sector.

instruments.name: Athena Magazine
instruments.summary: Publication of a free monthly magazine Athena aimed at popularising science and making it accessible to everyone, along with raising the public's and especially young people's awareness, of the challenges, prospects and professions in the fields of research and new technologies.

instruments.name: AI 4 Belgium
instruments.summary: Experts have written AI guidelines for Belgian policy makers.

instruments.name: Clusters Hub.Brussels
instruments.summary: The Regional Innovation Plan for 2014-20 sets out the new role of clusters (strengthening the regional cooperation and the rest of the R&I ecosystem) and the internationalisation of clusters.

instruments.name: Regional Innovation Plan
instruments.summary: The Regional Innovation Plan is the upshot of a comprehensive and inclusive process. More than 200 people from different sectors were consulted, including companies, colleges and universities, (regional) public institutions, representatives of the other Belgian Regions and Communities, professional associations and civil society.

instruments.name: National Convergence Plan for the Development of AI
instruments.summary: Belgium has adopted the National Convergence Plan for the Development of AI, which was approved by the Council of Ministers on 28 October 2022 and proposes concrete actions to make Belgium a #SmartAINation.

instruments.name: Open Data Portal
instruments.summary: The Federal government transposed the EU PSI Directive into the 2016 Law related to the re-use of public sector information, accompanied by the development of a Federal Open Data Strategy.

instruments.name: Open Data Initiatives (Data.gov.be and Statbels Open Data)
instruments.summary: The Federal government has established open databases.

instruments.name: AI Ethical Guidelines
instruments.summary: Objectives:To draw clear guidelines for the AI development and applications in Hungary.

instruments.name: AI Use Cases in the Portuguese Public Sector
instruments.summary: AI use cases in the public sector in Portugal.

instruments.name: Data Market Platform
instruments.summary: To raise awareness of the economic value of commercially viable data, and to encourage their secondary use.

instruments.name: AI in Practice Website
instruments.summary: To raise awareness of AI applicability in business.

instruments.name: Australian Identity - Matching Services Bill
instruments.summary: The Identity-Matching Services Bill 2019 (IMS Bill) authorises the Department of Home Affairs (DOHA) to create and maintain facilities for the sharing of facial images and other identity information between government agencies, and in some cases, private organisations.

instruments.name: Mathematical Foundations of AI
instruments.summary: A consortium of ground researchers focusing on the basic questions of AI.

instruments.name: AI Capability Fund
instruments.summary: The AI Capability Fund was an allocation of over $29 million Australian dollars to build Australia's artificial intelligence capability and support the responsible development of AI.

instruments.name: Space Infrastructure Fund - Robotics, Automation and AI Command and Control Centre
instruments.summary: The Space Infrastructure Fund (SIF) is a AUD $19.5 million (EUR 11.8 million) investment in seven infrastructure projects to drive the growth of Australia's space sector. The Space Infrastructure Fund: Robotics, Automation and AI Command and Control Centre grant opportunity provided a single grant of up to AUD 4.5 million (EUR 2.7 million) over three years, to establish the Robotics, Automation and AI command and Control Centre (the Centre) in Western Australia.

instruments.name: IndiaAI 2023: Expert Group Report
instruments.summary: IndiaAI has a mission-centric approach which ensures a precise and cohesive strategy to bridge the gaps in existing AI ecosystem viz-a-viz Compute infrastructure, Data, AI financing, Research and Innovation, targeted Skilling and institutional capacity for Data to maximize the potential of AI for advancing India's progress.

instruments.name: Next Generation Technologies Fund
instruments.summary: The Next Generation Technologies Fund is a AUD 730 million Australian government program that supports innovation by bringing together Defence, universities, industry, and research organizations. It aims to develop advanced technologies and create new commercial opportunities. This initiative helps strengthen national security and boost collaboration for future technology breakthroughs.

instruments.name: R&D Competitiveness and Excellence Co-operation Programmes
instruments.summary: The programme supports the solution of major and complex tasks and the achievement of R&D and innovation results in several areas of expertise in the cooperation of the most outstanding actors in the field.

instruments.name: ML and AI Future Science Platform
instruments.summary: Future Science Platforms (FSPs) are an investment in science that underpins innovation and that has the potential to help reinvent and create new industries for Australia.

instruments.name: CSIRO ML and AI Future Science Platform
instruments.summary: The MLAI FSP's cross disciplinary teams solve fundamental problems in scientific and data-driven research applications, creating a new ongoing capability within CSIRO to address core research challenges for the benefit of Australia.

instruments.name: Algorithms Research
instruments.summary: On 31 March 2023, the Australian Government began work to better understand how algorithms operate on digital platforms and the potential harms they may cause. The initiative aims to explore regulatory options to keep users safe and improve platform transparency. This effort will help inform policies and build expertise to manage the impact of AI-driven algorithms.

instruments.name: AI Solutions to Build a Stronger Australia
instruments.summary: The AI Solutions to Build a Stronger Australia program will provide challenge-based funding to support public-private partnerships that address challenges of national significant by piloting artificial intelligence solutions.

instruments.name: AI Regulation and Ethics Knowledge Centre
instruments.summary: To create and co-ordinate an extensive pool of experts to help resolve legal issues and matters of ethics relating to the regulation of artificial intelligence and the implementation of the strategy.

instruments.name: Standards Australia: AI Roadmap
instruments.summary: To develop a roadmap of Australia's engagement in the development of AI standards nationally and internationally.

instruments.name: Public Data Portal
instruments.summary: The aim of the public data portal is to establish a complete and responsible national data management scheme, which includes sharing non-personal data assets created in the public sector and having a significant multiplier effect in order to exploit the potential economic stimulation effect associated with their wide availability.

instruments.name: Safe and Responsible AI in Australia: Interim Response
instruments.summary: The Australian Government's interim response to public consultation on Safe and responsible AI in Australia.

instruments.name: Automated Administrative Procedures in Hungarian
instruments.summary: Objectives:- To support the automation of administrative procedures using AI-based services based on a language processing technology for the Hungarian language.- To collect both oral and written training data sets to train the language processing technology tool.- To develop a telephone-based customer service for the public administration using AI solutions.

instruments.name: AI Phd Scholarships
instruments.summary: The Artificial Intelligence Capability Fund included AUD1.4 million to support PhD scholarships in artificial intelligence and machine learning, delivered through the CSIRO's Data61 Scholarships Program.

instruments.name: The Bhashini Initiative (National Language Translation Mission)
instruments.summary: This initiative aims to harness natural language technologies to enable a diverse ecosystem of contributors, partnering entities and citizens for the purpose of transcending language barriers, there by ensuring digital inclusion and digital empowerment

instruments.name: National Laboratory for Autonomous Vehicles
instruments.summary: The Laboratory aims to provide efficient and innovative autonomous solutions for road vehicles, aircraft and mobile robots by relying on a wide group of Hungarian experts. Activities focus on research, development, and demonstration of the components and functional design of experimental vehicles, cyber-physical manufacturing and logistics systems. The Laboratory collaborates with the ZalaZone autonomous vehicle test track.

instruments.name: Aus4innovation (Australia and Vietnam)
instruments.summary: Aus4Innovation is an AUD 11 million development assistance program that aims to strengthen Vietnam's innovation system, prepare for and embrace opportunities associated with Industry 4.0, and help shape Vietnam's innovation agenda in science and technology.

instruments.name: Manufacturing Modernisation Fund
instruments.summary: The $50 million Manufacturing Modernisation Fund provides co-funding for capital investments by manufacturers to scale-up, invest in new technologies and develop high-value products.

instruments.name: National Data Assets Agency
instruments.summary: To co-ordinate and stimulate the strategic management of the data assets. It does not perform independent data processing but aims to encourage and support data utilisation.

instruments.name: Catalysing the AI Opportunity in Our Regions
instruments.summary: The Catalysing the Artificial Intelligence Opportunity in our Regions will co-fund collaborative projects which support regional industries, businesses and communities benefit from the development, adoption and use of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies.

instruments.name: Industry 4.0 Testlab for Australia Pilot Program
instruments.summary: A pilot program that provides $6 million in matched funding to establish six Industry 4.0 testlabs at six Australian universities.

instruments.name: AI and Digital Capability Centres
instruments.summary: Four Digital Capability Centres will be appointed through a competitive process that will focus on specific applications of AI, such as robotics or AI assisted manufacturing

instruments.name: MeitY Quantum Computing Applications Lab
instruments.summary: This initiative aims to accelerate quantum computing-led research and development and enable new scientific discoveries.

instruments.name: Hungary's AI Coalition
instruments.summary: In 2018, the government and a number of academic institutions and companies joined forces to create the AI Coalition. The Coalition is working on developing a national strategy and positioning Hungary as a leader in AI in chosen field. The AI Strategy is going to be released early 2020. Key agenda points planned to create the 2019-2020 AI Map of Hungary that should result in an ai-hungary.com website giving an overview for both internal and external parties on the AI competencies of the country.

instruments.name: Supporting AI in Schools
instruments.summary: Creation and curation of curriculum resources to support teaching and learning about AI and emerging technologies in schools.

instruments.name: Medical Research Future Fund
instruments.summary: The Australian Government provides funding for research through the Medical Research Future Fund (MRFF) and the National Health and Medical Research Council (NHMRC).

instruments.name: AI Action Plan
instruments.summary: Hungary announced an AI Action Plan, which analysts are calling the first pillar of a national AI strategy to define and form the institutional framework of the Hungarian data market and the AI ecosystem. The AI strategy itself should be completed by the start of 2020.

instruments.name: National Data & Analytics Platform
instruments.summary: This initiative aims to democratize access to public government data.

instruments.name: Csiro Innovation Fund Managed by Main Sequence Ventures
instruments.summary: The CSIRO Innovation Fund managed by Main Sequence Ventures is a AUD 242 million venture capital fund to invest in new spin-off companies, and existing startups and SMEs, which are developing technology from, or have ongoing research connections with, CSIRO, universities and other publicly funded research agencies.

instruments.name: India Urban Data Exchange
instruments.summary: This initiative aims to provide a seamless interface for data providers and data users, including ULBs, to share, request, and access datasets related to cities, urban governance, and urban service delivery.

instruments.name: Co-operative Research Centers Program
instruments.summary: The Co-operative Research Centres (CRCs) program supports collaboration between research and industry.

instruments.name: Hungary's AI Strategy
instruments.summary: The Hungarian AI Coalition was established in October 2018 to offer a community and forum for all stakeholders in the Hungarian AI ecosystem who wish to make an active contribution to the development of the Hungarian AI environment and skills. The National AI strategy is the joint, action-oriented product of the Coalitions professional community, consisting of over 240 organisations and over 1000 delegated experts.

instruments.name: KOTAK-IISC AI-ML Centre
instruments.summary: The IISc has set up the AI-ML Centre to promote innovation in AI and ML to develop a talent pool that can meet the industry's emerging requirements.

instruments.name: New Experience Studio at NITI Aayog Cloud Innovation Center
instruments.summary: The studio will help showcase the potential of technologies such as artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), Internet of Things (IoT), augmented reality and virtual reality (AR/ VR), blockchain, and robotics to accelerate their application in public sector use cases; encouraging open innovation, government, healthcare, education, and nonprofit startups from India to showcase their solutions.

instruments.name: Financial Support Instruments
instruments.summary: The purpose of these financial support instruments is to foster innovation, entrepreneurship, and economic growth in Greece. These initiatives aim to create a dynamic and competitive economy by supporting innovation, technological advancement, and the growth of new businesses.The beneficiaries range from businesses, public institutions, and non-profit organizations, to startups, including those in AI sector, and innovative and technology-driven companies, including AI start-ups and scale-ups.

instruments.name: AI Projects in Greece
instruments.summary: The purpose of these AI initiatives in Greece is to foster innovation, support digital transformation, and enhance the competitiveness of various sectors.The beneficiaries of the projects range between startups and entrepreneurs, researchers, startups, and SMEs, local communities, scientists, and technologists, manufacturing sector, and civil servants.

instruments.name: Law 5142/2024 Completion of land registration, simplification of procedures, use of artificial intelligence and provisions for the operation of the Hellenic Land Registry Cadastre", other provisions of the Ministry of Digital Governance.
instruments.summary: It focuses on completing land registration, simplifying procedures, and integrating AI into the Greek Cadaster. It benefits public and private entities, local governments, and citizens by enhancing legal security and reducing bureaucracy. The law addresses inefficiencies in land registration and leverages AI to improve accuracy and speed. It aims to transition Greece to a fully functional land registry system by 2025, using AI to streamline legal reviews and correct records.

instruments.name: Centre of Excellence in Artificial Intelligence and Innovation-Driven Entrepreneurship
instruments.summary: AIIDE-CoE aims to nurture an AI innovation ecosystem, which leads to supporting innovative enterprises and technology facilitation, networking & mentoring, provide data-driven advisory, establishing industry connections, and support business development.

instruments.name: Centre of Excellence for Jewelry AI and Data Science Excellence
instruments.summary: This initiative aims to address the challenges of the supply chain of India's gems and jewellery industry.

instruments.name: Centre of Excellence for AI Internet of Things (IoT) & AI
instruments.summary: The Centre of Excellence for IoT and AI takes advantage of India's IT strengths and helps the country attain a leadership role in the area of hardware and software. The main objective of the centre is to create innovative applications and domain capability by harnessing the innovative nature of the start-up community in India and leveraging the experience of corporate players

instruments.name: ARIS Infrastucture
instruments.summary: ARIS (Advanced Research Information System) is the most powerful computing system in Greece for scientific applications. It was launched in July 2015 by GRNET S.A. under the auspices of the Greek Ministry of Digital Governance, offering a powerful research tool to the Greek scientific community. The ARIS computing system today has a maximum theoretical computing power of 535 TFlop/s (i.e. it can perform 535 trillion mathematical operations/sec) and offers multiple data processing capabilities.

instruments.name: Centre of Excellence for AI and Emerging Technologies
instruments.summary: The project seeks to explore the role of cloud, AI and emerging technologies for transforming and shaping the future of public finance management in India.

instruments.name: National Programme for Government Schools: Responsible AI for Youth
instruments.summary: The aim of this Program is to give the young students of our country a platform and empower them with an appropriate new-age tech mindset, relevant skill sets and access to required tool sets to make them digitally ready for the future.

instruments.name: Artificial Intelligence Task Force for India's Economic Transformation
instruments.summary: Objectives:To leverage AI for economic benefits.To create a policy and legal framework to accelerate the deployment of AI technologies.To issue concrete 5-year horizon recommendations for specific government, industry and research programmes.

instruments.name: mAigov
instruments.summary: mAigov is an AI-powered digital assistant integrated into Greece's unified public administration portal, gov.gr. Launched in December 2023 by the Ministry of Digital Governance, mAigov aims to streamline citizens' interactions with public services by simplifying access to information and procedures.

instruments.name: Law n. 4961/2022 Emerging information and communication technologies and societies, enhancing digital governance and other provisions
instruments.summary: Greek Law 4961/2022 regulates emerging technologies like AI, IoT, and 3D printing to ensure their safe, lawful use. It aims to modernize public services, enhance digital governance, and promote Greece's digital transformation. Beneficiaries include public and private entities, as well as citizens who will experience improved services and data protection. The initiative addresses the need for a structured framework to manage the rapid adoption of advanced technologies.

instruments.name: AI Standardisation Committee
instruments.summary: To tackle standardization challenges, the Department of Telecommunications (DoT) established an AI standardization committee aimed at creating various interface standards and developing India's AI stack. This stack will be organized across all sectors, focusing on data protection, data federation, data minimization, an open algorithm framework, defined data structures, interfaces and protocols, as well as proper monitoring, auditing, logging, and data privacy, among other aspects.

instruments.name: Generative AI Greece 2030 "Futures of Generative AI in Greece"
instruments.summary: This research presents four scenarios of possible alternative future images of Gen AI in Greece by 2030.

instruments.name: AI Centre of Excellence
instruments.summary: Given the long-term investment of the Greek society in highly-educated young scientists and the increasing demand for such talent world-wide, Greece is becoming a very attractive place for setting up Centers of Excellence and Innovation, like DICE. This is gradually impacting the nature of the Greek IT industry, which focuses on innovation and provides services and products throughout the world.

instruments.name: Hellenic Ministry of Digital Governance
instruments.summary: The Hellenic Ministry of Digital Governance is advancing AI initiatives to modernize public services and enhance administrative efficiency in Greece. Law 4961/2022 establishes regulations to ensure the rights of natural and legal persons, enhancing accountability and transparency in AI use. It defines conditions for AI use in both public and private sectors and establishes control mechanisms for AI development.

instruments.name: Special Secretariat of Foresight to the Presidency of Government
instruments.summary: The mission of the Special Secretariat of Foresight isa) the application of foresight methods to identify potential future challenges, risks or opportunities for the country,b) the support of the Government's long-term planning in order to ensure the resilience and strategic autonomy of the country and the emergence of public policies suitable for these objectives,c) the support of the active participation of Greek society in shaping the future.

instruments.name: Responsible AI Principles for Audiovisual Collections
instruments.summary: The NFSA is commencing development of responsible AI principles to guide the uptake and development of AI technologies in service of cultural institution operations; and identifying best practices to share with the wider cultural and collecting sectors preserving and making audiovisual collections accessible.

instruments.name: High Level Advisory Committee on Artificial Intelligence
instruments.summary: The Committee provides evidence-based advice and proposals on how Greece can exploit the multiple potentials and opportunities arising from the use of AI, and how it can implement a coherent framework to protect against the potential challenges and adaptations, inequalities and risks involved.

instruments.name: Quad Principles on Technology Design, Development, Governance, and Use
instruments.summary: The Quad countries (Australia, India, Japan, and the United States of America) affirm that the ways in which technology is designed, developed, governed, and used should be shaped by our shared democratic values and respect for universal human rights.

instruments.name: Brazilian Strategy for Digital Transformation
instruments.summary: Brazil's digital transformation strategy (E-Digital), published on March 2018, harmonises and co-ordinates different governmental initiatives on digital issues to advance the Sustainable Development Goals in Brazil.

instruments.name: Brazilian AI strategy
instruments.summary: The EBIA assumes the role of guiding the actions of the Brazilian State in favor of the development of actions, in its various aspects, that stimulate research, innovation, and development of solutions in Artificial Intelligence, as well as its conscious, ethical, and in favor of a better future use.

instruments.name: Governance Committee of the Brazilian AI strategy
instruments.summary: The Governance Committee is responsible for monitoring and evaluating the Brazilian Artificial Intelligence Strategy, and it is composed of private and public organisations, civil organisations and specialists.

instruments.name: Hellenic National Bioethics Commission
instruments.summary: The Commission is an advisory body to the State in the fields of life sciences and new technologies in general. Its mission is to investigate the ethical, social and legal aspects and implications in the fields of, in particular, biology, biotechnology and biology, biotechnology, medicine and genetics, and new technologies such as artificial intelligence, advanced algorithms and robotics.

instruments.name: NSW AI Assurance Framework
instruments.summary: The NSW AI Assurance Framework is a set of rules by the New South Wales government to ensure AI systems are safe and fair in public services. It helps government staff use AI responsibly and protects the public from risks. This initiative was created to build trust in AI and make sure it works well for everyone.

instruments.name: Human Rights and Technology Discussion Paper
instruments.summary: The Australian Human Rights Commission has launched the Human Rights and Technology Discussion Paper, which makes wide-ranging proposals for safeguarding human rights and encouraging accessible, equal and accountable use of new technology in Australia.

instruments.name: Brazilian AI Bill, n. 21/2020
instruments.summary: Bill No. 21/20 outlines guidelines to develop and utilize AI in Brazil.

instruments.name: Jaque and Services Guide
instruments.summary: Jaque is an AI-based virtual clerk to guide citizens through the digital catalogue that centralises all information regarding public services offered by the State Government of Alagoas.

instruments.name: AI use cases in the Public Sector
instruments.summary: A series of use cases of AI in the Brazilian public sector.

instruments.name: Public Consultation for the Brazilian AI strategy
instruments.summary: The Brazilian AI Strategy will cover relevant topics on AI and its impact on economy, ethics, development, education and jobs, as well as co-ordinate specific public policies addressing such issues.

instruments.name: Applied Technology Centres for Urban Efficiency
instruments.summary: Evidence-based assessment, simulation and demonstration centres for technologies applied to greater efficiency in urban dynamics.

instruments.name: Australia's AI Ethics Framework
instruments.summary: Australia has developed an AI ethics framework.

instruments.name: Australian Framework for Generative AI in Schools
instruments.summary: The Australian Framework for Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Schools (the Framework) is a set of six principles which are supported by 25 guiding statements. The Framework was developed in consultation with teachers, students, unions, industry, academics, and parent and school representative bodies from all sectors.

instruments.name: Tech Trends Position Statement: Generative AI
instruments.summary: One of a series of position statements by Australia's independent online safety regulator on emerging tech trends and challenges. The statement outlines steps industry can take to prevent online safety risks of generative AI.

instruments.name: Prosperity Through Innovation
instruments.summary: Innovation and Science Australia report to the Australian Government “ Australia 2030: Prosperity through innovation (the 2030 Plan) sets out the path to a more innovative Australia in 2030.

instruments.name: Australia's Tech Future
instruments.summary: In December 2018, the Australian government released its digital economy strategy called "Australia's Tech Future", which is a vision for how businesses, government and the community can work together to maximise the benefits and opportunities afforded by advanced digital technology.

instruments.name: Guide to Artificial Intelligence Ethical, Transparent and Responsible in the Public Administration
instruments.summary: The guide define what AI is and how it works, show how is present in society and to identify some of the effects resulting from its use.It also informs about the framework of AI in the World and in Portugal, and identifies the ecosystem and the main actors in the national context. On the other hand and considering the importance of data for the development and feeding of these systems, also makes reference to the data ecosystem in the Public Administration (AP) and to the principles that must

instruments.name: LEAM - Large European AI Models
instruments.summary: LEAM is an initiative of the German AI Association (KI Bundesverband) and leading representatives from industry and research that promotes the development of large AI models.

instruments.name: Regulatory Sandboxes Enabling Innovation and Advancing Regulation
instruments.summary: It is a cross-cutting initiative. Regulatory Sandboxes can be used for various fields of innovation, such as AI, blockchain, digital platforms, sharing economy, eHealth, modern mobility and logistics solutions, digital administration and energy research.

instruments.name: "Automated Vehicles" Bill in the Road Traffic Act
instruments.summary: Following an amendment to the Vienna Convention on Road Traffic, the German government introduced in January 2017 a bill that would allow the use of automated vehicles.

instruments.name: KI4KL
instruments.summary: The aim is to strengthen growth potential and promote future-orientated development. The acquired knowledge and research results will be transferred to the economy and local authorities in a targeted manner.

instruments.name: Universal AI Platform for the BFV
instruments.summary: Development of an AI platform for universal use within the federal revenue administration. The platform can be used in various AI projects of the federal revenue administration and allows for a comprehensive portfolio of AI technologies.

instruments.name: Real-world Test Field for Digital Mobility
instruments.summary: The initiative combines traditional traffic planning with mobility and innovation management using AI. A total of 10 sub-projects on digital mobility are being were implemented in parallel and scientifically monitored in order to deduce how digitalization can effectively contribute to achieving the climate goals in the mobility sector. The results of the project will be presented at the ITS World Congress 2021 in Hamburg, Germany in October 2021.

instruments.name: Funding Priority: Digital Innovations for the Improvement of Patient-centred Care in Healthcare
instruments.summary: The advancing digitalization in the healthcare system offers a variety of opportunities to strengthen and further develop the recognized high quality and cost-effectiveness of German health care. Artificial intelligence (AI) methods in combination with the use and evaluation of large amounts of data offer special opportunities. This offers considerable potential, especially for further developments in the areas of decision support through knowledge-based expert systems.

instruments.name: Funding Initiative in the Field of AI
instruments.summary: The initiative is intended to finance research projects from all areas of AI research in various funding programmes. One focus of the initiative is the funding of independent junior research groups in the DFG's Emmy Noether Programme.

instruments.name: Special Program "Autonomous - Performing Arts and AI"
instruments.summary: Objectives:To support the artistic and social relevance of the independently producing arts.To create occasions for increased qualifications and further development.

instruments.name: Trilateral French-Japanese-German Research Projects on AI
instruments.summary: Based on the added value obtained through the collaboration of the three countries, the aim is to present the direction of future digital economy and society through technical progress in AI research to strengthen trust, transparency and fairness as well as improving performance and investigating AI methods.

instruments.name: Reality Lab for AI in Civil Protection
instruments.summary: To test and develop solutions that make AI-based technologies accessible and useable for practitioners and responders.

instruments.name: AI Startup Hubs
instruments.summary:
Objectives: 
- Support science-related start-ups in the field of artificial intelligence as well as their scaling and internationalization
- Promote start-ups with a special focus on artificial intelligence in aviation, maritime tech, GreenTech and MedTech sectors in Hamburg metropolitan region.
- Establishment of an internationally visible AI innovation ecosystem.

instruments.name: German Accelerator
instruments.summary: Objectives:Equip AI startups with the necessary skills and tools to build a successful, scalable business early on.Support German AI startups in validating their business model in new potential target markets.Offer German AI startups individualized programs to support them in entering international innovation hubs.Connect German AI startups with experts around the world to provide high-end mentoring sessions tailored to the startups needs.Increase visibility of German AI start ups.

instruments.name: EURO HPC Supercomputer
instruments.summary: The European High Performance Computing Joint Undertaking (EuroHPC JU) and the Minho Advanced Computing Centre (MACC) have launched a call for tender for the procurement of a petascale supercomputer, capable of executing more than one Petaflop, or 1 million billion calculations per second.

instruments.name: Funding Initiatives on AI and Machine Learning
instruments.summary: The AI initiatives contribute to the Federal government's AI Strategy, which was launched in November 2018. The machine learning initiatives follow the research initiatives on Big Data. Methods and technologies for analyzing data have already been developed in those initiatives. The funding initiatives focus on topics like explainability and transparency, on young researchers and infrastructure.

instruments.name: Calls for High Performance Computing R&D projects: artificial intelligence on the cloud in collaboration with Google
instruments.summary: The collaboration agreement between FCT and Google will result in the availability of US$ 2 million in Google Cloud platform credits over a period of two years for artificial intelligence R&D projects.

instruments.name: Ethical Guidelines for Self-driving Cars
instruments.summary: To address ethical issues of automated and connected driving at the national, European and international level.

instruments.name: Platform Industry 4.0
instruments.summary: The platform serves as a unique communication channel to the public and closely cooperates with regional and local multipliers to spread Industry 4.0 to the German regions.

instruments.name: Mobilizing Program to Foster AI in the Public Administration
instruments.summary: Program in Artificial Intelligence and Data Science in the Public Administration through open call for R&D projects.

instruments.name: Network AI in Employment and Social Protection Services
instruments.summary: Facilitate exchange on the topics of artificial intelligence and digitalisation strengthen practical cooperation between public authorities in these areas.

instruments.name: Digital Hub Initiative
instruments.summary: Germany's federal structure with broad regional start-up communities includes cross-sectoral innovation hubs such as Berlin, Hamburg and Munich as well as specific sectoral innovation hubs like Frankfurt.

instruments.name: Technological Free Zones
instruments.summary: The ZLTs will focus on innovation and testing emerging technologies like artificial intelligence (AI), blockchain, big data, and 5G in real environments. The project is part of the Portuguese government's digital transition plan that is aimed at boosting social-economic progress and facilitating the country's transition to a sustainable economy.

instruments.name: National Internet of Things Plan - Decree n 9854
instruments.summary: The Decree institutes the National Internet of Things Plan and provides for the Management and Monitoring Chamber for the Development of Communication Systems Machine to Machine and Internet of Things.

instruments.name: General Law on Protection of Personal Data
instruments.summary: The Brazilian data protection law includes information on the protection of personal data as well as a section on database ownership and database rights.

instruments.name: Doctoral Graduates' Employment
instruments.summary: FCT runs a career development program to ensure the integration of highly qualified and international competitive scientists into research and academic centers.

instruments.name: Applied Artificial Intelligence Research Centers
instruments.summary: Brazil has announced its aims to establish eight applied research centres hosted by established academic and research institutions.

instruments.name: Act Amending the Road Traffic Act and the Compulsory Insurance Act (Autonomous Driving Act)
instruments.summary: The Autonomous Driving Act is one of several measures to create a legal framework to implement the German federal government's 2015 Strategy for Automated and Connected Driving. The Federal Ministry of Transport and Digital Infrastructure has authorized testing of connected vehicles under real-life conditions. In 2017, Germany amended its Road Traffic Act to allow drivers to transfer control of their vehicles to highly or fully automated driving systems and for them to be used on public roads.

instruments.name: Fair Forward AI for All
instruments.summary: FAIR Forward is committed to the goals of the German AI strategy with a particular focus on international networking. The initiative seeks to establish capacities and knowledge about AI in emerging and developing countries so that economic and social opportunities can be utilised there. The objective is to bring global partners into a position to utilize the potential of AI for sustainable development and thus to help achieve the sustainable development goals (SDG) in the Agenda 2030.

instruments.name: Funding Initiative International Future Labs for AI
instruments.summary: Objectives:Bringing together researchers from around the world to work on current artificial intelligence research and development issues.Fostering the transfer of knowledge and technology.Raising the international profile of Germany as a research and innovation hub.

instruments.name: AI Graduate and Undergraduate Courses
instruments.summary: The National Higher Education System offers undergraduate and graduated degrees that empower student with basic skills, competences, and knowledge to explore artificial intelligence. Computer Science, Computational Science, and Computer and Electronic Engineering cover mathematics, algorithm design and analysis, and programming, to name a few disciplines that are the backbone of the artificial intelligence programmes.

instruments.name: Court Ruling on the Use of AI Software in Hesse and Hamburg
instruments.summary: To prohibit the use of Palantir's AI software for predictive policing in Hesse and Hamburg.

instruments.name: MFUND
instruments.summary: mFUND supports founders, start-ups, businesses, but also authorities and institutions of higher education. Funding recipients develop digital business ideas that are based on mobility, spatial and weather data. There are two funding lines, which allow long-term support from the initial idea to the development of a prototype. Another funding programme which is included in the mFund focuses on funding structural reform in former lignite mining areas. mFUND will provide funding totalling EUR 480 mi

instruments.name: Police AI Strategy (KI@Polizei)
instruments.summary: AI in the sense of more complex algorithmic systems has been used in the police for a long time. They are part of police-specific software applications. Growing application possibilities and increasing complexity of algorithmic processes lead to new challenges, which we want to address on the basis of the following strategy.

instruments.name: Regulatory Framework for Automated Vehicles in Australia
instruments.summary: Policy paper, which was subsequently endorsed by the Infrastructure and Transport Ministers' Meeting in February 2022. The paper outlines the proposed end-to-end regulatory framework for the commercial deployment of automated vehicles in Australia. The design of this framework represents the culmination of work led by the NTC over the five years on national reforms for automated vehicles, and was developed in consultation withgovernments and industry.

instruments.name: Australia's National Enforcement Guidelines for Automated Vehicles
instruments.summary: These Guidelines clarify concepts of control and proper control for different levels of automation.

instruments.name: National AI Strategy
instruments.summary: The update aims to strengthen Germany as aninternationally competitive centre of AI research, development and application. This entails further establishing and expanding AI ecosystems in Germany and Europe to strengthen the application of AI on a broad scale and at the same time to promote the visibility of outstandinginitiatives and structures.

instruments.name: Action Plan for Digitalisation and AI in Mobility
instruments.summary: The measures are divided into five priority areas of action:-Expansion of a high-performance, digital infrastructure-Equipping transport infrastructure with the necessary digital technology-Creation of a comprehensive and reliable database-Promotion of innovative technologies and their regulation for the automation and networking of vehicles, processes and services for all modes of transport-Networking of measures and actors across all modes of transport

instruments.name: Data Ethics Commission
instruments.summary: Objectives:To develop ethical benchmarks and guidelines as well as specific recommendations for action, aiming at protecting the individual, preserving social cohesion, and safeguarding and promoting prosperity in the information age.

instruments.name: Opinion of the Data Ethics Commission
instruments.summary: Overarching recommendations to the German federal government on future legislation to regulate artificial intelligence.

instruments.name: AI Technology Roadmap
instruments.summary: Published by the Australian government in November 2019, and co-developed by CSIRO's Data61 and the Department of Industry, Innovation, and Science, the Roadmap identifies strategies to help develop a national AI capability to boost the productivity of Australian industry, create jobs and economic growth, and improve the quality of life for current and future generations.

instruments.name: Next Generation AI Graduates Program
instruments.summary: The Next Generation Artificial Intelligence Graduates Program will attract and train the next generation of specialist workers in artificial intelligence by awarding industry co-funded scholarships to Australian students to work with industry on research projects and internships.

instruments.name: Regulatory Technology Innovation Challenges
instruments.summary: Regulatory Technology Innovation Challenges will provide AUD 10.0 million (EUR 6 million) in grants to Australian businesses to develop regulatory technology solutions that will help reduce compliance burdens on business. This initiative will establish a new round under the Business Research and Innovation Initiative (BRII).

instruments.name: Intellectual Property Laws Amendment Act
instruments.summary: Intellectual property legislative measures in Australia have been adapted for AI use.

instruments.name: Australian Federal Police Technology Strategy
instruments.summary: The AFP Technology Strategy outlines the orginaisation's direction and the capability it needs to acquire to achieve its crititical outcomes. The strategy provides a high-level roadmap that identifies the necessary changes and actions required to achieve these outcomes. The strategy consists of six strategic shifts in technology use, which includes AI-enabled data analysis.

instruments.name: Artificial Intelligence for Law Enforcement and Community Safety (AiLECS) Lab
instruments.summary: AiLECS Lab is a collaboration between the Australian Federal Police (AFP) and Monash University. The aim of the AiLECS lab is to pursue the research and development of artificial intelligence technologies that aid law enforcement agencies and enhance community safety.AiLECS Lab includes research on explainable algorithms, machine learning classification algorithms for illicit image video and text, frameworks for ethical AI as well as techniques for leveraging law enforcement datasets.

instruments.name: National AI Centre
instruments.summary: The National AI Centre will be established to help drive business adoption, development and use of transformative AI technologies across the Australian ecosystem.

instruments.name: NSW AI Advisory Committee
instruments.summary: The NSW government has named an 11-member advisory committee of experts to advise it on the appropriate use of artificial intelligence.

instruments.name: Intellectual Property Policy Group - Artificial Intelligence Working Group
instruments.summary: A cross-departmental working group established to ensure that relevant government agencies are involved in the conversation on AI related IP Policy matters. This group provides an opportunity to seek views from diverse stakeholders on how the current IP settings intersect with AI development and adoption in Australia and whether the government could consider any potential changes.

instruments.name: Knowledge Economy Initiatives
instruments.summary: Implementation of three kinds of policies: tax promotions for companies who adopt 4.0 technologies in their productive processes; funding for 4.0 solutions in companies affected by pandemics and training in 4.0 technologies in local administrations.

instruments.name: IBM WATSON AI Piolt
instruments.summary: Argentina is testing the IBM AI Platform, using an Aquaculture project, to evaluate AI technology and formally incorporate this platform into the Ministry of Science, Technology and Productive Innovation.

instruments.name: AI Use Cases in the Public Sector
instruments.summary: Argentina has begun to implement artificial intelligence in the provision of its public services (i.e. Prometea, an AI application used in the judicial system of Argentina).

instruments.name: The Ethics of AI as a UNESCO Recommendation
instruments.summary: From May 2020 to 31 July 2020, Argentina participated in the Global Online Consultation on the first version of the Draft Recommendation on the Ethics of AI of UNESCO.

instruments.name: Business Diagnosis and Networking in 4.0 Technologies
instruments.summary: To strengthen the capacities of Argentine companies through diagnosis and containing actions for the adoption of 4.0 technologies.

instruments.name: AI Covid-19 Response
instruments.summary: The project will help develop a central objective for the national sanitary policy: promoting quality and equitable access to public health services despite gender, age, economic or geographic conditions.

instruments.name: AI Center
instruments.summary: The AI Center (Argentina) is a technical cooperation project between the Argentine government and the Inter-American Development Bank (IDB). Its main goal is to strengthen the country's institutional capacity in artificial intelligence by establishing an AI center that follows global best practices. The initiative supports the national strategy to promote AI research, development, and adoption across public and private sectors.

instruments.name: Law on Mobility Orientation
instruments.summary: The Mobility Orientation Bill commits to a profound transformation of public mobility policies, with one objective in mind: to improve mobility on a daily basis for all French people and in all regions.

instruments.name: Development of Scikit-learn Ecosystem
instruments.summary: Support the development and maintenance of the Scikit-Learn library, augmentation of its ecosystem with data exchange and data wrangling tools and framework.

instruments.name: Good Practice Recommendations to Integrate Ethics in the Development of AI Solutions in Healthcare
instruments.summary: This report lists all the ethical requirements required by AI solutions in healthcare in the double sense of "by design", i.e. both during the design phase, to integrate as much as possible, ethical values in the hardware and software architecture of the systems, and architecture of the systems, and at the end of the realization, to validate the proposed solutions and avoid the risks resulting from the mainly inductive nature of AI today.

instruments.name: France AI
instruments.summary: A national report was published in March 2017.

instruments.name: Presidential Committee on AI
instruments.summary: The Committee will deliberate and coordinate on the following: key AI-related policies, AI-related R&D strategies, AI-related investment strategies, and public-private cooperation and AI industry development strategies aimed at boosting the national AI competitiveness.

instruments.name: Addressing Human Rights Concerns Arising From Facial Recognition Technology
instruments.summary: The French government is co-designing a policy framework to address human rights concerns arising from the use of facial recognition technology in collaboration with the World Economic Forum.

instruments.name: Artificial Intelligence Safety Institute (AISI)
instruments.summary: The Korea AISI is Korea AISI) is an organization dedicated to evaluating the risks associated with AI models or systems and researching technologies for preventing and mitigating those risks. We represent the Republic of Korea in collaborating with AI safety research institutes and related organizations worldwide.

instruments.name: AI Seoul Summit
instruments.summary: Following the AI Safety Summit held by the UK in 2023, the AI Seoul Summit contributed to making the AI Summit a leader-level platform for comprehensive discussion on global AI governance.The Seoul Declaration suggests a balanced global AI governance that promotes AI safety while also supporting AI innovation and inclusivity, and received endorsement from global AI leaders, including the G7.

instruments.name: AI Research Programs
instruments.summary: A large program for advanced research in AI, centred on trustworthy AI, embedded and frugal AI and mathematical foundations.

instruments.name: AI Challenges
instruments.summary: The AI Challenge system promotes open and collaborative innovation approaches between, on the one hand, companies or public entities facing digital challenges and, on the other hand, start-ups or SMEs which will provide innovative technologies. Their objective is to bring out radically new solutions for all economic players.

instruments.name: Roadmap for the Development and Application of Artificial Intelligence in Colombia
instruments.summary: To be determined

instruments.name: AI Programs of the National Laboratory of Metrology and Testing
instruments.summary: -Evaluation, qualification and testing methods for AI-Certification program (of a development process, not an AI)-LEIA :

instruments.name: AI Sandbox Program of the National Data Protection Authority
instruments.summary: The CNIL, Commission Nationale Informatique & Libertes, is the French Data Protection Agency. As part of its support strategy, the CNIL has launched a first "personal data sandbox" session, in the form of a call for projects in the field of health.

instruments.name: Voluntary AI Safety Standard
instruments.summary: The Voluntary AI Safety Standard gives practical guidance to all Australian organisations on how to safely and responsibly use and innovate with AI.The standard consists of 10 voluntary guardrails that apply to all organisations throughout the AI supply chain. They include transparency and accountability requirements across the supply chain. They also explain what developers and deployers of AI systems must do.

instruments.name: Digital Republic Bill
instruments.summary: The Digital Republic Bill is the result of large-scale direct consultations with the community and has three components: (1) data and knowledge flow; (2) protection of citizens in the digital society; and (3) access to digital for all.

instruments.name: Mandatory Guardrails for Safe and Responsible AI
instruments.summary: The paper outlines proposed options for mandatory guardrails as preventative measures that would require developers and deployers of high-risk AI to take specific steps across the AI lifecycle.The paper includes:- a proposed definition of high-risk AI- 10 proposed regulatory guardrails to reduce the likelihood of harms occurring from the development and deployment of AI systems- regulatory options to mandate guardrails, building on current work to strengthen and clarify existing laws

instruments.name: Development of Embedded Deep Learning N2D2 Ecosystem CEA
instruments.summary: Sovereign framework for deep learning at the edge.

instruments.name: Bio-ethics Law Project
instruments.summary: Bill addressing ethical considerations for neuro-technologies.

instruments.name: National Framework for Standardisation and Implementation of AI
instruments.summary: Initiative relates to implementation of 8th strategic goal of the National AI programme ensuring an appropriate legal and ethical framework. An AI Standards Observatory to produce reports, assess the regulatory framework, and compile lists of international, EU, and national standards to ensure AI solution compliance will be established.

instruments.name: Franco-German Roadmap on AI
instruments.summary: OECD UNABLE TO DETERMINE - NCP, PLEASE ADD IF APPLICABLE

instruments.name: Development of the Legal and Conceptual Framework for the Establishment and Operation of a National Regulatory Sandbox for Artificial Intelligence
instruments.summary: This initiative establishes a national regulatory sandbox for AI in Slovenia,   The main objective is to create a legal and governance framework that allows for safe and compliant testing of AI solutions while addressing legal challenges. At the same time, the initiative ensures that AI development respects human rights, environmental protection, and market competitiveness.

instruments.name: Trilateral French-Japanese-German Research Projects on AI
instruments.summary: The Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft (DFG, German Research Foundation) together with the French National Research Agency (ANR, France), and the Japan Science and Technology Agency (JST, Japan) announced the first trilateral call for research proposals on Artificial Intelligence (AI).

instruments.name: Creation of a High-level Commission for Digital Government
instruments.summary: The optimization of processes through the construction and implementation of new solutions that facilitate and expedite procedures and services.

instruments.name: CONFIANCE.AI Program
instruments.summary: A consortium of industrial and academics institutes unifying their forces develop tools and standards for a safe and trustworthy AI.

instruments.name: National Laboratory for AI
instruments.summary: An AI co-operation declaration signed in 2020 seeks to explore the possibilities of establishing a national laboratory in Costa Rica.

instruments.name: HPC Support to NLP Bigscience Workshop
instruments.summary: The BigScience project is a one year-long international collaboration of more than 800 researchers on large multilingual language models anda dataset, aiming at publishing all materials and finding ; in addition to the scientific contribution of INRIA and the CNRS France is also providing HPC support for the training of the Workhop's models

instruments.name: Improvements in the Efficiency of Public Spending Through the Appropiate Use of Digital Technologies in the Costa Rican Public Sector
instruments.summary: The Central Administration is ordered and the Decentralized Administration is instructed to take the necessary technical and financial measures that allow them to plan, specify and implement technological solutions in accordance with the national reality.

instruments.name: The Development of the Digital Government of the Bicentenary
instruments.summary: A directive for the project formulation, articulation of actions, inter-institutional collaboration, and transversal generation of digital government capacity.

instruments.name: Regulation And Standardisation Of Technology Acquisitions And/Or Development Of Management Support Computer Systems
instruments.summary: Guidelines to rationalize the use of public resources, especially those destined to the acquisition of electronic equipment, as well as those aimed at the development of computer programs and / or developments of computer systems to support its management.

instruments.name: Data Sharing Commons
instruments.summary: General availability of a selection of public and (some) private data with an appropriate license as to allow their use at research and innovation purpose.

instruments.name: Implementation of Accessible Websites in the Costa Rican Public Sector
instruments.summary: This guideline is meant to implement accessible websites in the Costa Rican public sector.

instruments.name: AI Advisory Board
instruments.summary: The Austrian AI Advisory Board consists of eleven members from academia, civil society, industry and public administration. Its tasks include advising the Austrian government and the AI service desk on developments related to AI, including technical, ethical and societal aspects and prioritising topics in the field of AI, as well as strategic planning and advice in relation to the Austrian AI strategy.

instruments.name: Breakthrough Innovation Challenge on AI for Health
instruments.summary: To be determined

instruments.name: Digital Transformation Strategy Of Costa Rica
instruments.summary: This Strategy promotes public policy actions to improve people's quality of life through the implementation of secure and resilient digital solutions at the service of citizens and all sectors of society with a perspective of co-creation and collaboration.

instruments.name: Teleworking: The Rules and Best Practices to follow
instruments.summary: Initial guidance on teleworking and employee surveillance from the National Commission for Computing and Liberties (CNIL).

instruments.name: AI Stakeholder Forum
instruments.summary: The AI Stakeholder Forum, founded March 2024, consists of various associations and interest groups and is intended to strengthen a lively and active exchange between the federal government and Austria's various stakeholders in the field of artificial intelligence. Part of the AI Stakeholder Forum are amongst others representatives of employers and labour in Austria, AI and IT associations, as well as associations for youth and for disabilities.

instruments.name: OUR AI: Our Ambition for France
instruments.summary: On March 13, 2024, the Artificial Intelligence Commission submitted a report to the French President containing 25 recommendations to make France a major player in the artificial intelligence (AI) technological revolution.

instruments.name: AI Policy Forum
instruments.summary: The ministries responsible for Austria's AI strategy jointly lead the inter-ministerial working group AI Policy Forum, which consists of representatives of all twelve ministries. The AI Policy Forum was set up 2021 to support the inter-ministerial implementation of the national AI strategy. Its main tasks include the ongoing monitoring of AI strategy measures and the coordination of AI activities in the specialist ministries.

instruments.name: ETALAB
instruments.summary: Etalab is a department of the Interministerial Digital Directorate (DINUM), whose missions and organization are set by the decree of October 30, 2019.

instruments.name: National Cybersecurity Strategy
instruments.summary: This Strategy promotes public policy actions to improve people's quality of life through the implementation of secure and resilient digital solutions at the service of citizens and all sectors of society with a perspective of co-creation and collaboration

instruments.name: Investments for the Future Programme
instruments.summary: The Investments for the Future Programme (PIA) aims to increase the long-term growth potential of the French economy, by strengthening investment in four priority sectors: higher education and research, industries and SMEs, sustainable development and digital economy. The program seeks to accelerate and strengthen a  of the French higher education, research and innovation system.

instruments.name: Law No. 9943 Creation of the National Digital Government Agency
instruments.summary: Transform and make more efficient and effective the cross-cutting services that public institutions provide to citizens and businesses, through the intensive use of information and communication technologies.

instruments.name: EDGE AI Initiative
instruments.summary: A set of measures and programmes to place France as a leader in the sector of embedded AI.

instruments.name: Grants4Companies
instruments.summary: Grants4Companies is an application in the Austrian Business Service Portal, the main point of contact between businesses and Austrian public administration. It uses methods of symbolic AI to display a list of grants, which match the logged-in business based on its data available in the registries of public administration. The internal representation of the grants also enables analysis of the landscape of Austrian business grants.

instruments.name: Network of the Interdisciplinary Institutes for AI
instruments.summary: A network composed of the 4 interdisciplinary institutes of artificial intelligence, which aim at fostering AI research closely to the industry, with ANITI, Prairie, MIAI, C´te d'Azur.

instruments.name: Law as Code for Procedures of Public Administration
instruments.summary: The Law as Code approach aims to represent rules or legal texts in the form of formalized and executable logic-based rules, using methods of symbolic AI. Such a representation ensures transparency, explainability and predictability of the execution of the underlying regulations, and hence is especially suited for procedures of public administration. The Law as Code-initiative aims to create a basis for such an approach in the context of Austrian public administration.

instruments.name: Labour AI - Centre of Expertise of the Global Partnership on AI
instruments.summary: Labor AI is one of the two centres of expertise of the GPAI. The other one is located in Canada. It aims at studying AI impact on work, employment, and social dialogue.

instruments.name: Data Strategy for Austria
instruments.summary: The national data strategy for Austria follows the vision to use data for the common good. The strategy was published in 2024 with three goals that aim to develop sustainable data infrastructures, enable responsible data usage and create a data culture as well as strengthen data literacy. The three goals are detailed across 45 measures that address various stakeholders in the public sector and the data economy.

instruments.name: Health Data Hub
instruments.summary: The Health Data Hub gathers data from the French national health system to enable research and innovation on large datasets.

instruments.name: AI Labeling
instruments.summary: In order to ensure transparency and trust in AI, Austria intends to introduce a labelling for AI systems used in the Austrian federal administration. The primary goal is to ensure that users of modern technologies are immediately informed when they interact with artificial intelligence.

instruments.name: AI Education & Training Development Plan
instruments.summary: An ambitious massively funded national training plan on AI, aiming both at the emergence of excellence internationally renowned centres and at the massification of AI in the whole higher education ecosystem (short or long studies, from AI specialists to introductory modules etc.)

instruments.name: National Strategy on AI
instruments.summary: France’s national AI strategy was launched in 2018. Its first phase, which ran between 2018 and 2022 and had a budget of EUR 1.85 billion, enabled the creation and development of a network of interdisciplinary AI research institutes, the establishment of chairs of excellence and doctoral programmes, and the deployment of the Jean Zay supercomputer. The second phase (2022-25) focuses more strongly on disseminating AI technologies  and enabling AI development and innovation.

instruments.name: Long-term Plan for the Education and Development of the Educational System of the Czech Republic 2023-2027
instruments.summary: The Long-term plan for the education and development of the educational system of the Czech Republic is a document implementing Strategy 2030+, the key education strategy of the Czech Republic.

instruments.name: International Panel on AI
instruments.summary: A global point of reference for understanding and sharing research results on AI issues and best practices.

instruments.name: embrAIsme - Improving Conditions and Policies for SMEs to Embrace AI
instruments.summary: EmbrAIsme is an Interreg Europe project co-financed by the Austrian Federal Chancellery which aims to encourage uptake of AI by SMEs, in particular by raising awareness of AI and the importance of AI skills, facilitating access to funding and building tools to ease the compliance burden of SMEs.

instruments.name: National Consultative Committee on Digital Ethics and AI
instruments.summary: Produce reference documents relating to the ethical issues raised by advances in science, technology, uses and innovations in the digital field and their various impacts, particularly social, economic, entrepreneurial, individual or educational.

instruments.name: AI 4.0
instruments.summary: The programme and its networks have taken Finland towards the age of artificial intelligence through 11 key actions.

instruments.name: Finland's Fit for Digital Program (Fifi4Digi)
instruments.summary: Finland Fit for Digital Program is an initiative to bring together the national efforts on promoting the digitalization of business.

instruments.name: AI Business Program
instruments.summary: AI Business program was launched as part of AI Programme. In 2018, with public funding amounting to EUR 34 million and a total of 115 projects, the AI Business program, focusing on AI and the platform economy, was Business Finland's biggest programme. The programme, launched at the beginning of 2018, has been reserved an authorisation to allocate EUR 100 million over a four-year period, as well as an authorisation to grant EUR 60 million of capital loan for the first two years to be all

instruments.name: National Bioethics and Techno-ethics Committee (Substitue of National Bioethics Committee)
instruments.summary: The Commission advises the State on life sciences and new technologies, focusing on ethical, social, and legal aspects in fields like biology, biotechnology, medicine, genetics, AI, advanced algorithms, and robotics. It comprises eleven scientists chosen for balanced representation of sciences and humanities, appointed by the Prime Minister. Members serve four-year terms, renewable once. In May 2023, a High-level Expert Group on AI was appointed to provide recommendations on ethical AI and digit

instruments.name: AURORA AI
instruments.summary: AuroraAI aims to deliver a comprehensive range of personalized, AI-driven services for individuals and businesses, prioritizing a human-centered approach that ultimately enhances well-being. This initiative is designed to facilitate seamless access for citizens to diverse services offered by various government and cross-sector providers, ensuring that the activities of relevant authorities are structured to support people's needs effectively.

instruments.summary: Short and simple description*The Artificial Intelligence Programme is a network ofnetworks.In the Artificial Intelligence Programme, we have called for new cooperation modelsfor private-public partnerships, but also for cooperation done within the publicand private sectors.
