instruments.name: AI Governance Center
instruments.summary: The AI Governance Center (AIGC) ensures responsible AI adoption in Thailand through policies, testing frameworks, and global collaborations.Founded under the National AI Strategy and action Plan (2022 - 2027), AIGC tackles AI risks, promotes ethical use, and aligns Thailand with global AI governance standards to ensure safe and sustainable AI development.Policymakers, businesses, and researchers benefit from its guidelines, AI testing tools, and advisory services.

instruments.name: Leading the Way Into the Age of AI
instruments.summary: In October 2017, Finland presented the first eight key actions for making Finland one of the leaders in the application of AI. This work was later supplemented with separate analyses and recommendations for measures on the future of work, ethics and security.

instruments.name: Finland's AI Accelerator
instruments.summary: First Artificial Intelligence Accelerator (FAIA) helps established organisations deploy artificial intelligence (AI). The accelerator is run by Silo AI.

instruments.name: Finland AI Enforcement and Case Law in Employment
instruments.summary: Objectives:To share relevant enforcement decisions and case law.

instruments.name: AI as Focus Area in the Performance Agreements With the Public Universities
instruments.summary: The focus on AI in the performance agreements resulted in a bundle of projects and activities with a focus on AI, some individual measures, some inter-university. The goal was to support the uptake of AI in academia and expanding AI-Literacy/skills and advancing AI research. Measure are for e.g. the establishment/ expansion of HPC infrastructure, the creation of (further) training opportunities on AI for teachers, researchers and students, new AI degree programs or more AI professorships.

instruments.name: AI Register
instruments.summary: AI Register is a window into the artificial intelligence systems used by the City of Helsinki. Through the register, you can get acquainted with the quick overviews of the city's artificial intelligence systems or examine their more detailed information based on your own interests. You can also give feedback and thus participate in building human-centred AI in Helsinki.

instruments.name: AITHYRA Institute - Research Institute for Biomedical Artificial Intelligence
instruments.summary: AITHYRA is a research initiative by the Austrian Academy of Sciences primarily funded by the Boehringer Ingelheim foundation and focused on using artificial intelligence to advance biomedical research. It aims to improve healthcare outcomes by developing new AI technologies that can analyze complex medical data more effectively. This initiative addresses the need for better diagnostic tools and treatments, ultimately benefiting patients, healthcare providers, and policymakers.

instruments.name: Overarching National AI Strategy
instruments.summary: The Danish government's vision is that developing and using AI should always be citizen-centric. Danish companies must be globally competitive, and Denmark should be a world leader in using AI in the public sector. The strategic Approachsets up three guiding principles and initiate four new national initiatives for the usage and development of responsible AI.

instruments.name: Argentina
instruments.summary: A national initiative launched in 2022 to promote AI research, innovation, and collaboration in Argentina, supported by the Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation and the Inter-American Development Bank.

instruments.name: Robotics Public-private Partnership in HORIZON 2020
instruments.summary: Public private partnership in Horizon 2020 on robotics.

instruments.name: Berufsinfomat
instruments.summary: The Berufsinfomat uses the possibities of GenAI  (LLM) to inform the public and interested parties about job profiles, education and trainings. Due its nature it allows to access information in several languages with questions and answers which otherwise would be spread over three databases and in German only. It's available for everyone with internet access and of course for all employees of the AMS itself.

instruments.name: FET Flagship - Human Brain Project
instruments.summary: The Human Brain Project (HPB) FET Flagship, as part of its multiple R&D activities, pushes the use of most advanced AI techniques for accelerating progress neurosciences and simultaneously develops more empowering robotics and AI approaches inspired by the latest understanding in the human brain, in particular regarding environment awareness and decision making (related budget part is indicated below).

instruments.name: Establishment of an AI Observatory for Labour Market Monitoring
instruments.summary: The Federal Ministry of Labour and Economy is planning to establish an AI observatory.

instruments.name: AI4EU Consortium
instruments.summary: In January 2019, the AI4EU consortium was established to build the first European Artificial Intelligence On-Demand Platform and Ecosystem with the support of the European Commission under the H2020 programme.

instruments.name: HORIZON 2020
instruments.summary: The EU framework programme for Research and Innovation for 2014-2020.

instruments.name: Public-private Partnership on Data
instruments.summary: Creation of a public-private partnership on Data to derive a strategy for coordinated R&D&I funding between industry and the European Commission on this topic.

instruments.name: Special Committee on Artificial Intelligence in the Digital Age (AIDA)
instruments.summary: The European Parliament set up a special committee on AI on 18 June 2020.

instruments.name: Guidelines: Use of AI-Based Tools in Final Papers
instruments.summary: The Austrian Ministry of Education, Science and Research provides guidelines on the responsible use of AI tools in final papers. These tools may support students but must be transparently acknowledged. Measures include updated assessment rubrics, monitoring processes, and clear citation rules to ensure academic integrity and prevent misuse.

instruments.name: European Network for AI Excellence Centres
instruments.summary: Allowing the best research teams in Europe to join forces to tackle major scientific and technological challenges, hampering the deployment of AI-based solutions.

instruments.name: AI Badge for eEducation Schools
instruments.summary: The AI Badge for eEducation Schools is a new accreditation within the network eEducation Austria. It fosters ongoing commitment with AI topics in schools by integrating AI activities into school development. Completion of at least one AI Badge is mandatory for all schools by the end of the 2024/25 school year.

instruments.name: High-level Expert Group on Artificial Intelligence (HLEG-AI)
instruments.summary: Following an open selection process, in June 2018 the Commission has appointed 52 experts to a new High-Level Expert Group on Artificial Intelligence, comprising representatives from academia, civil society, as well as industry. One output of the group are the ethical guidelines for trustworthy AI were presented in April 2019 which are now being piloted (June - December 2019).

instruments.name: AI MOOC: Basic AI Training through a MOOC
instruments.summary: The AI MOOC is an online course accessible to all Austrian teachers, offering self-paced, flexible learning. Participants can explore AI fundamentals, ethical considerations, and practical tools tailored to their teaching context. The course aims to empower educators with knowledge and skills for integrating AI into education.

instruments.name: Artificial Intelligence Act (AI ACT)
instruments.summary: The AI Act is the first-ever legal framework on AI. It  seeks to address the risks of AI and position Europe to play a leading role globally. The Code of Practice helps industry comply with the AI Act legal obligations on safety, transparency and copyright of general-purpose AI models.

instruments.name: Teaching Materials on AI Eduthek, digi.case
instruments.summary: The Austrian Federal Ministry of Education, Science, and Research offers digital teaching materials on artificial intelligence (AI) through platforms like Eduthek and digi.case. Eduthek provides a curated collection of AI-focused educational resources, while digi.case introduces primary school students to computational thinking and creative problem-solving through both analog and digital tools.

instruments.name: Digital Services Act Package
instruments.summary: The Digital Services Act and Digital Markets Act aim to create a safer digital space where the fundamental rights of users are protected and to establish a level playing field for businesses.

instruments.name: AI Pilot Schools: Learning and Teaching with AI Tools
instruments.summary: The initiative žAI Pilot Schools explores the integration of AI tools in Austrian classrooms through empirical research. It includes three phases: an initial survey on AI use, a second survey documenting practical experiences, and ongoing documentation by teachers. The initiative aims to provide insights into AI-supported teaching and learning.

instruments.name: General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR)
instruments.summary: The EU General Data Protection Regulation went into effect on May 25, 2018, replacing the Data Protection Directive 95/46/EC.

instruments.name: European Data Governance Act (DGA)
instruments.summary: The Data Governance Act aims to make more data available and facilitate data sharing across sectors and EU countries in order to leverage the potential of data for the benefit of European citizens and businesses.

instruments.name: Policy and Investment Recommendations for Trustworthy Artificial Intelligence
instruments.summary: This Policy document, published in June 2019, puts forward recommendations that can guide Trustworthy AI towards sustainability, growth and competitiveness, as well as inclusion “ while empowering, benefiting and protecting human beings.

instruments.name: "AI in Everyday Consumer Life" - Teaching Materials on Artificial Intelligence for Secondary School
instruments.summary: Thes teaching materials are intended to support teachers in addressing the topic of AI in the classroom. The materials encourage a conscious examination of the opportunities and risks associated with artificial intelligence in the context of consumer education. They inspire students to critically reflect on how AI influences their everyday lives, such as in purchasing decisions, personalized advertising, or digital voice assistants.

instruments.name: Ethics Guidelines on Artificial Intelligence
instruments.summary: The guidelines postulate that in order to achieve trustworthy AI', three components are necessary: (1) it should comply with the law, (2) it should fulfil ethical principles and (3) it should be robust. They also list 7 key requirements that AI systems should meet in order to be trustworthy. These requirements will go through a piloting process expected to conclude with the presentation of a revised document in early 2020.

instruments.name: Enlightenment 4.0 “ Understanding AI decisions as a human being
instruments.summary: The AI Act contains the "Right to Explanation of Individual Decision-Making" (Art 86) for persons subject to a decision based on high-risk AI (Annex III). The prerequisites for asserting this right and the corresponding obligations for deployers require further clarification. The output of the project are separate guidelines both for consumers and companies for a pracitcable application of the Right to Explanation.

instruments.name: Advanced Technologies for Industry
instruments.summary: The Advanced Technologies for Industry (ATI) provides a systematic monitoring of technological trends and data on advanced technologies such as AI, to properly support the implementation of policies and initiatives and to promote a competitive European industry.

instruments.name: Ensuring an Appropriate Legal Framework for AI in Healthcare
instruments.summary: The initiative covers the examination of the initial national situation, including obstacles, regarding AI in healthcare. It aims at ensuring both secure and innovation-friendly conditions for AI in the healthcare sector, by providing guidance, the facilitation of networking, and potentially the adaptation of existing legal regulations.With the AI act coming into application, it is necessary to analyze the interplace between this one, and other national and European regulations.

instruments.name: European Digital Innovation Hubs  (EDIH)
instruments.summary: Digital Innovation Hubs are helping organisations in the industry and public sector become more competitive regarding their business/production processes, products or services by using AI and other advanced digital technologies.

instruments.name: Guide Digital Administration: AI, Ethics and Law - Practical Guide for the Administration, Version 2.0
instruments.summary: The guide mentioned supports public administration in planning, developing, and implementing digital applications, especially AI. The goal is to enhance efficiency, citizen-friendliness, and transparency while ensuring ethical, legal, and ecological standards. The guide provides practical tools to leverage digital opportunities while minimizing risks like discrimination and data protection violations.

instruments.name: AI Innovation Package to Support Atificial Intelligence Startups and SMEs
instruments.summary: The Commission has launched a package of measures to support European startups and SMEs in the development of trustworthy Artificial Intelligence (AI) that respects EU values and rules. The package comprises a broad range of measures to support AI startups and innovation, including a proposal to provide privileged access to supercomputers to AI startups and the broader innovation community. It also includes the decision to establish an AI Office within the Commis

instruments.name: Justice Chatbot
instruments.summary: Information on legal topics and assistance and registration for justice Online portal

instruments.name: Dragon Naturally Speaking
instruments.summary: The orally pronounced judgment must be written down so that it can subsequently be served on the parties or, if necessary, subsequently published

instruments.name: AI Hub for Sustainable Development
instruments.summary: As affirmed in the G7 Leaders' Declaration, the AI Hub aims to enable multi-stakeholder partnerships to support local AI digital ecosystems, strengthen capacities to advance  AI for sustainable development, and complement existing initiatives including the AI for Development Donors Partnership.

instruments.name: European Lighthouse on Secure and Safe AI (ELSA)
instruments.summary: ELSA is a growing network of excellence that spearheads efforts in foundational safe and secure AI methodology research. ELSA builds onand extends the internationally recognized and excellently positioned ELLIS (European Laboratory for Learning and Intelligent Systems) network of excellence.

instruments.name: Literature Search Linking With Legal Databases
instruments.summary: Content of documents is searched for legal citations and sources, hyperlinks to sources are inserted as an overlay in the document display

instruments.name: Joint Press Statement by Michael McGrath, European Commissioner for Democracy, Justice, the Rule of Law and Consumer Protection and Denise Wong, Acting Commissioner of Singapore's Personal Data Protection Commission
instruments.summary: Building on previous collaboration, the European Commission and PDPC  intend to further develop their partnership on issues of common interest, notably through the exchange of knowledge, experience and best practices to enhance data protection and trusted data flows, including exploring the use of privacy-enhancing technologies, in support of the digital economy and advancing the protection of children in the digital environment, which is a priority area for both sides.

instruments.name: Financing of Artificial Intelligence and Blockchain Technologies
instruments.summary: This is a call for tender to develop and operate an investment support programme for the first dedicated, EU-wide investment fund focused on innovative Deep-Tech startups and companies. In particular the programme will carry out activities focused on supporting the further development and adoption of Artificial Intelligence and Blockchain Technologies in Europe.

instruments.name: Anonymization of Court Decisions
instruments.summary: In Austria, all decisions of the Supreme Court and other selected decisions of the ordinary courts are published in the federal legal information system and can therefore be viewed by anyone seeking justice. All personal data and information that allows conclusions to be drawn about the case or the person must be removed in advance, This process is now carried out using AI

instruments.name: AU Data Policy Framework
instruments.summary: This framework sets out a common vision, principles, strategic priorities and key recommendations to guide African countries in developing their national data systems and capabilities to effectively use and derive value from data.

instruments.name: HORIZON Europe
instruments.summary: The Commission has published its proposal for Horizon Europe, an ambitious 100 billion research and innovation programme that will succeed Horizon 2020.

instruments.name: Case assignment
instruments.summary: Support for administrative distribution of cases based on characteristics, no change / intervention in document content

instruments.name: ASEAN Digital Masterplan 2025
instruments.summary: The ADM 2025 will guide digital cooperation between ASEAN members over the next five years in order to position ASEAN as a leading digital community and economic bloc powered by secure and transformative digital services, technologies and ecosystems.

instruments.name: Digital Europe Programme
instruments.summary: Digital Europe is the EU's programme focused on building the strategic digital capacities of the EU and on facilitating the wide deployment of digital technologies, to be used by European citizens and businesses.

instruments.name: Input processing
instruments.summary: AI-supported generation of metadata, automatic categorization including designation proposal and case assignment

instruments.name: AfCFTA Digital Trade Protocol
instruments.summary: The AfCFTA strives to create a more harmonized framework to promote Africa's digitalization and the development of digital-related industries and trade in digital products.

instruments.name: European High Performance Computing Joint Undertaking (EuroHPC JU)
instruments.summary: The European Union has launched the EuroHPC initiative that will permit the EU and participating countries to coordinate their efforts and share resources with the objective of deploying in Europe a world-class supercomputing infrastructure and a competitive innovation ecosystem in supercomputing technologies, applications and skills, including fostering (generative) AI innovation.

instruments.name: Automatic Document Assignment in the Inbox
instruments.summary: Assignment and processing of electronic or scanned incoming items, extraction of metadata and assignment of a case number for existing and new cases

instruments.name: Declaration of Montevideo
instruments.country: The United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization
instruments.summary: Ministers and High-Level Authorities representing the countries gathered at the Second Ministerial and High-Level Authorities Summit on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence in Latin America and the Caribbean, on October 3rd and 4th, 2024.  Countries include Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Cuba, Curacao, Ecuador, El Salvador, Honduras, Jamaica, Mexico, Panama, Paraguay, Peru, Dominican Republic and Uruguay.

instruments.name: Implementation Plan for Nationwide Diffusion of AI into Everyday Life
instruments.summary: Expand international cooperation on AI; Nationwide diffusion of AI into everyday life; Establish the Digital Bill of Rights; Ensure AI ethics and trust

instruments.name: Declaration of Santiago
instruments.country: The United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization
instruments.summary: In October 2023, Santiago de Chile became the epicenter of a significant movement in the realm of Artificial Intelligence (AI) as it hosted the landmark Ministerial and High-Level Authorities Summit of Latin America and the Caribbean.

instruments.name: Strategy to Realize Trustworthy Artificial Intelligence
instruments.summary: Support the private sector's voluntary commitment to AI ethics and trust; foster an institutional and technological foundation for world-class AI ethics and trust; and raise public awareness about responsible AI

instruments.name: European Digital Infrastructure Consortium (EDIC)
instruments.summary: European Digital Infrastructure Consortium is an instrument made available to Member States under the Digital Decade Policy Programme 2030 to speed up and simplify the setup and implementation of multi-country projects (including on generative AI), thus facilitating the achievement of the Digital Decade general objectives and targets.

instruments.name: ASEAN Data Management Framework
instruments.summary: The establishment of an ASEAN Data Management Framework will promote sound data governance practices by helping organisations to discover the datasets they have, assign it with the appropriate categories, manage the data, protect it accordingly and all these while continuing to comply with relevant regulations.

instruments.name: National AI Strategy Policy Direction
instruments.summary: The initiative is aimed at making Korea a global pivotal state in AI by becoming one of the G3 AI nations. It outlines the four nationwide AI flagship projects and four key pillars of the AI ecosystem: 1) Develop startup talent, 2) Innovate technology and infrastructure, 3) Lay a foundation for inclusion and fairness, and 4) Secure global leadership.

instruments.name: MoU on Cooperation in the Fields of Digital Development between Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, India and Ministry of Communication and Digital Affairs, Indonesia.
instruments.summary: The MoU outlines several key areas of cooperation, including the development of emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence (AI), the Internet of Things (IoT), and digital infrastructure.

instruments.name: National Policy on Artificial Intelligence (CONPES 4144)
instruments.summary: This initiative aims to maximize the capabilities for research, development, adoption and ethical and sustainable use of AI systems in strategic social, economic and environmental issues in Colombia.

instruments.name: AI, Data and Robotics Partnership in Horizon Europe
instruments.summary: This Partnership is the European focal point for AI, Data and Robotics.

instruments.name: AI-Semiconductor Technology Initiative
instruments.summary: To focus on supporting the nine key technological innovation tasks for AI-semiconductors, the government will pursue the following initiatives to comprehensively support the entire AI-semiconductor value chain: 1)Comprehensive investment and financial support, 2) Talent development, 3) Establishment of industrial and research innovation infrastructure, 4) Global cooperation and market entry, and 5)Leadership in AI ethical standards

instruments.name: MoU on Cooperation in the Fields of Digital Development between Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, India and Ministry of Communication and Digital Affairs, Indonesia.
instruments.summary: The MoU outlines several key areas of cooperation, including the development of emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence (AI), the Internet of Things (IoT), and digital infrastructure.

instruments.name: Framework of Ethical Aspects of Artificial Intelligence, Robotics and Related Technologies
instruments.summary: This European Parliament resolution includes provisions on development, implementation and the evolution of technology through machine-learning or deep-learning.

instruments.name: Horizon Europe Gate
instruments.summary: The Horizon Europe Programme is the fundamental instrument for carrying out the EU's R+I policies, its general objective is to achieve a scientific, technological, economic and social impact of investments in the European region, thus strengthening the scientific and technological bases of member countries and partners in the world.

instruments.name: ALAIT Austrian Lab for AI Trust
instruments.summary: The "ALAIT" project employs scientific methods to design and test an innovative, interdisciplinary approach to technology assessment for AI, grounded in the principles of trustworthy AI. This approach is piloted directly in society through an AI Trust Lab, which features dialogue formats and feedback loops to promote participatory design. By doing so, the project tackles a critical societal challenge: fostering social trust and governance in AI within industries and professional fields.

instruments.name: Civil Liability Regime for Artificial Intelligence
instruments.summary: This European added value assessment (EAVA) suggests that the revision of the EU civil liability regime for artificial intelligence systems (AI) would likely generate substantial economic and social added value.

instruments.name: AI Defence Strategy
instruments.summary: This initiative aims to fulfil the integration of AI-enabled systems across the Federal Ministry of Defence and the Austrian Armed Forces; strengthening national defence by accelerating the digital transformation of the Austrian Armed Forces; developing a framework for ethical and secure AI integration and application in the defence sector; and preparing for future risks and threats originating from rapid developments in the fields of AI and related emerging technologies.

instruments.name: Closing the Digital Gender Gap: Womens Participation in the Digital Economy
instruments.summary: This report addresses the digital gender gap and the place of women in the digital economy.

instruments.name: Austrian Society for Artificial Intelligence (ASAI)
instruments.summary: The Austrian Society for Artificial Intelligence (ASAI) is a non-profit association for the promotion of Austria as a research location in the field of Artificial Intelligence (AI) with all its scientific and technical sub-disciplines as well as related inter- and transdisciplinary aspects. ASAI considers itself as platform for the AI community in Austria.

instruments.name: BG ETEM
instruments.summary: BG ETEM is leading the Reha Plus project, in which AI is helping to identify accident victims in need of early rehabilitation.

instruments.name: AI Service Desk
instruments.summary: The AI Service Desk is set up at Austrian Regulatory Authority for Broadcasting andTelecommunications (RTR-GmbH) and serves as a point of contact and information hub for the general public on the topic of AI from a regulatory perspective. It also supports the implementation of the European AI Act by providing information on the regulatory framework for the use of artificial intelligence as well as aspects relating to cybersecurity, data economy and its use in the media sector.

instruments.name: AI in Education, Culture and the Audiovisual Sector
instruments.summary: A report to better understand the development of AI in education, culture and the audiovisual sector.

instruments.name: Collection of Knowledge and Development of a Guideline on Green AI
instruments.summary: Systematic survey and target group-specific preparation of the current state of research state of research on ecologically sustainable AI systems and AI applications and development of a guideline on Green AI.

instruments.name: Robotics for a Safer World
instruments.summary: The robots for a safer world' challenge focused on research and innovation in advanced robotics and autonomous systems.

instruments.name: AI Monitor
instruments.summary: The AI Monitor aims to provide information about usage of AI as well as opportunities and challenges related to AI. Updated annually, it will comprise a dashboard with a broad range of quantitative data, alongside short introductions to lighthouse projects and initiatives within the Austrian AI ecosystem and contributions by the Austrian AI Advisory Board and the AI Stakeholder Forum.

instruments.name: Shaping Digital Education Policy
instruments.summary: The report calls for the creation of an AI and robotics initiative in the field of digital education.

instruments.name: Further development of the AI infrastructure
instruments.summary: Examination of the acquisition and operation of a supercomputer for AI (AI-oriented HPC) within the framework of the EuroHPC Joint Undertaking as a fundamental element of an AI Factory. The aim is to determine the specific requirements, the use, operation and possible connection and cooperation with existing infrastructures existing infrastructures are to be coordinated with the key stakeholders. The measure will be implemented depending on the availability of additional funds.

instruments.name: AI4WorkplaceSafety
instruments.summary: The goal of this project is to automate the detection and monitoring workplace injuries precursor using artificial intelligence algorithms.

instruments.name: Academic AI Services
instruments.summary: The aim of this project is to establish a secure environment for testing and using generative and other AI technologies, taking into account data protection and information security, and to make this technology available to research, teaching and administration. In addition, an experimental open source environment will be made available on the MUSICA server, in particular to train specific models and develop new innovative services for teaching, research and university administration.

instruments.name: The Robustness and Explainability of Artificial Intelligence
instruments.summary: The EU has identified the concepts of robustness and explainability of AI systems as key elements for a future regulation of this technology.

instruments.name: Preparation of an AI Hub Austria in the area of research and innovation
instruments.summary: Preparatory work on how an AI Hub Austria could be designed for all relevant stakeholders from science, research and industry and what framework conditions and framework conditions and incentives should be created for bundling and structured cooperation should be created in order to enable a joint external presence and achieve increased added value for all those involved.

instruments.name: DIAL AI
instruments.summary: The DIAL-IA project (Dialogue on AI) was led and coordinated by IRES with the support of ULTRA LABORANS.

instruments.name: Imagine AI for Dignity: Feminine Visions for Regeneration
instruments.summary: The development and presentation of an AI exhibition geared towards Intergovernmental dialogue and exchange with civil society in the sense of a holistic Regenerative Digital Humanism aims to transfer the results into future foreign policy cultural work. Cultural and scientific stakeholders and dialogue partners are the target groups. Critically examining the risks of AI for the dignity of humans and nature, as well as for democratic functioning, is the key motivation of the initiative.

instruments.name: Recommendations for a trustworthy Artificial Intelligence
instruments.summary: On June 1st, 2023, the Undersecretariat for Information Technologies approved under Disposition No. 2/2023 the "Recommendations for Trustworthy Artificial Intelligence". These recommendations provide a theoretical and practical guide that establishes a set of ethical principles to be considered and incorporated into every phase of an AI project within the public sector.

instruments.name: Leveraging the potential of AI in the direct holdings of the Federal Ministry for Climate Action, Environment, Energy, Mobility, Innovation and Technology and other legal entities
instruments.summary: Addresses a total of 18 different activities, initiatives and projects, such as the development of internal AI strategies, training measures, concrete AI-based solutions and automated assistance in the following areas AI-based solutions and automated assistance in the following organizations: AIT, ASFINAG, AustriaTech, E-Control, –BB, Silicon Austria Labs (SAL), Federal Environment Agency and viadonau.

instruments.name: Serving Confidence in AI by Deal
instruments.summary: The aim of SeCoIA Deal project, co-funded by the European Commission, is to address the many challenges posed by the development of artificial intelligence and affecting employment and work, particularly in the area of social dialogue.

instruments.name: Open Austria East Coast
instruments.summary: Expansion of the successful OPEN AUSTRIA brand to Washington, D.C., as well as the start-up hub and life sciences hotspot Boston - OPEN AUSTRIA East Coast. Since 2016, the BMEIA and WK– have jointly run the San Francisco office and the Austrian Federal Economic Chamber. OPEN AUSTRIA San Francisco has become a pioneer of the BMEIA's tech diplomacy and a joint brand with the WK– as a gateway to the future.

instruments.name: Big Data National Observatory
instruments.summary: The National Big Data Observatory works on issues related to the responsibility of internet intermediaries, the processing of personal data in digital environments and the socio-economic impacts derived from the use of automated information processing technologies.

instruments.name: Call for proposals: AI for Tech, AI for Green & AI for Transformation (research funding)
instruments.summary: Call for proposals for the three funding programs

instruments.name: AI Talent Development
instruments.summary: The Federal Ministry of Communications, Innovation & Digital Economy (FMCIDE)  announced new support from Google to accelerate AI talent development across Nigeria.

instruments.name: AI National Plan
instruments.summary: The strategy will establish policies to promote AI development in alignment with ethical and legal principles, contributing to national development goals and the SDGs. It aims to create, develop, and implement AI technologies that enhance human capacities and provide innovative solutions to drive Argentina's development.

instruments.name: A Blueprint for Greece' s AI Transformation
instruments.summary: a) Examines how AI can promote innovation and enhance the business ecosystem, positioning Greece as an attractive hub for startups and investments.b) Emphasizes strengthening education and research, essential for developing skills and advancing knowledge in the AI sector.c) Explores the regulatory framework, emphasizing the importance of ensuring responsible and safe use of AI. d) Proposes ways to apply AI technologies in the public sector to improv

instruments.name: MY-AI Portal
instruments.summary: This portal is the first national online platform dedicated to resources and issues related to Artificial Intelligence (AI).

instruments.name: Federal Act Concerning the Protection of Personal Data
instruments.summary: Authorizes the Austrian data protection authority to enforce GDPR and supplements GDPR with Austrian-specific provisions, such as restricting the collection of workplace images to monitor employees.

instruments.name: IndiaAI Future Skills
instruments.summary: This pillar aims to reduce barriers to entry into AI programs by increasing AI courses at the undergraduate, master's, and Ph.D. levels. Data and AI Labs will be established in Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities to offer foundational courses.

instruments.name: UN Secretary-General's High-level Advisory Body on Artificial Intelligence (HLAB-AI)
instruments.summary: HLAB-AI, established in October 2023, comprises 39 preeminent AI leaders from 33 countries across all regions and multiple sectors, serving in their personal capacity. In its final report, the Body presented seven recommendations for global cooperation on AI governance. The recommendations provided inspiration for Member States adopting the Global Digital Compact during the Summit of the Future in September 2024.

instruments.name: 32nd Amendment to the Austrian Motor Vehicles Act
instruments.summary: This Act grants permission for certain automotive functions or tasks to be done by automated systems.

instruments.name: Australia's AI Action Plan
instruments.summary: The Artificial Intelligence (AI) Action Plan set out a vision for Australia to be a global leader in developing and adopting trusted, secure and responsible AI. This plan was published under a previous Australian Government. It included Australian Government actions to realise this vision and ensure all Australians share the benefits of an AI-enabled economy.

instruments.name: Methodology to Identify Lessons Learned
instruments.summary: The project seeks to improve the capture of lessons learned in organizations, avoiding the repetition of errors and promoting continuous improvement. Many companies do not document learning due to fear, emotions or lack of time. ChatGPT was trained with a methodology to formulate lessons objectively and quickly, reducing tensions in meetings and improving accuracy. It benefits project teams by generating useful knowledge without friction or long consensus processes.

instruments.name: AI for All
instruments.summary: AI For All' is a self-learning online program designed to raise public awareness about Artificial Intelligence.

instruments.name: AI Task Force
instruments.summary: The Presidency of the Republic of Colombia, with the support of the Development Bank of Latin America (CAF), is working towards the design and implementation of a task force for AI in Colombia. This Task Force will be in charge of fostering the implementation of AI Policy. It will also promote and facilitate the use of AI in the public sector. The Presidency of the Republic is launching a website presenting the AI Project and its work.

instruments.name: EDUC.AR
instruments.summary: Argentina is taking action to build AI-relevant human capacities from the earliest stages in education, targeting children from ages 6 to 18.

instruments.name: National Code of Digital Technologies
instruments.summary: The Artificial Intelligence chapter aims to provide a comprehensive framework for the adoption and governance of artificial intelligence in the country. These guidelines have been developed in alignment with the National Artificial Intelligence Strategy (ENIA) and are based on fundamental principles such as peace, human dignity, transparency, equity, responsibility, sustainability, and cybersecurity.

instruments.name: AI for the People
instruments.summary: AI untuk Rakyat' is a self-learning online programme, crafted to enhance public understanding and awareness of Artificial Intelligence (AI).

instruments.name: AI Expert Mission
instruments.summary: The Artificial Intelligence Expert Mission consists of a group of experts who will meet periodically to evaluate the different dimensions of AI and produce concrete recommendations in the short, medium and long term. The Mission is necessary as a mechanism to establish a prospective roadmap to achieve the implementation of an AI Policy based on the technical and integral vision of the experts to complement and guide the path that Colombia is advancing in this regard.

instruments.name: National Committee of Ethics in Science and Technology
instruments.summary: The CECTE is a pluralistic and independent space for the critical and interdisciplinary analysis of topics related to the ethics of research in all areas of science and new technologies.

instruments.name: National Artificial Intelligence Strategy (NAIS)
instruments.summary: Costa Rica's National AI Strategy aims to promote the ethical, safe, and responsible use of AI for the benefit of its citizens. Its objectives include developing regulatory frameworks, strengthening skills, fostering R&D&I, improving public services, and enhancing competitiveness. Its strategic pillars focus on ethics, territorial development, capacity building, infrastructure, innovation, and international leadership.

instruments.name: Artificial Intelligence Training for Public Administration
instruments.summary: AGESIC provides training on Artificial Intelligence (AI) for members of public agencies.

instruments.name: Technology committee within the framework of the National System of Competitiveness and Innovation.
instruments.summary: Through Decree 2212 of 2023, the organization and operation of the National Competitiveness and Innovation System (SNCI) was adjusted. The Technology Committee, through an action plan, facilitates the implementation and application of public policies on productivity, competitiveness, and innovation. The committee addresses topics of a transversal and non-specific sector-specific nature that impact competitiveness and innovation to drive, guide, and generate initiatives for decision-making.

instruments.name: European Strategy for Data
instruments.summary: Together with the digital strategy, the Commission published the European strategy for data.

instruments.name: The Government strengthens AI skills among professionals and students
instruments.summary: AI is increasingly affecting everyday life. Professionals need up and reskilling in AI. Therefore, seven higher education institutions have been assigned to develop short courses with a focus on AI.

instruments.name: 4IR Training Programs to Capacitate Public Servants
instruments.summary: The National School of Government (NSG) enhances public servants' capabilities through training programs to equip them with essential digital skills pertinent to the Fourth Industrial Revolution (4IR).

instruments.name: Good Practice Guide for the Identification, Prevention and Mitigation of Gender Biases in the Life Cycle of Artificial Intelligence
instruments.summary: A good practices guide that includes tools and public policy recommendations, to promote gender equity in the life cycle of artificial intelligence. The tools include: i) a decision tree designed to guide developers or purchasers of AI-based solutions in identifying and preventing gender bias;  ii) a catalog of tools available for identifying, preventing, and mitigating gender biases

instruments.name: Report on Safety and Liability Implications of Artificial Intelligence, the Internet of Things and Robotics
instruments.summary: This report aims to analyse the fitness of currently European Union legislation on product safety and liability to emerging new technologies.

instruments.name: Africa Centre of Competence for Digital and Artificial Intelligence Skilling
instruments.summary: In partnership with the Ministry of Information, Communications and Digital Economy and Microsoft, UNDP Kenya is co-creating a groundbreaking Africa Center of Competence for Digital and Artificial Intelligence Skilling.

instruments.name: Government assignment to 25 Swedish national authorities to report on their use of AI
instruments.summary: The Government has decided to assign 25 national authorities to report on their use of AI. The assignment includes reporting on what collaborations exist with other authorities and what training or other competence-enhancing initiatives have been offered to the staff. The authorities must also report on the challenges linked to ethics, regulation and security.

instruments.name: AI in the Public Sector
instruments.summary: This initiative presents the most significant projects of use and deployment of Artificial Intelligence systems in Colombias public sector. It describes projects that present a high degree of progress and impact.

instruments.name: Juri Reports on "Making AI European"
instruments.summary: The European Parliament Committee on Legal Affairs (JURI) adopted reports on AI.

instruments.name: The Swedish Government's appointed inquiry with the task of reviewing the need for national adaptations because of the EU AI Act
instruments.summary: A special inquiry will review the need for national adaptations because of the EU AI Act.Among other things, the inquiry shall:- make proposals on how the market surveillance, governance and enforcement system should be structured,- map other needs for national adaptation as a result of the EU AI Act and propose how such needs should be met, and- submit the necessary national legislative proposals.

instruments.name: Training for Public Servants
instruments.summary: The government is sending civil servants to India for a six-month course in artificial intelligence

instruments.name: Govtech Ecosystem for AI Implementation
instruments.summary: The Colombian government is currently developing a new Govtech policy to facilitate the procurement of new solutions in the Govtech industry.

instruments.name: Digital Education Action Plan
instruments.summary: The Digital Education Action Plan (2021-2027) outlines the European Commission's vision for high quality, inclusive and accessible digital education in Europe.

instruments.name: National Artificial Intelligence Trust
instruments.summary: Nigeria is setting a global precedent with the establishment of the National Artificial Intelligence (AI) Trust. This first-of-its-kind body will consist of 10 AI experts, the Minister of Communications, Innovation & Digital Economy, and the Minister of Science, Innovation and Technology. The Trust's mandate includes mobilizing resources, providing oversight, and guiding AI development in Nigeria. It will ensure strategic investment in AI across key economic sectors.

instruments.name: Colombian Supercomputing Network
instruments.summary: The Ministry of Information Technology and Communications, along with the Center for Bioinformatics and Computational Biology of Colombia (BIOS), will launch the Colombian Supercomputing Network - ANALITIC4. This initiative aims to develop and implement strategies for extracting valuable insights from large datasets, addressing the needs of the private sector, academia, and government.

instruments.name: White Paper on Artificial Intelligence
instruments.summary: Within the framework of a wide range of digital initiatives taken by the European Commission, the White Paper on AI promotes a coordinated EU approach on the human and ethical implications of AI.

instruments.name: Readiness Assessment Methodology (RAM) for the AI "Ethical Framework"
instruments.summary: With the support of UNESCO, this initiative is being developed, applying a diagnostic tool to help the country assess its readiness in AI ethics across five dimensions: legal/regulatory, social/cultural, technical/infrastructural, economic, and scientific/educational, as well as the subsequent implementation of the AI ethical framework.

instruments.name: Call for Contributions to the Regulatory Sandbox for Artificial Intelligence and Data Protection
instruments.summary: The program consists of a controlled environment to test technologies associated with artificial intelligence (AI) developed by participants. The objective is that by fostering innovation in this controlled space, good practices are implemented to ensure compliance with personal data protection rules and principles.

instruments.name: Funding and Grants for AI Research
instruments.summary: Support projects that contribute to achieving the goals of the 2030 Agenda - Sustainable Development Goals, through the development and pre-commercial and commercial validation of new technologies (including AI-based technologies) that consider the use of scientific and technological knowledge developed in Colombia.

instruments.name: AI Watch
instruments.summary: AI Watch monitors industrial, technological and research capacity, policy initiatives in the Member States, uptake and technical developments of Artificial Intelligence and its impact in the economy, society and public services.It provides a number of analyses necessary to monitor and facilitate the implementation of the European Strategy for AI.

instruments.name: National Digital Security Strategy
instruments.summary: The National Digital Security Strategy of Colombia 2024-2026 is a comprehensive and proactive response to the challenges and opportunities arising in a constantly evolving digital environment. It aims to strengthen Colombia's digital security, adapting to emerging threats and leveraging technological innovations, including AI, to create a safer and more resilient cyberspace.

instruments.name: Regulatory Sandbox
instruments.summary: The sandbox enables greater collaboration between ICT innovators and the Communications Authority of Kenya, the regulatory authority for the communications sector in Kenya responsible for facilitating the development of the information and communications sectors including broadcasting, cybersecurity, multimedia, telecommunications, electronic commerce, postal and courier services. The Authority is also responsible for safeguarding the interests of Consumers of ICT product and services.

instruments.name: Data Sandbox Platform
instruments.summary: The Data Sandbox platform is a collaborative space for Colombian public entities, which enables to carry out different pilot projects in Analytics and Big Data. The previous allows public entities to use the latest technologies in data science to test, experiment, assess and determine applicable solutions in a real-life context to public and/or citizen-related problems.

instruments.name: Common European Data Space
instruments.summary: The creation of common European data spaces in a number of areas such as manufacturing and energy will constitute a major asset for European innovators and businesses.

instruments.name: Government Digital Innovation Regulatory Sandbox
instruments.summary: To facilitate research and development on emerging technologies a Government Regulatory Sandbox is provided through which digital innovations could be developed and tested safely.

instruments.name: AI Regulatory Sandbox Mexico
instruments.summary: In Mexico, ANIA organizes working groups on AI to democratize knowledge and contribute to public policies and best practices. The need for an AI "sandbox" as a flexible mechanism to address technical, legal, and ethical implications was highlighted. In collaboration with the UK Embassy and AMCID, an analysis was initiated to promote technical exchange between the two countries and update the AI landscape in Mexico.

instruments.name: Ethical Framework for Artificial Intelligence in Colombia
instruments.summary: The Ethical Framework for AI provides a set of ethical principles that should be considered in the design, development and implementation of AI systems. The document describes a methodology for determining how these principles should be considered and implemented in countries such as Colombia. Additionally, it includes a toolbox that describes a series of strategies that can be implemented to develop these principles in public entities.

instruments.name: EU Strategy for Artificial Intelligence
instruments.summary: This Coordinated Plan sets out the European Union's strategic objectives and priorities for artificial intelligence. It is a European umbrella strategy for AI, which was developed in cooperation with Member States, and calls on Member States to implement the Coordinated Plan at national level.

instruments.name: Bill of Rights of the Person in the Digital Environment
instruments.summary: the Bill of Rights of the Person in the Digital Environment is a bulwark for all those people who have not bothered to read the fine print every time we download an application, enter a social network or make an electronic purchase, as it will help us to become aware of the risks we face when making use of technologies,  but also that we are not alone in defending our rights.

instruments.name: Sandbox Framework for Adoption of Innovative Technologies in the Public Sector
instruments.summary: Under the Sandbox Framework, interested companies (local or international as well as incubators) will be required to offer a Minimum Viable Product (MVP), that is, a version of the new product with sufficient features, to allow the public organisation to evaluate its appropriateness with the least efforts and resources.

instruments.name: Forecasting the Impact of Automation and the Technologies of the Fourth Industrial Revolution 4RI
instruments.summary: The national government is planning to monitor the labor market to obtain timely evidence on the effects of AI and fourth industrial revolution technology.

instruments.name: Artificial Intelligence Readiness Stage Assessment
instruments.summary: This report presents a fundamentally optimistic view that is shared across UNESCO: that ethical governance and responsible regulation of AI are fully consistent with innovation and economic growth, and are essential to ensure a technology ecosystem that benefits the public good. With the data from the RAM and the report, Mexico has a clear roadmap to achieve this.

instruments.name: IndiaAI Safe and Trusted AI
instruments.summary: The Safe & Trusted AI pillar aims to design and develop adequate guardrails to advance the responsible development, deployment, and adoption of AI.

instruments.name: Policy on Research Ethics, Bioethics and Scientific Integrity
instruments.summary: Through Resolution 0314 of 2018, Colombia has adopted the Policy on Research Ethics, Bioethics and Scientific Integrity.

instruments.name: The European Alliance
instruments.summary: An open multi-stakeholder platform with nearly 3800 members (October 2019), that was set up to provide broader input for the work of the AI high-level expert group, engaged in a broad and open discussion of all aspects of AI development and its impacts.

instruments.name: Inter-institutional AI Committee
instruments.summary: The Inter-institutional Artificial Intelligence Committee is a strategic body designed to coordinate, promote, guide, and articulate, in an inter-institutional manner, the public policy initiatives of the national government of Colombia in the field of AI.

instruments.name: AI4Dev Reference Group
instruments.summary: On 3 November 2023, United Nations Development Programme and Microsoft launched the AI4Dev Reference Group to help shape prospective AI opportunities in Nigeria. The collaboration is the latest in ongoing UNDP<>Microsoft Partnerships in Nigeria, which aim to support the acceleration of development in the country through digital transformation.

instruments.name: Emerging Technologies Handbook
instruments.summary: This handbook guides national and territorial government entities in the use and adoption of new technologies and tools.

instruments.name: European Public Procurement Data Strategy
instruments.summary: The European Public Procurement Data Strategy will define the building blocks and objectives for a European Public Procurement Data Space.

instruments.name: Digital Transformation and Telecommunications Agency
instruments.summary: The Agency for Digital Transformation and Telecommunications is a new entity created by the government of Mexico, Its main objective is to digitize government procedures that are currently carried out in person. This seeks to simplify the lives of citizens, reduce corruption and improve administrative efficiency, among its specific objectives is to unify the technological capabilities of the government, generate technological autonomy. reduce budget costs and facilitate access to digital service

instruments.name: India Stack
instruments.summary: India Stack is the moniker for a set of open APIs and digital public goods that aim to unlock the economic primitives of identity, data, and payments at population scale.

instruments.name: Guidelines for the Implementation of Data Trust and Data Commons Models
instruments.summary: Initiative establishing the guidelines for formulating and developing data trusts and data commons in Colombia.

instruments.name: Proposal for the National Agenda for Artificial Intelligence for Mexico 2024-2030
instruments.summary: This document is a collaborative effort of experts from the public and private sectors, academia, organized civil society, international organizations, and the general public, coordinated by the National Alliance for Artificial Intelligence, in collaboration with UNESCO, for the benefit of the entire Mexican population.

instruments.name: AI Hub Tetouan
instruments.summary: A groundbreaking 386MW data center and AI hub is planned in Tetouan, Morocco. Named Eureka Park, this hub aims to become a premier global technology center, focusing on advanced AI computation and data storage. It will feature the Iozera AI Data Center, GenV Data Management Services for AI training and data handling, Ryse Research for startup incubation and workforce training, and an AI Expo to showcase global advancements in AI technology.

instruments.name: Data Marketplace And Data Infrastructure - MOONSHOT
instruments.summary: Colombia is in the process of developing a data marketplace and data infrastructure strategy to facilitate data sharing.

instruments.name: TechGarden
instruments.summary: Tech Garden is an innovation cluster established by the Government of Kazakhstan in order to foster technology innovation ecosystem and further development of economic and social sustainability that will boost investment in research and development (R&D) and technology transfer and commercialization.

instruments.name: Big Data Policy (Data Governance Framework)
instruments.summary: The BigData policy aims to increase the use of data, by developing the conditions for them to be managed as assets for generate social and economic value.

instruments.name: Sectorial AI Testing and Experimentation Facilities under the Digital Europe Programme
instruments.summary: To make the EU the place where AI excellence thrives from the lab to the market, the European Union is setting up world-class Testing and Experimentation Facilities (TEFs) for AI.Together with Member States, the Commission is co-funding the TEFs which are specialised large-scale reference sites open to all technology providers across Europe to test and experiment at scale state-of-the art AI solutions, including both soft-and hardware products and services, e.g. robots, in real-world environme

instruments.name: Srijan/YuvAI
instruments.summary: The Center will empower students and young developers to leverage AI for real-world problem-solving, targeting key sectors like education, mobility, and healthcare.

instruments.name: Building a Regulatory Ecosystem for AI
instruments.summary: The main goal is to develop an environment for regulatory experimentation and mechanisms to test different regulatory models.

instruments.name: AI Skills for Business Competency Framework
instruments.summary: To address the skills barriers limiting AI adoption in businesses, the AI Skills for Business Competency Framework presents guidance, including the high-level skills and competencies employees need to support AI adoption. This is the first of a series of products designed to enable businesses to understand their AI upskilling needs and training providers to develop relevant training solutions.

instruments.name: OBIA
instruments.summary: OBIA serves as a public, open-access repository designed to compile and provide information on AI developments in Brazil and to connect with other international observatories.

instruments.name: Co-ordination Bodies for AI Policy Implementation
instruments.summary: The Technical Committee for Transformation and Digital Economy and the Presidential Advisory Office for Digital Transformation (or Consejer­a Presidencial para la Transformacin Digital in Spanish) are two public entities aimed to promote, coordinate, and support the implementation of AI policies in Colombia.

instruments.name: Science and Technology Options Assessment (STOA) Panel Centre for AI
instruments.summary: The STOA Centre for AI produces studies, organises public events and acts as a platform for dialogue and information exchange on AI-relevant topics within the Parliament and beyond.

instruments.name: National AI Service Platform
instruments.summary: The National AI Service Platform is part of the national strategy to develop infrastructure for artificial intelligence technology.

instruments.name: AI Covid-19 Response
instruments.summary: Colombia promotes the development of solutions for problems caused by the COVID-19 pandemic and other acute respiratory infections (ARIs) with a great impact on public health, through the selection and funding of AI projects that promote scientific and technological results in the diagnosis, treatment, mitigation and monitoring of the corresponding diseases.

instruments.name: European Group on Ethics in Science and New Technologies (EGE)
instruments.summary: Independent, multi-disciplinary body appointed by the President of the European Commission which advises on all aspects of Commission policies where ethical, societal and fundamental rights issues intersect with the development of science and new technologies.

instruments.name: Empowering Education Leaders: A Toolkit for Safe, Ethical, and Equitable AI Integration
instruments.summary: This relevant, user-friendly resource was developed through engagement with educators, community members and technology leaders and is shaped by the real-world challenges faced by schools and districts of all sizes. Whether an education leader is at the beginning stages of AI adoption or is already exploring its applications, this toolkit offers critical guidance to support the intentional use of AI in education

instruments.name: NSTDA Supercomputer
instruments.summary: NSTDA Supercomputer center (ThaiSC), founded in 2018, is one of the national science and technology infrastructure (NSTI) located in Thailand Science Park.

instruments.name: 4IR Technologies for Agriculture (In Progress)
instruments.summary: The Center for the Fourth Industrial Revolution in conjunction with the Ministry of Information Technology and Communications seeks to develop 10 pilot projects with the installation and use of 4.0 technologies regarding coffee, cocoa, and avocado crops from different regions of Colombia with the purpose of collecting, analyzing, and using their information to provide recommendations that allow small and medium farmers to improve their productivity and competitiveness.

instruments.name: Open Data Directive
instruments.summary: The Directive on open data and the re-use of public sector information provides a common legal framework for a European market for government-held data (public sector information). It is built around two key pillars of the internal market: transparency and fair competition.

instruments.name: Artificial General Intelligence for Science of Transformative Research Innovation Platform (TRIP-AGIS)
instruments.summary: Utilizing an AI foundation model and letting the model additionally learn scientific research data (multi-modalization), develop domain-oriented foundation models for scientific research (AI Foundation Models for Science).

instruments.name: Mechanism for the Implementation of Principles and International Standards in AI
instruments.summary: Plan to follow up the implementation of the recommendations of the OECD Artificial Intelligence Council and the international standards established by multilateral organizations and international treaties on this matter.

instruments.name: Kenya Education Network (KENET)
instruments.summary: Kenya Education Network Trust (KENET) is a not-for-profit membership operator incorporated to support research and education institutions.
